Quomodo ergo imagines corporeæ eorum à corpore separatorum similitudinem gerunt? Et quæ tandem Divinitatis, juxta quam solam Christus adorationis objectum est, effigies exsculpi potest? Neque posterius iconolatras expediet felicius, tum quia similis intentio nec Judæos vitulum, nec Paganos idola seu imagines supremi Numinis colentes ab idololatriæ culpa liberavit; tum quia incurvatio versus imagines Deiparæ & Sanctorum, ceu eorundem præsentium symbola, & vetita planè est, & omnipræsentiæ omniscientiæque excellentiam Deiparæ & Sanctis eximiam facit, adeóque honorem Dei non-Diis impertitur.
units.tr: {a} The reference of images to prototypes. Neither the likeness of images to the prototypes nor the intention of the image-worshippers can be the foundation of religious worship in bowing before them. For, first, the external lineaments apart from the prototypes have nothing venerable and excellent in them; second, the principal part of the prototype, the mind, which alone is venerable, is not represented in the image; and the Papist images do not even have the forms of the prototypes. For the cross of Christ, and Christ himself, were not expressed by any image, but by a symbol and type, until the Sixth General Council, as Cassander proves from Paulinus. And Christ was usually represented by a lamb, and the cross by a crown woven everywhere with flowers. Whence then is that image of Christ and the cross, which has been carried about since the General Council? What indubitable mark of a likeness founding religious worship is it? The same reasoning holds for images of the Mother of God, of the Apostles, of the ancient saints; no one will persuade us that they express the exact form of the prototypes. Most images differ only in beards, insignia and dress. Indeed, images are often like men known to us, born yesterday or the day before, sometimes notoriously wicked; and such worship and honour would fall on them. What of the fact that images are set up for saints who are in heaven, enjoying the heavenly vision? They, however, live in heaven not in the body but only in the soul. How then can corporeal images bear the likeness of those who are separated from the body? And what image of the Deity, in respect of which alone Christ is the object of adoration, can ever be carved? Nor will the second alternative serve the image-worshippers any better: first, because a similar intention did not free the Jews from the guilt of idolatry in worshipping the calf, nor the pagans who worshipped idols or images of the supreme Deity; second, because bowing towards images of the Mother of God and the saints, as symbols of their presence, is plainly forbidden, and it attributes to the Mother of God and the saints the eminent excellence of omnipresence and omniscience, and so gives the honour of God to non-gods.

units.la: LXIX. Iconolatriæ species haud infima est Staurolatria, seu cultus imaginis crucis & crucifixi Christi. quo cultu vix aliud Hierarchia solennius habet. Et quidem latriæ summum in hoc genere cultum, totiusque religionis apicem cruci Thomas Aquinas 3. par. 4. 25. 4. vindicat. Quæ sententia publica fere Ecclesiæ Romanæ authoritate constituitur. Nam Pontificale, publicum atque authenticum volumen, à Papa non uno confirmatum Parte 3 p. 480. Crux Legati, inquit, quia debetur ei latria, erit à dextris. Quin & crucem, statim atque consecrata est, uti ibidem par. 2. p. 361. habetur, Pontifex flexis ante eam genibus devote adorat & ofculatur. Idem faciunt, quicunque alii voluerint. Solennis maxime ejus adoratio fit feria sexta Parasceve antePaschali. Ritus adorationis ejus in Missali Romano fer. 6. in Parafc. p. 225. 226. legere est. Completis orationibus Sacerdos primò crucem jam in altari præparatam accipit à Diacono. Ubi ad locum ventum est, quo chorus cantat, Venite, adoremus; tum omnes se prosternunt, excepto celebrante, qui disco operit brachium dextrum crucis, ac elevans eam tertiò, altius incipit: Ecce lignum crucis; aliis cantantibus & adorantibus: Ecce lignum crucis, in quo salus mundi pependit, Chorus respondet: Venite adoremus. Postea Sacerdos solus portat crucem ad locum ante altare præparatum, & genu flexus ibidem eam locat; mox depositis calceamentis accedit ad adorandam crucem, ter genua flectens, antequam eam osculetur. Hoc facto revertitur, & recipit calceamenta & casulam. Hæc Sacerdos, vix quæsitiorem & sanctiorem adorationis cultum ipsi Christo exhibiturus, si in terris esset. Demum ministri altaris, dein alii clerici & laici bisti & bini ter genibus flexi crucem adorant. Inde cantatur communiter Antiana: Crucem tuam adoramus, Domine, & sanctam resurrectionem tuam laudamus & glorificamus. Ecce enim propter lignum venit gaudium in universo mundo. Post cantatur: Crux fidelis, inter omnes arbores una nobilis, Nulla silva talem profert, fronde, flore, germine, dulces clavos, dulce pondus sustinet. Sed & die Septembris 14. in solennibus Missæ Sacris, ea parte, quæ Offertorium vocatur, sic Deum precari mos est: Protege, Domine, plebem tuam per signum sanctæ crucis ab insidiis inimicorum omnium, &c. In secreto rogant, ut sicut illud (crucis vexillum) adorare meruerunt, ita perenniter ejus gloriæ salutaris potiantur effectu. In Missa de Sancta cruce: Tuam crucem adoramus, Domine. Mensis Maii die tertio, quo crucem ab Helena inventam credunt, inter cetera sacra oratio dicitur, qua crucem, ceu vivum Numen sic invocant: O crux splendidior cunctis astris, mundo celebris, hominibus multum amabilis, sanctior universis, quæ sola fuisti digna portare talentum mundi; dulce lignum, dulces clavos, dulcia ferens pondera, SALVA præsentem caterva m in tuis hodie laudibus congregatam. Oratio in Breviario Rom. festo Maii p. 892. extat. Christi ipsius, & imaginis crucis ejus adorationi differentiam nullam relinqui, liquet. Unde Guilhelmus Philander Annot. in Vitruv. de architect. lib. iv. 8. crucifixi Christi imaginem Christi in cruce pendentis appellatione insignit. Et in solennitate Parasceves Paschæ supra memorata, Presbyter imaginem crucifixi ex sepulchro recipiens, templum circuit, & portas ejusdem clausas pulsat, dicens: Attollite portas principes vestras, & elevamini portæ æternales, & introibit Rex gloriæ. Interrogante eo, qui in portis excubat: Quis est iste Rex gloriæ? Presbyter respondet: Dominus fortis & potens in prælio, Dominus virtutum, ipse est Rex gloriæ. Simulachrum ergo crucis est Dominus, Rex gloriæ.
units.tr: LXIX. A not unimportant species of image-worship is Staurolatria, that is, the cult of the image of the cross and of the crucified Christ. Hierarchy has hardly any more solemn rite than this. Indeed Thomas Aquinas, in 3 par. 4. 25. 4., claims the highest latria in this kind of worship, and the summit of all religion, for the cross. This opinion is almost wholly established by the authority of the Church of Rome. For the Pontificale, a public and authentic volume confirmed by more than one Pope, says in Part 3, p. 480: "The Cross is to be carried at the legate's right hand, because latria is due to him." Moreover, as soon as the cross has been consecrated, as is stated in the same work, par. 2, p. 361, "the Pontiff devoutly adores it on bended knees and kisses it. Whoever else wishes to do the same may do so." Its adoration is most solemn on the sixth feria before Easter, Good Friday. The rite of its adoration may be read in the Roman Missal, fer. 6 in Parasceve, pp. 225–226. When the prayers are finished, the priest first receives the cross, already prepared on the altar, from the deacon. When they reach the point where the choir sings, "Come, let us adore," then all prostrate themselves, except the celebrant, who uncovers the right arm of the cross with a veil, lifts it up three times, and begins more loudly: "Behold the wood of the cross." While the others sing and adore, "Behold the wood of the cross, on which the salvation of the world hung," the choir responds: "Come, let us adore." Afterwards the priest alone carries the cross to a place prepared before the altar, and there, kneeling, sets it down; then, having taken off his shoes, he approaches to adore the cross, bending his knees three times before he kisses it. When this is done, he returns and puts on his shoes and chasuble. This priest, about to offer Christ himself, were he on earth, a more exquisite and holier worship of adoration. Finally the ministers of the altar, then the other clergy and laity, two by two and in pairs, kneel three times and adore the cross. Then the antiphon is sung together: "We adore your cross, O Lord, and we praise and glorify your holy resurrection. For behold, by the wood joy has come into the whole world." After this is sung: "Faithful Cross, noblest of all trees, no forest bears one like you in leaf, flower, or bud, sweet nails, sweet weight, you bear." Also on the 14th of September, in the solemn Mass, in that part called the Offertory, it is customary to pray to God thus: "Protect, O Lord, your people by the sign of the holy cross from the snares of all enemies, etc." In the secret prayer they ask "that, just as they have been granted to adore that banner of the cross, so they may forever enjoy the saving effect of its glory." In the Mass of the Holy Cross: "We adore your cross, O Lord." On the third day of May, the day on which they believe the cross was found by Helena, among other holy prayers one is said in which they invoke the cross as a living deity: "O cross more splendid than all the stars, celebrated in the world, most lovable to men, holier than all things, you alone were worthy to bear the ransom of the world; sweet wood, sweet nails, bearing sweet weights, SAVE the company gathered here today in your praises." This prayer is found in the Roman Breviary, feast of May, p. 892. It is clear that no difference is left between the adoration of Christ himself and the adoration of the image of his cross. Hence Guilhelmus Philander, in his Annotations on Vitruvius, On Architecture, book 4, chapter 8, marks the image of the crucified Christ with the title "Christ hanging on the cross." And in the solemnity of Good Friday and Easter mentioned above, the elder, taking the image of the crucified from the sepulchre, goes around the church and knocks on its closed doors, saying: "Lift up your gates, O princes, and be lifted up, eternal gates, and the King of glory shall come in." When the one who keeps watch at the gates asks, "Who is this King of glory?" the elder answers: "The Lord, strong and mighty in battle, the Lord of hosts, he is the King of glory." Therefore the image of the cross is "the Lord, the King of glory."

units.la: LXX. Quæ verò, quantáque à crucibus suis Staurolatræ expectent, ne ignoremus, Pontifex inter cetera, quibus crucem novam dedicat, uti Pontif. Rom. p. 359. & Ritual. p. 375. recitatur, à Domino Sancto Patre Omnipotente Deo sempiterno poscit, ut dignetur benedicere hoc signum crucis suæ, ut sit, inquit, remedium salutare generi humano, sit soliditas fidei, profectus bonorum operum, redemptio animarum, sit solamen & protectio ac tutela contra sæva jacula inimicorum. Non majora sunt, quæ Christiani non dico à Christi Sacramentis, sed ab ipso Christo expectant. Sequitur dein longum carmen, in quo, præeunte Pontifice, multa de ligni mysteriis apud Deum philosophati, inter alia sic orant: Sit ei (plebi) crux fidei fundamentum, spei suffragium, in adversis defensio, in prosperis adjuvamen. Sit ei in hostes victoria, in civitate custodia, in campis protectio, in domo fultura. Postremo carmine sic consecratur crux: Sanctificetur lignum istud in nomine Patris, & Filii, & Spiritus S. Et benedictio illius ligni, in quo membra sancta Salvatoris suspensa sunt, sit in isto ligno; ut orantes inclinantésque se propter Deum ante istam crucem inveniant corporis & animæ salutem. Atque illud singulare est, quod Christum rogant, ut crucem illis manibus accipiat, quibus suam amplexus est. De sanctitate illius, inquiunt, hanc sanctifica; & sicuti per illam mundus expiatus est à reatu: ita offerentium famulorum tuorum animæ devotissimæ Hujus crucis MERITO omni careant perpetrato peccato, & tuæ veræ crucis obtectu enitescant succeßibus assiduis triumphatores. Radiet hic unigeniti Filii tui Domini nostri splendor Divinitatis in auro: emicet gloria passionis ejus in ligno: in cruce rutilet nostræ mortis redemptio, in crystalli splendore vitæ nostræ purificatio. Sit eorum protectio; spei certa fiducia eos simul cum gente & plebe fide fide confirmet; spe & pace consociet; augeat triumphis; amplificet in secundis; proficiat eis ad perpetuitatem temporis, ad vitam æternitatis, ut eos temporali florentes gloria muniat, & ad perpetuam redemptos coronam ad regna cœlestia potenti virtute perducat. Crux proficiscentium in subsidium terræ Sanctæ, sic ibid. p. 381. consecratur, ut Pontifex hæc à Deo poscat: Te supplíciter exoramus, ut digneris hanc crucem paternà pietate benedicere. & COELESTEM EI VIRTUTEM ET GRATIAM impertiri, ut quicunque eam in passionis, & crucis Unigeniti tui signum ad tutelam corporis & animæ super se gestaverit, Cœlestis gratiæ in ea plenitudinem, & munimen valeat tuæ benedictionis accipere. Quis non videt, in simulachrum crucis virtutem crucis, in qua Christus pependit (cui absolutum latriæ cultum illi deputant) meritum, Cœlestem virtutem & gratiam, aliáque merè Divina ὑλικὴ λατρεία effundi, atque illud qua tale, adorari?
units.tr: LXX. Lest we be ignorant of what and how great things the Staurolaters expect from their crosses: among other prayers with which the Pontiff dedicates a new cross, as is recited in the Pontificale Romanum, p. 359, and the Ritual, p. 375, he asks of the Lord, the Holy Father, almighty and eternal God, that he deign to bless this sign of his cross, "so that it may be," he says, "a saving remedy for the human race, a firmness of faith, progress in good works, the redemption of souls, a comfort and protection and defence against the savage darts of enemies." Christians do not expect greater things, I do not say from the sacraments of Christ, but from Christ himself. Then follows a long poem, in which, with the Pontiff leading, many things are reasoned out before God about the mysteries of the wood, and among other things they pray thus: "Let the cross be for the people a foundation of faith, a support of hope, a defence in adversity, a help in prosperity. Let it bring victory over enemies, guard in the city, protection in the fields, support in the house." At last the cross is consecrated with this verse: "Let this wood be sanctified in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. And let the blessing of that wood on which the holy limbs of the Saviour were hung be in this wood, so that those who pray and bow themselves before this cross for God's sake may find salvation of body and soul." And this is remarkable: they ask Christ that he take the cross "into those hands with which he embraced his own. Sanctify this," they say, "by its holiness, and as the world was cleansed of guilt through it, so may the souls of your servants who offer it, most devoted, by the MERIT of this cross, be free of every sin committed, and by the covering of your true cross may they shine as triumphers in continual successes. Let the splendour of the Divinity of your only-begotten Son, our Lord, shine here in the gold; let the glory of his passion gleam in the wood; let the redemption of our death glow on the cross; let the purification of our life be in the brightness of the crystal. May it be their protection; may the sure confidence of hope strengthen them in faith together with their nation and people; may it unite them in hope and peace; may it increase their triumphs; may it advance them in prosperity; may it benefit them for the duration of time and for the life of eternity, so that it may protect them, flourishing in temporal glory, and by its mighty power lead those redeemed to the perpetual crown of the heavenly kingdoms." The cross of those setting out to help the Holy Land is consecrated in the same way, ibid. p. 381, and the Pontiff asks of God this: "We humbly beseech you that you deign to bless this cross with a fatherly kindness, and to impart to it HEAVENLY POWER AND GRACE, so that whoever bears it upon himself as a sign of the passion and cross of your only-begotten Son, for the protection of body and soul, may receive the fullness of heavenly grace and the defence of your blessing in it." Who does not see that in the image of the cross they pour out the power of the cross on which Christ hung (to which they assign the absolute latria), the merit, the heavenly power and grace, and other things purely Divine, [material worship: ὑλικὴ λατρεία], and that it is adored as such?

units.la: LXXI. Ad Lipsanolatriam, seu Reliquiarum cul- tum venimus.
units.tr: LXXI. We come now to Lipsanolatry, or the worship of relics.

units.la: in quo non minus ἀνδριάντος εἰδωλολατρεία nefaria idololatria, ut cum S. Petro loquar, grassatur. Tridentini iidem Sess. xxv. sic de reliquiarum honore loquuntur: Sanctorum Martyrum, & aliorum cum Christo viventium Sancta corpora, quæ viva membra fuerunt Christi, & templum Spiritus S. ab ipso ad æternam vitam suscitanda & glorificanda, à fidelibus venerada esse: per quæ multa beneficia à Deo hominibus præstantur: ita ut affirmantes, Sanctorum reliquiis venerationem atque honorem non deberi; vel eas aliáque sacra monumenta à fidelibus inutiliter honorari; atque eorum opis impetrandæ causa Sanctorum memorias frustra frequentari; omnino damnandos esse, prout jam pridem eos damnavit, & nunc etiam damnat Ecclesia. Puduit Tridentinos dicere, quod res est. Non ergo palam Ecclesiæ suæ sententiam describunt, sed tectè admodum & versutè. Non enim de veneratione, honore reliquiarum, sed de specie honoris & venerationis illius disceptari probè noverant; an videlicet religiosa iis adoratio competat. Competere equidem Synodus credidit, sed verbis exprimere erubuit, quia crudele nimis videbatur, à Synodo Christi nomen professa damnari quenquam eo nomine, quòd hominum mortuorum corpora adorare palam refugiat.
units.tr: in which the idolatry of the statue [ἀνδριάντος εἰδωλολατρεία], impious idolatry, as I may say with St Peter, rages no less. The Tridentines themselves, in Sess. xxv., speak thus of the honour due to relics: The holy bodies of the holy martyrs and of the others living with Christ, which were living members of Christ and a temple of the Holy Spirit, and which are to be raised up and glorified by him to eternal life, are to be venerated by the faithful; through them God bestows many benefits on men. So those who affirm that veneration and honour are not due to the relics of the saints, or that these and other sacred monuments are uselessly honoured by the faithful, or that the memorials of the saints are frequented in vain for the sake of obtaining their help, are wholly to be condemned, as the Church has long since condemned them and now condemns them. The Tridentines were ashamed to say what is the case. They therefore do not openly set out the opinion of their Church, but do so very covertly and craftily. For they well knew that the dispute concerns not the veneration or honour of relics, but the kind of honour and veneration, namely whether religious worship is owed to them. The Synod believed that it was owed, but it blushed to say so in words, because it seemed too cruel that anyone should be condemned by a Synod that professes the name of Christ for that name alone, merely because he openly refuses to adore the bodies of dead men.

units.la: LXXII. Adorandas esse Sanctorum reliquias, summo consensu Ecclesia Romana docet. Nititurque earum adoratio authoritate Concilii Nicæni II. cujus Act. 4. hæc verba sunt: Offa, cineres, pannos, sanguinem, sepulchra denique adorantes, illis tamen non sacrificamus. Catechesis Tridentina in præcept. 3. probat juramenta per reliquias: Ad faciendam, inquit, fidem, per res creatas juramus, ut per sacra Dei Evangelia, per crucem, per Sanctorum reliquias & nomen. Qui honor ad latriæ cultum pertinet. Per quem enim juramus, eum testem conscientiæ invocamus, & ultorem imprecamur, si fefellerimus. Quæ potestas & scientia solius Dei est. In Pontificali Romano legere sancitur, ne ullum altare absque reliquiis consecretur. Ideo capite de consecrat. alt. altare sepulchrum vocatur, dicitúrque altare dedicari in honorem & nomen Sancti, cujus reliquiæ altari includuntur. Pertinet id ad Missæ integritatem & dignitatem. Nam in ea Sacerdos prona facie altari incumbens has voces submurmurat: Oramus te Domine, per merita Sanctorum, quorum reliquiæ hic sunt, & omnium Sanctorum, ut indulgere digneris omnia peccata mea. Vasquez ingenuè magis, quàm alii, tegentes isthoc dedecus, sic in 3. Thom. q. 25. disp. 112. c. 2. in ipso limine scribit : Apud Catholicos veritas indubitanda est, reliquias Sanctorum, sive fuerint partes ipsorum, ut ossa, carnes & cineres, sive res aliæ, quæ ipsos tegerunt, vel ad ipsos pertineant, ADORANDAS & in hoc honore sacro habendas esse. Mox disp. 113. cinctoria & sudaria ait adorationis cultu fuisse veneranda. Disputatione absoluta perorat, se contra hæreticos constituisse, reliquias esse adorandas. Atque ita passim loquitur. Thomas Waldensis Doctr. part. 3. Tit. 13. cap. 120. ex Damasceno definit, non modo lignum crucis Domini, sed etiam sepulchrum, præsepe, clavos, lanceam, vestes, Sion, & Golgotha esse adoranda; eósque, qui sic adorare detrectant, velut hæreticos refutat, qui Deum quidem in his locis aut rebus adorari concedunt, res vero ipsas aut loca adoranda negant. Mox cap. 121. dicit, omnes Dei Sanctos & eorum reliquias esse suis gradibus adorandas. Ibidem dictum quoddam Ambrosii ab Adversario objectum expendens vehementer contendit, Helenam Constantini matrem Regem Christum sic adoraviisse, ut etiam lignum adoraverit propter Regem. Baronius A. 821. ff. 14. dicit se à Clemente missum, licet tanto munere indignissimum, ut exploraret & adoraret venerandum Cæciliæ corpus Prædicare Evangelium res est in Cardinali sordida; at adorare Cæciliæ ossa res est, quam longè supra dignitatem Cardinalis esse Baronius agnoscit.
units.tr: LXXII. The Roman Church teaches, with the greatest unanimity, that the relics of the saints are to be adored. Their adoration rests on the authority of the Second Council of Nicaea, whose Act. 4 contains these words: Adoring bones, ashes, cloths, blood, and indeed tombs, yet we do not offer sacrifice to them. The Tridentine Catechism, in in praecept. 3, approves oaths by relics: To make, it says, our faith sure, we swear by created things, as by the holy Gospels of God, by the cross, by the relics and name of the saints. This honour belongs to the worship of latria. For when we swear by someone, we call him as witness of our conscience and pray for his vengeance if we have sworn falsely. That power and knowledge belong to God alone. The Roman Pontifical lays down that no altar is to be consecrated without relics. Hence, in the chapter de consecrat. alt., the altar is called a sepulchre, and it is said that the altar is dedicated in the honour and name of the saint whose relics are enclosed in the altar. This pertains to the integrity and dignity of the Mass. For in it the priest, lying face down upon the altar, murmurs these words: We beseech you, Lord, by the merits of the saints whose relics are here, and of all the saints, that you deign to forgive all my sins. Vasquez, more frankly than others, covering this disgrace, writes at the very threshold of sic in 3. Thom. q. 25. disp. 112. c. 2. in ipso limine: Among Catholics it is beyond doubt that the relics of the saints, whether they are parts of them, such as bones, flesh and ashes, or other things that covered them or belonged to them, are TO BE ADORED and held in this sacred honour. Soon after, in disp. 113, he says that girdles and handkerchiefs were to be venerated with the worship of adoration. Having finished the disputation, he concludes that he has set himself against the heretics by maintaining that relics are to be adored. And he speaks in this way throughout. Thomas Waldensis, in Doctr. part. 3. Tit. 13. cap. 120, following Damascene, lays down that not only the wood of the Lord's cross but also the sepulchre, the manger, the nails, the lance, the garments, Sion and Golgotha are to be adored. He refutes as heretics those who refuse to adore in this way, who grant that God is to be adored in these places or things, but deny that the things or places themselves are to be adored. Soon after, in cap. 121, he says that all God's saints and their relics are to be adored in their proper degrees. In the same place, weighing a saying of Ambrose that his opponent had raised, he vehemently contends that Helena, the mother of Constantine, so adored the King Christ that she even adored the wood on account of the King. Baronius, in A. 821, ff. 14, says that he was sent by Clement, though most unworthy of so great a task, to search out and adore the venerable body of Cecilia. To preach the Gospel is, for a cardinal, a lowly business; but to adore the bones of Cecilia is a thing which Baronius acknowledges to be far above the dignity of a cardinal.

units.la: LXXIII. Sed nunc res, non verba spectemus.
units.tr: LXXIII. But now let us look at the thing, not the words.

units.la: Quocunque enim nomine reliquiarum cultum appellent, sive adorationis, quod simplicius, & ipsi rei consentaneum est; sive venerationis, quod fortasse callidius, ad Sophisticen potius pertinet, parum equidem laboramus, dum constet, rem ipsam non aliud, quàm Divinum & religiosum cultum prodere. Jam verò apertum est, Hierarchicos & iisdem obnoxios corpora, cineres, offa & Sanctorum ex sepulchris jam diu quietis eruta elevare; quandoque supra altare collocare; auro, argento, serico exornare; in supplicationibus & processionibus, à populo Christiano spectanda, tangenda, osculanda circumferre; coram semesis illis piorum monumentis gestibus & animo supplices & adorabundos procidere; ab iis gratiam & beneficia Dei exposcere; iis pretiosa dona offerre; ad loca, ubi reliquiæ esse putantur, peregrinationes religiosas instituere; eadem altari, ad sanctitatem Eucharistiæ conciliandam includere; in collo ex devotione & fiducia ad Deum & Sanctos gestare; tactis iis juramenta præstare; denique tali reliquiarum venerationi gratiam, beneficia Dei, efficaciam precum apud casfularum, remissionem peccatorum polliceri. Atque sic, quod alicubi Erasmus, queritur, æquè Lipsanolatræ illi Francisci cucullam, Annæ pectinem, caligam Josephi, Thomæ calceum, ac ipsum Dei filium suspiciunt: quod nullo piaculo luent.
units.tr: For whatever name they give to the worship of relics, whether adoration, which is the plainer term and better suited to the thing itself, or veneration, which is perhaps the more cunning and belongs rather to sophistry, I hardly trouble myself, provided it is agreed that the thing itself reveals nothing other than divine and religious worship. Now it is plain that the hierarchs and those subject to them lift up the bodies, ashes and bones of the saints, long since drawn from their tombs and at rest; sometimes they set them upon the altar; they adorn them with gold, silver and silk; in supplications and processions, to be seen, touched and kissed by the Christian people, they carry them about; before these half-dead monuments of the pious they fall down in gesture and spirit as suppliants and adorers; from them they seek the grace and benefits of God; to them they offer precious gifts; they make religious pilgrimages to the places where the relics are thought to be; they enclose them in the altar to lend holiness to the Eucharist; out of devotion and trust in God and the saints they wear them around the neck; they swear oaths by touching them; and finally they promise such veneration of relics grace from God, benefits, the efficacy of prayers with the saints, and the remission of sins. And so, as Erasmus complains somewhere, they revere the hood of Francis, the comb of Anne, the shoe of Joseph, the sandal of Thomas, no less than the Son of God himself; and they pay no penalty for this sacrilege.

units.la: LXXIV. Frustra ergo Centuriatoribus & Calvino, reliquias à Latinis adorari & Divinis honoribus affici scribentibus, Bellarminus lib. 11. de reliq. & imag. Sanct. cap. 2. succensens, reliquias à se Divino honore affici, vel Christi loco adorari, negat.
units.tr: LXXIV. It is therefore in vain that Bellarmine, in lib. 11. de reliq. & imag. Sanct. cap. 2, flares up against the Centuriators and Calvin, who write that relics are adored by the Latins and honoured with divine honours, and denies that relics are honoured with divine honour by him or adored in place of Christ.

units.la: Nos enim, inquit, reliquias honoramus & osculamur, ut sacra pignora patronorum nostrorum; sed nec adoramus, ut Deum, nec invocamus ut sanctos. Hac scilicet stropha probè se fe defunctum arbitratur, si se id, quod præter Deum adorant, ut Deum adorare negaverit. quasi ulla religiosa adoratio sit, quæ alterius sit, quàm Dei. Et quid prodest protestatio contraria facto? Neque etiam adorationis latreutica, duleutica, absoluta, relativa differentiam, à Sophistis hic decantari ad ravim usque solitam, non semel supra profligatam, moramur quicquam. Dei judicium erit secundum veritatem, non secundum ingeniosas illas præcisiones & intentiones hominum prævaricantium & προφανα ζοντων Etiam qui Baalem osculati tantùm sunt, eum adorasse dicuntur.
units.tr: For we, he says, honour and kiss relics as the sacred pledges of our patrons; but we neither adore them as God nor invoke them as saints. By this verse he evidently thinks he has acquitted himself well, if he has denied that he adores as God what they adore besides God, as God. As if there were any religious adoration that belongs to anyone other than God! And what good is a protestation that contradicts the deed? Nor shall we linger over the distinction of adoration into latreutic, duleutic, absolute, relative, which the sophists chant here to the usual point of weariness, and which has been overthrown more than once above. God's judgment will be according to truth, not according to those ingenious distinctions and intentions of men who prevaricate and pretend [προφασιζόντων]. Even those who only kissed Baal are said to have worshipped him.

units.la: 1. Reg. xix. 8. & propter religiosum illud osculum idolatriæ rei peraguntur.
units.tr: 1 Kings 19:8. And on account of that religious kiss they are convicted of the crime of idolatry.

units.la: LXXV. Lipsanolatria cujusmodi adoratio, absoluta an relativa sit, ipsæ adorationis reliquiarum formulæ produnt. Paucas exponamus. In hymno super ferro lanceæ hæc habentur: Ave ferrum triumphale &c. Felix hasta nos amore per te fixi saucia. An hæc Christo dici possunt ? Lignum crucis sic alloqui mos est: O crux, ave spes unica, hoc passionis tempore, Auge piis justitiam, Reisque dona veniam. Ac ne quis putet, hæc Christo dici metonymicè, vel relativè ad Christum, eidem cruci dicuntur, quæ Christo dici non possunt: Sola digna fuisti ferre Sæcli pretium, Crux fidelis inter omnes Arbores una nobilis. Nec tantùm hæc ligno crucis, sed ejus etiam imagini dicuntur. In æde S. Petri Romæ asservatur sudario impressa effigies vultus Christi, quam Veronicam vocant, nomine mulieris, à qua, ita Baronius A. 34. habet, sudarium traditur faciei Christi sanguine & sudore aspersæ admotum esse, & vultus ejus effigiem in se retinuisse. Est & urbs Hispaniæ, quæ eodem sudario gloriatur; neque immeritò, si Regio Historiographo Marinæo Siculo de rebus Hisp. lib. 5. credimus: æquè sanè merito, ut ego credo, ac Roma. Ad utrum horum sudariorum dicenda sit oratio, quam Johannes XXII. edidit, nescio. Sed ab illo Papa libro Orationum, qui Antidotarius animæ inscribitur, concessa memorantur decem millia dierum indulgentiarum devotè dicentibus orationem certam, & inter dicendum Veronicam inspicientibus. Orationis formula haec est: Salve sancta facies nostri Redemptoris, In qua nitet species Divini splendoris, Impressa panniculo nivei candoris, Data aque Veronicæ signum ob amoris. Salve decus Seculi, speculum Sanctorum, Quod videre cupiunt spiritus Cælorum; Nos ab omni macula purga vitiorum, Atque nos consortio junge beatorum. Salve vultus Domini imago beata, Ex æterno munere mirè decorata: Lumen funde cordibus ex fide tibi data, Et à nostris sensibus tolle calligata. Salve robur fidei nostræ Christianæ, Destruens hæreticos qui sunt mentis vanæ: Horum auge meritum, qui te credunt sanè, Illius effigie, qui Rex fit ex pane. Salve nostrum gaudium in hac vita dura, Labili & fragili citò peritura: Nos adhuc ad propria, O FELIX FIGURA, Ad videndam faciem quæ est Christi pura.
units.tr: LXXV. The kind of adoration Lipsanolatry is, whether absolute or relative, the very formulas of the adoration of relics reveal. Let us set out a few. In a hymn on the iron of the lance these words occur: Hail, triumphal iron, etc. Happy lance, wounded, I was fixed through you by love. Can these words be said to Christ? It is customary to address the wood of the cross thus: O cross, hail, sole hope, in this time of suffering, increase justice in the devout and grant pardon to the guilty. And lest anyone think these things are said to Christ metonymically, or relatively to Christ, they are said to the cross itself, things that cannot be said to Christ: You alone were worthy to bear the price of the age, faithful cross, the one noble tree among all trees. And these are said not only of the wood of the cross but also of its image. In the church of St Peter at Rome is kept the likeness of Christ's face impressed on a cloth, which they call the Veronica, from the name of a woman, to whom, as Baronius records under the year 34, the handkerchief is said to have been brought, soaked with the blood and sweat of Christ's face, and to have retained the image of his countenance. There is also a city in Spain that boasts of the same handkerchief, and not without reason, if we believe the royal historiographer Marineo Siculo, de rebus Hisp. lib. 5: and with as much reason, I believe, as Rome. Which of these two handkerchiefs the prayer published by John XXII is to be said over, I do not know. But that Pope's book of prayers, entitled Antidotarius animae, records that ten thousand days of indulgence are granted to those who devoutly say a certain prayer and, while saying it, look upon the Veronica. The formula of the prayer is this: Hail, holy face of our Redeemer, in which the form of the divine splendour shines, impressed on a little cloth of snowy whiteness, given as a sign of love to Veronica. Hail, glory of the age, mirror of the saints, which the spirits of heaven desire to see; cleanse us from every stain of sin, and join us to the company of the blessed. Hail, blessed image of the Lord's face, marvellously adorned with an eternal gift: pour light into our hearts, given to you by faith, and take away the dimness from our senses. Hail, strength of our Christian faith, destroying the heretics who are of vain mind: increase the merit of those who truly believe you, by that likeness of him who becomes King from bread. Hail, our joy in this hard life, soon to perish, frail and fleeting: bring us still to our own home, O HAPPY FIGURE, to behold the pure face of Christ.

units.la: Parentem, nisi fallor, Durandum Fœtus ille insignis habet. Annon sic Divina & maxima quæque à pi�āa & fiẃa facie Redemptoris, specie Divini splendoris pan-niculo impressa, imagine vultus Domini, felice illa Figura supplices implorant? Nam quomodo orationem illam sic Lipsanolatræ fingere vel refingere, ut ipsi Christo quadret, poterunt?
units.tr: That famous offspring, unless I am mistaken, has Durandus as its parent. Do not the pious and faithful supplicants implore all divine and great things in this way from the face of the Redeemer, the appearance of the divine splendour impressed on the cloth, the image of the Lord's countenance, that happy figure? For how will the relic-worshippers be able to frame or reframe that prayer so that it fits Christ himself?

units.la: LXXVI. Ad Lipsanolatriæ fœditatem pertinet, quòd qui hodie reliquias colunt, ferè venerantur id, quod quale fit, ignorant. Tot enim imposturæ detectæ passim olim & nuper, universas suspectas reddunt. Mitto ocreas Martini, Georgii vaginam, culcultrum Crispini, calcearium, aut quæ in urbe quadam Liguriæ asservari dicitur, caudam asini, cui insedit Christus, aut Rochi canem, aut Antonii suem. Quis mihi Macarius inter tot densas arborum sylvas veram crucem dabit? Aut quæ Helena e tot ferreis montibus clavos? Mirumne, si aruspices ipsi arridla sibi, dum hæc populo ostentant. Fatetur Cassander Consult. de Reliq. Sanct. avaritiæ causa ad simplicem populum alliciendum falsas reliquias plures suppositas, ficta miracula prædicata, iisque miraculis alitam populi superstitionem esse. Nonnunquam, addit aστu & illusione dæmonis, hominum superstitione abutentis, per insomnia & visa novæ reliquiæ revelabantur, & ejusdem operatione miracula edi videbantur. Næ ille elephanti corio circumtectus sit oportet, non suo, qui post tot patefactas fraudes, non tantum incertis adeo reliquiis venditatis fidem habuerit, sed ante eas etiam supplex procubuerit, ut Divinam inde virtutem, sive sanationis, sive sanctificationis reportet.
units.tr: LXXVI. It belongs to the foulness of relic-worship that those who today honour relics mostly venerate what they do not know to be genuine. So many impostures have been detected, here and there, both long ago and recently, that they make all of them suspect. I pass over Martin's greaves, George's scabbard, Crispin's cushion, his shoe, or what is said to be kept in a certain city of Liguria, the ass's tail on which Christ sat, or the dog of Roch, or the pig of Anthony. Who will give me the true cross, Macarius, among so many dense forests of trees? Or which Helena will give me the nails out of so many iron mountains? Is it any wonder if the diviners themselves smile at one another while they display these things to the people? Cassander confesses in Consult. de Reliq. Sanct. that, for the sake of greed, many false relics were foisted on to lure the simple people, invented miracles were proclaimed, and the people's superstition was nourished by those miracles. Sometimes, he adds, by the cunning and illusion of a demon who abuses human superstition, new relics were revealed through dreams and visions, and miracles were seen to be performed by their operation. Surely he must be wrapped in an elephant's hide, and not his own, who, after so many frauds have been exposed, would not only believe in relics hawked so uncertainly, but would even prostrate himself before them, in order to obtain from them divine power, whether for healing or for sanctification.

units.la: LXXVII. Restat Hierolatria, sive rerum consecratarum cultus.
units.tr: LXXVII. There remains hierolatry, or the worship of consecrated things.

units.la: Missis benedictionibus & consecrationibus Chrismatis, aquæ lustralis, oleorum, cerei Paschalis, campanarum, quas res Papa consecratione sua Divina virtute mactatas & impregnatas in idola convertit; specimen unicum delibabimus, ut ἐκ ἔ Κςχαρπίδα τὸ ὑφαςμα γινώσκειν. liceat; cultum videlicet Agnorum Dei cereorum. quibus Papalis consecratio Divinam venerationem cultumque conciliat. Consecrat enim eos solus Papa, Papatus sui primo & septimo quoque anno recurrente. Materia Agnorum est balsamus, sacrum chrisma, aqua benedicta, & cera alba seu munda. Ritus Papæ eos consecrantis Marcelli Corcyrensis Ceremoniale Romanum lib. 1. sect. 7. ejusmodi prodit: Cubicularii ad Papam portant Agnos Dei, quos Pontifex immergit in aquam, & Prælati adstantes eos extrahunt, & in pelvibus argenteis portant super mensas &c. Et omnibus baptizatis per Pontificem, vel per ejus Prælatos, surgens Pontifex sine mitra dicit super eos has orationes: O alme Spiritus &c. qui in aquarum substantia maxima Sacramenta constituisti, quæ sunt tuo flatu sanctificatæ, atque imperante lavacri suscep tione, S. Trinitatis nomine invocato, omnia peccata diluunt: quæsumus Domine, hi Agni sacra & perenni unda balsamóque sacri chrismatis perfusi, tu illo benedicere &c. Unde in fonte natos dixit Poeta, id est, in Baptismo, quia Papa eos in nomine S. S. Trinitatis cum horribili Sacramenti profanatione baptizat.
units.tr: Setting aside the blessings and consecrations of chrism, holy water, oils, the Paschal candle, and bells, which the Pope, by his consecration, turns into idols, having been endowed and impregnated with divine power, we shall offer one single specimen, so that one may know the whole web from a single thread [ἐκ κρόκης τὸ ὕφασμα γινώσκειν]: namely the worship of the wax Agnus Dei, to which papal consecration brings divine veneration and worship. Only the Pope consecrates them, in the first year of his papacy and in every seventh year after that. The matter of the Agnus is balsam, holy chrism, blessed water, and white or pure wax. The rite of the Pope consecrating them is reported thus by Marcellus of Corcyra, Ceremoniale Romanum lib. 1. sect. 7.: The chamberlains bring the Agnus Dei to the Pope, and the Pontiff immerses them in water, and the prelates standing by take them out and carry them on silver dishes over the tables, etc. And for all who have been baptized by the Pontiff, or by his prelates, the Pontiff rises without his mitre and says over them these prayers: O gentle Spirit, etc., who in the substance of waters has established the greatest sacraments, which are sanctified by your breath, and by whose command, with the name of the Holy Trinity invoked, the reception of washing washes away all sins: we beseech you, Lord, bless these Lambs, sprinkled with holy and everlasting water and the balsam of holy chrism, etc. Hence the poet said born at the font, that is, in Baptism, because the Pope baptizes them in the name of the Holy Trinity, with a dreadful profanation of the sacrament.

units.la: LXXVIII. Quæ virtus Agnis hisce Dei insit, & quis honor debeatur iisdem; tum ex Papæ consecrantis precatione; tum ex carmine, cum quo Urbanus V. tres Agnos Dei Græcorum Imperatori misit, cognoscitur. Utraque in Ceremoniali eodem consignata extat.
units.tr: LXXVIII. What power is in these Lambs of God, and what honour is owed them, is known both from the Pope's prayer of consecration and from the song with which Urban V sent three Lambs of God to the Greek Emperor. Both are recorded in the same Ceremonial.

units.la: Papa consecrans inter alia sic precatur. Et quemadmodum ille Agnus innocens, tua voluntate immolatus, in ara crucis Jesus Christus filius, Protoplastum nostrum de Diabolica potestate eripuit: sic isti agni immaculati virtutem illam accipiant, quos consecrandos offerimus in conspectu Divinæ Majestatis tuæ. Tu eos benedicere, sanctificare, & consecrare digneris, ut tua larga benedictione sanctificati EANDEM virtutem accipiant contra omnes Diabolicas versutias, & fraudes maligni Spiritus: ut illos devote super se serentibus, nulla tempestas eisdem prævaleat, nulla adversitas dominetur, nulla aura pestilens, nulla acris corruptio, nullúsque morbus caducus, nulla maris procella & tempestas, nullum incendium, neque ulla iniquitas domincminetur eis, neque prævaleat homo: partus cum matre incolumis servetur, per intercessionem Unigeniti, &c. Tandem adjicit, per Jesum Christum, quasi ei illusurus, petens, ut ejus intercessione Agni cerei eandem cum ipso virtutem recipiant.
units.tr: Among other things, the consecrating Pope prays thus: And just as that innocent Lamb, Jesus Christ the Son, offered by your will on the altar of the cross, snatched our first parent from the power of the Devil, so may these spotless lambs receive that same power, which we offer for consecration in the sight of your divine Majesty. Deign to bless, sanctify, and consecrate them, so that, sanctified by your generous blessing, they may receive the SAME power against all the Devil's wiles and the frauds of the evil spirit: that to those who devoutly bear them upon themselves no storm may prevail, no adversity hold sway, no pestilential breeze, no harsh corruption, no falling sickness, no storm or tempest at sea, no fire, nor any iniquity hold sway over them, nor may any man prevail: may the child be kept safe with its mother, through the intercession of the Only-begotten, etc. Finally he adds through Jesus Christ, as if he were going to mock him, asking that by his intercession the wax Lambs may receive the same power as he himself.

units.la: LXXIX. Carmen, cum quo Urbanus V. tres Agnos ad Imperatorem Græcum transmisit, ejusmodi est:
units.tr: LXXIX. The song with which Urban V sent three Lambs to the Greek Emperor is of this kind:

units.la: Balsamus, & munda cera, cum Chrismatis unda Conficiunt agnum, quod munus do tibi magnum Fonte velut natum, per mystica sanctificatum, Fulgura desursum depellit, omne malignum, Peccatum frangit, UT CHRISTI SANGUIS, & angit: Prægnans servatur, simul & partus liberatur. Dona defert dignis, virtutem destruit ignis, Portatus munde, de fluctibus eripit undæ. Palam est, non soli Christo, non soli sanguini ejus, sed Agno Dei, à Christi sanguine distincto, & cum eodem comparato effectus hosce verè Divinos tribui. Canit enim Vates ille: Peccatum frangit, ut Christi sanguis, & angit. Ergo virtus sanguini Christi propria huic Agni Dei idolo tribuitur. Elegantiori carmine elegiaco eadem complexus est Guilhelmus Estius apud Molanum cap. 13. sed qui versum illum maximè blasphemum modò repetitum hoc Pentametro commutavit: Et pietas animo surgit, abitque tepor. Quod an sit Paraphrasten agere, judicent alii. Impudentior equidem Estio Gretserus contra mysterium Plesslæi cap. 60. illos versus & agnoscit & tuetur: at Urbano antiquiores esse pertendit. Flavius quoque Cherubinus in Compendio Bullarii, Notis ad Bullam Gregorii XIII. A. 1572. editam, ad idem illud Urbani Octastichon provocat, ut plures alios mittam. Molani & Gretseri Κπησφύγιπ Celeb.Gisb. Voetius Disp. Tom. III. p. 953. &c. diluit.
units.tr: Balsam and pure wax, with the water of the chrism, make a Lamb, a great gift I give you, born as it were from the font, sanctified through mystic rites. It drives down the lightning from above, and every evil; it breaks sin, as the blood of Christ does, and afflicts it. The pregnant woman is kept safe, and at once the birth is freed. It bestows gifts on the worthy, and destroys the power of fire; carried cleanly, it snatches from the waves of the water. It is plain that these truly divine effects are attributed not to Christ alone, nor to his blood alone, but to the Lamb of God, distinguished from the blood of Christ and set alongside it. For the poet sings: it breaks sin, as the blood of Christ does, and afflicts it. Therefore the power proper to Christ's blood is ascribed to this idol of the Lamb of God. Guilhelmus Estius included the same in a more elegant elegiac poem, cited by Molanus, ch. 13, but he replaced that most blasphemous line, now repeated, with this pentameter: And piety rises in the mind, and lukewarmness departs. Whether this is paraphrase, let others judge. Gretser, more shameless than Estius in his defence against Plessis's mystery, ch. 60, both acknowledges and defends those verses, but contends that they are older than Urban. Flavius Cherubinus too, in the Compendium Bullarii, in the notes to the bull of Gregory XIII issued in 1572, appeals to that same octastich of Urban, to pass over many others. Voetius, in Disp. vol. III, p. 953, etc., refutes Molanus and Gretser.

units.la: LXXX. Abunde sic Assumptioni nostrae, quod Hierarchia creaturas nonnullas, veluti Papam, Eucharistiam, Sanctos, imagines, reliquias, & res consecratas religiosè venerans, creaturis Divinum cultum exhibeat, & exhibere populum sibi obnoxium jubeat, fidem nos fecisse confidimus. Relinquitur, ut fas nobis integrumque sit concludere, Hierarchiam, Papam, Eucharistiam, Sanctos, imagines, reliquias, res consecratas religiosè venerantem idololatriam committere, & ad idololatriam populum sibi obnoxium seducere; adeóque, in quo rei nostrae cardo vertitur, caeteris paribus, Babylonem Magnam, Matrem fornicationum & abominationum terrae esse.
units.tr: LXXX. Our minor premise, that the Hierarchy, religiously venerating certain creatures, such as the Pope, the Eucharist, the saints, images, relics, and consecrated things, exhibits divine worship to creatures and orders the people subject to it to exhibit it, we trust we have sufficiently established. It remains that we may rightly and fully conclude that the Hierarchy, religiously venerating the Pope, the Eucharist, the saints, images, relics, and consecrated things, commits idolatry, and seduces the people subject to it into idolatry; and therefore, on which the hinge of our case turns, other things being equal, Babylon the Great, the Mother of fornications and abominations of the earth, is that same Hierarchy.
DISSER-
Dissertation Twelve.

units.la: QUA Hierarchiam, seu Clerum Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominantem esse Babylonem Magnam probatur Septimò, quia Sanctos veri Dei cultores, omnesque dissen- tientes, atrociter persequitur. BREVIARIUM.
units.tr: In which it is proved, in the seventh place, that the Hierarchy, or the clergy of the Roman Church that dominates, is Babylon the Great, because it savagely persecutes the saints, the true worshippers of God, and all dissenters. SUMMARY.

units.la: I. Erroribus Hierarchiæ Tyrannicis crudelitas seu tyrannis erga Sanctos, omnesque dissentientes cohæret. II. Tyrannidem ejusmodi Babyloni M. Prophetia tribuit. iIII. Ejusdem ream esse Hierarchiam, Syllogismo probatur. cujus propositio ex terminis constat. IV. Assumptio per membra sua asseritur. Hierarchiæ crudelitas adversus eos, qui Deo magis quàm Papæ adhærent, adeóque Sanctos & dissentientes omnes intenditur. V, Quos illa hæreticorum probrosò titulo necquicquam proscindit. VI. Quin Hierarchiam persequendo eos verè Meretricem Babylonicam se prodere ; & persecutionem ejus sustinentes plurimos verè Sanctos esse, legitimo prejudicio evincitur, quia Sancti vim patiuntur, Meretrix religionis causa vim infert.
units.tr: I. Cruelty, or tyranny, towards the saints and all dissenters goes together with the tyrannical errors of the Hierarchy. II. The Prophecy ascribes such tyranny to Babylon the Great. III. That the Hierarchy is guilty of it is proved by a syllogism, whose major premise consists of its terms. IV. The minor premise is asserted through its parts: the cruelty of the Hierarchy is aimed at those who cling to God more than to the Pope, and so at all the saints and dissenters. V. Those whom it tears apart in vain with the shameful title of heretics. VI. Indeed, by persecuting them, the Hierarchy betrays itself as truly the Babylonian Harlot, and it is shown by a sound presumption that the many who suffer its persecution are truly saints, because the saints suffer violence while the Harlot inflicts violence for the sake of religion.

units.la: VII. Religionem vi & armis adstruere, pugnat cum doctrina & praxi Christi, Apostolorum;
units.tr: VII. To impose religion by force and arms is contrary to the doctrine and practice of Christ and the Apostles;

units.la: VIII. Doctorum veteris Ecclesiæ, Lactantii, Augustini, Tertulliani, Athanasii, Hilarii &c.
units.tr: VIII. The teachers of the ancient Church: Lactantius, Augustine, Tertullian, Athanasius, Hilary, etc.

units.la: IX. Cum natura religionis, quæ doctore opus habet, non tortore; cum coactio simulatores efficiat.
units.tr: IX. It is contrary to the nature of religion, which needs a teacher, not a torturer; and coercion makes hypocrites.

units.la: X. Cum culpæ & pœnæ proportione, quoad externam societatem;
units.tr: X. It is contrary to the proportion of fault and punishment, as far as external society is concerned;

units.la: XI. Cum proprietate Ecclesiæ, cujus est non sævire ad sanguinem usque, vim facere.
units.tr: XI. It is contrary to the nature of the Church, whose part is not to rage to the shedding of blood, nor to use violence.

units.la: XII. Cum judicio denique saniorum inter Pontificios, Ximenii, Cujacii, Bodini, Thuani, Curiæ Parisiensis, Nicolai Fabri, Seldi, Lazari Schwendii, &c.
units.tr: XII. Finally, it is contrary to the judgement of the saner men among the Papists: Ximenes, Cujas, Bodin, de Thou, the Parisian Curia, Nicolas Faber, Selden, Lazarus Schwendi, etc.

units.la: XIII. Tyrannidis ergo rea est Hierarchia, quæ legibus latis solius religionis causa cum aliis, tum Sanctos inprimis persequendos scisci t.
units.tr: XIII. The Hierarchy is therefore guilty of tyranny, since, by laws enacted for the sake of religion alone, it has decreed that others, and above all the saints, are to be persecuted.

units.la: XIV. De pœnis hæreticorum sententia Bellarmini, legibus Ecclesiæ Pontificiæ, & Conciliorum decretis innixa.
units.tr: XIV. On the punishments of heretics: the opinion of Bellarmine, resting on the laws of the Papal Church and the decrees of Councils.

units.la: XV. Ordo, quo Ecclesia Papalis in puniendis hæreticis procedit, ex eodem proponitur & perstringitur.
units.tr: XV. The order in which the Papal Church proceeds in punishing heretics is set out and censured.

units.la: XVI. Ejusdem distinctio inter pœnas infidelium, & à fide deficientium, examinatur.
units.tr: XVI. Its distinction between the punishments of unbelievers and of those who fall away from the faith is examined.

units.la: XVII. Sciopii ferales sententiæ de hæreticorum Regum aliorumque excidio procurando, ab Inquisitione Papiensi approbatæ.
units.tr: XVII. The deadly opinions of Sciopius, on procuring the destruction of heretical kings and others, approved by the Inquisition of Pavia.

units.la: XVIII. Hierarchicorum de religione vi proferenda sententia concluditur.
units.tr: XVIII. The opinion of the Hierarchy on propagating religion by force is concluded.

units.la: XIX. Inquisitionis origo & progressus ex Paulo Veneto, aliisque narratur.
units.tr: XIX. The origin and progress of the Inquisition is related from Paulus Venetus and others.

units.la: XX. Dominationis & tyrannidis Hierarchicorum apex est, vinculum ac necessitas splendi.
units.tr: XX. The summit of the domination and tyranny of the Hierarchy is the chain and the necessity of the stake.

units.la: XXI. Judices tribunalis illius sunt Monachi, juxta Dianam, Jurisconsulti potius quàm Theologi; ipsis Principibus formidabiles.
units.tr: XXI. The judges of that tribunal are monks, according to Diana; they are lawyers rather than theologians, and feared even by the princes themselves.

units.la: XXII. Potestatem habent delegatam in Papa, & juxta quosdam accedentem ad ordinariam; illegitimam plane.
units.tr: XXII. They have a power delegated by the Pope, and, according to some, one that approaches the ordinary power; but it is plainly illegitimate.

units.la: XXIII. Judicii illorum norma ex Cornelio Agrippa exponitur; non verbum Dei, vel recta ratio, sed Pontificum posteriorum decreta Persica.
units.tr: XXIII. The rule of their judgement is set out from Cornelius Agrippa: not the word of God or right reason, but the Persian decrees of the later Pontiffs.

units.la: XXIV. Modus in eodem procedendi infernalibus furiis, quàm hominibus dignior est.
units.tr: XXIV. The manner of proceeding in it is more worthy of infernal furies than of men.

units.la: XXV.XXVI. Injustitia & crudelitas processus ex Gonsalvo, Diana, aliis repræsentatur.
units.tr: XXV–XXVI. The injustice and cruelty of the process is represented from Gonsalvus, Diana and others.

units.la: XXVII. XXVIII. Horribiles torquendi captivos modi edisseruntur.
units.tr: XXVII–XXVIII. The horrible methods of torturing captives are set forth.
XXIX. The cruelty of the punishments.

units.la: XXX. Cui Monachi hypocritæ, pro traditis Seculari brachio in speciem, & recepto juxta Baronium more, intercedentes, ludibrium addunt.
units.tr: XXX. To which the hypocritical monks add mockery, interceding, in appearance, for those handed over to the secular arm, and following, as Baronius has it, the accepted custom.

units.la: XXXI. Inquisitionem non Sanctuarium Domini, sed fornacem Babylonicam esse, concluditur.
units.tr: XXXI. It is concluded that the Inquisition is not the sanctuary of the Lord but a Babylonian furnace.

units.la: XXXII. Crudelitatis Papæ documentum proximum est, quòd per Legatos & Emissarios dissentientes Regum & Principum furori exponit. De Babyloniis his Legatis Prophetia phialæ sextæ Apoc.xv i.12 & c.comparatur.
units.tr: XXXII. The next proof of the Pope's cruelty is that, through legates and emissaries, he exposes dissenters to the fury of kings and princes. The prophecy of the sixth vial, Apoc. xvi.12 and following, is compared with these Babylonian legates.

units.la: XXXIII. Nuntii & Emissarii spirituales Papæ prophetiæ ei exactè quadrant.
units.tr: XXXIII. The spiritual nuncios and emissaries of the Pope fit the prophecy exactly.

units.la: XXXIV. Sùntque duorum generum, vel à Papa immediatè missi, Legati à latere, Nuntii Apostolici.
units.tr: XXXIV. There are two kinds: legates a latere sent directly by the Pope, and apostolic nuncios.

units.la: XXXV. Vel Monachi, Jesuitæ inprimis, voto proprio ad missionem obstricti.
units.tr: XXXV. Or monks, above all Jesuits, bound by their own vow to the mission.

units.la: XXXVI. Legatorum & Missionariorum Papæ & Apostolorum seu Legatorum Christi immane discrimen.
units.tr: XXXVI. The enormous difference between the legates and missionaries of the Pope and the Apostles, or legates of Christ.
XXXVII. They are spirits, and indeed unclean spirits.

units.la: XXXVIII. Ranis Ægyptiacis similimi, quod utrumque comparatione ostenditur.
units.tr: XXXVIII. They are very like the Egyptian frogs, which is shown by comparison of the two.
XXXIX. They are demoniacal spirits, shedim [שדים], endowed with cruelty, craft and demonic impurity.
They are endowed with cruelty, craft and demonic impurity.

units.la: XL. Miracula ostentant. uti relationes inprimis Indicæ
units.tr: XL. They display miracles, as the Indian reports in particular
bear witness.

units.la: XLI. Eunt ad, & in Reges ac Principes terræ & ha-
units.tr: XLI. They go out to, and among, the kings and princes of the earth and of the inhabited world;
they go round the whole world.

units.la: XLII. Congregant Reges & Principes ad bellum sacrum.
units.tr: XLII. They gather kings and princes to a holy war.

units.la: XLIII. Coaxatus & coccysmus eorum perpetuus quo Re-
units.tr: XLIII. Their perpetual croaking and cuckoo-cry, by which they stir up the kings and princes of the world to a holy war.

units.la: ges & Principes mundi ad bellum sacrum incendunt.
units.tr: Kings and princes of the world kindle a holy war.
XLIV. The laws of the Hierarchy binding men to religious tyranny, the Inquisition, and the sending of legates.
and so the actual cruelty of the Hierarchy is laid open from history.

units.la: & successus, adeóque actualis Hierarchiæ crudelitas ex
units.tr: XLV. The Hierarchy is guilty of tyranny over the consciences of its subjects.
XLVI. The Walenburgs object the same to us in vain.
XLVII. They have shown the tyranny of the same over the bodies and fortunes of the saints and dissenters.
XLVIII. The Papal wars with the Greek emperors,
XLVI. The Walenburgs object the same to us in vain.

units.la: XLVII. Tyrannis ejusdem in corpora & fortunas Sanc-
units.tr: XLVII. The tyranny of the same [Hierarchy] against the bodies and property of the saints and of dissenters.
XLVIII. The Papal wars with the Greek emperors,
XLIX. As well as with the Western ones: the Henrys, the Fredericks,
Ludwig of Bavaria.

units.la: L. Factiones Italicæ, bellum Siculum, Sacrum, Schis-
units.tr: L. The Italian factions, the Sicilian war, the Sacred War, the Papal schisms, and the Greek empire betrayed by the Pope argue the cruelty of the Hierarchy.

units.la: mata Pontificia, Imperium Græcum à Pontifice prodi-

units.tr: LI. The history of persecutions against the saints. As a witness
LX. Specimens of Spanish cruelty against the Church.
it has offered its testimony.
LII. The Bohemians.

units.la: LIII. Per Reformationem ab Ecclesia Romana separa-
units.tr: LIII. Those separated from the Roman Church through the Reformation.
LIV. LV. The horrible punishments of the martyrs after the Reformation,
related in summary, surpassing all those that went before.

units.la: LVI. Prætextus militaris licentiæ iisdem obduɛtus dis-
units.tr: LVI. The pretext of military licence cast over these same events is examined.

units.la: LVII. Leonis X. Hadriani VI. Clementis VII. adversus Ecclesiam molimina.
units.tr: LVII. The schemes of Leo X, Hadrian VI and Clement VII against the Church.

units.la: LVIII. Tridentinum Concilium à Paulo III. indictum. Francisci I. Galliarum Regis & Caroli V. æmulatio in persequenda Papæ instinctu Ecclesia. Waldensium prefide Oppa strages horrenda.
units.tr: LVIII. The Council of Trent convened by Paul III. The rivalry of Francis I, King of France, and Charles V in persecuting the Church at the instigation of the Pope. The horrible slaughter of the Waldenses under Oppa as leader.

units.la: LIX. Mariana Angliæ persecutio, & Jesuitarum adversus Elisabetham & Jacobum Regem molimina. Laniena Hibernica.
units.tr: LXXII. The pretext of civil war is refuted.
LX. Specimens of Spanish cruelty against the Church.
LXI. Especially in Belgium, under the leadership of Alba.

units.la: LXII. Nec non Gallicæ sub Henrico II & fratribus Valesiis.
units.tr: LXII. Also French cruelty under Henry II and the Valois brothers.

units.la: LXIII. Papæ & Italiæ Principum, Sabaudi inprimis novi adversus Waldenses furores. Laniena vallis Telinæ, & nupera Pedemontana horribilis.
units.tr: LXIII. The raging of the Pope and the princes of Italy, and especially of the new Savoy, against the Waldenses. The slaughter in the Valley of Telina and the recent horrible one in Piedmont.

units.la: LXIV. Pax religiosa in Imperio Passavii & Augustæ constituta ab Hierarchicis oppugnatur, ceu vi extorta, & quia hæreticis fides data servanda non sit. cujus dogmatis impietas demonstratur. Cum Turca quàm cum Papa tutius iniri fœdera possunt.
units.tr: LXIV. The religious peace established in the Empire at Passau and Augsburg is assailed by the men of the Hierarchy, as if it had been extorted by force, and because faith need not be kept with heretics. The impiety of this doctrine is shown. Treaties can be made more safely with the Turk than with the Pope.

units.la: LXV. Pax eadem religiosa in Germania, Bohemia, Hungaria, Polonia &c. sancita ab iisdem Hierarchicis pro viribus extremis infringitur & violatur.
units.tr: LXV. The same religious peace, sanctioned in Germany, Bohemia, Hungary, Poland and so on, is broken and violated by the same men of the Hierarchy with all their might.
LXVI. The series of Jesuit cruelty is briefly unfolded.

units.la: LXVII. Crudelitas Hierarchicorum in Orientem despumans, velut adversus Americanos, quos prætextu convertendorum ad Christum Cleri instinctu Hispani immanissimè vexârunt.
units.tr: LXVII. The cruelty of the Hierarchy breaking out against the East, as against the Americans, whom the Spaniards most savagely harassed under the pretext of converting them to Christ, at the instigation of the clergy.

units.la: LXVIII. Nec non Æthiopes Habessinos, Japonenses, Sinenses, Clero machinante mirè perturbatos, & mutuis cœdibus commissos.
units.tr: LXVIII. Likewise the Abyssinians, Japanese and Chinese, wonderfully disturbed by the machinations of the clergy and drawn into mutual slaughter.

units.la: LXIX. Conclusio, quòd Hierarchia sit Mulier, Sanctorum Tom. II. & testium Jesu sanguine ebria, adeóque Babylon Magna, verbis Francifci Petrarchæ astruitur.
units.tr: LXIX. The conclusion, that the Hierarchy is the Woman ... drunk with the blood of the saints and of the witnesses of Jesus, and therefore the Great Babylon, is confirmed in the words of Francis Petrarch.

units.la: LXX. Bellarmini objectio, quòd persecutio Hierarchicorum adversus nostros Ethnica veteri longè inferior, & veri nominis persecutio non sit, sed civile bellum; ipsi contra à nostris persecutionem patiantur, proponitur.
units.tr: LXX. Bellarmine's objection is set out: that the persecution of our people by the Hierarchy is far inferior to the ancient pagan persecution and is not a persecution in the true sense but a civil war; and that, on the contrary, they themselves suffer persecution from our people.

units.la: LXXI. Hierarchicorum persecutio veterum Gentilium persecutionem superat pluribus modis, etiam numero cæsorum & suppliciorum immanitate.
units.tr: LXXI. The persecution by the Hierarchy surpasses the persecution of the ancient Gentiles in many ways, including the number of those slain and the savagery of the punishments.
LXXII. The pretext of civil war is refuted.

units.la: LXXIII. Persecutio Ecclesiæ ab Hierarchicis imminens adhuc, crudelitatis eorundem mensuram implebit.
units.tr: LXXIII. The persecution of the Church by the Hierarchy, still impending, will fill up the measure of their cruelty.

units.la: LXXIV. Hierarchicos à Protestantibus persecutionem nullam sustinuisse ostenditur, & pererator.
units.tr: LXXIV. It is shown that the Hierarchy has sustained no persecution from the Protestants, and this is pursued to the end.

units.la: I. Yrannicos & idololatricos Hierarchiæ errores satis equidem superiore diatriba perstrinximus. Priusquam tamen ad Magicos procedamus, tum rei ipsius necessitas, tum Prophetiæ ordo postulat, ut utriusque connexa capita nonnulla pari methodo demonstranda suscipiamus. Et Tyrannicis quidem, in Christum Ecclesiæ caput, ejúsque universa officia arietantibus erroribus cohæret tyrannis in ejusdem corpus, Sanctos & fideles testes Jesu, omnésque dissentientes. Idem enim erga membra Christi, qui erga Christum caput affectus haud dubiè æstuat. Qui caput ferit, corpori quomodo parceret? Imò tantò minùs parcit, quantò invalidiores ictus sunt, quibus Christum caput, in Cœlis ad dextram Dei triumphans, impetit. Sicut enim Leopardus, animal μιαιθρωπώταιον homine absente, vel imaginem ejus solam videns, sive pictam, sive sculptam, confestim in oculos ejus involat, eámque lacerat & discerpit: sic hi cùm ad Christum absentem, & in Cœlis regnantem penetrare nequeant, ejus imaginem & εἰκόνα, homines fideles, corpus Christi in terris militans insectantur, exagitant, infestant. Idololatricis vero erroribus tum blasphemiæ erga verum Deum, tum corporalis scortatio conjunctissimæ sunt. In præsentiarum Tyrannidem Babylonis & Hierarchiæ erga corpus Christi omnes Sanctos, fidelésque cultores Dei & dissentientes alios apertam in lucem proferre, atque sic Septimum demonstrationis nostræ caput exhibere constitutum nobis est.
units.tr: I. The tyrannical and idolatrous errors of the Hierarchy we have indeed touched upon sufficiently in the previous discourse. Before we come to the magical errors, however, both the necessity of the matter itself and the order of the prophecy require that we take up, by the same method, some connected heads of both. Now the tyranny against the body of Christ is bound up with the tyrannical errors, which assail Christ, the Head of the Church, and all his offices: the tyranny against his body, the saints and faithful witnesses of Jesus, and all dissenters. For the feeling towards the members of Christ is surely the same as towards Christ the Head. He who strikes the head, how would he spare the body? Indeed he spares it so much the less, the weaker the blows are with which he assails Christ the Head, triumphing in heaven at the right hand of God. For just as the leopard, an animal [μιαιθρωπώταιον, very man-hating] when a man is absent, or seeing only his image, whether painted or carved, flies at once at its eyes and tears and rends it: so these men, since they cannot reach Christ absent and reigning in heaven, pursue, harass and assail his image and likeness, the faithful men, the body of Christ militant on earth. Moreover, with the idolatrous errors are most closely joined both blasphemies against the true God and bodily whoredom. Now it is our purpose to bring fully into the light the tyranny of Babylon and of the Hierarchy against the body of Christ, against all the saints, the faithful worshippers of God and the other dissenters, and so to set forth the seventh head of our demonstration.

units.la: II. Tyrannidem & crudelitatem in persequendis atrociter Sanctis & dissentientibus quibusvis Angelus Babyloni Magnæ clarissimè tribuit. Nam & habitum ejus cap. XVII.4. πορφύραν καὶ κόκκινον purpuram & coccinum, crudelitatis symbola, uti supra ostendimus, statuit: & v. 6. Mulierem describit, ceu μεθύουσαν ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν ἁγίων ebriam sanguine Sanctorum, & sanguine testium Jesu: & in ea Sanguinem Prophetarum, Sanctorum & omnium in terra mactatorum inventum esse, cap. XVIII. 24. testatur. Quomodo etiam Matth. XXIII. 35. Hierosolymæ imputatur sanguis Habelis. Quippe omnis homicida communionem cum omnibus homicidis habet, omnium homicidiorum reus fit, & cum homicidis omnibus punitur.
units.tr: II. The tyranny and cruelty with which Babylon the Great fiercely persecutes the saints and all dissenters are clearly ascribed to her by the Angel. For in chapter 17:4 he sets her attire, purple and scarlet [πορφύραν καὶ κόκκινον], as symbols of cruelty, as we have shown above. In verse 6 he describes the woman as drunk with the blood of the saints [μεθύουσαν ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν ἁγίων] and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus, and in chapter 18:24 he testifies that the blood of the prophets, of the saints, and of all who have been slain on the earth was found in her. In the same way, at Matthew 23:35, the blood of Abel is charged against Jerusalem. Indeed, every murderer shares fellowship with all murderers, becomes guilty of all murders, and is punished along with all murderers.

units.la: III. Planum igitur est, Hierarchiam Ecclesiæ Romanæ, cæteris paribus, Babylonem Magnam jure haberi ab omnibus, si tyrannidis & crudelitatis erga Sanctos & dissentientes quosvis rea peragi possit. Nos autem ream peragimus sequenti Syllogismo:
units.tr: III. It is therefore plain that, other things being equal, the Hierarchy of the Roman Church must be held by everyone to be Babylon the Great, if she can be proved guilty of tyranny and cruelty towards the saints and any dissenters whatever. We, however, prove her guilty by the following syllogism:

units.la: Quicunque cætus adversantes sibi eos, qui Verbi Divini scripti authoritate, aliisque legitimis rationibus freti ei se subjicere detrectant, probrosò hæreticorum titulo traductos, & lege lata cogendos, puniendos, excludendos decernit: & instituto tribunali
units.tr: Whatever assemblies decide that those who refuse to submit to them, though they rest on the authority of the written Word of God and on other lawful grounds, are to be branded with the shameful title of heretics, and are to be compelled, punished and excluded by a law that has been passed; and who, having set up a tribunal,

units.la: t nali injustis modis torquet, punit, occidit: & per emissarios Regum Principúmque indignationi & furoribus exponit: & sanguinariorum decretorum suorum executione pro viribus suis & extremis modis quoad conscientias, corpora, honores & fortunas omnes infestat; is Sanctos veri Dei cultores, omnésque dissentientes atrociter persequitur, adeóque cæteris paribus, Babylon Magna est.
units.tr: torture, punish and kill them by unjust methods; who expose them, through the agents of kings and princes, to indignation and rage; and who, by carrying out their bloody decrees with all their strength and by the most extreme means, harass all of them in their consciences, bodies, honours and fortunes; such an assembly cruelly persecutes the saints, the true worshippers of God, and all dissenters, and therefore, other things being equal, is Babylon the Great.

units.la: Atqui Hierarchia, seu Clerus Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominans adversantes sibi eos, qui Verbi Divini scripti authoritate, aliisque legitimis rationibus freti ei se subjicere detrectant, probroso hæreticorum titulo traductos, & lege lata cogendos, puniendos, excidendos decernit: & instituto tribunali injustis modis torquet, punit, occidit: & per emissarios Regum Principúmque indignationi & furori exponit: & sanguinariorum decretorum suorum executione pro viribus suis, & extremis modis quoad conscientias, corpora, honores & fortunas omnes infestat.
units.tr: But the Hierarchy, or the ruling clergy of the Roman Church, decides that those who refuse to submit to it, though they rest on the authority of the written Word of God and on other lawful grounds, are to be branded with the shameful title of heretics, and are to be compelled, punished and cut off by a law that has been passed; and, having set up a tribunal, it tortures, punishes and kills them by unjust methods; it exposes them, through the agents of kings and princes, to indignation and rage; and by carrying out its bloody decrees with all its strength and by the most extreme means, it harasses them in all their consciences, bodies, honours and fortunes.

units.la: Ergo Hierarchia, seu Clerus Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominans Sanctos, Veri Dei cultores, omnésque à se dissentientes atrociter persequitur; adeóque cæteris paribus, Babylon Magna est.
units.tr: Therefore the Hierarchy, or the ruling clergy of the Roman Church, cruelly persecutes the saints, the true worshippers of God, and all who dissent from it; and therefore, other things being equal, it is Babylon the Great.

units.la: Propositionis veritas ex terminis cognoscitur. Assumptio proin sola nobis demonstranda venit.
units.tr: The truth of the major premise is known from the terms themselves. Only the minor premise, therefore, remains for us to demonstrate.

units.la: IV. Hierarchiæ crudelitas & persecutio omnis adversus eos, qui verbi Divini authoritate, aliisque legitimis rationibus freti ei se subjicere detrectant, adeóque adversantur, intenditur. Non aliud enim majus crimen illa interpretatur, quàm non obedire Papæ, eum pro summo Ecclesiæ capite & dictatore, quin & pro Summo in Spiritualibus & temporalibus Rege ac Domino non agnoscere, imperata ejus non facere, definitiones non recipere. Pro authoritate & potestate illa sua, tanquam pro aris & focis, sed pro his magis, quàm pro illis dimicat. Qui ei se subjicere renuunt, & freti Scripturis ac rationibus legitimis, quibus vetamur fidem & conscientiam obstringere hominibus, & legitimo Magistratui, non potestatis violento raptori & usurpatori contra omne fas, obedire jubemur, jugum iniqui Domini excutiunt, unius soliusque Dei, ejusque verbi obedientiam & fidem ἀννπκεῖ​νν profitentur, & opere ipso, amore Dei & proximi sincero, humilitate, & in persecutionibus patientia, constantiaque praestant: illi ἅγιοι καὶ μάρτυρες Ιησοῦ te-stes Jesu, adeóque ii ipsi, quorum sanguine ebriam Mulierem Prophetia dicit; sunt. Qui non tam Scriptura, forte incognita vel non intellecta, quàm ratione & jure legitimo freti jugum Papæ detrectant: ii si non Sanctorum, saltem legitimè dissentientium, adeóque affectatæ Papæ πνρμβαπολάα adversantium locosunt.
units.tr: IV. The cruelty of the Hierarchy, and all its persecution, is directed against those who, resting on the authority of the Word of God and on other lawful grounds, refuse to submit to it and so oppose it. For it considers no greater crime than not obeying the Pope, whom it acknowledges as the supreme head and ruler of the Church, and indeed as the supreme king and lord in spiritual and temporal matters; not doing what he commands; and not accepting his definitions. It fights for that authority and power of his as for altars and hearths, though more for the latter than for the former. Those who refuse to submit to him, relying on the Scriptures and on lawful reasons, by which we are forbidden to bind faith and conscience to men, and by which we are commanded to obey the lawful magistrate and not a violent seizer and usurper of power against all right, shake off the yoke of an unjust lord. They profess [ἀννπκεῖ​νν] the obedience and faith due to the one and only God and to his Word, and by their deeds, through sincere love of God and neighbour, humility, and patience and steadfastness under persecution, they show it. They are holy ones and witnesses of Jesus [ἅγιοι καὶ μάρτυρες Ἰησοῦ], and so they are precisely those whose blood the prophecy says the woman is drunk with. Those who refuse the yoke of the Pope, relying not so much on Scripture (perhaps unknown or not understood) as on reason and lawful right, are, if not saints, at least lawfully dissenters, and so opponents of the Pope's [πνρμβαπολάα] pretended authority.

units.la: V. Nihil autem refert, quo nomine, Sanctorum, & simpliciter dissentientium, an Hæreticorum vel Infidelium etiam Hierarchicis tales veniant. Etenim pridem res sua nomina perdiderunt: & pessimi quique bonum malum, & malum bonum dicere consueverunt.
units.tr: V. Nor does it matter by what name the Hierarchy calls such people, whether saints and simply dissenters, or even heretics and unbelievers. For things have long since lost their proper names, and the worst men are accustomed to call good evil and evil good.

units.la: Res, non vel opinio, vel suspicio, vel iniqua hominum, qui non quæ Christi, sed quæ sua sunt, quærunt, judicia æstimanda sunt. Nunquam certè vel Meretrix Babylonica eos, quos odit, & persequitur, Sanctos & testes Jesu: vel Sancti & testes Jesu Meretricem Babylonicam castam Virginem, honestámque matronam insignient. Hæretici sunt S. Augustino lib. de utilitate credendi, qui alicujus temporalis commodi, & maximé gloriæ, principatúsque sui gratia, falsas ac novas opiniones vel gignunt, vel sequuntur. Tales certè non illi sunt, qui Hierarchiæ repugnant. Nam repugnando nec temporale commodum, nec gloriam, nec principatum ambiunt; certi potiùs, se repugnando talium jacturam facere. Neque etiam qui Scripto Dei verbo adhærent, & dogmatis in eo revelatis assentiuntur, parati cedere iis, qui ex Scripturis rectiora demonstraverint, novas opiniones vel gignere, vel sequi censentur merito. Argumentorum certè affatim est, quibus nos magis infamatos, quàm convictos hæresium esse, demonstremus. Olim quoque Ariani Orthodoxos hæreticorum pipulo differre ausi sunt. Audiamus Salvianum de Arianis sic loquentem: Hæretici sunt, sed non scientes: denique apud nos sunt hæretici, apud se non sunt. Nam in tantum se Catholicos esse judicant, ut nos ipsos titulo hæreticæ pravitatis infament. Quod ergo illi nobis sunt, & hoc nos illis. Nos illos injuriam Divinæ generationi facere, certi scimus, quòd minorem Patre filium dicant. Illi nos injuriosos Patri existimant, quòd æquales esse credamus. Veritas apud nos est, sed illi apud se esse præsumunt. Honos Dei apud nos est: sed illi hoc arbitrantur honorem Divinitatis, quod credunt. Inofficiosi sunt, sed illis hoc est summum religionis officium. Impii sunt, sed hoc putant veram esse pietatem. VI. Cœterùm eos, quos Hierarchia, ceu Papæ immorigeros, persequitur, & quorum sanguine inebriatur; verè Sanctos esse, tum eorum recta fides, charitas & patientia demonstrat: tum legitimum quoddam præjudicium evincit. Nam eo ipso, quòd Hierarchia eos religionis causâ, & quia Regno Papæ colla submittere renuunt, odit & persequitur, se quidem Meretricem Babylonicam esse palam prodit, quia non eos, qui persecutionem patiuntur, sed qui inferunt, Babylonis & Meretricis Magnæ stigmate Prophetia inurit; eos verò qui persecutionem sic illatam fideliter & constanter patiuntur, Sanctos & testes Jesu Prophetia eadem declarat. Non Ifacus filius promissionis Ismaelem, filium secundum carnem, sed Ismael carnalis Isacum spiritualem persequitur. Ipsum Jus Canonicum Causa 23. can. 13. q. 4. hanc sententiam tulit: Nunquam Spirituales Carnalem persequitur; sed carnalis spiritualem.
