units.la: XLII. Postremum officium congregandi Reges & Principes terræ & totius mundi in prælium Dei Dei omnipotentis illius Magni, ad quod reliqua omnia tendunt, haud minùs obeunt gnaviter.
units.tr: XLII. The last function, that of gathering the kings and princes of the earth and of the whole world to the battle of God, that great Almighty God, to which all the rest tend, they discharge no less diligently.

units.la: In hoc enim illorum otium, in hoc negotium: in hoc vigilia, in hoc somnus, denique curæ eorum omnes reponuntur, ut Reges Principesque Religiosis bellis implicent, involvant, & violento quodam impetu abripiant; Congregationes, Ligas, Uniones instituant. Media, quibus ad scopum eum grassati haetenus sunt, in propatulo etiam sunt. Sunt enim illa perjuria publica, ad quae Reges praecipue inducunt, religiosae pacis hinc inde constitutae, quam ut canes lapidem, quo se petitos sentiunt. oderunt, & rabiose admordent, fraudulenta & violenta perturbatio; parricidia, veneficia, vis conscientiis illata. fraudulentae & insidiosae pacificationes, Juris corruptelae, Innocentiae oppressio, & similia, per quae Papatum amplificare, collapsum Ecclesiae statum reparare, Concilium Tridentinum exequi, haereses fictitias ex agro Domini extirpare conantur. Ex quibus, secundum naturae creatae cursum, non aliud quam bella; & quidem perniciosissima exoriri potuerunt, poterúntque deinceps.
units.tr: For in this lies their leisure, in this their business; in this their watching, in this their sleep; in short, all their cares are directed to this end: that they may entangle and involve kings and princes in religious wars, and sweep them away with a violent rush; and that they may set up congregations, leagues and unions. The means by which they have so far pursued that goal are also in plain view. For they are public perjuries, to which they chiefly induce kings; the religious peace, once established on this side and that, which, like dogs that sense a stone thrown at them, they hate and bite at furiously; fraudulent and violent disturbance; parricides; poisonings; violence done to consciences; fraudulent and deceitful pacifications; corruptions of law; oppression of the innocent, and the like. By these means they try to extend the Papacy, to repair the collapsed state of the Church, to carry out the Council of Trent, and to root out fictitious heresies from the Lord's field. From these, according to the ordinary course of created nature, nothing else could arise, and nothing else can arise hereafter, but wars, and indeed most destructive ones.

units.la: XLIII. Hic scilicet est assiduus ranarum illarum coaxatus, hic Jesuitarum, & Jesuiticorum consiliorum coccyfmus, quo generosorum Regum Principumque aures animosque, postquam in eos semel intrârunt, insatiabiliter tundunt, obtundúntque, & ad religiosa bella incendunt. Subditis vestris bona conscientia tantam licentiam concedere non potestis; nec fides haereticis jurata servanda est, quia juramentum vinculum iniquitatis esse non debet. Religionis libertas non aliud est, quàm manifesta Majestatis diminutio, cum opprobrio conjuncta. Túne, qui vivis & flores, non possis retractare, quae Antecessor, Parens, Avus &c. vel imprudens maleque persuasus, vel etiam vi & armis coactus indulsit. Annon eodem jure Imperator, Rex, Princeps es, quo illi fuerunt? Ferendúmne est, ut demortui memoria & authoritas plus apud subditos valeat, quam praesentis & Regnantis persona? Annon vides, eos, qui pericula tibi objectant, quae turbatam Religionis pacem, turbata edicta sequuntur, tibi non tam consulere, quàm aperte minitari: Diaboli haec tentamenta sunt, per quae generosis cogitatis & conatibus tuis remoram injicere studet. Mulierculárum hic, non magnanimorum Principum, metus est. Illi juventutem tuam, æquitatem spernunt. Severiore fronte opus est, ut noverint, te virum esse, animumque tam excelsis natalibus parem gerere. Has consiliorum suorum rationes in publicis etiam scriptis, ex quibus hæc ad verbum descripta sunt, neutiquam illi dissimulant. Apud superstitiosos & cunctantiores alia adjiciuntur, puta Reges & Principes, qui hanc Religionis libertatem indulserunt, in Purgatorio gravissimas peccati pœnas luere: vix ac ne vix, quandiu peccatum hoc continuatur, à reliquis peccatis absolutionem concedi posse: Non Turcas, non Tartaros veros & nativos Reip. Christianæ hostes esse, sed hæreticos, contra Ecclesiam Romanam insurgentes; in his proin opprimendis veram & Catholico Principe dignam laudem quæri: Cavendum ne Princeps bello Turcico implicetur, ne rebelles hæretici christas attollant. Denique seviore tantum vultu opus esse. Unius enim & alterius Clamatoris supplicio rem posse confici: ducibus remotis nil ausuram plebem &c. Interea hac ratione Principem animam suam ab inferno liberaturum. Sic, sic tandem Hierarchiæ venenati illi bufones, turbarum flabella, Sanctorum & testium Jesu flagella Reges & Principes in locum, qui vocatur, Harmageddon, congregant, & ad Sacrum illud minimè sacrum bellum conclamant.
units.tr: XLIII. Here, of course, is the constant croaking of those frogs; here is the clamour of the Jesuits and of Jesuitical counsels, by which they beat relentlessly upon the ears and minds of generous kings and princes once these have entered them, and kindle them to religious wars. You cannot grant such license to your subjects with a good conscience; nor must faith sworn to heretics be kept, because an oath ought not to be a bond of iniquity. Liberty of religion is nothing other than a manifest diminution of majesty, joined with disgrace. Can you, who are alive and flourishing, not revoke what your predecessor, parent, grandfather, etc., granted, whether unwisely and wrongly persuaded, or even compelled by force and arms? Are you not an emperor, king, prince, by the same right as they were? Must it be endured that the memory and authority of the dead should count for more with subjects than the person of the present and reigning ruler? Do you not see that those who set before you the dangers that follow a disturbed peace of religion and disturbed edicts are not so much advising you as openly threatening you? These are the temptations of the Devil, by which he tries to put a check upon your generous thoughts and endeavours. It is the fear of little women, not of magnanimous princes. Those men despise your youth and your fairness. There is need of a sterner brow, so that they may know that you are a man and bear a spirit equal to so lofty a birth. These grounds of their counsels they by no means conceal even in their public writings, from which these words have been copied exactly. Among the superstitious and the more hesitant other things are added, such as: Kings and princes who have granted this liberty of religion will pay the most grievous penalties for sin in Purgatory; scarcely, if at all, can absolution from other sins be granted as long as this sin continues; the Turks and the Tartars are not the true and native enemies of the Christian commonwealth, but heretics rising up against the Roman Church; in crushing these, the true praise worthy of a Catholic prince is to be sought; care must be taken that the prince not be entangled in a Turkish war, lest the heretic rebels raise their heads. In short, only a sterner countenance is needed. For the business can be done by the execution of one or two agitators; with the leaders removed, the common people will dare nothing, etc. Meanwhile, by this method, the prince will save his soul from hell. Thus at last those poisonous toads of the Hierarchy, the fanners of disturbances, the scourges of the saints and witnesses of Jesus, gather kings and princes into the place called Harmagedon, and proclaim that most unholy so-called holy war.

units.la: XLIV. Sic fuerunt leges Hierarchicorum, ad tyrannidem religiosam obligantes: Tribunal sacrum Inquisitionis: Legati & Emissarii, per quos Papa classicum canit, & dissentientes Regum Principúmque indignationi & furoribus exponit. Horum verò omnium executionem sanguinariam, & successum horribilem, ipsa persecutionum & exercitæ in conscientias, corpora, honores & fortunas omnes tyrannidis reli-
units.tr: XLIV. Such were the laws of the Hierarchy, binding men to religious tyranny: the sacred tribunal of the Inquisition, and the legates and emissaries through whom the Pope sounds the trumpet and exposes those who dissent to the anger and fury of kings and princes. The bloody carrying out of all these measures, and their dreadful success, is shown by the very history of the persecutions and of the religious tyranny exercised against consciences, bodies, honours and all fortunes.

units.la: giosæ historia demonstrat. Pertexui eam magnam partem in Historia Papatus, eundem ferè in finem adornata, nata, quam hic repetere supervacaneum foret. Pauca tamen, fidem facturus dictis, & instituto nostro inserviturus, attingere non pigrabor; in cœteris ad historiam ipsam, aliósque, qui Papalia bella, & persecutiones sævissimas religionis causa agitatas posteritati tradiderunt, lectorem amandans.
units.tr: I have traced that history at great length in my History of the Papacy, written largely to the same end, and it would be superfluous to repeat it here. Still, to make my claims credible and to serve my present purpose, I will not hesitate to touch on a few points, sending the reader for the rest to that history itself and to others who have handed down to posterity the Papal wars and the most savage persecutions waged in the name of religion.

units.la: XLV. Tyrannidem in conscientiam Hierarchia in omnes sibi subjectos exercet. Eos enim Papa, ceu Legislator & Judex saltem in terris Supremus libertate ea, quam Deus concessit, spoliatos, suis, adeóque humanis legibus regit, suo judicio subjicit, & ἑκὼν ἀκὼν γε θυμῶ, superstitione dementatos, ignorantia voluntatis Dei corruptos, vel certè metu coercitos in officio & obedientia continet. Χάραγμα illud, quod Deus Ecclesiæ dedit, ponendum in fronte & dextra manu, est scripta lex Mosis, cui omne Divinum verbum auditum lectúmque consonet oportet. Exod. xiii. 16. Deut. vi. 6. 7. 8. xi. 13. 18. Et erunt verba hæc, quæ ego præcipio tibi hodie, apud cor tuum, & acues ea filiis tuis, & loqueris de eis, cùm sedebis domi, & cùm ambulabis in via, & cùm decubes, & cùm surges, & alligabis ea in signum in manu tua, & erunt in monilia inter oculos tuos. Præter hoc χαἐγγμα Hierarchia legem aliam, de qua nihil Moses, Prophetæ, Christus, Apostoli dixerunt vel scripserunt, salsum & idololatricum, uti ostendimus, cultum, & quidem authoritate Ecclesiæ, quam Divinam & ipsius Spiritus S. esse jactant, præscriptum obtrudunt, eam prositendam & sequendam iis, qui in Christi nomine baptizati sunt, tanquam sibi subjectis, quemadmodum homo Deo subjectus est, imperant, atque sic fidei & conscientiæ subditorum omnium dominantur. Eos vero, qui pie volentes vivere non recipiunt χαἐγγμα eorum in frontem, ut præ se ferant, & profiteantur, & in manum dextram, ut inter actiones suas id intueantur pro regula, excommunicant, adeóque Agnum, Christum, & qui eum sequuntur, & χαράγμα ipsius in frontibus suis habent, Apoc. xiv. 1. denique verbum ejus, tanquam non perfectè & candidè docens, & fidem in verbum ejus, tanquam non purificantem corda, non justificantem blasphemant; excommunicatos, carnali gladio interficiunt. Hanc tyrannidem omnium crudelissimam, quam Hierarchia tum in subjectos omnes exercet, tum in non subjectos exercere tentat, ejusque etiam historiam, tum in Historia Papatus, inde à Periodo III. Ecclesiæ Romanæ; tum supra etiam Differt. vii. 64. viii. ff. 3: 1. 2. &c. x. xi. expositimus.
units.tr: XLV. The Hierarchy exercises tyranny over conscience over all who are subject to it. For the Pope, as lawgiver and judge, the supreme ruler on earth at least, strips them of the liberty that God granted, governs them by his own and therefore human laws, subjects them to his judgement, and keeps them in obedience and submission, whether they are willing or unwilling, [ἑκὼν ἀκὼν γε θυμῶ], driven mad by superstition, corrupted by ignorance of the will of God, or at least held in check by fear. That mark [χάραγμα] which God gave the Church, to be placed on the forehead and the right hand, is the written law of Moses, to which all the divine Word that is heard and read ought to agree. Exod. 13:16; Deut. 6:6–8; 11:13, 18: And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up. And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes. Besides this, the Hierarchy imposes another mark [χαράγμα], a law about which Moses, the Prophets, Christ and the Apostles said or wrote nothing: a salted and idolatrous worship, as we have shown, which it forces upon men by the authority of the Church, which they boast is divine and the very work of the Holy Spirit. It commands those who have been baptized in the name of Christ to profess and follow this worship, as subjects, just as man is subject to God, and so it lords it over the faith and conscience of all its subjects. As for those who, wishing to live piously, do not receive its mark on the forehead, to be displayed and professed openly, or on the right hand, to be looked upon as a rule in their actions, it excommunicates them. Thus they excommunicate the Lamb, Christ, and those who follow him and have his mark on their foreheads (Rev. 14:1). Finally, they blaspheme his Word as teaching imperfectly and insincerely, and faith in his Word as neither purifying the heart nor justifying; and those they excommunicate they put to death with the carnal sword. This most cruel of all tyrannies, which the Hierarchy exercises both over its subjects and attempts to exercise over those who are not subject to it, I have set out in the History of the Papacy from the Third Period of the Roman Church onward, and also above in Dissertations 7 (§64), 8 (ff. 3, 1, 2, etc.), 10 and 11.

units.la: XLVI. Neque tyrannidem similem in nostros Wal- enburgii, aliíque jure ullo retorquent.
units.tr: XLVI. Nor do they turn a similar tyranny back upon our people, as Walenburgius and others do, with any right.

units.la: Etenim verbo Dei consentanea præcipere, Orthodoxam fidem ab hæreticorum perfidia vindicare, ad Divinum cultum, conciones & preces publicas authoritate verbi Divini subditos adigere, refractarios moderatis pœnis in ordinem redigere, hæreticos vitare, non tyrannicum, sed legitimi Magistratus, cui custodia utriusque legis Divinæ tabulæ Divinitus concredita est; & postremum illud, sanciente Dei verbo, omnium Christianorum officium est. Sed præcipere contraria omnia, fidei & conscientiis dominari, libertatem Christianam omnem abrumpere, vi sola metuque perspicaciores in officio continere, reliquos superstitione, ignorantia, cœca obedientia corrumpere; in pœnis irrogandis ac supplicis sumendis modum excedere, omnem humanitatem exuere, crudelitatem belluinam exercere; id vero tyrannidem sapit, qua nulla alia major fingi potest. Quanquam tyrannidem hanc non tam supplicia, quam causa perdita arguunt. Si causa Hierarchicorum bona esset, nec immorigerii, quos affligunt & occidunt, martyres essent: nec ipsi tyranni, siquidem praescriptum à Deo ordinem sequerentur. Atqui pios ac fideles Christi servos excarnificant, omnique crudelitate dilacerant non aliam ob causam, quàm quia ob timorem Christi haeresibus eorum assentiri nolunt, idololatriam per conscientiam approbare non possunt. Similes pravis illis servis, qui Domino juxta opinionem suam cunctante, lymphari, inebriari, conservos suos verberare coeperunt.
units.tr: For to command what agrees with the Word of God, to defend the orthodox faith from the treachery of heretics, to compel subjects by the authority of the divine Word to worship God, to attend sermons and public prayers, to bring the refractory back into order with moderate penalties, and to avoid heretics: this is not tyranny but the duty of the lawful magistrate, to whom the custody of both tables of the divine law has been entrusted by God; and that last point, too, is the duty of all Christians, as the Word of God commands. But to command all the contrary, to lord it over faith and consciences, to cut off all Christian liberty, to hold the more perceptive in obedience by force and fear alone, to corrupt the rest by superstition, ignorance and blind obedience, to exceed all measure in inflicting punishments and in exacting penalties, to strip off all humanity and to practise beastly cruelty: that is the very flavour of tyranny, and no greater can be imagined. Yet it is not so much the punishments as the lost cause that proves this tyranny. If the cause of the Hierarchists were good, those whom they afflict and kill would not be obstinate men but martyrs; nor would the tyrants themselves be tyrants, if they followed the order prescribed by God. But they tear apart and butcher the pious and faithful servants of Christ, and tear them to pieces with every cruelty, for no other reason than that, for fear of Christ, they refuse to agree with their heresies and cannot approve idolatry in good conscience. They are like those wicked servants who, when their lord delayed, according to their own reckoning, began to beat their fellow servants and to drink and get drunk (Matt. 24:48–49).

units.la: XLVII. Conscientiarum porro tyrannisilla quam finis est crudelitatis Babylonicae, qua Mulier Sanguine Sanctorum & testium Jesu inebriata inducitur, non tamen ipsa haec crudelitas sanguinaria est. utpote quae in fortunas & corpora eorum, qui tyrannidis spiritualis impatientes sunt, atque jugum vel jam excusserunt, vel excutere tentant, vel nunquam antehac experti, subire detrectant, intenditur. De hac ergo potissimum sermonem instituamus, & selecta ex immenso cumulo Babylonicae crudelitatis exempla colligamus.
units.tr: XLVII. Moreover, the tyranny over consciences, which is the end of Babylonian cruelty, in which the Woman is shown drunk with the blood of the saints and the martyrs of Jesus, is not itself the bloody cruelty. It is directed against the property and bodies of those who cannot bear spiritual tyranny, who have either already thrown off its yoke or are trying to throw it off, or who, never having experienced it before, refuse to submit to it. So it is about this above all that we shall speak, and we shall gather selected examples from the immense heap of Babylonian cruelty.

units.la: XLVIII. Omitti equidem tragoediae ab Hierarchia adversus Imperatores Graecos & Latinos excitatae potuerant. Cùm tamen hi & Christiani fuerint, & ob Sacrosanctam potestatem Dii, Sancti, utpote Unctì Domini dicantur merito, cúmque insuper bella illa gesta sint praetextu pietatis, & uti loquebantur, extirpandae haeresis Simoniacae, ab iis exordiri quid vetat? Quàm primùm illa ergo invisa Deo idololatria, seu ἐικονοδυλεία, imaginum cultus, fundi Christiani calamitas, & malorum omnium, quibus Ecclesiae status convulsus est, seminarium quoddam in Ecclesiam incessit, illud ea occasione moliti Pontifices, ut & Imperatoris authoritatem in Occidente everterent, & suam in Oriente stabilirent, omnia turbis bellisque miscuerunt. Indixerat imaginibus bellum Leo Imperator Isaurus. Gregorius ergo junior, Romanus Episcopus, si Theophani Histor. miscell. lib. xxi. Cedreno, Zonarae, Sigeberto, aliis credimus. Romani mam cum tota Italia ab illius Imperio recedere fecit. Eidem etiam vectigalia, nescio qua authoritate (inquit Marsilius Patavinus Tract. de Translat. Imp.) sed bene qua temeritate, solemniter interdixit; Romaeque congregans Synodum venerationem imaginum confirmavit, & violatores hujusmodi anathemate condemnavit. Id Baronius A. 730. 5. commendans, Dignum, inquit, posteris Gregorius reliquit exemplum, ne in Ecclesia Christiana regnare finirentur haeretici Principes. Eadem occasione Papa Imperatorum Graecorum in Italia Exarchos, Ravennæ Paulum, in Campania Adrianum & filium ejus occidi curavit. Tandem Irene, Constantini Mater, Erynnis potius dicenda, cum Adriano I. conspirans proprio filio, Constantino VII. adulto, iconolatriam oppugnanti, & oculos exccavit, & Imperium eripuit: quod factum si non fuisset, certè non improbavit Adrianus: at Baronius A. 796. 8. laudavit. horrendum dictu!
units.tr: XLVIII. Certainly the tragedies stirred up by the Hierarchy against the Greek and Latin emperors could have been passed over. Yet since these were Christians, and since they are rightly called gods and saints because of their sacred power, as anointed lords, and since those wars were waged under the pretext of piety and, as they used to say, for the uprooting of the Simoniacal heresy, what prevents us from beginning with them? As soon as that idolatry hateful to God, the worship of images (εἰκονοδουλεία), the calamity of the Christian empire and a kind of seedbed of all the evils by which the state of the Church was convulsed, crept into the Church, the Pontiffs, seizing the occasion, stirred everything up with disturbances and wars, both to overthrow the authority of the Emperor in the West and to establish their own in the East. Leo the Isaurian, the Emperor, had declared war on images. So Gregory the Younger, Bishop of Rome, if we believe Theophanes (Historia miscella, bk. 21), Cedrenus, Zonaras, Sigebert and others, caused Rome along with all Italy to withdraw from his empire. He also solemnly forbade the payment of taxes to him, by what authority I do not know (says Marsilius of Padua, Tract. de Translatione Imperii), but certainly with great recklessness; and, gathering a synod at Rome, he confirmed the veneration of images and condemned violators of this kind with anathema. Baronius, praising this in the year 730, §5, says: "Gregory left posterity a worthy example, so that heretical princes should not reign in the Christian Church." On the same occasion Pope Gregory had the Emperor's exarchs in Italy killed: Paul at Ravenna, and Adrian and his son in Campania. At last Irene, the mother of Constantine, better called a Fury, conspired with Adrian I against her own son, Constantine VII, now grown, who was opposing the worship of images; she blinded him and snatched the empire from him. If Adrian had not approved of this deed, he at least did not condemn it; yet Baronius praised it in the year 796, §8. Horrible to relate!

units.la: XLIX. Saeva inprimis fuerunt bella adversus Imperatores Latinos à Pontificibus Hildebrandinis suscepta atque gesta; quae si non ad Sanctorum sanguinem, at certè ad Hierarchiae crudelitatem pertinent. Quam primum allecta ad superstitionem Barbaria Occidentalis Ecclesiae Romanae jugum subivit, & Hierarchia circa undecimum Seculum virilem togam ambiyit, & sumpsit; statim dulci fortuna ebria in Summi Imperii sceptrum manus petulanter injecit, & Caesaribus de Supremae dominationis jure, bello nefario indicto, controversiam movit. Extractum est funestum certamen in ducentos annos; quo tempore spatio quantum sanguinis effusum, quae civilia, hostium & strages factae, quàm gravis Christiano nomini strages illata, quot regiones vastatae, urbes incensae sint, nullo sermone adaequari potest. Primum belli signum fax illa infernalis Gregorius VII. Hildebrandus dictus, dedit, qui insana dominandi cupiditate inflammatus, adversus Henricum IV. Imperatoriæ Majestatis jura tuentem, bruti fulminis aciem distrinxit, percussorem in caput optimi Principis subornavit, subditos ad sumenda in Dominum arma concitavit, Rodolpho Suevo Imperii insignia contulit, qui tertio cum Imperatore prælio congressus, vitam manúque dextram amisit. Urbanus post nihil eo vindicatæ perfidiæ documento territus, pari adversus Imperatorem furoris æstro percitus, Hermannum Lucenburgensem in arenam eduxit; eóque sublato Conradum filium adversus Patrem inflammavit. Ambitionis odiique hæres Paschalis II. sumpta Regii honoris purpura, triplicíque diademate, ex monte Tarpejo in Imperatorem fulminans, Henricum filium adversus Patrem armavit, quo ille oppresso custodiæque tradito, Papa mandante, Imperium arripuit. Cùm verò nec ille Papæ morem gerere videretur, ab eodem cum Principibus & Episcopis collisus, à Calixto II. extorto, per vim, eligendorum Episcoporum jure, pessimè vexatus, ferò intolerabilem Pontificum ambitionem, suámque ipse stultitiam & impietatem damnavit. Prosecuti hoc bellum sunt incredibili animorum contentione Adrianus II. & Alexander III. qui cum maxima nominis Christiani clade universam Europam in Fridericum Barbarossam concitárunt. quod bellum diu varioeventu gestum sedari priùs non potuit; quàm Imperator publicæ cladis misertus, & suas cervices, & Imperii Majestatem turpissimi Sacrificuli pedibus calcandam subjiceret. Derivatum odium est in Friderici filios posterósque, neque ante depositum est, quàm maximâ Reipublicæ Christianæ clade, familiæ nobilissimæ fobbles omnis extincta esset. Nàm Henricum VI. filium, Papæ jussu, Coloniensis, aliíque armis oppugnárunt. Philippum Innocentius tius II. per Othonem Saxonem divexavit, quem à se coronatum, & copiis suis adjutum, isdem mox artibus deturbavit, quibus paulo ante evexerat. Friderico II. Nepoti Gregorius IX. & Innocentius IV. bellum moverunt, donato omnibus Cœlo, qui arma in eum converterent: unde detestabilem Respublica perniciem traxit. Restabant ex illa domo Conradus, Friderici filius, & Conradinus nepos, ultimæ stirpis propagines. Quorum illum Alexander IV. sibi vexandum sumpsit: hunc Clemens IV. insidiis circumventum Carolo Andegavensi in manus tradidit, & Romæ trucidari jussit. Ita pessimè multatis Imperatoribus, & stabilita Tarpeii Jovis dominatione, cùm post septendecim annorum Interregnum Rodolphus Habspurgicus Imperii habenas capessivisset; & Papæ partis Italiæ possessionem, ac supremæ in ea dominationis jus cessisset, sopita aliquandiu cum Cæsaribus bella quieverunt, donec illa sub Ludovico Bavaro in exitialem Reip. flammam erumperent. Ita enim Cæsarem omni laude majorem Johannes XXII. Benedictus XII. & Clemens VI. exagitárunt, ut toto Imperii tempore vix unquam tranquillum ei spiritum trahere datum fuerit.
units.tr: XLIX. The wars that the Hildebrandine Popes undertook and waged against the Latin emperors were especially savage, and if they do not pertain to the blood of the saints, they certainly pertain to the cruelty of the Hierarchy. As soon as the Western barbarians, drawn into superstition, submitted to the yoke of the Roman Church, and the Hierarchy, around the eleventh century, put on and assumed the manly toga, it at once, drunk with sweet fortune, laid wanton hands on the sceptre of the supreme empire, and, having declared a wicked war, raised a dispute with the Caesars over the right of supreme rule. That deadly struggle was prolonged for two hundred years, and during that time no words can convey how much blood was shed, what civil and foreign slaughters and massacres were carried out, how grievous a blow was dealt to the Christian name, how many regions were laid waste and how many cities burned. The first sign of war was given by that infernal torch Gregory VII, called Hildebrand, who, inflamed by a mad lust to dominate, aimed the edge of his brutal thunderbolt against Henry IV, who was defending the rights of the Imperial Majesty; he suborned an assassin against the head of that excellent prince, incited the subjects to take up arms against their Lord, and bestowed the insignia of the Empire on Rudolf of Swabia, who, joining battle with the Emperor for the third time, lost his life and his right hand. Urban, afterwards terrified by no lesson of vindicated treachery, roused by the same gadfly of fury against the Emperor, brought Herman of Luxembourg into the arena; and when he had been removed, he inflamed Conrad, the son, against his father. Paschal II, the heir of ambition and hatred, took up the purple of royal dignity and the triple crown, and thundering from the Tarpeian rock against the Emperor, armed his son Henry against his father; when the father had been overpowered and handed over to custody, the son, at the Pope's command, seized the Empire. But when Henry did not seem to comply with the Pope either, he was struck by him together with the princes and bishops; and, having been forced by Calixtus II to yield by force the right of electing bishops, he was shamefully harassed, and at last, condemning the intolerable ambition of the Pontiffs as well as his own folly and impiety, he died. Adrian II and Alexander III pursued this war with incredible intensity of spirit, and with the greatest disaster to the Christian name they stirred all Europe against Frederick Barbarossa. This war, waged for a long time with varying fortune, could not be quieted until the Emperor, pitying the public ruin, submitted both his neck and the majesty of the Empire to be trampled under the feet of a most shameful little priest. The hatred passed on to Frederick's sons and descendants, and it was not laid aside until the most noble family was utterly extinct, to the greatest loss of the Christian commonwealth. For at the Pope's command they attacked Henry VI, the son, with arms, through the Archbishop of Cologne and others. Innocent III harassed Philip through Otto of Saxony, whom, after crowning him and aiding him with his own forces, he overthrew by the same arts by which he had recently raised him up. Gregory IX and Innocent IV made war on Frederick II, the grandson, offering heaven to all who would turn their arms against him, and from this the commonwealth drew a hateful ruin. There remained from that house Conrad, son of Frederick, and Conradin, grandson, the last shoots of the line. Of these, Alexander IV took the one to harass; Clement IV, having ensnared the other by treachery, handed him over into the hands of Charles of Anjou, and ordered him to be butchered at Rome. Thus the Emperors were most wretchedly crushed, and the domination of the Tarpeian Jupiter was established; and when, after an interregnum of seventeen years, Rudolf of Habsburg had seized the reins of the Empire and had yielded to the Pope the possession of the Italian party and the right of supreme lordship there, the wars with the Caesars rested for some time. But they broke out again under Louis of Bavaria into a deadly fire for the commonwealth. For John XXII, Benedict XII and Clement VI so harassed the Caesar, who deserved all praise, that for the whole of his reign he was scarcely ever granted to draw a peaceful breath.

units.la: L. Nihil dicam de factionibus Gibellinis & Guelphicis, quæ Italiam, Papa, ut partam dominationem commissis inter se Principibus firmaret, eadem alente, infestam habuerunt; quæque brevi tempore horribiles & urbibus vastitates, & hominibus strages intulerunt: Nihil de Ursina & Columnia factione, ex qua foeda sæpe in Provinciam labes & pernicies manavit: Nihil de bello Siculo, quod sub Cœlestino III. geri coeptum, demum sub Clemente VII. finitum, trecentos pone annos duravit; & cum ipso Regum Regnorumque exitio finem accepit; Romanis Pontificibus Christianæ Reipublicæ Principes, objecto Regni Siculi, tanquam Eridos pomo, in cruentissimas contentiones distrahentibus; & jam Imperatores Suevos adversus Tancredum & Normannos adscisentibus; jam Carolum Ludovici Regis fratrem, & Gallos; jam Arragonios; demum Hungaros; iterum Gallos; denique Hispanos & Austrios, mercetricio plane prostibulorum, quae nausea priorum capta alios pelliciunt, ausu, advocantibus: Nihil de Belli Sacri minimè Sacri & infelicis inflato classico, quo multae hominum myriades, tertia minimum Europæi roboris pars, & in una urbe Ptolemaïde capta, hominum trecenta millia ferro cæsa, pessimo fato defuncta, litárunt ambitioni Papæ, Principes Christianos, fucato prætextu vindicandæ Crucis Dominicæ, ad Orientem ablegantis, ut dominatione Occidentis potiretur fructetúrque & tutius, & securius: Nihil de Schismatibus Pontificiis, quibus & pluribus, & pertinacissimis, cùm satis ampla fundendi sanguinis materies ad manum non esset, in se ipsos Cadmæa arma converterunt, tractisque in partes & factiones suas Principibus, Europam universam funestissimis bellis implicárunt: Nihil denique de Imperio Orientali, & Constantinopoli Sede Imperiali, quæ conjunctis Occidentis viribus servari poterat, deserta, adeóque, cùm servari posset, prodita, haud aliam ob causam, quàm quia Graeci cervices suas jugo Papæ submittere renuerunt; adeóque consultius visum est, ut in Occidente Papa, in Oriente Muhammed, Ecclesiam illè Latinam, hic Graecam, velut tempestas & nox tenebrosa ac formidabilis involverent, ac tanquam patrimonium hercisecerentur. Hæc alibi deductius narrata, & certissima licet crudelitatis Hierarchicæ adversus quosvis dissentientes, & iniquæ dominationi obsistentes, documenta, ab instituto tamen paulò remotiora ad compendium ponimus.
units.tr: L. I will say nothing of the Gibelline and Guelphic factions, which kept Italy in constant turmoil, the Pope nourishing them so that the dominion he had won might be made secure by setting the princes against one another. In a short time these factions brought horrible devastation to cities and slaughter to men. I will say nothing of the Ursine and Colonna faction, from which a foul disgrace and ruin often spread into the province. I will say nothing of the Sicilian war, begun under Celestine III and finally ended under Clement VII, which lasted nearly three hundred years and came to an end only with the ruin of kings and kingdoms. The Roman Pontiffs, dangling the kingdom of Sicily like the apple of Eris, drew the Christian princes into the bloodiest quarrels: now they summoned the Swabian emperors against Tancred and the Normans, now Charles, brother of King Louis, and the French, now the Aragonese, then the Hungarians, again the French, and finally the Spaniards and Austrians. Like a whore's brothel, they lured others with bold invitations, after the nausea of earlier men had been satisfied. I will say nothing of the Crusade, by no means holy and unfortunate, whose trumpet was sounded so that many myriads of men, at least a third of Europe's strength, sacrificed themselves to the ambition of the Pope. When Ptolemais was taken, three hundred thousand men were cut down by the sword and died a wretched death. Under the false pretext of avenging the Lord's Cross, the Pope sent Christian princes away to the East, so that he might gain and secure dominion over the West. I will say nothing of the Papal schisms, in which, since there was not enough material for shedding blood at hand, and when there were several, and very stubborn, the Papists turned their Cadmean arms upon themselves, dragging princes into their parties and factions, and entangled all Europe in the most deadly wars. Finally, I will say nothing of the Eastern Empire and of the imperial see of Constantinople, which could have been preserved by the united strength of the West, but was deserted and therefore betrayed, though it could have been saved, for no other reason than that the Greeks refused to submit their necks to the yoke of the Pope. So it seemed more expedient that the Pope in the West and Muhammad in the East should envelop the Latin Church and the Greek Church respectively, like a storm and a dark and dreadful night, and divide them as an inheritance. These matters have been narrated at greater length elsewhere. Although they are most certain proofs of the Hierarchy's cruelty against all dissenters and against those who resist its unjust domination, I have here set them down briefly, since they lie somewhat outside my present purpose.

units.la: LI. Propius instituram demonstrationem contingit histohistoria atrocissimarum persecutionum adversus verè Sanctos, & fideles testes Iesu. Harum selectiora exempla repræsentaturi, initium facimus à Waldensibus, seu Albigensibus, qui diu satis intra privatos parietes, & in silvis ac speluncis cum Elia & aliis Prophetis delitescentes, tandem Seculo duodecimo in publicum prodierunt, errores Papatus, quem Babylonem, & confusionis omnis Matrem dixerunt, detexerunt, Ecclesias reformárunt; & propter ποφ- ηγτίαν hancce suam Hierarchiæ odium acerrimum incurrerunt. Non tantùm enim in hæreticorum serie eos numeravit solenni nequitia, quali hodiéque veritatem Cœlestem hæresibus idololatriæ & tyrannidi suæ oppositam onerare consueverit; ut injusto odio gravaret eos, contra quos nulla erat verorum criminum accusatio: (nam Reinerus ipse Inquisitor, inter Bohemicarum rerum scriptores à Frehero editus, gravissimè de iis testari coactus fuit, quòd cùm omnes aliæ hæreses cum immanitate blasphemiarum in Deum horrorem inducant, hæc (Waldensium, quos etiam Leonistas appellat) magnam habeat speciem pietatis, eò quòd coram hominibus juste vivant, & bene omnia de Deo credant, & omnes articulos, qui in Symbolo continentur; solam Romanam Ecclesiam blasphement & oderint,) sed etiam in eodem sacro priùs igne ab Alexandro III. afflatos, suppliciorum crudelitate, qua potuit, maxima in eos sæviit. Innocentius Pontifex, sic Æmilius de Gestis Franc. lib. vi. scribit, belli adversus eos sacri suscipiendi author fuit; legatósque (en statim Zephardeas, seu ranas Ægyptiacas) circummisit ad excitandos in nefariam sectam animos. Gaguinus in Philippo Augusto: Pontifex Innocentius III. misso Gallone Cardinali Legato, Philippum, Pontificis authoritate monet in hæreticos armari: peccatorum remissione concessa his, qui insigne crucis ad id bellum sumerent. Nam Cruciatas expeditiones adversus Saracenos institutas, in Sedis suæ adversarios Papa converterat. ad quam flammam suscitandam Prædicatorum inprimis familia uti placuit; instituto etiam Crucigerorum ordine, qui Fratres de militia B. Dominici dici consueverant. Primus impetus factus est in urbem Bitterensem: inde itum Carcassonem, quò confugerant totius regionis incolæ, Bitterensium excidio territi. Tandem abire omnes nudi compelluntur, ut qui pudendis membris (inquit Gaguinus) per summum nefas abusi fuerant, ea ad ignominiam videnda exhiberent. Dignum Legatis Apostolicis spectaculum: mansuetudinisque Romanæ documentum illustre! Paulus tamen Æmilius iis concessa vestimenta scribit; velans, credo Legati infamiam. Vaurum & ipsum vi captum, ita Æmilius subjicit; ibi quoque impii igni traditi, cùm in amentia perstarent, ne mulieribus quidem temperatum. Girarda ejus oppidi Princeps fœmina in puteum conjecta, & saxis insuper obruta. Belli historiam scripsit Johannes Chassanianus, ex Manuscriptis, narrans inter alia, capto Minerbio, tum viros, tum fœminas in ignem conjectos esse, quòd in gremium Ecclesiæ Romanæ redire abnuerent. Ipse Bellarminus de Nat. Eccl. cap. ult. non diffitetur, non die cœsa fuisse Albigensium centum millia. Plura à Celeb. Usserio de Succeff. Eccl. cap. 9. 10. & in Papatus Historia ff. xcix. c. aiv. dicta repetere nihil attinet. LII. Qui ex carnificum crucigerorum manibus elapsi sunt nonnulli, per Germaniam, Angliam & Bohemiam Cœlestis veritatis lucem diffuderunt. Ea illustrati Wiclefus in Anglia, & per eundem in Bohemia Johannes Hussus & Hieronymus Pragensis, aliique Papæ in os oblocuti, Romam Antichristi natalem, idololatriæ officinam, superstitionum Scholam, abominationum matrem, Meretricem illam magnam, quæ prostituto obscœnum ad usum corpore, homines ad pessima quævis inducat, palam insigniverunt. Sed sacros hosce apices violatos neutiquam impune illi tulerunt. Wiclefum Dei bonitas & Eduardi Regis favor protexerant. Hussus A. 1415. die 6. Julii, quo Sol aversatus sanguinarium scelus, orbíque tenebras minatus, radios suos suppressit; & mox etiam Hieronymus Constantiæ contra fas obstrictæ fidei horribiliter combusti sunt. Inde Germania plures exercitus validos pro Papæ dominatione in Bohemiam missos deletósque luxit: Bohemia post Ziskæ Ducis mortem incendiis deformata, rapinis exhausta, cœdibus confecta, omnibus miseriis cooperta, variis deinceps procellis horribiliter jactata est, donec victore Ferdinandi exercitu, non ita pridem Babyloni victas manus dare coacta est. Taceo νίφος μαςτύρων, immensam testium Jesu adversus Hierarchiam, à Catalogo Testium veritatis & Martyrologiis repræsentatam nubem, quorum usque ad Reformationis tempus Meretrix hæc Babylonica sanguinem plenis, quod aiunt, cyathis, ad temulentiam usque potavit. Adeo quidem, ut jam suo tempore Franciscus Petrarcha Epistola 20. Romam his verbis alloqui non dubitaverit: Illa ipsa es, quam in Spiritu sacer vidit Evangelista. Illa eadem, inquam, es, non alia: sedens super aquas multas, &c. Audi reliqua: Et vidi Mulierem ebriam de sanguine Sanctorum, & de sanguine Martyrum Jesu. Quid siles? Aut aliam hoc sanguine ebriam ostende, aut omnino, si potes, Te hanc ebriam nega. Quod si te in Spiritu videns miratus est Apostolus admiratione magna: quanta nos admiratione perfundimur, qui te oculis aperte videmus. Qui sic ante trecentos annos admiratione stupuit Petrarcha, si hodie vigeret, extra se haud dubiè raperetur totus.
units.tr: LI. Closer to the demonstration I intend is the history of the most atrocious persecutions against the truly holy and faithful witnesses of Jesus. To present the choicer examples of these, I begin with the Waldenses, or Albigenses. For a long time they lay hidden within private walls, and in woods and caves, along with Elijah and the other prophets, until at last, in the twelfth century, they came out into the open. They exposed the errors of the Papacy, which they called Babylon and the mother of all confusion, and they reformed churches. On account of their prophecy [προφητείαν] they incurred the bitterest hatred of the Hierarchy. For it not only numbered them among heretics, with that solemn wickedness with which it is still accustomed today to load the heavenly truth with heresies opposed to its idolatry and tyranny, so as to burden with unjust hatred those against whom there was no accusation of real crimes. (Reinerus himself, the Inquisitor, whose work is printed by Freher among the writers of Bohemian affairs, was compelled to bear witness most gravely concerning them: although all other heresies bring horror through the monstrousness of their blasphemies against God, this one of the Waldenses, whom he also calls Leonists, has a great appearance of piety, because they live justly before men, believe all things well about God, and hold all the articles contained in the Creed; they blaspheme and hate only the Roman Church.) But it also raged against them with the greatest cruelty of punishments that it could devise, against men who had earlier been inflamed by that same sacred fire of Alexander III. Pope Innocent, as Æmilius in his Deeds of the Franks, book 6, writes, was the author of the holy war to be undertaken against them, and he sent out legates (behold, at once the Zephardeas, or Egyptian frogs) to stir up minds against the impious sect. Gaguinus, in his life of Philip Augustus: Pope Innocent III, having sent Cardinal Gallo as legate, urges Philip by the authority of the Pontiff to take up arms against the heretics, with forgiveness of sins granted to those who would take up the badge of the cross for that war. For the Pope had turned against the adversaries of his See the crusading expeditions instituted against the Saracens. To kindle this flame, it pleased him above all to use the family of the Preachers, and also to institute the order of the Cross-bearers, which used to be called the Brothers of the Militia of Blessed Dominic. The first attack was made on the city of Béziers. From there they went to Carcassonne, where the inhabitants of the whole region had fled, terrified by the destruction of Béziers. At last they were all compelled to leave naked, so that those who (says Gaguinus) had been abused in their private parts by a supreme wickedness should display them for shame. A spectacle worthy of Apostolic Legates, and a splendid proof of Roman gentleness! Yet Paulus Æmilius writes that clothing was granted them, veiling, I suppose, the infamy of the legates. Vaur, too, was taken by force, Æmilius adds, and there the impious were also given to the fire; and since they persisted in their madness, not even women were spared. Girarda, the woman who was princess of that town, was thrown into a well and buried under stones. John Chassanion wrote the history of the war from manuscripts, relating among other things that when Minerve was taken, both men and women were thrown into the fire because they refused to return to the bosom of the Roman Church. Bellarmine himself, On the Notes of the Church, last chapter, does not deny that on one day one hundred thousand Albigenses were slain. It is pointless to repeat more things said by the celebrated Usher, On the Succession of the Church, chapters 9 and 10, and in his History of the Papacy, pages 99 and following, and page a4. LII. Some of those who escaped from the hands of the crusading executioners spread the light of heavenly truth through Germany, England and Bohemia. Illuminated by it, Wycliffe in England, and through him in Bohemia John Hus and Jerome of Prague, along with others who spoke openly against the Pope, openly branded Rome as the birthplace of Antichrist, the workshop of idolatry, the school of superstitions, the mother of abominations, that great harlot who, by the lewd use of her prostituted body, leads men into every kind of wickedness. But they did not suffer for violating these sacred marks with impunity. God's goodness and the favour of King Edward protected Wycliffe. Hus was burned horribly, on 6 July 1415, the day on which the Sun, turning away from the bloody crime and threatening darkness upon the world, hid its rays; and soon Jerome too was burned at Constance, contrary to right, despite the faith that had been pledged to him. Thereafter Germany mourned many strong armies sent into Bohemia to uphold the Pope's domination and destroyed there. After the death of Duke Zizka, Bohemia was disfigured by fires, exhausted by plunderings, worn down by slaughters, overwhelmed by every misery, and horribly tossed about by various storms, until, when Ferdinand's army was victorious, it was compelled to surrender to Babylon, not long ago. I pass over the snow of martyrs [νίφος μαρτύρων], the immense cloud of the witnesses of Jesus against the Hierarchy, displayed in the Catalogue of the Witnesses of Truth and in the Martyrologies, whose blood this Babylonian harlot drank, as they say, from full cups, to the point of drunkenness, up to the time of the Reformation. Indeed, already in his own time Francis Petrarch did not hesitate to address Rome in these words (Epistle 20): You are that very one whom the sacred Evangelist saw in the Spirit. You are the same, I say, not another: sitting upon many waters, etc. Hear the rest: And I saw a woman drunk with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus. Why are you silent? Either show me another woman drunk with this blood, or, if you can, deny altogether that you are drunk with it. If the Apostle, seeing you in the Spirit, was struck with great wonder, how greatly are we overwhelmed with wonder, who see you plainly with our eyes. If Petrarch, who was thus astonished three hundred years ago, were alive today, he would without doubt be utterly beside himself.

units.la: LIII. Ex quo enim domitis profligatisque Hussitis, opprel-
units.tr: LIII. For once the Hussites had been subdued and crushed, the Church of Christ was oppressed, and

units.la: Per Re-formatiooppressa Christi Ecclesia, nimium homo ille peccatis extulit; atque impotentiæ & blasphemiarum ejus impatientes, Heroes & Viri Dei, Huldricus Zwinglius, Lutherus, aliique veritatis Antistites, Divino Spiritu afflati, contra Babylonem eruperunt, eámque vivis coloribus depinxerunt, applaudentibus populis compluribus, Tyrannidis Hierarchicæ plus satis pertæsis; tum demum efferatissima hæc Mulier omnem sui furoris impetum in Christi gregem convertere, gladios, funes, rogos ad opprimendam Ecclesiæ emergentis lucem, & delendum Reformatæ religionis nomen, omnium virium conatu intendere, Imperatorum, Regum Principúmque auxilia solicitare, Cœlum terræ commiscere. Sic infinitum concitatum est odium, laxatæ odio habenæ, deventúmque in extremum furorem, sævitum in omnes, cujuscunque sexus, ætatis, conditionis, ut nihil aliud esse Christianitas, quàm universalis carnificina videretur. Nihil justi, nihil æqui, nihil sancti. Non tantùm humanitatis promiscuus sensus suffocatus, sed &c. φυσικαῖς τοφγυῶς vis illata est, ne quid ad immanitatis cumulum deesset.
units.tr: the Church of Christ, oppressed, was lifted up beyond measure by that man through his sins. Impatient of his arrogance and blasphemies, the heroes and men of God, Huldrych Zwingli, Luther and other bishops of the truth, inspired by the Divine Spirit, broke out against Babylon and painted her in vivid colours, while many peoples applauded, already weary of hierarchical tyranny. Then at last this most savage woman turned the full force of her fury against Christ's flock. With all her strength she directed swords, cords and stakes to crush the light of the emerging Church and to wipe out the name of the Reformed religion, sought the aid of emperors, kings and princes, and mingled heaven with earth. Thus an infinite hatred was stirred up, the reins of hatred were loosed, and they came to the extreme of madness, raging against everyone of every sex, age and condition, so that Christianity seemed nothing but a universal slaughterhouse. Nothing just, nothing fair, nothing holy. Not only was the common sense of humanity suffocated, but violence was done also against nature [φυσικαῖς], so that nothing might be lacking to the heap of inhumanity.

units.la: LIV. Longum sanè esset singulorum martyrum nomina exsequi, & singulorum martyria describere. quod alii ad perpetuam Babylonicæ crudelitatis, & invictæ Sanctorum & fidelium testium Jesu constantiæ memoriam & verissimè & luculentissimè executi sunt. Extant publicè ejus rei monumenta, nunquam hactenus à quoquam falsitatis convicta. Possumus certè, nemine, nisi eo, cui veritas odio est, ringente, Apostolum veterum supplicia Hebr. xi. 35. &c. succinctè narrantem, sic imitari: Alii aut incruces acti, aut ad pedes suspensi; aut compressis laqueo faucibus elisi vitam finiverunt. Alii aut cratibus imimpositi, aut ad palum alligati, aut pyræ injecti, supposito igne, per acerbissimos cruciatus animam efflarunt. Aliqui aquarum fluctibus immersi, bestiis objecti, vivi in terram defossi, in frusta dissecti, ferreis cuspidibus impacti, hastis contisque transverberati, rotis confracti, virgis excarnificati, de vita excesserunt. Quibus dampnatis est detracta; caput, lingua, manus detruncata, oculi effossi, oleum laceratis corporibus candens infusum. Longè plurimos fames, rerumque omnium penuria, frigora, æstus, pædor carcerum, tormentorum diritas, lictorum acerbitas miserabiliter absumpsit. Reliqui, à quibus cædium satietas, & carnifex fatigatus abstinuit, in fugam acti, fortunis spoliati, à conjugum liberorumque amplexibus avulsi, convitiis calumniisque deformati, ludibriis contumeliisque scurrarum exposti, vexati, verberati, pro purgamentis habiti, in extremas miserias detrusi, in mœrore, lachrymis, corporis animique ægritudine duriorem morte vitam tolerârunt. Hæc tamen, horrenda satis, lenissimè tamen, & longè infra modum dicta facilè animadvertet, quisquis vel solas præ cæteris nobiles lanienas & persecutiones, Parisiensem Sant-Bartholomæanam, Vallis Telinæ, Hibernicam, Pedemontanam & Hungaricam, cùm ab aliis, tum à nobis in Historia Papatus, & Dissertatione de Martyrio ex vero narratas, quarum vel sola recordatio frigidum membris horrorem incutit, animo recoluerit.
units.tr: LIV. It would indeed be a long task to list the names of individual martyrs and describe the martyrdom of each. Others have carried this out both truthfully and most brilliantly, to keep alive the memory of Babylonian cruelty and of the unconquered constancy of the saints and faithful witnesses of Jesus. Monuments of this matter stand publicly, never yet convicted of falsehood by anyone. Certainly, unless he who hates the truth grumbles, we can imitate the Apostle, who briefly recounted the ancient punishments (Heb. 11:35 etc.): Others were tortured, not accepting release, that they might obtain a better resurrection. Others suffered mockings and scourgings, yes, moreover of bonds and imprisonment. They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword; they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins, being destitute, afflicted, tormented. Yet anyone who calls to mind, whether alone or in addition to others, the especially famous slaughters and persecutions, the Paris St Bartholomew's massacre, the Valley of Telina, the Irish, Piedmontese and Hungarian persecutions, narrated truly both by others and by us in the History of the Papacy and in the Dissertation on Martyrdom, will readily notice that these things are horrible enough, yet told very gently and far below their measure. The mere recollection of some of these makes a cold horror creep through the limbs.

units.la: LV. Ibi enim, uti τὸ κακὸν ἀπειρον inprobitatis infiniti modi sunt, dapes insuper ex cerebro humano instituitas; Mulierum priùs compressarum, pectora abscissa, & mammas omasorum ritu frixas mensæ impositas, infantes mulierum gravidarum in flammas identidem immersarum, igni priùs baptizatos, mox in vorax illud elementum remissos, & una cum matribus, com-bubustos, apertos gravidarum uteros, & infantes in eundem retrufos, maternóque sanguine suffocatos; viros per pudenda sua suspensos; partes genitales resectas; vulnera ad candelæ flammam frixa; ungues per ignitos forcipes divulsos; nudas fœminas veru per pudenda transfixas, eásque in humeris aliquandiu gestatas; brachia & crura in longas corrigias, ligularum coriacearum instar, excoriata, hominésque sic excoriatos in ergastula detrusos atque in iisdem fame enectos; miseros mulæ caudæ alligatos, per compita tractos, corpora lapidibus allisa, & lateribus à populo rabiente petita; pulverem pyrium in ora & guttura infantum, & accensa eodem capita frustratim disrupta; genitalia abscissa, ori indita, oculos erutos, hominésque sic mutilatos spectaculo aliquot diërum expositos, ac demum vivos excoriatos, atque sic excoriatorum pelles quadripartitas ex præcipuis oppidi fenestris suspensas; corpora insepulta porcorum & canum laniatibus exposita; aliáque plus quàm Diaboli- cæ crudelitatis in innocuum Christi gregem exercita genera summo cum stupore perspiciet; & cum S. Johanne, qui Apoc. xvii. 6. Mulierem sic sanguine Sanctorum & testium Jesu inebriatam in Spiritu admirabundus vidit, ingeminabit hæc verba: Καὶ ἰδὼν γυναῖκα μεθύουσαν ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν ἁγίων, Et miratus sum, videns eam, (Mulierem inebriatam) admiratione magna. Quid enim plus quàm Cannibalica hàc crudelitate, & exquisito acumine novorum ejusmodi suppliciorum tormentorumque, qualia nec barbara sævitia ulla, nec Scythica immanitas excogitare potuit; architectandorum stupendum, quid horrendum magis cuiquam obtingere potest? Non mensæ Thyesteæ, non aræ Busiridis, non taurus Phalaridis, tam inhumanæ crudelitatis exempla edidere, quàm in imbellem fidelium gregem Romanæ Babylonis sanguinarii satellites.
units.tr: LV. There, indeed, just as the evil that is without limit [τὸ κακὸν ἀπειρον] is of infinite kinds of wickedness, feasts were moreover prepared from human brains. The breasts of women who had first been violated were cut off and fried like tripe and placed on the table. Infants of pregnant women were repeatedly plunged into the flames, first baptized with fire, then thrown back into that voracious element, and burned together with their mothers. The wombs of pregnant women were opened and infants thrust back into them, suffocated in their mothers' blood. Men were hanged by their genitals; genitals were cut off; wounds were fried at a candle flame; nails were torn out with red-hot pincers; naked women were run through on spits through the genitals and carried for a while on shoulders; arms and legs were flayed into long strips like leather thongs, and men so flayed were thrown into dungeons and starved to death there. Wretched men were tied by the tail to a mule and dragged through the crossroads, their bodies dashed against stones and gored in the sides by a raging crowd. Gunpowder was put into the mouths and throats of infants, and their heads were blown to pieces by the same charge. Genitals were cut off and stuffed into mouths, eyes were gouged out, and men so mutilated were exposed to the spectacle for some days, then finally flayed alive, and the skins of the flayed were hung in quarters from the chief windows of the town. Corpses were left unburied, exposed to the mangling of pigs and dogs. Other kinds of cruelty, more than diabolical, exercised against Christ's innocent flock, he will observe with great amazement. And with St John, who in Apoc. 17:6 saw the woman drunk with the blood of the saints and witnesses of Jesus, marvelling in the Spirit, he will repeat these words: And when I saw her I wondered with great admiration [Καὶ ἰδὼν γυναῖκα μεθύουσαν ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν ἁγίων]: and I wondered greatly, seeing her (the woman made drunk). For what more horrible thing can befall anyone than this cannibal cruelty and exquisite ingenuity in devising new kinds of punishments and torments, such as no barbarous savagery or Scythian brutality could think up? Not the feasts of Thyestes, not the altars of Busiris, not the bull of Phalaris, produced examples of such inhuman cruelty as the bloodthirsty henchmen of Roman Babylon have shown against the defenceless flock of the faithful.
LVI.

units.la: Frustra talia non Hierarchiæ mandato, sed Nam justè quidem facta esse, ne Diabolus ipse affirmaverit. Et palea certè hæc fecit, non triticum, quod frustra in ipsa Hierarchia requiras. Si palea, hoc est, populus, furibundus miles hæc omnia fecit, neque Hierarchia culpam sustinet, eradite ergo Pontificum, Episcoporum, Imperatorum, Regum, Principum Papæ obsequentium, & ejusdem signaturam recipientium, edicta contra Reformatam religionem! Ostendite Pontifices, Episcopos à talibus abhorrentes, & crudeliter adeo facta detestantes, censuris ecclesiasticis notantes! Atqui laudarunt etiam nonnulli aperte, veluti lanienam Parisiensem, in qua similia patrata sunt, Gregorius XIII. qui tam immanem casum in sacri sui Magistratus auspiciis maximè, inter prospera ducebat, & temperare sibi non potuit, quò minùs lætabilem adeò ob causam toti orbi Christiano Jubilæum publicaret. Neque citra voluptatem Jesuitas ejus recordari, quin eandem laudare, Histor. Pap. ff 197. ostendimus. Sanè etiam personatus ille Jesuita, Ludovicus Dorleanus, in expostulatione cum eo, qui partes Regias in Gallia A. 1593. tuebatur, inter alia sic scripsit: Quis nescit saluberrimam illam venæ-sectionem D. Bartholomæi, qua nostèr Elias in Prophetas Baal, nostèr Jehu in idololatras, nostèr Quadus in Manichæos armata manu infremuit? Sic planè Dæmoniacus hic Spiritus in recordatione immanissimi facinoris subsultavit, ut in ea suaviter se oblectaverit, non aliter, quàm videmus lupum, si quando à dilaniata pecude abigitur, cruentas fauces lingere. Et sanè cum Hierarchiæ Ministri & assectlæ ab ipsamet edocti sint, omnes, qui ex ipsorum Ecclesia non sunt, hæreticos, omnésque hæreticos canibus pejores, pejúsque, si quando sic ei placuerit, tractandos esse; imò meritorium esse, & à purgatorii poenis exsolvere, si quis tanto cum zelo in hæreticos insurgat, & pacta religiosa universa dissuadeat; inita rescindenda, ceu jure nulla, vociferetur; imò non tantùm ferali doctrina, sed exempli etiam, quale supra in Inquisitionis Busiridico tribunali exhibuimus, authoritate & gravitate præcat; quæ causa dici potest, cur à culpa tantorum scelerum immunis censeri debeat? Vel solius Lojolitæ, Petri Ribaldi Peruani ferale adversus nostros, quos rebelles ille nuncupat, carmen, quo velut ex suggestu carnificis exquisita supplicia docet; Hist. Pap. ff. 268. narratum, quis reliquis omnibus sit δυμὸς ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, demonstrat. Saltem denique sic impletum est, quòd in ea, Babylone, & plateis ejus, sanguis Prophetarum, & Sanctorum & omnium in terra mactatorum obvius futurus sit, uti Apoc. xvIII. 24. prædictum legimus. Quod in subditorum Babylonis plateis reperitur, in ipsa quoque Babylone reperiri, quis inficias iverit?
units.tr: It is vain to claim that such things were done by the command of the Hierarchy, or that they were done justly; not even the Devil himself would affirm it. Certainly this was the chaff's doing, not the wheat's, and in the Hierarchy itself you will look in vain for wheat. If the chaff, that is the people, a raging soldiery, did all this, and the Hierarchy bears no blame, then let the Pontiffs, Bishops, Emperors, Kings and Princes who obey the Pope and accept his signature publish edicts against the Reformed religion! Let the Pontiffs and Bishops show that they abhor such deeds, detest acts so cruel, and mark them with ecclesiastical censures! Yet some have openly praised them, such as the Parisian slaughter, in which similar things were committed. Gregory XIII, who counted so monstrous an event among the prosperous happenings under his sacred Magistracy, could not restrain himself from proclaiming a jubilee for the whole Christian world on so joyful an occasion. Nor have the Jesuits recalled it without pleasure; we have shown that they praise it Histor. Pap. ff 197. Indeed that masked Jesuit, Louis d'Orléans, when remonstrating with a man who defended the royal cause in France in 1593, wrote among other things: Who does not know that most wholesome bloodletting of St Bartholomew, by which our Elijah thundered with armed hand against the prophets of Baal, our Jehu against the idolaters, our Quadus against the Manichaeans? Thus this demonic spirit so exulted in the memory of that most monstrous crime that it delighted in it, just as we see a wolf, when driven from a torn carcass, licking its bloody jaws. And since the ministers and followers of the Hierarchy have been taught by it themselves that all who are not of their Church are heretics, and that heretics are to be treated worse than dogs, and worse still whenever it pleases them; and that it is even meritorious and frees one from the pains of purgatory if anyone rises up with such zeal against heretics and cries out that all religious pacts should be dissolved, as void in law; and since this teaching is backed not only by deadly doctrine but also by example, such as we have displayed above in the Busirian tribunal of the Inquisition, what reason can be given why they should be deemed free of guilt for such great crimes? The ferocious poem of the Jesuit Pedro de Ribadeneira, the Peruvian, against our people, whom he calls rebels, in which he teaches exquisite tortures as if from the executioner's platform, shows well enough, when recounted, who is their delight on the day. Hist. Pap. ff. 268. At last, then, this has been fulfilled: that in Babylon and in her streets the blood of the prophets and saints and of all who have been slain on earth is to be found, as we read was foretold in Apoc. xviii. 24. What is found in the streets of Babylon's subjects, who would deny that it is also found in Babylon herself?

units.la: LVII. Hæc in genere de crudelitate Hierarchiæ erga Ecclesiam à se per Reformationem separatam dicta sufficiant. Possemus per singula excurrentes, innumera afferre: Vix ergo signo Reformationis per Lutherum, Zwinglium &c. dato, Leo X. illud Ecclesiæ portentum & prodigium, antequam gladiatorius ille Sanguinariorum Patrum Senatus haberetur,
units.tr: LVII. Let what has been said in general about the cruelty of the Hierarchy toward the Church separated from it by the Reformation suffice. We could go through the particulars and bring forward countless instances. Scarcely had the sign of the Reformation been given through Luther, Zwingli and others, when Leo X, before that gladiatorial senate of the bloodthirsty Fathers was held, began his prelude to that monster and portent of the Church:
The sand, strewn for the fight, has given its prelude.

units.la: Luthero aqua & igni Wormatiæ per Imperii Ordines, & Romæ vibrato bruto fulmine interdicens, libros ab ipso scriptos hæreseos damnans, & Vulcano consecratos exurens. Ejusdem vestigiis insistens Adrianus VI. promissa licet reformatione in capite & membris, Thyeftea tamen execratione Testes Christi prosequitur; multandos præfentibus suppliciis hæreticos, difsipandos fidelium cœtus, proclamat: Imperatorem & Principes in eorum necem inflammat. Adriani Successor Clemens VII. tibias easdem inflans, Ratisbonam Campegium mittit, cujus impulsu de subvertendis Protestantibus fœdus Religiosum percutitur. Statim Henricus Sutphanienfis, Monachis facem subjicientibus, apud Dithmarfos ob Evangelii doctrinam igni crematur. Eo fervore excitati Bruxellenfes, Passavienfes, Colonienfes, Conftantienfes, Bavari, Tornacenfes Veritatis profeffores ultricibus flammis mancipârunt Gallorum præ cæteris in opprimenda Ecclesia studia æstuare cœperunt. qui Parifiis, omni deposito humanitatis sensu, fideles ad machinam alligatos, igníque è sublimi immissos, & rursus adductos, itaque demum per lentos cruciatus enecuerunt. Cepit inde crudelitatis exemplum Sabaudus, qui adversus vicinos Genevenfes Evangelium amplexos copias conscripsit, ut urbi, Episcopo impellente, bellum indixit. Neque Oceani fluctus, & adsitæ littoribus rupes præcipitem crudelitatis cursum sufflaminârunt, quò minùs in Angliam fe effunderet, & Henricum Regem ad pyras rogósque Religioni struendos inflammaret.
units.tr: Forbidding Luther, by fire and water, at Worms through the orders of the Empire, and hurling the brute thunderbolt at Rome, condemning the books written by him as heretical and burning them, consecrated to Vulcan. Following in his footsteps, Adrian VI, though he had promised a reformation in head and members, still pursues the witnesses of Christ with Thyestean curse; he proclaims that heretics must be punished with present torments and the assemblies of the faithful scattered; he inflames the Emperor and Princes to their slaughter. Adrian's successor Clement VII, blowing the same pipes, sends Campeggio to Ratisbon, at whose instigation a religious league for overthrowing the Protestants is struck. Immediately Henry of Sutphen, with the monks heaping on the fire, is burned at the stake among the Dithmarsians for the doctrine of the Gospel. Stirred by the same zeal, the men of Brussels, Passau, Cologne, Constance, the Bavarians and the men of Tournai delivered the professors of truth to avenging flames. The French began to surpass all others in studying to crush the Church: at Paris, having cast off every sense of humanity, they bound the faithful to a machine, sent them down into the fire from on high, drew them up again, and at last put them to death by slow tortures. The Savoyard then took up the example of cruelty: against the neighboring Genevans, who had embraced the Gospel, he raised troops, and at the bishop's urging he declared war on the city. Nor could the waves of the ocean, nor the cliffs beside its shores, check the headlong course of cruelty from pouring into England and inflaming King Henry to build pyres and stakes for religion.

units.la: LVIII. Ita accensis in religionem odiis, depofitóque satis crudelitatis tyrocinio, Paulus III. Concilium Tridentum, fatalem Europæarum regionum limitem, indicit; validissimum interea in Germaniam exercitum submittit, sub duce tali, qui palam profitebatur, fe non prius in Italiam reditururm, quàm equum suum in Lutheranorum sanguine abluisset. Ea tempestate Jesuitica ranarum vermiculatio provenit, & horrenda.
units.tr: LVIII. With hatreds thus kindled against religion, and with a sufficient apprenticeship in cruelty completed, Paul III summoned the Council of Trent, that fatal boundary of the regions of Europe. Meanwhile he sent a very strong army into Germany, under a leader who openly professed that he would not return to Italy until he had washed his horse in Lutheran blood. At that time the Jesuitical croaking of frogs appeared, and a horrible one.

units.la: Tom. II. dd missiomissionem, extinguendæ veritatis, & Metaphysicæ potestatis Papæ consecrandæ & amplificandæ gratia, speciali, uti supra vidimus, voto suscepit. Franciscus Gallorum Rex, ut primùm classicum Papa cecinit, Et tristem in limo Ranæ cecinere querelam, adversus Ecclesiam aciem instruit, acerbam per universum Regnum fidei Inquisitionem indicit, & per omnia immanitatis exempla exercet. Nil cunctatus Carolus, ne à Gallo sibi palma præripi videretur, in Belgio in Religionis Reformatæ professores severè inquirit, compertis convictisque ferrum, ignes, laqueos intendit, & exigui temporis spatio quinquaginta millia hominum, ob veritatis confessionem, vario supplicíorum genere perimit. Inflammatus hoc æmuli sui studio Gallus copias iterum ipse adversus Ecclesiam educit, Waldenses, Merindolenses & Caprarienses, immisso milite crudeliter trucidat, miseros in speluncis ferarumque latibulis carnificum metu delitescentes, bestiarum instar, indagine circumventos mactat; pueros, senes, mulieres, nulla ætatis sexúsque verecundia, crudelissima morte absumit. Tragœdiam descripserunt è medio Papatu Thomas Carmerius Alenconius Rer. Gest. Henrici II. lib. 11. & Thuanus Histor. lib. 11. ubi, horrenda, inquit, & supra modum atroci sententia ante decennium damnati fuerant, præsidente tum Senatui Bartholomæo Cassanæo, magni nominis Jurisconsulto; Senatusconsulti illius sententia in Patres familias igne vindicatur, dum natorum bona, conjuges, liberique & cætera familia fisco addicuntur. Et quia Merindolium hactenus hac peste infectorum spelunca ac receptaculum fuerat, edicitur, ut ædificia omnia à fundamentis evertantur, antra, caverna ac fornices subterranei, quibus laterent, diruantur & obturentur, sylva circum cædatur, & arbores etiam hortorum evellantur: possessiones verò eorum, qui Merindolii domicilium habuerint, ejusdem vel stirpis, vel etiam nominis cum prioribus Dominis nemini colende elocentur. En Scævolas, Papinianos, Tribonianos, an potiùs Cajaphas! Et tamen variis rationibus negotium in annum decimum differtur. Tum verò præside Oppeda furor erupit. Pupis, Mola, Martiniacum, vici ad Druentium capiuntur, diripiuntur, inflammantur. Villalaurea, Lauromarinum, Gensonium, Trezeminæ, Rupes, vici, unde multitudo profugerat, crudeliter incenduntur, pecore omni abacto. Oppeda Waldensibus aqua ignique interdixerat, & capite sanxerat, ne quis ulla re illos juvaret: sed quocunque loco deprehensi, nullo sexus aut ætatis discrimine habito, omnes occiderentur. Captariæ tam intra, quàm extra oppidum jugulati omnes. Fœminæ jussu Oppedæ in horreum Araminis plenum conjectæ, & subjecto igne, cùm per fenestram se saltu dejicere molirentur, contis & hastis repulsæ, fumóque suffocatæ, ac postremò flammis omnes consumptæ sunt. Costæ contra datam fidem ad unum omnes trucidati sunt. De viginti duo vicis Oppeda supplicium sumpsit. Eadem tempestate Carolus, ne concedere aliquid in oppugnandis hæreticis Gallo videretur, in Wormatiensibus Comitiis, à Cardinale Farnesio, Pontificio Emissario, ad delendos armis Evangelicos incitatus, bellum in Protestantes Principes parat: quibus acie victis profligatisque, Ecclesiæ res in aciem novaculæ, captis Principibus, Doctoribus in exilium & ergastula detrusis, edita hinc inde civium strage maxima, adductæ sunt.
units.tr: Tom. II. Vol. II. He undertook the mission, for the sake of extinguishing the truth and of consecrating and enlarging the metaphysical power of the Pope, with a special vow, as we saw above. King Francis of France, as soon as the Pope sounded the trumpet, And in the mud the frogs sang a sad lament, drew up his battle line against the Church, proclaimed a harsh inquisition into the faith throughout the whole kingdom, and practised every kind of monstrous cruelty. Charles, not hesitating at all lest the palm be snatched from him by the Frenchman, searched closely in Belgium for professors of the Reformed religion; once they were discovered and convicted, he brought sword, fire and nooses against them, and in a short span of time he destroyed fifty thousand people, by various kinds of torments, for confessing the truth. Inflamed by the zeal of his rival, the Frenchman again led out troops against the Church: he cruelly slaughtered the Waldenses, Merindolians and Caprarians by sending in soldiers; he butchered the wretched people hiding in caves and lairs of wild beasts for fear of the executioners, hemmed in by the hunt like beasts; he destroyed boys, old men and women, with no regard for age or sex, by the most cruel death. Thomas Carmerius of Alençon, in his Deeds of Henry II, book 11, and de Thou, in his History, book 11, have described this tragedy from the midst of Papistry, where, as he says, "horrible and beyond measure atrocious sentences had been passed ten years before, while Bartholomew Cassanaeus, a jurist of great name, presided over the Senate. By the sentence of that senatorial decree the heads of families were punished by fire, while the goods of the sons, the wives, the children and the rest of the household were handed over to the treasury. And because Merindol had until then been the cave and refuge of those infected with this plague, it was ordered that all the buildings be overthrown from their foundations, the caves, grottoes and underground vaults in which they might hide be destroyed and blocked up, the woods around be cut down, and even the trees of their gardens be uprooted; and the properties of those who had dwelt in Merindol were to be let to anyone at all, of the same stock or even the same name as the former owners." Behold the Scaevolas, Papinians, Tribonians, or rather Caiaphases! And yet for various reasons the business was put off for ten years. Then indeed the fury broke out under the presidency of Oppède. Pupis, Mola, Martiniacum and the villages on the Durance were taken, plundered and set on fire. Villelaure, Lauris, Gensonnet, Trézémines, Rustrel and the villages from which the crowd had fled were cruelly burned, all the herds driven off. Oppède had forbidden the Waldenses fire and water and had decreed by penalty of death that no one should help them in any way; but wherever they were caught, all were to be killed, with no distinction of sex or age. At Cabrières all were butchered, both within the town and outside it. By Oppède's order the women were thrown into a barn full of straw and set alight; when they tried to leap out through the window they were thrust back with pikes and spears, and at last all were consumed by flames, having been suffocated by smoke. The men of Cosne, contrary to their given faith, were all slaughtered to a man. Oppède exacted punishment from twenty-two villages. At the same time Charles, lest he seem to yield anything to the Frenchman in attacking heretics, was incited at the Diet of Worms by Cardinal Farnese, the Papal emissary, to destroy the Evangelicals by arms, and he prepared war against the Protestant Princes. When these were defeated and routed in battle, and the Princes were captured, the teachers were thrust into exile and dungeons, and the affairs of the Church were brought to the edge of the razor, with great slaughter of citizens on every side.

units.la: LIX. In Anglia mortuo Henrico Eduardus succesfit, qui Cœlestis veritatis luce imbutus Ecclesiam à superstitione purgandam suscoperat. Sed eo mox non fine veneni suspicione defuncto, Maria Soror imperium adepta, sanguinariis Poli Cardinalis consiliis, religionem in herba, quod ajunt, suffocare adnixa est.
units.tr: LIX. In England, after Henry died, Edward succeeded him. Imbued with the light of heavenly truth, he had resolved to purge the Church of superstition. But Edward died soon afterwards, not without suspicion of poison, and his sister Mary gained the throne. Through the bloody counsels of Cardinal Pole, she strove to smother religion in the bud, as they say.
dd

units.la: Nam fideles crudelissimè vita fortunisque provolvit, & intra biennium octingentos, atque inter eos Archiepiscopum & Episcopos, flamma ferróque, ob religionis professionem, carnificis manu horribiliter interfecit. Extincta ea quaeque quaeso insidiis sacrum Elisabethae, sacrum Jacobi Regis caput appetierunt? Quàm crudele huic, Regiae familiae, & toti Nobilitati Anglicae exitium per pulverem tormentarium intentatum fuit, Archipyrobolo Sathana incentore, & post illum Jesuitis, Garneto, qui confitentes à scelere confesso & professo absolvit, & ad Missae suae Eleusinia admisit, Oldecorn, Cres, Weel &c. primas in tragoedia partes tractantibus? Taceo reliqua Cleri in pervertenda Anglia, toxicaria inprimis molimina novissima. Testantur relationes ex authenticis actis omni fide majores, quorum licet Surius EudaemonJohannes, aliíque ejusdem commatis ferrei homines fidem minuere conati hactenus sunt, frustra tamen illi in Sole tenebras quaesitaverunt. Vellent enim illi nos expectare, donec isti Daemones suum ipsorum fecelus proderent. Accessit hoc etiam Seculo Hibernica laniena, quae inauditis antehac supplicciorum generibus in tota insula per bestias plusquam infernales saevicns, paucorum mensium intervallo plusquam ducenta hominum millia, & in sola Ultonia centum quinquaginta quatuor millia, in gratiam Romani Molochi, abfumplit. Haec fusiùs in Historia Papatus tradita repetere libens supersedeo.
units.tr: For she cruelly stripped the faithful of life and property, and within two years she horribly had eight hundred put to death by fire and sword, the executioner's hand falling on them for professing their religion, among them an archbishop and bishops. Once these were destroyed, I ask, what plots did they not aim at the sacred head of Elizabeth and the sacred head of King James? How cruel a destruction was threatened against the royal family and the whole English nobility by gunpowder, with the arch-incendiary Satan as instigator and, after him, the Jesuits. Garnet absolved men of a crime they had confessed and professed, and admitted them to the Eleusinian rites of his Mass, while Oldecorn, Cres, Weel and others played the leading parts in the tragedy. I pass over the rest of the clergy's efforts to pervert England, above all their latest poisonous schemes. Reports drawn from authentic records, more than worthy of belief, bear witness to these things. Surius, Eudaemon-Johannes and other men of the same iron cast have so far tried to diminish that credit, but in vain do they seek darkness in the sun. For they would have us wait until those demons betray their own crimes. In this century there was also the Irish butchery, which raged across the whole island with tortures unheard of before, by beasts more than infernal. In a span of a few months it consumed more than two hundred thousand people, and in Ulster alone one hundred and fifty-four thousand, to gratify the Roman Moloch. I gladly leave these matters to be recounted more fully in the History of the Papacy.
LX.

units.la: Postquam in Anglia, Maria fato defuncta, Heroico plane & Divino Elisabethae Reginae spiritu, veritas confossa & jugulata revixit, in Hispaniam se crudelitas recepit, in sinum complexumque Philippi Regis effusa, ubi nacta dignum ingenio suo hospitium, plane ex voto Pontificum, orbem terrarum uni-
units.tr: After Mary died in England, and truth, pierced and throttled, revived through the truly heroic and divine spirit of Queen Elizabeth, cruelty withdrew into Spain. Poured into the bosom and embrace of King Philip, it found a home worthy of its nature, entirely according to the wishes of the Pontiffs, and it drenched the whole world...

units.la: {h} Hispania adversus Ecclesiam crudelitatis spectmina. universum Sanctorum Martyrum cœde cruentavit.
