Quantum non sanguinis fidelium sub illo Philipporum imperio per Hispanias effusum est, Cyclopico Inquisitorum Senatu in fortunas, corpora, cineres mortuorum grassante ! Quoties combustis Martyribus de interitu piorum , de victoria Babylonis gloriosissimè triumpharunt?
units.tr: {h} Spain's spectacles of cruelty against the Church. ...with the slaughter of the saints and martyrs. How much of the faithful's blood was spilled throughout Spain under that empire of the Philips, while the Cyclopean senate of Inquisitors raged against their property, bodies and the ashes of the dead! How often, having burned the martyrs, did they triumph gloriously over the ruin of the pious and the victory of Babylon?
Who could tell such things

units.la: Myrmidonum Dolopumve, aut duri miles Ulyssis Temperet a lachrymis !
units.tr: Or refrain from tears, Myrmidon or Dolopian, or a soldier of hard Ulysses?

units.la: Martyrologia,& Inquisitionis historia locuples ei rei testimonium perhibent. Adeo quidem gens ista Despotikyriis, seu Dominis dominorum, aliisque Senatoribus Inquisitorio spiritu tumentibus obnoxia est, atque ab iis Ducitur, ut nervis alienis mobile lignum :
units.tr: The martyrologies and the rich history of the Inquisition bear witness to this. So far indeed is that nation subject to its lords of lords [δεσποτικυρίοις], and to other senators swollen with the inquisitorial spirit, that it is led by them like a wooden puppet moved by another's strings.

units.la: Ut eorundem seu suasu, seu ductu, Rex Philippus II. tristi documento demonstraverit orbi, quàm dissicile ant regnantibus etiam civilia filiorum ingenia, Carolo filio ejus unico vix ob aliud intercepto, quàm quia populum Belgicum æquo jure complecti, reddita libertate & religione, agitaverat. Adeo ne ab ipsis quidem viscetibus, suspicione sola religionis diversæ, manus atroces abstinuerunt.
units.tr: So it was that King Philip II, by their counsel or their guidance, showed the world by a sad lesson how difficult it is for even rulers to bear the civil dispositions of their sons. His only son Charles was almost removed for no other reason than that he had begun to embrace the Belgian people with equal right, restoring their liberty and religion. So far did savage hands refrain not even from their own vitals, merely on suspicion of a different religion.

units.la: LXI. Verberant interea aures miserabiles Belgarum pro aris suis cadentium calamitates, lamenta. quæ oratione condigna quis demum complecti potis est? Ibi Hispanus Pontificiæ religionis asserendæ prætextu, velut opportunitate annuli Gygis usus, ad flagitiosissima quæque viam sibi aperuit. Nam castellis passim in Rebuspublicis contra consensum Ordinum extructis, & peregrinis impositis præsidiis, injecti libero populo compedes : acriter exercita lex Majestatis, accusationum omnium complementum : Nobilissimæ domus delatorum interpretationitationibus subversæ, & locupletissimus quisque in prædam correpti: nonnulli etiam inauditi, procul omnis tribunalis vestigio, furcis affixi: ademptum per Inquisitiones loquendi audiendique commercium: Ordinum loco monstrosi sanguinolentissimæ Inquisitionis Episcopi constituti: omnes Magistratus in ordinem redacti: eversa tribunalia, suffragia comitiorum tam in urbibus, quàm provinciis abrogata: sublatæ funditus immunitates atque privilegia: destinati ad coedem electissimi ex utroque Ordine Belgico, Senatorio & Equestri: Ordinum, Principum, Nobilium, civium audita nonnisi exilia, proscriptiones, edicta, carceres, vincula, neces: denique noxa atque innocentia, sacra & prosana nullo discrimine habita sunt. In fabula hac præcipuas partes Albanus, lutum illud sanguine maceratum, egit, qui accepto à Papa galero & gladio, Pontificiis precibus sacrato, Belgium cum exercitu intravit, immanitérque adeo sævivit, ut sine fronte jactare aulus fuerit, se octodecim millia Belgarum & sexcentos carnifici contrucidandos tradidisse. Forte etiam intra numerum jactantia stetit. Horrendum enim plane est, quod Jesuita Possevinus in Epistola ad Poloniæ Regem fateri non erubuit, in Belgio & Gallia undecim annorum spatio quingenta millia hominum ob Evangelicæ religionis professionem interfecta esse. Ille Albæ Plutonius Dux, monstrum hominis, filii sui ductu, Mechlinium ultro imperium accipiens, contra militiæ leges plusquam hostiliter diripuit, ingenuarum feminarum corpora lictoribus subjecit, in omnem sexum, ætatem, ordines immanissimè sævit. Occupata Zutphania inermes homines, quibus Turca pepercisset, ad pedes suspendit, pueros mulieresque, in quibus necandis carnificum manus obtorpuerant, in glaciem præterfluentis Isulæ magnis copiis detrusit. Nardenum obsequio suo deditum inaudita carnificina laceravit, cives in templum vocatos miserrimè omnes trucidavit; liberos matrésque mutuis complexibus hærentes confodit. Harlemum fidem ejus implorantem ferro, fame, omni diritate exhausit. Ejusdem disciplina imbuti Requesenius, Johannes Austriacus, Parmensis, Mendoza, Spinola, alii ex crudelitatis ejus ludo discipuli, universum Belgium fluminibus sanguinis inundârunt.
units.tr: LXI. Meanwhile the miserable lamentations of the Belgians, who fell for their altars, strike our ears. Who could ever embrace these calamities in a worthy speech? There the Spaniard, under the pretext of defending the Papist religion, used the opportunity of Gyges' ring and opened a path for himself to every most shameful deed. Castles were built everywhere in the commonwealths against the consent of the estates, and foreign garrisons were placed in them. Chains were fastened on the free people. The law of treason was harshly enforced, and accusations of every kind were completed. The most noble houses were overthrown by the interpretations of informers, and the wealthiest men were seized as plunder. Some were hanged on gallows without any trace of a tribunal, having never been heard. Through the Inquisitions, the freedom of speaking and hearing was taken away. In place of the estates, monstrous and bloodthirsty bishops of the Inquisition were installed. All magistrates were reduced to order, the courts were overturned, and the votes of the assemblies were abrogated in cities as well as provinces. Immunities and privileges were utterly abolished. The most select men from both Belgian orders, senatorial and equestrian, were destined for slaughter. Of the estates, princes, nobles and citizens, nothing was heard but exiles, proscriptions, edicts, prisons, chains and killings. Finally, guilt and innocence, sacred and profane, were held in no distinction. The leading roles in this drama were played by Alva, that mud macerated in blood, who, having received from the Pope a hat and a sword consecrated by papal prayers, entered Belgium with an army and raged so savagely that he boasted, without shame, that he had handed over eighteen thousand Belgians and six hundred to be slaughtered by the executioner. Perhaps even that boast stayed within the bounds of exaggeration. For what the Jesuit Possevinus did not blush to confess in his letter to the King of Poland is truly horrifying: that in Belgium and France, in a span of eleven years, five hundred thousand men were killed for professing the Evangelical religion. That Plutonian duke of Alva, a monster of a man, under the leadership of his son, voluntarily accepted Mechlin, and against the laws of war plundered it more than hostilely. He subjected the bodies of freeborn women to the lictors, and raged most savagely against every sex, age and rank. When he occupied Zutphen, he hanged unarmed men by their feet, even those whom the Turk would have spared. He thrust boys and women, whose executioners' hands had grown numb from killing them, with great force onto the ice of the island flowing past. He mangled Naarden, which had surrendered to his obedience, with unheard-of butchery, and he slaughtered all the citizens summoned into the church. He stabbed children and mothers clinging in mutual embrace. He drained Haarlem, which implored his good faith, with the sword, famine and every atrocity. Trained in his discipline, Requesens, John of Austria, Parma, Mendoza, Spinola and others, disciples of his cruel game, flooded all of Belgium with rivers of blood.

units.la: LXII. Ex Hispania revocat nos ad se iterum Gallia, in qua, tanquam palæstra publica, crebrò nimis Babylon illa laniatorum Martyrum spectacula exhibuit. Quantæ in Regno illo factæ sint fidelium strages, quantum Christiani sanguinis per summam crudelitatem dilapidatum, imperium Francisci, Henrici II. Valesiorum fratrum, in id unicè incumbentium, ut purioris religionis igniculos omnes extinguerent, testatur. Quid stragem Vassiacenam commemorem? Cùm duce Guisio, præsente & vidente fratre ejus, Cardinali Lotharingo, armata cohors in concionem inermem irruit, promiscuámque cœdem virorum, mulierum, infantum fecit. Quid bella inde consecuta, promiscuas cœdes, quarum summam nemo unquam colligat, enumerem? Quid anno sexagesimo secundo supra mille quingentos, frequentissimas turbas apud Senonenses, Cenomannos, Meldenses, Trecenses, Vindocinos, Andegavos, Turonenses? Quid circa annum sexagesimum nonum aliquot hominum millia ex omnibus Ordinibus ad defensionem Hierarchiæ, & Huguenotorum extirpationem se devoventia. quorum tanta rabies fuit, ut occisorum carnes dentibus lacerárint, frontem & ora cruore, in signum exercitì zeli sui Catholici, illeverint. Iverunt, sic Surius in Supplemento Naucleri scribit, inter alios ad decem mille, qui instructi zelo Divino, & ardentes amore justitiæ, prædia amppla, & egregios liberos reliquerunt. Christóque se devoventes propriis militárunt stipendiis, solo victu contenti : de reliquo nudi nudum Christum sequentes cum hac inscriptione: (Joh: xi. 16.) Eamus nos, & moriamur cum Christo. (rabiei suæ Cannibalicæ prætextum petentes ex illo Christi itinere, in quo ipsemet se Patri suo pro salute nostra victimam obtulit) Propositum illi habuerunt omni die tremendis (verè tremendis, adeóque cruentis & nefariis) adesse mysteriis, & Deiparam (truculentorum scilicet homicidarum futuram Advocatam, cujus alias φιλανθρωπίαν ita prædicant, ut in hoc affectu eam Christo ipsi anteponant) vespertino tempore solita Antiphona, Salve Regina, salutare. Itaque Divino magis, quàm humano auxilio freti, multa hæreticorum millia oppresserunt. Quid anno septuagesimo primo lanienam Araufionensem? Quid septuagesimi secundi noctem illam infandam, Vesperas plusquam Siculas, (Matutinas Bartholomæanas Genebrardus vocat) quarum ne nomen quidem nunc auditur, non præ horrore stantibus comis? Quid inde secuta quaquaversus per Galliam universam similia facinora? Apud Meldenses, Trecenses, Aurelios, Lugdunenses, Andegavos, Rotomagenses, Tholosanos. Et apud Burdigalenses instigante, inflammante Edmundo Augerio Jesuita? Triginta hominum millia intra paucos dies sic cæsa, virorum, mulierum, infantium. Sanguineos torrentes huc illuc in subjectum Sequanum dimanantes Lutetiani viderunt. quod alias nunquam; & re tam feliciter & ex voto gesta, à Papa Jubilæum indictum, & supplicationes frequentissimo populo, à Rege & universa aula habitæ sunt Præterea libens, quæ post Edictum illud Sacrosanctum Nannetense, cui innixam Pacem religiosam securam in æternum fore nequicquam sibi piæ castæque mentes promiserant, proximè superiore & nostra ætate ibi gesta sunt, geruntúrque adhuc; laudante utroque pollice Papa, qui Innocentii nomen & omen mentitur; quibus describendis & ad vivum depingendis non tam prolixos libros, quàm prolixos fletus & gemitus deberi, cum S. Augustino Epist. 122. dicimus. Laborabit apud posteritatem ex vero tradentium fides: & sanctissimi quique in patientia animas suas possident.
units.tr: LXII. Gaul now calls us back again from Spain, where, as on a public arena, that Babylon all too often exhibited the spectacles of torn martyrs. How great were the massacres of the faithful in that kingdom, how much Christian blood was squandered through the utmost cruelty, the reigns of Francis and Henry II and of the Valois brothers testify, who devoted themselves wholly to extinguishing every spark of purer religion. Why should I recall the massacre at Vassy, when, under Duke Guise, in the presence and sight of his brother, Cardinal of Lorraine, an armed band rushed into an unarmed assembly and made a mixed slaughter of men, women and infants? Why should I list the wars that followed, the mixed killings whose total no one has ever gathered? Why the very frequent tumults in the year 1562, among the people of Sens, Le Mans, Meaux, Troyes, Vendôme, Angers and Tours? Why about the year 1569, when several thousand men of all ranks devoted themselves to the defence of the hierarchy and the extermination of the Huguenots, with such rage that they tore the flesh of the slain with their teeth and smeared their foreheads and faces with blood, as a sign of their Catholic zeal? They went, thus Surius writes in the Supplement to Naucler, among others about ten thousand who, armed with divine zeal and burning with love of justice, left behind ample estates and distinguished children. Devoting themselves to Christ, they served at their own expense, content with bare sustenance alone; thereafter, naked, following naked Christ, with this inscription: (John 11:16) Let us go too, and die with Christ. (seeking a pretext for their cannibal rage from that journey of Christ, in which he himself offered himself as a victim to his Father for our salvation) They made it their purpose to be present every day at the tremendous (truly tremendous, and so bloody and wicked) mysteries, and to greet the Mother of God (the future advocate, that is, of murderous butchers, whose love of humankind they proclaim in such a way that they place her even before Christ himself in this affection) at evening time with the customary antiphon, Hail Queen. Therefore, trusting more in divine than in human help, they overwhelmed many thousands of heretics. Why the Orange massacre of the year 1571? Why that unspeakable night of 1572, the Sicilian Vespers and more, which Genebrard calls the Matins of Bartholomew, whose very name is not now heard without hair standing on end in horror? What similar crimes followed from it everywhere throughout all of France? At Meaux, Troyes, Orléans, Lyon, Angers, Rouen and Toulouse, and at Bordeaux, at the instigation and inflaming of the Jesuit Edmund Auger, thirty thousand men, women and infants were slain within a few days. The Parisians saw streams of blood flowing hither and thither into the Seine below, as never before. And since the thing had been accomplished so happily and according to their wish, a jubilee was proclaimed by the Pope, and thanksgiving services were held by the king and the whole court, with a very large crowd. Moreover, I gladly pass over what has been done there since the sacrosanct Edict of Nantes, on which pious and chaste minds had vainly promised themselves that the religious peace would stand secure forever. What is done there even now, in our own time and the age just before, is applauded with both thumbs by the Pope, who falsely bears the name and omen of Innocent. To describe these things and paint them to the life, we say with St Augustine (Epist. 122) that they deserve not so much long books as long tears and groans. The faith of those who report them from the truth will suffer before posterity; and the most holy souls possess their own souls in patience.

units.la: LXIII. Ad finitimam Galliæ Sabaudiam Italiámque nos convertamus. Confederat Waldensium pars in vallibus ejus Alpinis, religionem orthodoxam constantissimè retinentes. Itaque verba sunt apud Thuanum lib. xxvii. sub ducatu Trinitarii, ei negotio à Sabaudo præfecti, Pontifici ac cæteris Italiæ Principibus ac civitatibus firmum ratumque fuit, Waldensium gentem ad internecionem delere. Nihil omissum, quo tam Romano-Catholicum decretum ad finem perduceretur; bellúmque adeò gestum anno sexagesimo superioris Seculi. Primo impetu sævitum in Meanenses, Arquenses, Meronenses ac Sufionenses. Direptis eorum bonis, pars extremo supplicio affecti; amplius sexaginta ad triremes damnati; alii supplicii metu, ejecrata, quam profitebantur, religione, periculum evaserunt. Truchesius explicatis signis, & tympanis adhibitis, Reuclaretum vicum sibi subditum nec opinato aggreditur. quo visouxores puerísque in montem vicinum, nivibus opertum per avia enituntur, majorem partem nudi. ubi per tres continuas noctes manere coacti, frigore pœne exanimati fuerunt. Pastor cum Sammartineo quodam vicano ignibus traditus est: direptæ vicanorum ædes; denique superstites Romanæ Ecclesiæ obedientiam jurare adacti sunt. Anno sequente Hispani Tagliaretum ineunt, & occupato loco viros ac mulieres, cum infantibus
units.tr: LXIII. Let us turn to Savoy, which borders France, and to Italy. A part of the Waldenses, who hold the orthodox religion most steadfastly, lives in the Alpine valleys of Savoy. Thus Thuanus reports in book xxvii., that under the leadership of a Trinitarian, a man appointed to the task by the Duke of Savoy, it was resolved and settled by the Pope and the other princes and cities of Italy to wipe out the Waldensian people completely. Nothing was left undone that might bring this decree of the Roman Catholics to its end, and so the war was waged in the sixtieth year of the last century. At the first assault they raged against the people of Meane, Arquenne, Meroune and Sufiane. Their goods were plundered, some were put to death with the utmost cruelty, more than sixty were condemned to the galleys, and others, through fear of punishment, escaped the danger by renouncing the religion they professed. Truchès, having unfurled his banners and sounded the drums, fell upon the village of Reuclaret, which was under his rule, when no one expected it. The wives and children there fled over pathless ways to a neighbouring mountain covered with snow, most of them naked. Kept there for three continuous nights, they were almost frozen to death by the cold. The minister was handed over to the flames together with a certain villager of Sammartin; the villagers' houses were plundered; finally, the survivors were forced to swear obedience to the Roman Church. The following year the Spaniards entered Tagliaret, and having seized the place, they slaughtered the men and women, together with the infants, who had been caught in their hiding places.

units.la: Papa & Italia Principum, Sabaudi interprimis novi adversus Waldenses furores, Lanienam, Valles Telliname, & pera Pedemontana horribilis. in cubilibus deprehensos ad internecionem delent. In Angronia hominis sexaginta circiter annos nati manibus post tergum revinctis, ad scamnum alligati, umbilico scarabeus admotus est testa tectus, qui fodicare ac rodere nunquam desiit, donec in alvum penetravit, atque ita miserum truculento & inaudito mortis genere enecnit. Ludus tamen & jocus forte isthaec fuerunt prae iis, quae praesenti Seculo in Pedemontii vallibus per innumeras & inauditas suppliciorum formas, adversus miseros Christi agnos patrata, documentorum haud dubiorum fides prodidit. ex quibus nonnulla Historia Papatus ff. ccLxv. ccLxvi. excerpsimus. Atque dum haec scribo, horrenda iisdem tempestas, a Vice-Deo illo Romano conflata, & radices eorundem, nisi Deus ἀπὸ μηχανῆς affulserit, consumptura imminet. clamantibus in Coelo sub altari defunctorum animabus: Quousque, o Domine, Sancte & verax, non vindicas sanguinem nostrum ab habitatoribus terrae! Ad Italicas etiam persecutiones laniena in primis horribilis, in Valle Telina hoc Seculo instituta pertinet. quam ibidem ff. ccxxix. perstrinximus.
units.tr: The Pope and the princes of Italy, and especially the new fury of the Savoyard against the Waldenses, made the slaughter in the valleys of Telline and the Pedemontane region horrible. In Angrogna, a man of about sixty years of age had his hands bound behind his back and was tied to a bench; a beetle, covered with a shell, was set against his navel, and it never ceased to gnaw and bore until it had penetrated his belly, and so the wretched man was killed by a savage and unheard-of kind of death. Yet these things were perhaps mere sport and jest compared with what was done in the present century in the valleys of Piedmont, by innumerable and unheard-of forms of torture against the wretched lambs of Christ; the trustworthiness of undoubted records has made this known. From these we have excerpted some in the History of the Papacy, pages 265 and 266. And while I am writing this, a dreadful storm, raised by that Roman Vicar of God, threatens to consume their roots as well, unless God shall appear as a god from the machine, while the souls of the dead cry out under the altar in heaven: How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not avenge our blood on the inhabitants of the earth? The slaughter in the Valtelline, carried out in this century, is also especially terrible among the Italian persecutions; I have touched on it in the same work, pages 229.

units.la: LXIV. In Germania Religiosa Pax Passavii A. C. M. D. LII. constituta, & trienni post Augustae, Deo teste, solenniter firmata est. Quam vero Pacificatio illa, absque qua fuisset, fluctuans illa Germaniae navis periisset priden, Hierarchicis sudes in oculis fuit, atque etiam num est? Clamant ergo & coaxant Ranae Aegyptiacae, vi extortam esse, irrita porro esse, quae per seditionem expresseris: (cum tamen temporis illius historiae omnia alia loquantur) haereticis datam fidem servandam non esse; & si qua cum iis conventione implicatus quis fuerit, eum aut ipso jure teneri: aut ad majorem cautelam haud difficulter a Romane Sedis Praetore restitutionem in integrum, seu absolutiotionem impetraturum. Nimirum etsi, Livio lib. IX. 9. æquo judice tam sponsiones, quàm fœdera sancta sunt apud eos homines, apud quos juxta Divinas religiones fides humana colitur; apud ipsos tamen religionis, & quidem Christianæ Antistites fidem per scelus abrumpere, laudi etiam ducitur. Sed per scelus abrumpi, negat Melchior Clesclius, Episcopus & Consiliarius Cæsareus in Scripto ad Archiducem Matthiam, quia, inquit, lux & tenebræ inter se conciliari non possunt: veritas cum mendacio: Pharisæi & Scribæ cum Christo. Talis ergo promissio pacis hæreticis facta, ipso jure nulla est. Quomodo etiam Hosius Cardinalis Epist. 193. 202. 220. Henricum Regem Poloniæ hortatur, ne unquam patiatur, ulla se ratione ad ea, quæ promiserit hæreticis, præstanda teneri: quia juramentum vinculum iniquitatis esse non debeat. Quasi scilicet Religionis pax id spectet, ut lux cum tenebris commisceatur, cum Christo Pharisæi, cum veritate mendacium jungatur; & non potius id sibi velit, ut quisque suo sensu abundans res suas sibi habeat; in religionis negotio nemo alterum interturbet: fruantur tenebris tenebricosi, luce lucidi (quanquam omnes, juxta Varronem sibi videntur sapere, nulli copreæ) cæteroquin cum omnibus hominibus pacem habeant; cujusmodi pacem, qui vinculum iniquitatis vocant, adeóque diversum in religione sentientes igne ferróque exterminandos judicant, næ illi fundamentum humanæ societatis ab imo labefactant. Nam humani juris, sic rectè Tertullianus ad Scopul. cap. 2. censet, & naturalis potestatis est, unicuique quod putaverit colere: nec alii obest aut prodest alterius religio. Sed nec religionis est religionem cogere, quæ sponte suscipi debeat, non vi: cùm hostiæ ab animo libenti exponi debeant. Adde, quòd Hierarchici Judæis, quamvis ut mulentur.
units.tr: LXIV. In Germany the religious peace was established at Passau in the year 1552, and three years later at Augsburg it was solemnly confirmed, God being witness. But that peace, without which the tottering ship of Germany would have perished the day before, has been and still is an eyesore to the hierarchs. So the Egyptian frogs croak and cry out that it was extorted by force, and that what was wrung out by sedition is void, although all the other records of that time say otherwise; that faith given to heretics need not be kept; and that anyone who has been bound by any agreement with them is either bound by law itself, or, for greater caution, will not find it difficult to obtain from the praetor of the Roman See restitution to its former state, or absolution. Certainly, although, according to Livy book IX. 9, by the fair judgement of ... both promises and treaties are held sacred among those men among whom human faith is honoured in accordance with divine religions, yet among these very bishops of religion, and indeed Christian ones, to break faith by crime is counted a glory. But that a faith broken by crime is not so, Melchior Clesclius, bishop and imperial councillor, denies in his writing to Archduke Matthias: because, he says, light and darkness cannot be reconciled; truth with falsehood; the Pharisees and scribes with Christ. Therefore a promise of peace made to heretics is in law itself null. So too Cardinal Hosius, in his letters 193, 202, 220, urges King Henry of Poland never to allow himself to be held, in any way, to perform what he has promised to heretics, because an oath ought not to be a bond of iniquity. As if, forsooth, the peace of religion aimed at this, that light should be mingled with darkness, the Pharisees joined with Christ, falsehood added to truth; and not rather that it should wish this, that each person, abounding in his own sense, should keep his own affairs to himself, and in matters of religion no one should disturb another: let those who dwell in darkness enjoy darkness, and those in the light enjoy light (although, as Varro says, everyone seems to himself wise, and no one is a fool to himself), and otherwise let them have peace with all men. Those who call such peace a bond of iniquity, and therefore judge that those who think differently in religion must be exterminated by fire and sword, undermine from the foundations the foundation of human society. For, as Tertullian rightly holds in his Scorpiace, chapter 2, it is a matter of human right and of natural power that each man should worship what he thinks fit; nor does one man's religion harm or help another. Nor is it of religion to compel religion, which ought to be undertaken voluntarily, not by force, since sacrifices ought to be offered with a willing mind. Add to this that the hierarchs grant the Jews, although they differ from them in their whole kind of religion, the power of keeping their faith, of living among them, and of enjoying the institutions of their religion with the greatest freedom, so that they may be changed.

units.la: c c 2 toto religionis genere discrepantibus, & fidem fervanti & secum commorandi, suaeque Religionis institutis summa cum libertate fruendi, potestatem faciunt; licet olim apud Pachimerem, Hist. lib. iii. 5. Orientales Ecclesiæ cum crucis Christi hostibus pacem facere nefas duxerint. cùm tamen Protestantes pro ἀσυγχύτοις haberi nequeant. Jam ergo fœdifragum hominum Punicorum consilium Romanam ablegandum fuerit, ubi loci tam exulat honestas, ut homines perjuri, sicarii, parricidæ, incendiarii, veneficii artifices, Papalis Regni instrumenta habeantur: ipse quinimo Papa & se ipsum, & alios quoscunque jurisjurandi religione solvendi potestatem sibi sumat. Quomodo Guicciardinus scriptor prudens & verax Histor. lib. viii. narrat, proprium id censeri Pontificum, non curare promissa: esseque statutum, ut Ecclesia, nullo contractu, promissione, adepto beneficio, possit retractare obligationes, & contra eas discerte etiam venire, quas peregerint Prælati solenniter. ita ut minùs tuto cum Papa, quàm cum Turca fœdus iniri possit. Adeò Romana fides, qua olim nihil tutius fuit, jamdudum in Punicam degeneravit. Sed hæc παρέργως ἰδίᾳ. nec tamen extra oleas planè.
units.tr: Although in former times, according to Pachymeres, Histories book iii. 5, the Eastern Churches thought it wicked to make peace with the enemies of the cross of Christ, since the Protestants cannot be regarded as unconfused [ἀσυγχύτοις], yet now the faithless counsel of the Punic men must be sent back to Rome, where honesty is so exiled that perjurers, assassins, parricides, incendiaries and makers of poisons are regarded as the tools of the Papal kingdom. Indeed the Pope himself claims for himself the power of loosing both himself and all others from the bond of an oath. As the prudent and truthful writer Guicciardini relates in his History, book viii., it is considered a peculiar trait of the Pontiffs not to care for promises; and it is established that the Church, by no contract, promise or benefit obtained, may retract its obligations, and may expressly go against those things which prelates have solemnly performed. So that a treaty can be made with the Pope less safely than with the Turk. So far has the Roman faith, which once was nothing more trustworthy, long since degenerated into Punic faith. But these things are said in passing, on a private matter [παρέργως ἰδίᾳ], and yet not altogether beside the point.

units.la: LXV. Hoc ergo impunè violandæ fidei principio freti Hierarchici vineas pluréofque admoverunt omnes, ut Religiosæ pacis semel placitæ & constitutæ soluto nexu, puriorem religionem Germania, Bohemia, Hungaria, Polonia, Austria, Silefia, Moravia, omnem exturbarent, & confessores orthodoxos omne genus supplicii involverent. Exorta hinc sunt in Germania funestissimum tricennale bellum, à Jesuitis in conscientia Imperatoris regnantibus, incensum, Papæ subsidiis & continua instigatione sævum in modum continuatum, & ægrè tandem nova Pacificatione Monasteriensi, cui Papæ Innocentii X. authoritate Fabius Chisius, Apostolicus Nuntius, post & ipsê Alexandri VII. nomine Papa, solenni Protestatione & plumbea Bulla, non aliam ob causam, quàm quòd Pacè ea pupillam oculi sui feriri, & ventrem, cujus quæsitissimus in Romana curia sensus est, tangi Papa exiltimasset, sic acerimè oppositum: sopitum: in Bohemia post abrogatam Evangelicis libertatem, quam iis paulo ante Rodolphus Imperator ob compertam fidelitatem concesserat, & literis Majestaticis sanxerat; post horrendas turbas, decussa Magnatum capita, & cuncta ferro flammáque vastata, extremum fidelium Unitatis fratrum dictorum, & Ecclesiarum orthodoxarum excidium, nova arte, quam dictam insignire placuit, post sanguinis innocentis effusiones Cainiticas, vivicomburia Huffitica & Hieronymiana, præcipitationes in fodinas Cuttenbergenses parùm hactenus proficientes, inventa, & abipso μωρίων suggesta, procuratum: in Hungaria post appetitam continuis insidiis Religiosam Pacem, quæ BotsKajum inter & Rodolphum A. C. M. D. C. VI. coluit, bella concatenata, persecutiones & vexationes fidelium, eorum inprimis, qui Ecclesiis præerant, plus quàm Scythicæ, quæ singula in Historia Papatus copiosius tradita narrare hèic supersedemus. In Polonia Pax Religiosa ab Henrico Rege A. C. M. D. LXXII. coepta, à successore Stephano Batorco, dicere solito, nolle se conscientiis dominari. quia Deus tria isthæc, creare ex nihilo, futura prænôsse, & conscientiis dominari, ceu eximia sibi reservaverit, confirmata non ita tranquillitatem Regni sustinuit hactenus, quò minùs majorem ac Minorem Poloniam & Lithuaniam turbæ ob religionem à Jesuitis maximè concitatæ perpetim infestarent. Posnoniæ Jesuita Piasecius his verbis ad incendenda Evangelicorum Templa A.M. D. C.V. plebem stimulavit: non vult Magistratus, non vult Curia Urbis. Tu igitur quisquis es è vulgo, haereticorum lustra in fumum & cinerem redige. Cleri in Polonia, Lithuania, Moravia &c. impia molimina, & exercitae crudelitatis specimina non pauca, Adrianum Regenvolscium in Systemate Historico-Chronologico Ecclesiarum Sclavonicarum Libro II. cap. II. 12. &c. prosequentem consulas licet.
units.tr: LXV. Therefore, relying on this principle of violating faith with impunity, the hierarchs have brought up all their vines and their many supporters, so that, once the religious peace had been agreed and established, the bond being loosed, they might drive out the purer religion from Germany, Bohemia, Hungary, Poland, Austria, Silesia and Moravia, and subject the orthodox confessors to every kind of punishment. From this arose in Germany the most deadly Thirty Years' War, kindled by the Jesuits who ruled in the emperor's conscience, and kept going in a savage manner by the Pope's subsidies and constant incitement; and it was with difficulty ended by the new Peace of Münster, against which, by the authority of Pope Innocent X, Fabio Chigi, the apostolic nuncio, and afterwards Pope Alexander VII himself, protested with a solemn protest and a leaden bull; and for no other reason than that the Pope judged that the pupil of his eye would be struck by that peace, and his belly, whose most exquisite sense is in the Roman court, would be touched. Thus it was violently opposed and quieted. In Bohemia, after the liberty granted to the Evangelicals had been abolished, a liberty which Emperor Rudolf had shortly before granted them for their proven loyalty and confirmed by royal letters, and after dreadful disturbances, the heads of the magnates were struck off and everything was laid waste with fire and sword, the final destruction of the faithful called Brethren of the Unity and of the orthodox churches was brought about by a new device, which they have been pleased to call dictam; it was devised and suggested by the fools [μωρίων] themselves, after the shedding of innocent blood in the manner of Cain, the burnings of Hus and Jerome, and the casting down into the Kuttenberg mines, which have so far achieved little. In Hungary, after the religious peace, which was maintained between Bocskai and Rudolf in the year 1606, had been sought with continual ambushes, there followed chained wars, and persecutions and vexations of the faithful, especially of those who presided over the churches, more than Scythian in their cruelty; these I shall not here stop to narrate, since they are handed down more fully in the History of the Papacy. In Poland, the religious peace begun by King Henry in the year 1573 and confirmed by his successor Stephen Báthory, who used to say that he did not wish to rule over consciences, since God had reserved to himself these three things, to create out of nothing, to foreknow the future, and to rule over consciences, as his special prerogatives, has not so far sustained the tranquillity of the kingdom; so that Greater and Lesser Poland and Lithuania have been continually harassed by disturbances about religion, chiefly stirred up by the Jesuits. At Posen, in the year 1605, the Jesuit Piasecki stirred up the common people to burn the Evangelical temples with these words: The magistrate does not wish it, the city council does not wish it. You, therefore, whoever you are, of the common people, reduce the dens of heretics to smoke and ashes. You may consult Adrian Regenvolscius, who in his Historico-Chronological System of the Slavonic Churches, book II, chapter II, 12 and following, pursues the impious devices of the clergy in Poland, Lithuania, Moravia and elsewhere, and their not few specimens of practised cruelty.

units.la: LXVI. Haec omnia, & longè plura etiam, incentoribus Pontificibus Romanis, tanta crudelitatis exercendae libidine flagrantibus, ut uno etiam ictu, si vires ipsis suae satis placerent, Ecclesiae Orthodoxae fauces incisuri sint, gesta, & Jesuitis, daemoniacis illis spiritibus, furoris Papalis suscruptoribus & satellitibus patrata esse, ne ipsa quidem impudentia inficias iverit. Haec enim Lojolae Patriarchae sui militari sanguine creta parricidalis gens, relictis Scholarum & Templorum Cathedris novo planè ausu aulas invasit, Regum negotiis se immiscuit, & eorum munimento insistens, omni potentiae suae malis artibus quaesitae conatu, inde à primo ortu suo in id unicè enitur hactenus, ut exturbata religione puriore, Sathanae regnum post-liminio ubique terrarum restituat. Hi nefarii scelerum machinatores, quicquid est bellorum inde à plus quàm centum annis in Europa gestorum, suis artibus genuerunt, aluerunt, & in detrimentum religionis confecerunt. Hi pacem religioni dandam dissuaserunt, datam omni virium contentione oppugnârunt; eam scelerata conjurationis, Scythicae barbarorum confoederationis, Diabolici Politicorum inventi probrosis nominibus traduxerunt; Principes suapte indole haud immites, nec planè malos, objecta religionis commentitiæ larva efferárunt. Hi flagrante bello Turcico, in conspectu hostium, nobilissimas Hungarici Regni Provincias turbárunt; Christianorum castra metu & diffidentia repleverunt; gladios in Scytham distrinctos jugulis fidelium intentárunt; & metu Turcæ liberatos eosdem mutuis odiis, dissensionibus, vexationibus distrinxerunt. Hi Transylvaniam, Silesiam, Moraviam gravissimis contentionibus & motibus concusserunt; Livoniam & Borussiam afflixerunt; Poloniam civilibus bellis distraxerunt; Moscoviam, personati Regis imperio lacerárunt; Sueciam legitimis Regni hæredibus exuerunt; Venetos gravi bello implicárunt; laudatissimæ Anglorum Reginæ Elisabethæ coædem haud semel spirárunt; Henrici III. & IV. Galliæ Regum jugulum per nefarios & conducticios sicarios appetierunt; Jacobo Magnæ Britanniæ Regi, Regiæ ejusdem familiæ, & Nobilitati totius Regni flori exitium per tormentarium pulverem machinati sunt; fortissimum Auraicum Principem per disciplinæ suæ alumnum trucidárunt; denique sua parricidia, perjuria, proditiones, aliáque inhumanæ crudelitatis facinora, Catholici zeli prætextu, impunè usque perpetrant; pedibus suis ad maleficium currunt, properantes, ut sanguinem innocentium fundant; cogitationes (eorum) malitiosæ sunt; pernicies & calamitas in semitis eorum, Esaj. LIX. 7.
units.tr: LXVI. All these things, and far more besides, were done by the Jesuits, those demonic spirits and henchmen who stoke the fury of the Papacy, while the Roman Pontiffs incite them, burning with such lust to exercise cruelty that they would cut the throat of the Orthodox Church with a single blow if their own strength were equal to it. Not even their shamelessness can deny this. For this parricidal breed, born of the military blood of their patriarch Loyola, abandoned the chairs of schools and churches, invaded the courts of kings with a truly novel boldness, meddled in the affairs of kings, and, relying on that stronghold, has strained with every evil art to gain power. From its very beginning until now it has aimed solely at this: that, with the purer religion driven out, the kingdom of Satan may be restored everywhere on earth by right of return. These wicked machinators of crime have produced, fostered and carried out, by their arts, whatever wars have been waged in Europe for more than a hundred years, to the detriment of religion. They have advised against giving peace to religion, and with all their might have opposed it where it was granted. They have branded it with disgraceful names, calling it "a wicked conspiracy, a Scythian confederation of barbarians, a diabolical invention of the politicians." They have stirred up princes who were by nature neither cruel nor wholly bad, using the mask of a feigned religion. In the midst of the Turkish war, in sight of the enemy, they threw the most noble provinces of the Kingdom of Hungary into confusion; they filled the Christian camps with fear and distrust; they aimed swords drawn against the Scythian at the throats of the faithful; and, when these were freed from fear of the Turk, they set them at odds with mutual hatreds, dissensions and vexations. They have shaken Transylvania, Silesia and Moravia with the gravest conflicts and disturbances; they have afflicted Livonia and Prussia; they have torn Poland apart with civil wars; they have lacerated Muscovy under the rule of a counterfeit king; they have stripped Sweden of its lawful heirs; they have entangled the Venetians in a grave war; more than once they breathed their plots against the most praised Queen Elizabeth of England; they have sought the throats of the kings of France, Henry III and Henry IV, through wicked hired assassins; they have contrived, by gunpowder, the destruction of James, King of Great Britain, of his royal family and of the flower of the nobility of the whole kingdom; they have murdered the most courageous Prince of Orange through a pupil of their own discipline; finally, their murders, perjuries, betrayals and other deeds of inhuman cruelty they still commit with impunity under the pretext of Catholic zeal: their feet run to evil, they hurry to shed innocent blood; their thoughts are wicked; ruin and calamity are in their paths, Isaiah LIX. 7.

units.la: LXVII. Atque his modis Hierarchici hactenus Oc- cidentem infestum exercitumque habuerunt.
units.tr: LXVII. In these ways the hierarchy has hitherto infested and harassed the West.

units.la: Non minor eorum rabies in Orientem despumavit. Quis dubitet, ipsam naturam obstupuisse, cùm feritas Iberica, Archi-Bileami maledictione subnixa, tam horribilem innocentissimorum hominum in America, speciosò propagandæ Christianæ religionis titulo, stragem fecisset? Etenim ex oculatorum, co-
units.tr: Their rage has boiled over no less against the East. Who could doubt that nature herself was stunned when Iberian savagery, relying on the curse of Balaam the Archer, carried out such a dreadful slaughter of most innocent men in America under the specious title of propagating the Christian religion? For from the reports of eyewitnesses,

units.la: Crudelitas Hierarchicorum in Orientem despumans, velut ad versus Americanos, quos prætextu, venientes ad rúmque Pontificiorum testium, Bartholomæi Casæ & Hieronimi Benzonis, fide dignis relationibus didicimus, ab Hispanis à Clero suo modum propagandi apud Indos Papatus edostis, extrustas passim arces, veluti libertatis compedes ac domitarum gentium frœnos: conditas colonias, ut sedem servitutis: pulsos domibus, exturbatos agris, inter vilissima mancipia habitos, laboribus asininis attritos, opibus omnibus exhaustos indigenas: canibus ad ludicrum oblestamentum objestos in escam: protritos equis: variis & portentosis carnisicinis, antea nec visis, nec auditis, infinita hominum millia sublata: quin & Reges contra dignitatem tractatos, solio soloque pulsos, imò plusquam Cerberea crudelitate, post infinitam vim auri quasi pro vita extortam; alios elisis intorto laqueo faucibus necatos: alios lento igne per summum cruciatum ustulatos: atque adeò nullam usquam illius terræ partem, nisi cruentam & maculatam, aut, ut ipsi prædicant, emendatam, correstam, religiosiorem cultiorémque redditam. Nam quæ alii scelera, hi remedia vocant: dum falsis nominibus severitatem pro sævitia, supplicia & contumelias disciplinam appellant. Cùm Rex Peruanus Attabaliba (sic Benzo lib. iii. 3. narrat) Breviarium, quod ei Vincentius ex familia Prædicatorum Monachus obtulerat, saucius dolore ob acceptum recens de terris ejus à Papa Hispano donatis nuntium, justa indignatione commotus, ceu rem sibi incognitam in terram abjicere:, mox Monachus ille ad Hispanos suos Evangelistas novos conversus exclamavit: Adeste Christiani, adeste Christiani, ulciscimini scelus. Evangelia contemnuntur, & pedibus calcantur. Cædite canes, cædite canes, cædite. Contumeliosè enim verbum Dei tractárunt. Hic Pantaleon Theveninus exclamaret merito: O Evangelium pistolicum! Sic intra quadraginta quinque annorum spatium, & quod paulùm excedit, plus quàm ducenties centena milliaHispanos, Monachis directoribus, mactasse, Historicus refert. Adeo atrocitatis hujus exempla eodem Benzone Hist. lib. iii. 21. teste, absurdam Peruanis de Christiano nomine, & ad religionis Christianæ dedecus pertinentem opinionem impresserunt, ut Christianos minimè, sicut Monachi Hispani alternis prope verbis jactaverant, Dei filios esse, sibi persuadeant; sed ne sic quidem in lucem editos, ut vulgò nasci homines solent. Fieri enim non posse, ut tam ferox & truculentum animal ab ullo homine genitum, & fœminæ partu editum sit. Itaque penitus hæc eorum animis opinio insedit, Christianos purgamenta quædam maris, & monstra ex barbari elementi spumis concreta ejectáque (Viracochias ex ea vocant) venisse in terras ad vastandum perdendúmque mundum. Denique mare diris Indi insectantur, quòd tam sævam ac truculentam sobolem in terram immiserit. Imò repertum esse Casa narrat, qui cùm è servitutis fuga retraheretur ad supplicium, & à Monacho Franciscano de mox consequendis, si Christianus fieret, æternæ beatitudinis præmiis, sin minùs, æternæ damnationis suppliciis, moneretur; cúmque Hispanis quoque Regnum Cœlorum patere percontanti responsum esset, Cælum nolle se petere dixerit, sed potiùs inferos, ne sibi cum adeò crudeli gente commune domicilium esset.
units.tr: The cruelty of the hierarchy, boiling over towards the East, as against the Americans, we have learned from trustworthy accounts of the Papist witnesses Bartolomé de las Casas and Girolamo Benzoni, how the Spaniards, taught by their clergy the manner of spreading Papacy among the Indians, raised fortresses everywhere, like fetters of liberty and bridles of subdued peoples; founded colonies as seats of slavery; drove the natives from their homes and out of their fields, treated them as the vilest slaves, wore them down with asses' labours, and drained them of all their resources; threw them as food to dogs for a sport-like entertainment; trampled them with horses; and, by various monstrous butcheries, never before seen or heard of, destroyed infinite thousands of men. Indeed, kings too were treated contrary to their dignity, driven from throne and soil, and, with a cruelty more than Cerberean, after an infinite amount of gold had been extorted, as it were, for their lives, some were strangled with a twisted noose, others were burned by a slow fire through the greatest torment. Thus no part of that land anywhere is left except bloodied and stained, or, as they themselves proclaim, "corrected," made more religious and more cultivated. For what others call crimes, these call remedies, while with false names they call severity cruelty, and punishments and insults discipline. When the Peruvian king Atahualpa (so Benzoni tells it, Book 3, ch. 3), wounded with grief at the recent news that his lands had been given by the Spanish Pope, and moved by just indignation, threw the Breviary that the monk Vincent of the Dominican order had offered him to the ground, as a thing unknown to him, that monk at once turned to his Spanish new evangelists and cried out: "Help, Christians, help, Christians, avenge the crime. The Gospels are scorned and trampled underfoot. Beat the dogs, beat the dogs, beat them. For they have treated the word of God insultingly." Here Pantaleon Thevenin rightly exclaimed: "O Gospel of the pistol!" So, the historian reports, within a span of forty-five years and a little more, the Spaniards, under the monks as directors, slaughtered more than twenty thousand times a hundred thousand. Benzoni, Hist. Book 3, ch. 21, attests that examples of this atrocity had so impressed on the Peruvians an absurd opinion about the Christian name, one that brought dishonour to the Christian religion, that they could not be persuaded that Christians were, as the Spanish monks had almost constantly boasted, "sons of God"; nor were they even thought to be born in the way men are usually born. For it could not be that so fierce and savage an animal had been begotten by any man and brought forth by a woman. Thus this opinion sank deep into their minds: that the Christians were certain filth of the sea and monsters formed from the foam of a barbarous element, cast ashore (for which reason they call them "Viracochias") to lay waste and destroy the world. Finally, the Indians curse the sea because it sent such a savage and cruel brood upon the land. Indeed, Casas tells of a man who, when he had been dragged back from flight into slavery to be punished, was warned by a Franciscan monk that, if he became a Christian, he would soon receive the rewards of eternal blessedness, but otherwise the torments of eternal damnation. When he asked whether the kingdom of heaven was open to the Spaniards too and received the answer yes, he said he did not want to seek heaven, "but rather hell, so that I would not have a common dwelling with a people so cruel."

units.la: LXVIII. Sed hæc in Oriente adversus Infideles & barbaros, non Sanctos & testes Jesu gesta sunt, fateor. Sed crudelitatem tamen incredibilem Mulieris hujus Sanguine humano se ingurgitantis nimiùm, clarè spirant. Neque iidem temperárunt sibi, quò minùs Orientis cardines, Christianæ religionis, seu potiùs Pontificiæ dominationis proferendæ specie, immaniter convellerent, & passim ima summis miscerent. Ex quo enim Euphrate siccato Ranæ illæ in Orientem, ipsa Regum Æthiopum Habessinorum, Japoniorum, Sinensium palatia penetrárunt, ut potentissima illa Regna Lusitanis, Hispanis, & per utrosque Pontificiæ sedi subjicerent, quot quæso ob Jesuitarum machinationes impias & conciones tribunitias, subditos ad seditionem & rebellionem adversus Superiores minùs sibi addiétos concitantium hominum; quot Christianorum in Habessinia, & in Japonia ac Sina tum advenarum, tum recens conversorum strages miserabiles factæ sunt? Nonnulla ex Celeberrimi Jobi Ludolphi, Varenii, Rejeri Gisberti, Caronii Commentariis excerpta Historiæ Papatus﻿. CXLII CXLIII. repræsentavimus. ex quibus velut ex fimbria vestimentum, seu potiùs Mulierem illam cocco & purpura indutam, Sanctorum aliorúmque, etiam Orientalium sanguine ebriam plane madentémque nullo negotio cognoscere licet.
units.tr: LXVIII. But these things, I admit, were done in the East against unbelievers and barbarians, not against the saints and witnesses of Jesus. Yet they clearly breathe an incredible cruelty of this Woman, too drunk with human blood. Nor have the same men restrained themselves from violently overturning the foundations of the East under the guise of spreading the Christian religion, or rather Papal dominion, and from mixing up high and low everywhere. For ever since the Euphrates was dried up, those frogs have penetrated into the very palaces of the kings of Ethiopia (the Abyssinians), of Japan and of China, to subject those most powerful kingdoms to the Portuguese and the Spanish, and through them to the Papal see. How many, I ask, of the wretched slaughters of Christians, both newcomers and recent converts, took place in Abyssinia, Japan and China because of the impious machinations of the Jesuits and their tribunician harangues, by which men inciting subjects, who were less devoted to them, to sedition and rebellion against their superiors? Some excerpts from the commentaries of the most celebrated Job Ludolf, Varenius, Gisbert Voetius and Caron we have set forth as a history of Papacy, CXLII, CXLIII. From these, as from the hem of a garment, or rather from that Woman clothed in scarlet and purple, drunk with the blood of the saints and of others, even of Orientals, and utterly dripping, one can recognize her without any difficulty.

units.la: LXIX. Supersedeo plura dicere. Quis enim finis, quis dicendi modus erit, si omnia colligere instituam? Si quæ ἐλως indicavi, exequar ἀνὰ μέρος. Si perfidiæ, feritatis, insolentiæ, grassationum omnium circumstantias colligam? Sufficient, quæ dixi, ut ex iis concludant pii omnes, Hierarchiam, non alium quenquam cœtum, esse Mulierem illam Meretricem, cocco purpuráque rubentem, & non tantùm sanguinem humanum fundentem, sed Sanctorum inprimis, & testium Jesu sanguine ebriam. Ubi enim tot tantáque immanitatis exempla extant? Liceat illa Petrarchæ ῥήσεις μάρτυρος longè nunc, quàm olim, veriora, certiora repetere. Quid siles? Aut aliam hoc sanguine ebriam mulierem ostende; aut omnino, si potes, te hanc ebriam nega. De qua mihi usurpare fas est illa, quæ de Romanis veteribus Justinus lib. xxxviii. 6. enuntiavit. Velut conditores Romæ lupæ uberibus alti, sic illi luporum animos, inexplebiles sanguinis atque imperii, perii, divitiarúmque avidos ac jejunos habent. Atque fas est eò magis, quòd nihil ab insanissimis immanissimisque Ethnicis cogitatum, auditum, visum esse, quod cum Papali isthac crudelitate comparari mereatur, pro certo constet.
units.tr: LXIX. I forbear to say more. For what end, what limit of speaking will there be, if I undertake to gather everything? If I have indicated the things briefly [ἐλως], I shall go through them part by part [ἀνὰ μέρος]. If I gather the circumstances of all the treachery, savagery, insolence and raids? What I have said will suffice, so that from these facts all the pious may conclude that the Hierarchy, and no other body whatsoever, is that Woman, the Harlot, red with scarlet and purple, who not only sheds human blood but is drunk above all with the blood of the saints and the witnesses of Jesus. For where do so many and so great examples of savagery exist? Let me repeat that saying of Petrarch's, the witness [ῥήσεις μάρτυρος], which is now much truer and more certain than it was once. Why are you silent? Either show me another woman drunk with this blood, or, if you can, deny altogether that this one is drunk. Of her I may fittingly borrow what Justin, Book 38, ch. 6, said of the ancient Romans: just as the founders of Rome, nurtured at a wolf's teats, so these have the minds of wolves, insatiable for blood and power, and hungry and greedy for plunder and riches. And I may do so all the more because it is certain that nothing thought, heard or seen among the most insane and most savage heathens deserves to be compared with this Papal cruelty.

units.la: LXX. Nam frustra profecto Bellarminus (ut hoc unum coronidis loco addam) de Rom. Pontif. lib. iii. 7. Hierarchiæ illam μαρτυροφονίαν, atque contractam indeBabylonicæ crudelitatis notam elevare & expungere his verbis conatur: Dicunt quidem hæretici, se magnam persecutionem ab Antichristo pati, quia interdum comburuntur aliqui de ipsorum numero. At quæ comparatio est talis persecutionis cum persecutione Neronis, Decii, Domitiani, Diocletiani & aliorum: siquidem pro uno hæreti-
units.tr: LXX. For Bellarmine, to add just one thing by way of a conclusion, clearly tries in vain in de Rom. Pontif. lib. iii. 7 to lift away and wipe out the Hierarchy's martyrophonia [μαρτυροφονίαν] and the mark of Babylonian cruelty fixed upon it, with these words: The heretics indeed say that they suffer a great persecution from Antichrist, because some of their number are sometimes burned. But what comparison is there between such a persecution and the persecutions of Nero, Decius, Domitian, Diocletian and others? For in former times a thousand Christians were put to death for one heretic who is burned, and this was carried out throughout the whole Roman world, not in one province alone. And although being burned alive is now the highest punishment, then the most incredible and most varied kinds of torture were practised, etc.

units.la: co, qui comburitur, mille Christiani olim interficiebantur, idque in toto orbe Romano exercebatur, non in una solum Provincia. Et cùm modò summa pœna sit comburi hominem: tunc incredibilia & diversissima tormentorum genera exercebantur &c. Scribit Damasus in vita Marcellini, supra xvii. millia Christianorum intra unum mensem à Diocletiano interfecta; & Eusebius, qui tum vivebat, scribit lib. viii. 6. adeò fuisse omnes carceres plenos Martyribus, ut nullus relinqueretur locus facinorosis. In toto verò orbe tot refert martyriis coronatos, ut impossibile sit numerum eorum inire. Adde, quòd multò plures Catholicorum hæretici nostri occiderunt his decem vel quindecim annis in Gallia & Flandria, quàm Inquisitores combusserint hæreticorum forte in centum annis. Itaque non possunt hanc appellare persecutionem, sed potiùs bellum civile. Namut Augustinus docet Epist. 80. ad Hesychium, quando erit vera persecutio Antichristi, solis Ecclesiæ filiis erit tribulatio, non autem eorum persecutoribus, sicut tempore Diocletiani & superiorum Principum Christiani solùm cædebantur, non autem cœdebant. Si verò persecutio est, Catholici potiùs eam patiuntur quàm Lutherani & Calvinista. Catholici enim sunt, qui ex multis provinciis ejecti, Ecclesias, patrimonia, & ipsam etiam patriam amiserunt, invadentibus nimirum res alienas novas istius Evangelii Ministris; & ut diximus, & ex Commentariis Laurentii Surii, aliísque hujus temporis historiis cognosci potest, multò plures Catholicorum furor Calvinistarum intra paucos annos absumpsit, quàm hæretici judicio Principum Catholicorum abnegatæ fidei pœnas dederint. Hactenus Bellarminus, Hierarchicorum hyperaspistes; sed eo ipso Hierarchiam esse Meretricem Babylonicam magis etiam prodens, quia imitata Meretricem illam propudiosam prov. xxx. 20. comedit, & deinde abstergit os suum, dicens: Non sum operata iniquitatem.
units.tr: Damasus writes in the life of Marcellinus that more than seventeen thousand Christians were slain by Diocletian within one month; and Eusebius, who was living at that time, writes in book 8, chapter 6, that the prisons were so full of martyrs that no room was left for criminals. Throughout the whole world he reports so many people crowned with martyrdom that it is impossible to count them. Add that our heretics have killed far more Catholics in France and Flanders in these ten or fifteen years than the Inquisitors have burned heretics in perhaps a hundred years. So they cannot call this a persecution, but rather a civil war. For as Augustine teaches in Epistle 80 to Hesychius, when the true persecution of Antichrist comes, tribulation will fall only on the sons of the Church and not on their persecutors, just as in the time of Diocletian and the earlier emperors only Christians were beaten, not beating others. If, however, it is a persecution, the Catholics suffer it rather than the Lutherans and Calvinists. For it is the Catholics who, driven out of many provinces, have lost their churches, their patrimonies and even their homeland itself, while the new ministers of this gospel, of course, invade their goods; and, as we have said, and as can be learned from the commentaries of Laurentius Surius and other histories of this time, the fury of the Calvinists has consumed far more Catholics within a few years than the heretics have paid the penalties of renounced faith by the judgment of Catholic princes. So far Bellarmine, the champion of the Hierarchists; but in the very act he reveals still more clearly that the Hierarchy is the Babylonian harlot, because, imitating that shameless harlot of Proverbs 30:20, he eats, and then wipes his mouth, saying: I have done no wickedness.

units.la: LXXI. Quicquid ergo ille προφᾶσηζόμενος fingat, causam certè non dicit, quin veterum Ethnicam cru- delitatem Papalis illa multis parasangis antecellat.
units.tr: LXXI. Whatever that man [προφασιζόμενος] pretends, he certainly does not show any reason why that Papal cruelty should not far surpass the cruelty of the ancient heathens by many leagues.

units.la: Nam præterquam quòd hæc & diuturnior fuit Ethnica, extracta immani sævitia inde à Gregorii VII. tempore, ex quo nunquam non sanguine Christianorum manus Pontificum destillârunt; per annos plus quàm sexcentos, & extrahenda forte per plures; cùm Ethnica non ultra trecentos duraverit: & magis continua, cùm vix ullum tempus à lanienis & mastationibus vacaverit & vacet adhuc; Gentilibus per intervalla & impetus fidèles divexantibus: & in animas potiùs quàm corpora, eorum scilicet, qui metu & vi sub jugo Papæ continentur, intentata; cùm Ethnica corporalis potiùs quàm spiritualis fuerit: & violentia pariter ac fraude instructissima, cùm Gentilium illa aperta tantùm & violenta fuerit: & à professis Christianis, imò ab illo, quem Bernhardus de Consid. ad Eugen.
units.tr: For, apart from the fact that this cruelty is also longer-lasting than the heathen one: it has been drawn out with monstrous savagery since the time of Gregory VII, from which time the hands of the Popes have never ceased to drip with Christian blood, for more than six hundred years, and perhaps for many more to come, whereas the heathen persecution lasted no more than three hundred years. It is also more continuous, since there has scarcely been any time free from slaughter and mangling, and there is none even now, while the Gentiles harassed the faithful only at intervals and in outbursts. It is aimed rather at souls than at bodies, namely of those who are held under the yoke of the Pope by fear and force, whereas the heathen persecution was rather bodily than spiritual. It is equally violent and fully equipped with fraud, whereas the heathen persecution was only open and violent. And it comes from professed Christians, indeed from him whom Bernard, in de Consideratione to Eugenius, calls a flatterer of the Church: primacy from Abel, government from Noah, patriarchate from Abraham, order from Melchizedek, dignity from Aaron, authority from Moses, judgment from Samuel, power from Peter, anointing from Christ.

units.la: Hierarchicorum persecutiones, etiam numero casorum & supplicium immanitate. gen. parasitabundus dicit esse primatu Abel, gubernatu Noe, Patriarchatu Abraham, ordine Melchisedec, dignitate Aaron, authoritate Mosen, judicatu Samuelem, potestate Petrum, unctione Christum; cui juxta Baronium in parænesi officium mactandi à Deo demandatum est, juxta illa Act. x. 13. Surge Petre, macta & manduca; adversus Christianos, quibus non aliud crimini dari potest, quàm illud ἵνα ἵνα solius Dei sequela; cùm gentiles nominis Christiani hostes se professi fuerint; etiam impar Martyrum sub Pontificibus & gentilibus numerus; & supplicia sub illis, quàm sub his longè graviora sævierunt. Etenim Diocletianus intra unum mensem septendecim Christianorum millia sustulit. quod ceu magnum quid Damasus retulit. Sustulit tamen in universo Imperio Romano. At in unica Gallia, olim Imperii Provincia A. C. M. D. LXXII. hominum cujusvis ætatis, utriusque sexus, intra paucissimos dies triginta millia. ut parcissimè loquar absumpta sunt. Nam numerum plurimùm augent alii. Supra quoque Posseuinum confitentem adduximus, quòd undecennii spatio in Gallia & Belgio quingenta hominum millia per causam religionis ceciderint. Nihil dicam de jactantia Albani; nihil de laniena Hibernica, Vallis Telinæ, Pedemontana supra alibique exposita. quibus innumerabilis hominum multitudo, cui parem gentiles nullam viderunt, ob solam religionem carnificum & sicariorum manu cæsa succubuit. Quin ipse Bellarminus de Notis Eccl. cap. ult. Albigensium centum millia uno die cæsa, tanquam rem præclarè gestam narrat. Neque etiam duriora Ethnicorum quàm Paparum supplicia fuerunt. Illorum enim usitatissima fuerunt cruces, gladius, lapicidinæ, catasta: horum vivicomburium, quod hæreticis, quos contumaces vocant, omnibus lege lata decreverunt. Gladii, undæ, laquei, triremes inter supplicia leviora & mitiora numerantur. Lentos ignes Papistæ habent eximios. quibus vix comparem nocturnas faces Ethnicorum. Et quo loco Hispanico-Romanam Inquisitionem, cujus nomen sine sacro & frigido horrore non auditur, lanienas, & in iis supplicia supra memorata recensebunt? An simile quid apud veteres extitit unquam?
units.tr: Hierarchicorum persecutiones surpass the heathen persecutions also in the number of those slain and in the enormity of the punishments. To him, according to Baronius in his exhortation, the duty of slaughter was committed by God, according to those words of Acts 10:13: Rise, Peter, kill and eat; and this against Christians, against whom no other charge can be brought than their following of God alone, whereas the heathens professed themselves enemies of the name of Christ. The number of martyrs under the Popes is no less than under the heathens, and the punishments raged far more severely under the former than under the latter. Diocletian, for example, put to death seventeen thousand Christians within a single month, which Damasus reported as something great. Yet he did this throughout the whole Roman empire. But in Gaul alone, formerly a province of the empire, in the year 1572, thirty thousand people of every age and both sexes were destroyed within a very few days, to speak most sparingly; for many others greatly increase the number. We have also cited above Possevino's admission that in the space of eleven years five hundred thousand people perished in France and Belgium for the sake of religion. I say nothing of the boasting of Alba, nothing of the Irish slaughter, nothing of the Valtelline and Piedmontese massacres described above and elsewhere, in which an innumerable multitude, whom the heathens never equalled, succumbed to the hand of executioners and assassins, slain for religion alone. Indeed Bellarmine himself, in de Notis Ecclesiae, last chapter, narrates the slaughter of a hundred thousand Albigensians in one day as a glorious deed. Nor were the punishments of the heathens harsher than those of the Popes. For the heathens' most common punishments were the cross, the sword, the quarries and the rack; the Popes' were burning alive, which by law they have decreed for all heretics whom they call obstinate. Swords, waves, nooses and galleys are counted among the lighter and milder punishments. The Papists have excellent slow fires, to which the heathens' nightly torches are hardly comparable. And where will those who recount the Spanish-Roman Inquisition, whose name is not heard without a sacred and chilling horror, recount its slaughters and, among them, the punishments mentioned above? Did anything similar ever exist among the ancients?

units.la: LXXII. Quod vero de bellis civilibus mussat & obloquitur Bellarminus, frigidum est. . Innumera enim supplicia de fidelibus extra bellum civile expetita esse, Martyrologia, & certissimæ narrationes aliæ testantur. An bella civilia erant, cum uti supra narravimus, & aliunde constat, in Anglia promiscuis cœdibus sæviisset Maria: cum in Vallibus, Gallia, applaudente Papâ Gregorio XIII. in Hibernia, Valle Telina subitò horrendum in modum, nulla belli legitimi solennitate vel specie invasi, oppressi, miserabiliter cæsi, & diristimè excruciati sunt? Profecto negabat Dux Albanus, cui Bellarminus lauream suam non debebat criipere, ut bonos oneraret. Nam homo ille μισάνθρωπος, vel ἀνάνθρωπος potiùs, pauculis annis in Belgio se authore & judice, carnificis manu, extra bellum civile, octodecim millia (triginta sex millia alii notant) periisse, ferocissimè impotentissimèque jactabat. An etiam nullius crudelitatis, tyrannidis, persecutionis crimine arcessi Antiochus Epiphanes, homo ex omnium scelerum colluvione natus, tetra & detestabilis bellua, potuit, quia post læsam diu patientiam, excarnificatos pios, tandem Machabæi cum ducibus ejus, Appollone, Serone, Gorgia aperto Marte, vim vi repellentes conflixerunt, & plures etiam internecione deleverunt? Et sane non ovum ovo similius est, quàm Epiphani Pontifices sunt. uti ex similitudine initii, progressus, indolis malignæ, & rerum gestarum proclive judicatu est. Ne dicam, Licinium & Maxentium inter persecutores Christianorum dirissimos non ideo non numerari, quia post sævitiam diu exercitam tandem Constantinus M de iisdem vindictam sumpsit, & partes eorum pessimè multavit. Persecutorem, crudelem, tyrannum causa injusta facit, sive in bello, sive extra illud innocentes is adoriatur, cruciet, occidat. Ad tyrannidem denique Papărum demonstrandam sufficit, quòd omnium tum Martyriorum, tum religiosorum bellorum, tum persecutionum religionis causa excitatarum qualiumcunque authores, faces, incentores soli sunt; atque legibus latis, & continuis ad sanguinariam earum executionem incitamentis, Christianum orbem, & Sanctos in eo ac testes Jesu cumprimis, turbis & incendiis perturbare, quin & ipsi strenuè belligerari non desinunt. Hi enim sunt, uti de Julio II. ejúsque clero quondam Budæus de Asse lib. 4. locutus est, Sancti illi liticines: hæc dira & portentosa vaecordia sacrosanctæ potestatis: hi animo plusquam gladiatorio ad Christiani nominis columen mundo stupente grassantur; à Marte sanguinariam frameam mutuati lanistæ sanguinarii, qui bellonæ sacris operantur. quales plures etiam Histor. Pap. ff. ccxciv. &c. sententia verbi Divini, vetustorum canonum, Gregorii M. nec non Erasmi & Wicelii verbis perstrinximus.
units.tr: LXXII. But what Bellarmine mutters and objects about civil wars is feeble. For that countless punishments were demanded against the faithful outside any civil war is attested by the Martyrologies and other most certain narratives. Or were these civil wars, when, as we have narrated above and it is clear from elsewhere, Mary raged in England with indiscriminate slaughters; when in the Valtelline, in France, in Ireland, with Pope Gregory XIII applauding, people were suddenly attacked and oppressed in a dreadful manner, without any formality or appearance of lawful war, miserably slaughtered and most horribly tortured? Certainly Duke Alba, whose laurel Bellarmine should not have snatched away, when he was burdening the good, denied it. For that man, inhuman [ἀνάνθρωπος] or rather misanthropic [μισάνθρωπος], boasted most fiercely and most unrestrainedly that in a few years in the Netherlands, under his authority and judgment, by the hand of the executioner, outside any civil war, eighteen thousand people had perished (others note thirty-six thousand). Or could Antiochus Epiphanes, a man born from the sewage of every crime, a foul and detestable beast, be exempted from the charge of any cruelty, tyranny or persecution, because after long suffering the pious had been tortured, and at last the Maccabees, with their leaders, fought openly in war, repelling force with force, and also destroyed many in slaughter, against Apollonius, Seron and Gorgias? And indeed the Popes are no more like Epiphanes than an egg is like an egg, as is easily judged from the similarity of their beginning, their progress, their malignant disposition and their deeds. Not to mention that Licinius and Maxentius are not therefore left uncounted among the most dreadful persecutors of Christians, because Constantine the Great at last took vengeance on them after long-practised savagery and punished their party most severely. A cruel tyrant makes a persecutor whenever he attacks, tortures or kills the innocent, whether in war or outside it, for an unjust cause. Finally, to demonstrate the tyranny of the Popes it is enough that they alone are the authors, torches and instigators of all the martyrdoms, all the religious wars, and all the persecutions of whatever kind stirred up for the sake of religion; and that, by laws enacted and continual incitements to their bloody execution, they never cease to disturb the Christian world, and the saints in it and especially the witnesses of Jesus, with tumults and fires, and even themselves to wage war vigorously. For these are, as Budé once said of Julius II and his clergy in de Asse, book 4, those holy trumpeters: this dreadful and monstrous madness of a sacrosanct power: these men, with a mind more than gladiatorial, rage against the pillar of the Christian name while the world stands stunned; bloodthirsty butchers who have borrowed the bloody sword from Mars, and who serve the rites of Bellona. Such examples, which Papal history records in many places, we have touched upon with the words of the divine Word, the ancient canons, Gregory the Great, and also Erasmus and Wicelius.

units.la: LXXIII. Quòd si Hierarchici cum Bellarmino frontem perfricuerint, atque crudelitatem à nobis descriptam tantam esse, ut Mulierem sanguine inebriatam, cocco & purpura indutam arguere possit, infi-
units.tr: LXXIII. But if the hierarchs, along with Bellarmine, brazen it out and deny that the cruelty we have described is so great that it could convict the Woman of being drunk with blood and clothed in scarlet and purple,

units.la: plebit. inficias iverint; noverint illi certè, nondum dierum omnium Soles occidisse, neque haftenus eos crudelitatis prædictæ, & longè fatis produĉtæ mensuram planè implevisse. Neque enim nos latet, plura & forte graviora etiam certamina ab iis Ecclesiæ imminere. Nondum enim certè Mulier postremum sanguinis poculum hausit: nondum ebrietas ad extremum perducta est. Sedet adhuc super aquis suis, & dicit in corde suo: Sedeo ut Regina, & viduanon ero, & luctum non videbo, Apoc. xviii. 7. Supersunt ejus conatus ultimi, qui in extremo annorum ejus aƈtu, ante tragicum ipsius exitum, haud dubiè omnium erunt acerrimi & vehementissimi, uti bestiarum morientium morsus venenatissimi esse solent. Et quid nì superesse putemus, cùm Ecclesiam adhuc in miseriarum caucaso hærentem lugeamus omnes; cùm terrorem nobis Bestiæ tot diademata: tot cornua, totà Draconis potentia & throno derivatæ prærogativæ incutiant; cùm Jesuitica illa ranarum vermiculatio, extremus ille Draconis, Bestiæ & Pseudoprophetæ partus equis virisque connitatur, ut ubique terrarum lucem Evangelii extinguat; cùm impuri illi & dæmoniaci Spiritus fi unquam antehac, hoc certè tempore ad moliendum opus giganteum, ad congregandum Reges terræ ad magnum Dei prœlium; ad bellum illud ultimum Harmageddonticum prodeant; abunde suppleturi haud dubiè, fi quid ad extremam Mulieris sanguine inebriandæ & furore dementandæ crudelitatem adhuc deesse videbitur. Imminet proximè fatis Divinorum oraculorum jam planè maturatis, & expressis ubique paturientis naturæ & Ecclesiæ vestigiis; decretorium illud tempus, quo brachium populi Sanctorum dissipabitur, quassabitur penitus; nihil erit inclusus & exclusus; & de victis Sanctis ac testibus Jesu Babylonii Pæana canent; ignari, ne bonam spem ejurare videamur, suorum fatorum, quibus post consummata domus Dei, urbis Hierosolymæ judicia, præcipitantibus horribiliter ab ipso Deo judice potente obruentur. quando confestim venient una die plagæ eorum, mors, luctus & fames, & igni comburentur ipsi, qui hactenus comburere Sanctos & innocentes testes Jesu pro ludo habuerunt, Apoc. xviii. 7. 8.
units.tr: they will deny it. Let them at least know that the suns of not all days have yet set, and that until now they have not filled up the full measure of the aforesaid cruelty, which was brought to its full extent long ago. For it is not hidden from us that even more numerous, and perhaps more grievous, struggles hang over the Church from them. The Woman has certainly not yet drained the last cup of blood; her drunkenness has not yet been carried to its end. She still sits upon her waters and says in her heart: I sit as a queen, and am no widow, and shall not see mourning, Rev. 18:7. Her final attempts remain, and in the last act of her years, before her tragic end, they will undoubtedly be the fiercest and most violent of all, just as the bites of dying beasts are wont to be the most venomous. And why should we not think these remain, since we all still mourn the Church, which still clings to the Caucasus of miseries; since the beast's many diadems, its many horns, and the prerogatives derived from the whole power and throne of the Dragon strike terror into us; since that Jesuitical croaking of frogs, the last offspring of the Dragon, the Beast and the False Prophet, strains with horses and men to extinguish the light of the Gospel everywhere on earth; since those impure and demonic spirits, if ever before, now at this very time come forth to undertake the gigantic work, to gather the kings of the earth to the great battle of God, to that last Armageddon war; no doubt they will more than make up for whatever still seems lacking to the final cruelty of making the Woman drunk with blood and maddened with rage. Very near is that decisive time, now surely ripened by the fulfilment of the divine oracles and everywhere marked by the clear signs of a travailing nature and Church, when the arm of the people of the Saints will be utterly scattered and shattered; nothing will remain enclosed or excluded; and the Babylonians will sing a paean over the vanquished Saints and witnesses of Jesus, unaware (lest we seem to abandon good hope) of their own fates, by which, after the judgments on the house of God and the city of Jerusalem are consummated, they will be horribly overwhelmed, plunged down by God himself, the mighty judge, when her plagues will come in one day, death, mourning and famine, and they will be burned with fire, those who have hitherto regarded it as a game to burn the Saints and the innocent witnesses of Jesus, Rev. 18:7, 8.

units.la: LXXIV. Sed Catholici, ita Bellarminus concludit, persecutionem potius patiuntur, quam Lutherani & Calvinistæ. Quid ita? Ex multis, inquit, Provinciis ejecti, Ecclesias, patrimonia, & ipsam patriam amiserunt, invadentibus res alienas novis illis Evangelii Ministris. Sic qui arguuntur occidisse hominem innocentem, vicissim arguentes accusant, quòd brachium hominis nocentis acu pupugerint. Proh scelus! Ubi ergo sanguinariæ nostrorum leges? Ubi infernalia Inquisitionis tribunalia? Ubi apud nos sunt Emissarii liticines, incendiarii orbis? Quis ob solam religionem, civilium delictorum culpa vacans, capite luit? Quis luit instigante, probante, laudante Ecclesia? Audi, Bellarmine, quem vivum petulanter vivus proscindere ausus es, Magnæ Britanniæ Regem Jacobum in Præfat. Monit. pag. 135. 136. sic asseverantem: Id constanter asseveo, quod & in apologia mea posui, hic neminem sive meis, sive defunctæ Reginæ temporibus, conscientiæ ac religionis causa ultimo supplicio affectum. Nam, quantumvis religioni suæ deditus sit, quantumvis eam aperte & constanter profiteatur, nullum ei à legibus impendet capitis periculum, nisi comperto contra leges externo aliquo actu deliquisse; aut conjurationem consiliùmve summæ rei perniciosum inivisse: exceptis solummodo sacrificulis, cæterisque Pontificiarum partium, qui in transmarinis regionibus sacris ordinibus initiantur: qui tot conjurationibus, tot proditionibus ab ipsis in Anglia vel conceptis
units.tr: LXXIV. But the Catholics, Bellarmine concludes, suffer persecution rather than the Lutherans and Calvinists. Why so? Driven out of many provinces, he says, they have lost their churches, their patrimonies and their very country, while those new ministers of the Gospel invade their property. Thus those who are accused of having killed an innocent man, in turn accuse the other side of having pricked the arm of a guilty man with a needle. Shameful! Where, then, are our bloodthirsty laws? Where are the infernal tribunals of the Inquisition? Where among us are the emissaries, the trumpeters, the incendiaries of the world? Who, free of any guilt for civil crimes, has paid with his head merely for religion? Who has paid at the urging, approval and praise of the Church? Hear, Bellarmine, you who dared wantonly to tear to pieces the living King James of Great Britain, in the Preface to the Monitory, pages 135 and 136, asserting thus: I firmly assert what I also stated in my Apology, that here no one, in the times of myself or of the late Queen, has been put to the ultimate punishment for reasons of conscience or religion. For however devoted someone may be to his religion, however openly and steadfastly he professes it, no danger of capital punishment hangs over him by the laws, unless it is discovered that he has offended against the laws by some outward act, or has entered into a conspiracy or plot against the sovereign and the public good; excepting only the little priests and the others of the Papist faction who are initiated into the sacred orders in foreign lands, who have been involved in so many conspiracies and so many treasons conceived against them in England

units.la: Tom. II. pugnatores scilicet jam diu ante annos quindecim ac viginti excruciatos miserè scripserunt pinxerúntque in suis illis pseudohistoriis Antuerpiæ excusis) noverit certè Bellarminus, noverint Hierarchici, non ut Christianos & διὰ Ιησῦν propter Jesum (2. Cor. iv. 11.) sed ut Κακοποιὸς maleficos & propter alios omnes, quàm Jesum, tales passos esse, justámque persecutionem sustinuisse. Martyrem enim juxta illud S.
