Augustini Epist. 61. & 106. decantatum non pœna, sed causa facit; & juxta ejusdem in Psal. 68. verba, laus Martyrii est in causæ bonitate, non in pœnæ acerbitate. Quanquam pœnarum supplicioru̅mque acerbitate ob solam religionis professionem sævire, Babylonis Magnæ esse: & Hierarchiam ob solam religionis, & quidem purioris confessionem immaniter sæviisse, irrefragabiliter demonstravimus. Unde, cæteris paribus, Hierarchiam Babylonem Magnam esse consequitur. ὅπερ ἔδει δεῖξαι.
units.tr: (namely, the fighters who, some fifteen or twenty years ago, miserably wrote and painted about them in those pseudo-histories printed at Antwerp, were tortured). Bellarmine surely knows, and the hierarchs know, that they suffered not as Christians and διὰ Ιησῦν [for Jesus] (2 Cor. 4:11), but as Κακοποιὸς [evildoers] and for all reasons other than Jesus, and that they sustained a just persecution. For a martyr is made, according to the saying of St. Augustine repeated in Epist. 61 and 106, not by the punishment but by the cause; and according to the words of the same man in Psal. 68, the praise of martyrdom lies in the goodness of the cause, not in the bitterness of the punishment. Yet we have irrefutably demonstrated that to rage with the bitterness of punishments and tortures solely for the profession of religion belongs to Great Babylon, and that the Hierarchy has savagely raged for the sake of religion alone, and indeed of the purer confession. Hence, other things being equal, it follows that the Hierarchy is Great Babylon. ὅπερ ἔδει δεῖξαι [which was to be shown].
MYSTERY. DISSERTATION THIRTEEN.

units.la: QUA A Hierarchiam, seu Clerum Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominantem esse Babylonem Magnam probatur Octavò, quia blasphemiis se nefariè polluit. BREVIARIUM.
units.tr: IN WHICH IT IS PROVED, IN THE EIGHTH PLACE, THAT THE HIERARCHY, OR THE CLERGY OF THE ROMAN CHURCH, WHICH DOMINATES, IS THE GREAT BABYLON, BECAUSE IT DEFILES ITSELF WITH BLASPHEMIES. SUMMARY.

units.la: I. Spiritus Dei Babylonem M. blasphemiarum ream perragit. II. Blasphemia definitur & distinguitur. III. Blasphemiæ nomina quo sensu in capitibus Bestiæ statuantur. IV. Dicitur Bestia à Muliere Babylonica infecta, adéoque etiam Babylon ipsa os suum aperire ad blasphemandum nomen Dei, tabernaculum ejus, & eos, qui in Cœlo habitant. V. Hierarchicos sic nomen Dei, tabernaculum ejus, & S. Cœlites blasphemare, Syllogismo demonstratur. cujus propositio ex terminis constat, & Assumptio per partes probatur. VI. In antecessum ex Casuistis, Diana, Azorio, Ledesma, Sanchez &c. probatur, Hierarchicos blasphemias verissimas leves ducere. VII. Idem nomen Dei blasphemant tum in universa Papolatria; VIII. Tum in idololatria. Blasphemia per icasmum pro idololatria apud Scriptores Sacros ponitur.
units.tr: I. The Spirit of God charges Great Babylon with blasphemies. II. Blasphemy is defined and distinguished. III. The names of blasphemy are placed on the heads of the Beast in what sense. IV. The Beast is said to be infected by the Babylonian Woman, and therefore Babylon herself opens her mouth to blaspheme the name of God, his tabernacle, and those who dwell in heaven. V. It is demonstrated by a syllogism that the Hierarchy thus blasphemes the name of God, his tabernacle, and the holy inhabitants of heaven; the major premise consists of the terms, and the minor is proved part by part. VI. In advance, from the Casuists, Diana, Azor, Ledesma, Sánchez and others, it is proved that the Hierarchy regards its blasphemies, which are most true, as slight. VII. They blaspheme the same name of God in the whole of Papolatry; VIII. and also in idolatry. In Sacred Writers, blasphemy is put for idolatry by a figure of speech.

units.la: IX. Ratio est, quia in ea est absoluta subsannatio & vilipendium Dei vivi.
units.tr: IX. The reason is that in it there is absolute mockery and contempt of the living God.

units.la: X. Blasphemiarum conspicua in primis documenta Mariolatria præbet.
units.tr: X. Mariolatry above all offers conspicuous proofs of blasphemies.

units.la: XI. Sed & superstitio Hierarchicorum omnis, præcipua eorum dogmata; errores inprimis Magici cum blasphemiis conjuncti sunt.
units.tr: XI. But also all the superstition of the Hierarchy, and its chief dogmas, and especially its magical errors, are joined with blasphemies.

units.la: XII. Blasphemia nominis Dei capitalis est adversus S. Scripturam.
units.tr: XII. The blasphemy of the name of God is a capital offence against Holy Scripture.

units.la: XIII. Vaticinium S. Pauli 2. Tim. iii. 2. 5. de blasphemia eorum, qui formulam pietatis Scripturam habentes, ejusdem abnegabunt potentiam, exponitur.
units.tr: XIII. The prophecy of St. Paul, 2 Tim. 3:2, 5, concerning the blasphemy of those who, having the form of godliness in Scripture, deny its power, is explained.

units.la: XIV. XV. Scripturæ Divinitatem ab humana authoritate suspendentes, & sine hac eam nefariis maledictis proscindentes, atrociter blasphemant.
units.tr: XIV. XV. Those who make the divinity of Scripture depend on human authority, and who, without that authority, tear it apart with wicked slanders, blaspheme atrociously.

units.la: XVI. Exceptio blasphemantium, quod verbum Ecclesiæ, hoc est, Papæ ex Cathedra docentis, non hominis, sed Dei verbum sit, eliditur.
units.tr: XVI. The objection of the blasphemers, that the word of the Church, that is, of the Pope teaching from the Chair, is not the word of man but of God, is refuted.
XVII. The blasphemy of those who deny the necessity of Scripture;

units.la: XVIII. Et libris Apocryphis, incertisque traditionibus Divinitatem arrogantium.
units.tr: XVIII. and of those who arrogate divinity to the Apocryphal books and uncertain traditions.

units.la: XIX. XX. XXI. Inprimis Scripturæ perfectionem seu sufficientiam oppugnantium. Fucus Cleri Gallicani novissimè congregati, scrarii, aliorum, qui Scripturæ perfectionem agnoscere videri volunt, discutitur.
units.tr: XIX. XX. XXI. Above all, of those who attack the perfection or sufficiency of Scripture. The deceit of the French Clergy lately assembled, of the Sorbonne, and of others who wish to seem to acknowledge the perfection of Scripture, is examined.

units.la: XXII. Ipsi sibi Sophistæ, Scripturæ sufficientiam differtis verbis negantes, larvam detrahunt.
units.tr: XXII. The Sophists themselves, who deny the sufficiency of Scripture in fine-sounding words, strip off their mask.

units.la: XXIII. Blasphemiæ Hierarchicorum circa sensum Scripturæ, quem non ex Scriptura ipsa demonstrandum; sed
units.tr: XXIII. The blasphemies of the Hierarchy concerning the sense of Scripture, which must not be demonstrated from Scripture itself, but which they know must be breathed into it by the arbitrary judgment of the Romanists.

units.la: sed humano Romanensium arbitrio ei inspirandum scis-
units.tr: but which they know must be breathed into it by the arbitrary judgment of the Romanists.
(continued)
XXIV. The same men accuse Scripture as obscure,
incomplete, a waxen nose, a dead letter, a stone
of stumbling, etc. The blasphemies of Pighius, Pictavius, Pamelius, Baronius,
Cosler, and the Walenburgs.
XXV. The causes of these accusations.
XXVI. Blasphemies against the purpose of Scripture.

units.la: XXVII. Canonem seu regulam esse, blasphemè insicia-
units.tr: XXVII. They blasphemously deny that Scripture is the canon or rule,
...are denied.

units.la: XXVIII. Eidem judicis partes abrogant, & in Papam
units.tr: XXVIII. They strip the same [Scripture] of the office of judge and transfer it to the Pope,

units.la: transferunt. cùm judicem ex Cælo petendum esse,
units.tr: since the judge is to be sought from heaven.
(continued)
(continued)
XXIX. Bellarmine's disputation on the judge of controversies is shown,

units.la: ex qua, Hierarchicos Spiritui S. in Scriptura loquenti
units.tr: from which it appears that the Hierarchy denies to the Holy Spirit, speaking in Scripture, all divine judgment, and asserts it for the Pope alone.

units.la: judicium omne Divinum abdicare, & Papæ soli assere-
units.tr: (continued)

XXX. The fraudulent exception of the Walenburgs is refuted.
(continued)
XXXI. The impious pretext of those who abrogate the divine judgment of Scripture. The blasphemy conceived by Gretser.
(continued)

XXXII. The jibe about private spirit is rebutted.
(continued)
XXXIII. Blasphemies against the tabernacle of God, Christ, are recognised from the tyrannical errors of the Hierarchy.

units.la: XXXIV. Nec non ex apertis dicteriis Leonis X. Bellar-
units.tr: XXXIV. Also from the open insults of Leo X, Bellarmine, Bertrand, Nicholas V, etc.
...mini, Bertrand, Nicholas V, etc.
XXXV. Blasphemies against the tabernacle of God, the Church,

units.la: lesiam, quam vel nullam Christus in mundo habet, vel
units.tr: which Christ either has none of in the world, or which he has only as the one that hears his voice and his teaching...

units.la: eam habet, quæ vocem ejus audit, & doctrinam suam
units.tr: (continued)

units.la: XXXVI. Blapsphemiæ Ecclesiæ communes. Calumniæ adversus Waldenses atroces notatæ.
units.tr: XXXVI. Blasphemies common to the Church. The atrocious calumnies against the Waldenses are noted.

units.la: XXXVII. Nec non adversus quoscunque pietate, zelo, eruditione Romanæ Curiæ suspectos, quos ilico hæreticorum in numerum retulit.
units.tr: XXXVII. Likewise against all whom the Roman Curia suspects of piety, zeal or learning, whom it at once numbers among the heretics.

units.la: XXXVIII. Adversus Reformatores Ecclesiæ, Lutherum, Zwinglium, Calvinum, Bezam, Junium &c. Ecclesias integras, Genevensem, Anglicanam, Helveticam.
units.tr: XXXVIII. Against the Reformers of the Church: Luther, Zwingli, Calvin, Beza, Junius, etc., and whole churches: the Genevan, the English, the Helvetic.

units.la: XXXIX. Doctrinam inprimis Evangelicorum, quam verbo Dei conformem licet obsoletarum hæresium convitiis spurcissimis aspergunt.
units.tr: XXXIX. Above all the doctrine of the Evangelicals, which, though it conforms to the word of God, they besmear with the most filthy abuse of long-discredited heresies.

units.la: XL. Dispar plane ratio est Babylonem & Hierarchiam, sine ulla blasphemia, comparantium.
units.tr: XL. The comparison of Babylon and the Hierarchy, made without any blasphemy, is quite a different matter.

units.la: XLI. Digressio, qua Cleri Gallicani novissimis de calumniis Protestantium querelis generatim occurritur.
units.tr: XLI. A digression, in which the latest complaints of the French Clergy about the calumnies of the Protestants are answered in general terms.

units.la: XLII. Authori impactum ab eodem Clero calumniarum crimen depellitur in doctrina de Traditionibus.
units.tr: XLII. The charge of calumny brought against the author by the same Clergy is repelled in the doctrine of Traditions.
XLIII. Concerning Attrition and Confession.

units.la: XLIV. De Peccati originalis per Baptismum expunctione.
units.tr: XLIV. Concerning the removal of original sin through Baptism.

units.la: XLV. De concupiscentia regenitorum, ubi per insignem calumniam Deicidii speciem Tridentinis à me objectam queritur.
units.tr: XLV. Concerning the concupiscence of the regenerate, where, through a notable calumny, the charge of deicide brought by me against the Tridentines is complained of.

units.la: XLVI. Denique de meritis operum & justitia propria.
units.tr: XLVI. Lastly, concerning the merits of works and one's own righteousness.
XLVII. Blasphemies of the Hierarchy against the dominions.

units.la: XLVIII. Adversus habitantes in Cœlis Angelos & homines Sanctos.
units.tr: XLVIII. Against the angels and holy men who dwell in heaven.

units.la: XLIX. De quibus honorificè nec sentire, nec loqui eos probatur. In Canone Missæ pro Sanctis orantes, injuriam iis, ceu exulibus à facie Dei, imò in Purgatorio cruciatus gravissimos & diuturnos sustinentibus, faciunt. ciunt. Qua injuria etiam Deiparam salutatione solenni, Ave Maria, interpellatam afficiunt.
units.tr: XLIX. It is proved that they neither think nor speak honourably of them. In the Canon of the Mass, by praying for the Saints, they do them an injury, as if they were exiles from the face of God, and indeed as if they endured the most grievous and long-lasting torments in Purgatory. By this injury they also afflict the Mother of God, whom they invoke with the solemn salutation, the Ave Maria.

units.la: L. Sanctis honorem debitum iidem detrahunt, arcentes populum à lectione Scripturæ, quæ honorem eorum genuinum tradit.
units.tr: L. The same men also take away the honour due to the Saints, keeping the people from reading Scripture, which hands down their genuine honour.

units.la: LI. Ne quidem Pastores & Theologi Scripturas condigne tractare, & ex iis veras Sanctorum laudes depromere sinuntur.
units.tr: LI. Neither are the Pastors and Theologians allowed to handle the Scriptures worthily, or to draw from them the true praises of the Saints.

units.la: LII. S. Petrum ex Apostolorum choro deturbantes, Romæ Pastorem faciunt. De eo disceptatio Cardinales inter & Græcum, apud Nilum.
units.tr: LII. In thrusting St. Peter out of the choir of the Apostles, they make him a Pastor at Rome. Concerning him there is a dispute between a Cardinal and a Greek, in Nilus.

units.la: LIII. S. Apostolos reliquos insigniter deprimunt, Petro soli potestatis plenitudinem vindicantes, & Papæ cuivis eos postponentes.
units.tr: LIII. They notably depress the remaining holy Apostles, claiming the fullness of power for Peter alone, and setting every Pope above them.
LIV. Insults to the Virgin Mother of God;
LV. likewise to the holy Fathers;
LVI. and finally, the outrages done to the bodies of the Saints.
LVII. Conclusion of the argument.

units.la: I. Rudelitatem & tyrannidem Hierarchiæ ejusdem blasphemiæ horrendæ excipiunt. His enim Spiritus Dei Babylonem Magnam censet, quando eam sedentem super Bestia, γεμόντ' ἀνοματων βλασφημίας, plena nominibus blasphemiæ Apoc. xvii. 3. inducit. Super ejusdem Bestiæ capitibus ὀνόματα βλασφημίας nomen blasphemiæ ib. cap. xiii. 1. quasi inscriptum ponitur. Quin datum ei esse στόμα λαλῶν μεγάλα καὶ βλασφημίας os loquens magna & blasphemias, atque eandem aperiendo & resolvendo os suum in blasphemiam in Deum, blasphemasse τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆς, nomen ejus, & tabernaculum ejus, & tabernaculum habentes in Cœlo, ib. v. 5. & 6. asseritur. Quod autem Bestiæ à Babylonica Muliere insessæ, inequitatæ, adeóque
units.tr: I. They join to these the harshness and tyranny of the same Hierarchy, a most horrible blasphemy. For the Spirit of God judges Babylon the Great to be such when he brings her in sitting upon the Beast, "full of names of blasphemy" [γεμόντ' ἀνομάτων βλασφημίας] (Rev. 17:3). Upon the heads of the same Beast a "name of blasphemy" [ὀνόματα βλασφημίας] is set, as if written on them (ibid. 13:1). Moreover, it is affirmed that she was given "a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies" [στόμα λαλῶν μεγάλα καὶ βλασφημίας], and that by opening and turning her mouth into blasphemy against God, she blasphemed "his name, and his tabernacle, and those who dwell in heaven" [τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ τοὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ σκηνοῦντας] (ibid. 13:5-6). That the Beast, which is sat upon, ridden and driven by the Babylonian Woman, is attributed to her as the one who guides and directs it, the Spirit of God depicts Babylon the Great as guilty of blasphemies.

units.la: Spiritus Dei Babylonem Magnam blasphemiarum ream peragit. que ab eadem directæ, adgubernatæ tribuitur, id ipsi quoque Babyloni Magnæ, Mulieri Bestiæ inequitanti tribuendum esse, propter conjunctionem intimam rectoris & directi, agitati, & hujus erga illum devotionem, ab eodem præscriptam, dubitari nequit. Neque enim Bestia Mulieri parere, religiosum obsequium deferre, sine expressis & claris Dei blasphemiis potest. Quæ blasphemiæ non possunt non ei, qui cultum & obsequium ejusmodi depaciscitur, ceu carundem authori, imputari.
units.tr: Spiritus Dei Babylonem Magnam blasphemiarum ream peragit. That this guilt should likewise be attributed to Babylon the Great herself, the Woman riding the Beast, is beyond doubt, on account of the intimate union between the ruler and the ruled, the one driven, and her devotion to him, prescribed by him. For the Beast cannot obey the Woman and render her religious service without express and clear blasphemies against God. Such blasphemies cannot but be imputed to him who bargains for this kind of worship and obedience, as their author.

units.la: II. Blasphemia famæ, seu nominis, quod virtutum eximiarum gloria & choragio comparatur, violati iniuriam & contumeliam significat. Quisquis ergo superiori maledicit, vel nomini & virtutibus ejus derogat, vel falsi quid, quo perfectio & excellens bonitas ejus minuitur conspurcatúrque, asserit, is blasphemat, &, juxta Levit. xxiv. 11. ⁠שם superiorem maledico ore transfigit, proscindit. Ita si quis Deo, Supremo Domino vel tribuit, quod ei non convenit: vel derogat eripitque, quod ei convenit, blasphemare dicitur. Neque refert, an indecora ei tribuat, & decora auferat: an quæ ipsi tribuenda soli fuerunt, in alium אלהים לא Non-Deum transferat. Utroque modo, illo directè, hoc indirectè, quod ajunt, blasphemat. Nam qui aliis merè Divina tribuit, is gloriam Dei alienat, profanat, & excellentiam parem Deo & non-Diis tribuendo, Deum ipsum & non-Deos æquiparat. quod sine manifesta Dei blasphemia fieri nequit. Neque adversarii, puto, dissentiunt, quos inter P. Avila Comp. verb. Blasphemi. sic scribit: Blasphemia est dicere aliquid contumeliosum contra Deum. Quod fit, Deo aliquid attribuendo, quod ei non convenit, vel auferendo, quod convenit; vel affirmando de creatura, quod est proprium Dei. Sic plane blasphemus est, qui vel falsos fos Deos colit, ut Deut. xxxi. 20. vel Deum colit per ἐϑελοϑρησκίαν cultum ingenio suo excogitatum. Quomodo qui Deum in celsis colebant, dicebantur צרף & חרף βλασφημεῖν, blasphemare, Esaj. lxv. 7. Ezech. xx. 27. 28. 29. Cultus enim electitius non aliud quàm veri Dei renuntiatio, abdicatio est. Quantò magis blasphemus est, qui quod Dei & Christi est, impertitur aliis.
units.tr: II. Blasphemy of reputation, or of name, which is gained through the glory and renown of outstanding virtues, signifies injury and insult to what is violated. Whoever therefore speaks evil of a superior, or detracts from his name and virtues, or asserts anything false by which his perfection and excellent goodness are diminished or defiled, blasphemes; and according to Lev. 24:11 he pierces and tears down the superior with a cursing mouth [שם]. Thus, if anyone attributes to God, the Supreme Lord, what does not belong to him, or takes away and snatches what does belong to him, he is said to blaspheme. It makes no difference whether he attributes to God unseemly things and takes away fitting ones, or transfers to another what was to be ascribed to God alone, to a "non-God" [אלהים לא]. In either way he blasphemes, the one directly, the other indirectly, as they say. For he who gives to others what is purely divine alienates and profanes the glory of God, and by giving equal excellence to non-gods, he equates God himself with non-gods, which cannot be done without manifest blasphemy against God. Nor, I think, do our opponents disagree; among them Father Avila, in Comp. verb. Blasphemi, writes thus: "Blasphemy is to say something insulting against God. This is done by attributing to God something that does not belong to him, or by taking away what does belong to him; or by affirming of a creature what is proper to God." Thus he is clearly a blasphemer who either worships false gods, as in Deut. 31:20, or worships God with a self-devised cult [ἐθελοθρησκίαν]. This is how those who worshipped God on the high places were said to blaspheme [חרף] (Isa. 65:7; Ezek. 20:27-29). For a self-chosen worship is nothing other than a renunciation and abdication of the true God. How much more a blasphemer, then, is he who bestows on others what belongs to God and Christ.

units.la: III. Blasphemiæ nomina in capitibus Bestiæ Apoc. xiii. 1. statuuntur. ὄνομα Nomen in Scripturis objectum fidei & adorationis significat. Cui paremus, credimus, confidimus, servimus, eum tanquam auctorem fidei, spei, actionum nostrarum nominamus. Ita solus Deus nominari vult, Act. iv. 12. iii. 16. Ephes. i. 21. Phil. ii. 9. 2. Tim. ii. 19. Quando igitur in cultu Dei alius nominatur quàm Deus; aut verbum, voluntas, revelatio non Dei habetur pro verbo Dei; aut cultus Dei adstringitur ad locum, in quo Deus memoriam nominis sui non posuisse comperitur, quid hæc aliud sunt quàm ὀνόματα βλασφημίας nomina blasphemiæ? Qualia cùm Bestiæ capitibus quasi inscripta dicuntur, quid aliud significatur, quàm in omnibus Bestiæ seu imperii magni partibus nomina blasphemiæ comparere, seu aliud nomen præter illud, in quo nos salvari oportet, nominari; adeóque Bestiam se mancipasse cultui Numinis alieni cum blasphemia. Solebant idololatræ stigma fronti suæ inurere, signum scilicet, cujus Dei se esse gloriarentur. Quod lex Divina expressè vetat Levit. xix. 28 כתבת קעקע לא תתנו בכם Scripturam nominis non facietis vobis. Ubi Baal Hatturim : קעקע שכתוב שם קעקע הטמאה In numeris tantum valet ac שם (utrumque 340 facit) Nam scribebant nomen pollutionis, hoc est, falsi Dei. Ita Apoc. xiv. Agni asseclæ nomen Patris in faciebus suis scriptum habere: & Gal. v. 17. S. Paulus stigmata Christi in corpore suo gestare: Sacerdos quoque summus Exod. xxviii. 36. laminam in fronte sua geslasse, in qua scriptum erat, קדש ליהוה Sanctum Domini (quo symbolo homo & minister Dei, ipsius cultui consecratus, declarabatur) dicitur. Hoc ergo hic quoque innuitur, quòd Bestia se denominet de falsis Numinibus, quibus per blasphemiam ea, quæ Dei & Christi sunt, attribuat: quódque se titulis contra Deum & sanctos eferat.
units.tr: III. The names of blasphemy are set out on the heads of the Beast, Rev. 13:1. In Scripture, ὄνομα (name) means an object of faith and worship. We name as the author of our faith, hope and actions the one whom we obey, believe, trust in and serve. In this way God alone wishes to be named: Acts 4:12; 3:16; Eph. 1:21; Phil. 2:9; 2 Tim. 2:19. So when in the worship of God someone is named other than God, or when a word, will or revelation that is not God's is held to be the word of God, or when the worship of God is confined to a place where God is found not to have placed the memory of his name, what are these but ὀνόματα βλασφημίας, names of blasphemy? When these are said to be written, as it were, on the heads of the Beast, what is signified except that names of blasphemy appear in every part of the Beast, or of the great empire; that is, that some name other than the one by which we must be saved is named; and so the Beast has given itself over to the worship of an alien deity, with blasphemy. Idolaters used to brand a mark on their foreheads, namely the sign of the god whose followers they boasted of being. The divine law expressly forbids this, Lev. 19:28: כתבת קעקע לא תתנו בכם (you shall not make any written mark upon yourselves). There Baal Hatturim says: קעקע שכתוב שם הטמאה (a tattoo on which is written the name of uncleanness). In numerical value it is the same as שם (both make 340), for they wrote the name of pollution, that is, of a false god. So in Rev. 14 the followers of the Lamb have the name of the Father written on their foreheads; Paul in Gal. 5:17 bears the marks of Christ in his body; and the high priest in Exod. 28:36 is said to have worn on his forehead a plate on which was written קדש ליהוה (holy to the LORD), a sign by which a man and minister of God, consecrated to his worship, was declared. So here too it is hinted that the Beast names itself after false deities, by which, through blasphemy, it attributes to them what belongs to God and Christ, and that it exalts itself with titles against God and the saints.

units.la: IV. Neque tantùm nomina blasphemiæ in capitibus suis Bestia habere, sed etiam os suum aperire ad blasphemandum nomen Dei, tabernaculum ejus, & eos qui in Cælo habitant, v.6. dicitur. Nomen Dei est vel Deus ipse, & virtus ejus, quatenus cognoscitur, & cognoscenda proponitur; vel ejus revelatio, qua revelatur seu describitur quis & qualis Deus sit. quæ in Scriptura extat. Qui ergo vel virtutes Dei, vel verbum ejus scriptum blasphemat, is nomen Dei blasphemat, quia negat, Dei virtutem, voluntatem & gloriam in Scriptura revelatam esse; atque adeò hoc, quod Scriptura revelat, nomen Dei esse inficiatur. Tabernaculum Dei tum Christus est, in quo omnis Deitas corporaliter habitat, & in quo est omnis περιχωρησις adductio, secundum illud: Tu pater in me, & ego in te, ut & illi in nobis unum sint. Joh. xvii. 21. tum Ecclesia, quæ domus Dei viventis est 1. Tim. iii. 15. Denique habitantes in Cælo Sancti sunt, qui in domo Cœlestis Patris μονὴν mansionem habent.
units.tr: IV. The Beast is said not only to have names of blasphemy on its heads, but also to open its mouth to blaspheme the name of God, his tabernacle, and those who dwell in heaven, v. 6. The name of God is either God himself and his power, insofar as he is known and set forth to be known, or his revelation, by which it is revealed or described who and what sort of God he is, and which is contained in Scripture. Therefore whoever blasphemes either the powers of God or his written word, blasphemes the name of God, because he denies that God's power, will and glory are revealed in Scripture, and so denies that what Scripture reveals is the name of God. The tabernacle of God is both Christ, in whom all the Godhead dwells bodily, and in whom is all περιχώρησις (mutual indwelling), according to: You, Father, in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us, John 17:21; and it is also the Church, which is the house of the living God, 1 Tim. 3:15. Finally, those dwelling in heaven are the saints, who have their μονή (abode) in the house of the heavenly Father.

units.la: V. Jam ergo cujusmodi sint blasphemiæ Bestiæ, quæ à Muliere Babylonica regitur, abunde constat. Nam populus, qui Bestiæ nomine venit, in alio, quàm Dei nomine gloriatur; virtutes Dei alienat, verbum Dei scriptum convitiis incessit, Christo uni solíque eximia detra-
units.tr: V. It is now abundantly clear what sort of blasphemies belong to the Beast that is ruled by the Babylonian Woman. For the people who come under the name of the Beast glory in a name other than the name of God; they alienate the powers of God, assail the written word of God with insults, detract from Christ alone and uniquely his singular honour, [...]

units.la: Dicitur Bestia à Muliere Babylonica insessa, adeoque etiam Babylon ipsa seu sa os suum aperire ad blasphemandum nomen Dei, tabernaculum ejus, & eos qui in Cælo habitant.
units.tr: The Beast is said to be sat upon by the Babylonian Woman, and so Babylon itself, or the Church of Rome, opens its mouth to blaspheme the name of God, his tabernacle, and those who dwell in heaven.

units.la: detrahit, Ecclesiam veram maledictis proscindit, Sanctis denique cum Christo regnantibus convitium facit. Atque hæc ipsa Hierarchiæ competere, sequenti Syllogismo fidem faciemus.
units.tr: It slanders the true Church with curses, and at last heaps abuse upon the saints who reign with Christ. We will show by the following syllogism that these charges apply to the hierarchy itself.

units.la: Ille cætus se blasphemiis nefariè polluit, hoc est, in alio quàm Dei nomine gloriatur, virtutes Dei alienat, verbum Dei scriptum convitiatur, Christo uni solique debitam gloriam detrahit, Ecclesiam & Sanctos cum Christo regnantes maledictis proscindit, adeoque cæteris paribus, Babylon Magna est; qui blasphemias quasdam leves ducit; atque insuper rector est ejus populi, qui in Papa ceu Numine suo gloriatur; virtutes & cultum Dei multiplicem per idololatriam, falsa dogmata, errores magicos creaturis impertitur; Scriptum Dei verbum in omnibus causis & attributis suis Divinitatis honore spoliat; Christi Salvatoris & Mediatoris honorem & gloriam communem aliis facit; Ecclesiam Dei, verbo ejus conformatam variis convitiis aspergit; denique Sanctis Cœlitibus indebitum honorem, cum gloriæ Divinæ detrimento tribuit, & debitum derogat.
units.tr: That body foully pollutes itself with blasphemies, that is, it glories in a name other than God's, alienates the powers of God, assails the written word of God with insults, detracts from the glory due to Christ alone, and tears to pieces the Church and the saints who reign with Christ with curses; and so, other things being equal, Babylon is Great; which regards certain blasphemies as light; and moreover is the ruler of that people who glory in the Pope as their Deity; who bestows on creatures the manifold powers and worship of God through idolatry, false dogmas and magical errors; who strips the written word of God of the honour of divinity in all its causes and attributes; who makes the honour and glory of Christ the Saviour and Mediator common to others; who sprinkles the Church of God, conformed to his word, with various insults; and finally who gives to the heavenly saints an honour not due them, to the detriment of divine glory, and takes away what is due.

units.la: Atqui Hierarchia, seu Clerus Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominans blasphemias quasdam leves ducit; atque insuper rectrix est ejus populi, qui in Papa ceu Numine suo gloriatur; virtutes & cultum Dei, multiplicem per idololatriam, falsa dogmata, errores Magicos creaturis impertitur; Scriptum Dei verbum in omnibus causis & attributis suis Divinitatis honorem spoliat; Christi Salvatoris & Mediatoris honorem & gloriam communem aliis facit; Ecclesiam Dei verbo ejus conformatam variis convitiis aspergit; denique Sanctis Cœlitibus indebitum honorem cu cum gloriæ Divinæ detrimento tribuit, & debitum derogat.
units.tr: But the hierarchy, or the dominant clergy of the Roman Church, regards certain blasphemies as light; and moreover is the ruler of that people who glory in the Pope as their Deity; who bestows on creatures the manifold powers and worship of God through idolatry, false dogmas and magical errors; who strips the written word of God of the honour of divinity in all its causes and attributes; who makes the honour and glory of Christ the Saviour and Mediator common to others; who sprinkles the Church of God, conformed to his word, with various insults; and finally who gives to the heavenly saints an honour not due them, to the detriment of divine glory, and takes away what is due.

units.la: Ergo Hierarchia, seu Clerus Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominans se blasphemiis nefariè polluit, hoc est, in alio quàm Dei nomine gloriatur, virtutes Dei alienat, verbum Dei scriptum convitiatur, Christo uni solique debitam gloriam detrahit, Ecclesiam & Sanctos cum Christo regnantes maledictis proscindit; adeóque cæteris paribus, Babylon Magna est.
units.tr: Therefore the hierarchy, or the dominant clergy of the Roman Church, foully pollutes itself with blasphemies, that is, it glories in a name other than God's, alienates the powers of God, assails the written word of God with insults, detracts from the glory due to Christ alone, and tears to pieces the Church and the saints who reign with Christ with curses; and so, other things being equal, Babylon is Great.

units.la: Propositio ex terminis constat. neque puto Hierarchicorum quenquam eò audaciæ processurum, ut in dubium eam revocare ausit. Assumptionem ὅλως positam ἀνὰ μέρος probamus.
units.tr: The major premise consists of its terms, and I do not think any of the hierarchy will go so far in audacity as to dare to call it into doubt. We prove the minor premise, taken as a whole, by taking its parts separately.

units.la: VI. Blasphemias quasdam ab Hierarchicis leves dici, Casuistæ illorum & Morales Theologi passim produnt. Juxta decretum Concilii Lateranensis Sess. 9. ff. ad abolendam blasphemus non potest absolvi à confessore, nisi gravissima pœnitentia ipsius arbitrio impositâ. Sic enim expresse ibi definitur: neque aliter Navarrus, Ludovicus Lopes, de Ledesma, aliíque docent. At decretum illud usu receptum esse, vel hodiéque oblivisci gare, Armilla verbo Blasphemia; & ibi Emmanuel Sa, Azorius, Suarez, alii pertendunt. Disputat Diana Resol. Moral. parte XVI tract. 14. Resol. 68. An incidat in casum reservatum blasphemia, si quis in ebrietate illam proferat, quam ante ebrietatem prævidit? Ait, affirmative quosdam respondere, quia talis blasphemia fit voluntaria in causa. Sed contrariam sententiam tueri Oliverium Mazuchellum, quia talis blasphemia in ebrietate probata non fit peccatum: ergo nec reservata. Imò id verum esse, etiamsi quis vinum usque ad ebrietatem sumeret ad finem blasphemandi; ratione hac addita, quia adhuc illi imputari non posset peccatum blasphemiæ, utpote.
units.tr: VI. That the hierarchy's casuists and moral theologians everywhere declare certain blasphemies to be light is shown by their own writings. By the decree of the Council of Lateran, Session 9, under the heading On abolishing blasphemy, a blasphemer cannot be absolved by his confessor unless a most grave penance is imposed at the confessor's discretion. This is expressly defined there, and Navarrus, Ludovicus Lopes, de Ledesma and others teach nothing different. But that the decree has fallen out of use, or has been neglected, and is even today forgotten, Armilla under the word Blasphemy, and Emmanuel Sa, Azorius and Suárez there, maintain. Diana, in Resolutions on Moral Matters, part 16, tract 14, resolution 68, discusses: Does blasphemy fall into the reserved cases if someone utters it while drunk, having foreseen it before drinking? He says that some answer affirmatively, because such a blasphemy becomes voluntary in its cause. But Oliverius Mazuchellus defends the contrary opinion, because blasphemy uttered in drunkenness is not held to be sin, and so not reserved; indeed this is true even if someone drank wine to the point of drunkenness for the purpose of blaspheming, on the ground that sin of blasphemy could still not be imputed to him, inasmuch as he lacks the use of reason.

units.la: In antecessum ex Casuistis, Diana, Azor, Ledesma, Sanchez &c. te quod usum rationis requirit. Astipulantem inducit Sanchez: & astipulatur ipse Diana, is scilicet, de quo Caramuel Epist. ad Dian. p. 24. dixit: Generose & cl menter sequimur AGNUM, Dianam, quocunque ierit. Certi enim sumus, tanto illius dogmata Theologorum firmari numero, ut quærenti, an hoc aut illud liceat, sufficiat respondere: Αὐλὸς ἰΦα, hoc est, Diana dixit. Idem ille Diana Par. 1. tract. 5. Resol. 62. quærit: An blasphemiæ inadvertenter prolatæ, ortæ tamen ex prava consuetudine blasphemandi sint peccata mortalia? Affirmantes Raphaelem de Torre, Tannerum, Azorium, alios inducit. Sed ipse tantùm non indignabundus, Si hæc opinio, inquit, vera esset, magnum onus pœnitens & Confessarii haberent, cùm talia maximè frequentia sint. Ideo contrariam sententiam in praxi sequendam esse puto. Sed quamvis aliquis habeat pravam consuetudinem peccandi, si tamen hic & nunc ex inadvertentia naturali & indeliberatè peccaret, non committeret novum peccatum mortale. Idem censet Toletus Jesuita & Cardinalis Instruct. Sacerd. lib. v. 13. ubi blasphemias horrendas licet, si ex inadvertentia, ira ebrietate, consuetudine &c. non advertendo ad verba, pronuntientur, inter peccata venialia numerat. quasi scilicet non ipsa inadvertentia, cùm de Dei honore agitur, gravissimum peccatum esset. Aliam quæstionem Diana par. V. tract. 13. Resol. 20. movet: An qui vocat amasiam Deam, vel idolum suum, sit blasphemus? Respondet, Confessarium quendam scrupulofum & parùm scientem affirmativam sententiam olim docuisse. Sed talem, inquit ipse, non esse blasphemiam, dicendum est, quia verba hæc nec proferuntur, nec accipiuntur in significatione propria, sed in hyperbolicâ. Et ita docent Lorca, & Hurtadus Mendoza. Zonardus Theolog.p.11.cap.1. blasphemos ex ira, semel, bis vel ter, si ira magna fuit, & ex causa justa, negat abjurare solere. Diana Tom.IV.tr.1.resol.51. eum, qui in blasphemiam non hæreticalem incidit, immunitate Ecclesiastica gaudere asserit. Talica indicasse, & doctrinam verissimis blasphemiis faventem prodere.
units.tr: Among the casuists, Diana, Azor, Ledesma, Sánchez and others, in advance, [...] Sánchez brings in a supporter, and Diana himself, of whom Caramuel says in his Letter to Diana, p. 24, supports him: We follow Diana generously and cheerfully wherever he goes, like a lamb. For we are sure that his doctrines are confirmed by so great a number of theologians that when someone asks whether this or that is lawful, it is enough to answer: Αὐτὸς ἔφα, that is, Diana said it. The same Diana, Part 1, tract 5, resolution 62, asks: Are blasphemies uttered inadvertently, yet arising from a bad habit of blaspheming, mortal sins? He brings in Raphael de Torre, Tanner, Azor and others who affirm this. But he himself, scarcely indignant, says: If this opinion were true, confessors and penitents would have a great burden, since such things are most frequent. So I think the contrary opinion should be followed in practice. But although someone may have a bad habit of sinning, if he sins here and now from natural inadvertence and without deliberation, he does not commit a new mortal sin. Toletus the Jesuit and Cardinal in Instruction of Priests, book 5, chapter 13, holds the same view, where he counts among venial sins the dreadful blasphemies that are permitted if they are uttered from inadvertence, anger, drunkenness, habit, etc., without attention to the words; as though inadvertence itself, when the honour of God is at stake, were not the gravest sin. Diana raises another question, Part 5, tract 13, resolution 20: Is one who calls his mistress a goddess, or his idol, a blasphemer? He answers that a certain scrupulous and not very learned confessor once taught the affirmative opinion. But such a thing, he says, is not blasphemy, because these words are neither uttered nor understood in their proper sense, but in a hyperbolical one. And so Lorca and Hurtado de Mendoza teach. Zonaras, Theology, p. 11, chapter 1, denies that those who blaspheme from anger, once, twice or three times, if the anger was great and the cause just, are usually made to abjure. Diana, Tome IV, tract 1, resolution 51, asserts that one who falls into a blasphemy that is not heretical enjoys ecclesiastical immunity. These are the things they have indicated, and by them they reveal a doctrine that favours the most evident blasphemies.

units.la: VII. Hierarchiam esse rectricem ejus populi seu Ecclesiæ, quæ in Papa, seu Numine suo gloriatur, ei Divinitatem & religiosum adorationis cultum tribuit, Disfertatione Decima tota, tum ex nominibus Divinis, quæ Papa assumit vel admittit: tum ex attributis Divinis octo, quæ ille sibi vindicat: tum denique ex publica ejusdem adoratione liquidò probatum dedimus. Si ergo blasphemia & verissima & crassa est, ipsomet, uti supra vidimus Avila judice, affirmare de creatura, quod est proprium Dei; certè pridem Hierarchia, quæ & postulat Divinos illos honores Papæ, & admittit, & regit cum populum, eam Ecclesiam, quæ honores Divinos Papæ toto, quod ajunt, horreo admetitur, horribilium blasphemiarum reatum contraxit. Et sanè hoc inprimis blasphemiarum genus Prophetiam Babyloni & Bestiæ ejus, cujus capitibus nomina blasphemiæ aptat, tribuere, constat satis, & supra etiam probavimus.
units.tr: VII. That the hierarchy, which glories in its Pope or Numen as the ruler of that people or Church, ascribes divinity and the religious worship of adoration to him, we have shown clearly in the whole of the Tenth Dissertation: from the divine names that the Pope assumes or admits, from the eight divine attributes that he claims for himself, and finally from the public adoration paid to him. If therefore blasphemy is both true and gross, as Avila, whom we saw above, judges when he says that to affirm of a creature what is proper to God is blasphemy, then the hierarchy has long since incurred the guilt of most horrible blasphemies. It both demands those divine honours for the Pope and admits them, and rules the people with them. The same holds for the Church which, as they say, abhors with its whole being the giving of divine honours to the Pope, and yet admits them. It is well established that this kind of blasphemy in particular belongs to the Prophecy's Babylon and her Beast, to whose heads it attaches names of blasphemy, and we have also proved this above.

units.la: VIII. Hierarchiam virtutes & cultum Dei, multiplicem per idololatriam, creaturis impertiri, Dissertationis UndecimæSectione posteriore tota ad liquidum perduximus. In omni enim idololatria blasphemiæ continentur. Estque blasphemia pro idololatria posita ἑικασμὸς, Icasmus, seu schema Propheticum, rerum & eventuum repræsentatio per ejusmodi symbola, quæ similitudinem gerunt earum rerum, ac eventuum, pro quibus ponuntur. Etenim quod verba in Deum contumeliosa sunt ad aures, id creaturarum, atque in-primis imaginum cultus est ad oculos. Utroque enim id, quod adversus Deum contumelia est, declaratur. Neque adeo mirum est, quòd stylus Propheticus artificiosam rerum κρύψιν affectans. unum blasphemiæ genus in locum alterius, adeóque etiam blasphemiam illam, quæ est διὰ λόγων καὶ ῥημάτων in locum illius, quæ est διὰ πραγμάτων καὶ τύπων uti Chrysostomus de Divinis prædictionibus, distinguit, substituit. Ita Esaj. LXV.7. Qui suffierunt super montes, & super colles הרוני מעשנאים מ, probro, contumelia me affecerunt, adeóque blasphemârunt. non utique διὰ λόγων, sed πραγμάτων, per actiones suas idololatricas. Nam qui colunt idola quasi Deos, exprobrant Deo arrogantiam Divinitatis, inquit ibi Cornelius à Lapide. Similis locus est Ezech. xx. 27. 28. Hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Adhuc & in hoc me blasphemârunt Patres vestri. Introduxi enim eos in terram, super quam levavi manum meam, ut darem illam eis, & viderunt omnem collem excelsum, & omnem arborem densam, & sacrificârunt ibi sacrificia sua, dederúntque ibi irritationem oblationis suæ. Quod idem à Lapide & Sanctius de idololatria eorum rectè interpretantur. Convenit illud Deut. xxxi. 20. Cùm comederint, & saturati crassíque fuerint, avertentur ad Deos alienos נאצוני & blasphemabunt me. quomodo vox ינא Esaj. LII. 5. Ezech. xxxv. 12. usurpatur. Denique ubi Psal. LXIX. 10. dicit David: חרפות הרפיך על ילי ὀνειδισμοὶ τῶν ὀνειδιζόντων σε opprobria exprobrantium tibi ceciderunt super me, (perinde ac si dixisset, οἱ ἐλασφημίαι τῶν ἐλασφημούντων σε blasphemiæ blasphemantium te) Chaldæus Paraphraftes illud de contumelia, quæ Deo, cultum illius idolis communicando fit, interpretatur.
units.tr: VIII. That the hierarchy bestows the virtues and worship of God, manifold through idolatry, upon creatures, we have brought to full clarity in the latter section of the whole Eleventh Dissertation. For blasphemies are contained in all idolatry. Blasphemy put in place of idolatry is eikasmos [ἑικασμὸς], Icasmus, that is, a prophetic schema: a representation of things and events through such symbols as bear a likeness to the things and events for which they stand. For just as words insulting to God are heard by the ears, so the worship of creatures, and especially of images, is seen by the eyes. Both declare what is an insult against God. Nor is it surprising that the prophetic style, aiming at an artful krypsis of things, substitutes one kind of blasphemy for another, and so substitutes that blasphemy which is dia logōn kai rhēmatōn [διὰ λόγων καὶ ῥημάτων] for that which is dia pragmatōn kai typōn [διὰ πραγμάτων καὶ τύπων], as Chrysostom distinguishes in his work on divine predictions. Thus Isaiah 65:7: "Who have burned incense upon the mountains and reproached me upon the hills" [הרוני מעשנאים מ], and so have blasphemed, not indeed dia logōn, but pragmatōn, by their idolatrous actions. For, as Cornelius à Lapide says there, "those who worship idols as gods cast in God's face the arrogance of divinity." A similar passage is Ezekiel 20:27–28: "Thus says the Lord God: In this also your fathers have blasphemed me. For I brought them into the land over which I lifted up my hand, that I would give it to them; and they saw every high hill and every leafy tree, and there they sacrificed their sacrifices and gave there the provocation of their offering." Á Lapide and Sanctius rightly interpret this of their idolatry. That also fits Deuteronomy 31:20: "When they have eaten and are satisfied and grown fat, they will turn to other gods and will despise me [נאצוני] and blaspheme me," where the word is used as in Isaiah 52:5 and Ezekiel 35:12. Finally, where David says in Psalm 69:10: "The reproaches of those who reproach you [חרפות הרפיך] [ὀνειδισμοὶ τῶν ὀνειδιζόντων σε] have fallen upon me," as if he had said "the blasphemies of those who blaspheme you" [βλασφημίαι τῶν βλασφημούντων σε], the Chaldee paraphrast explains it of the insult done to God when his worship is shared with idols.

units.la: IX. Eandem ob causam Alcasar Nomina blasphemia in capitibus Bestiæ septem de Templis idolorum explicât, atque Grotius χαμεν ὀνομάτων βλασφημίας sic exponit: Plena Diis, qui ita interpretantur in veri Dei injuriam. Blasphemiam igitur pro idololatria poni, clarissimum est, recepto Sarcasmo Prophetico, uti diximus. Nihil enim detestabilem idololatriæ indolem magis explicat, quàm quòd is, qui creaturas colit, eas sine blasphemia in Deum verum colere non potest. Est enim idololatria certissimus & absolutus μυκτηρισμὸς & ἐκφαυλισμὸς, subsannatio & vilipendium Dei vivi, æquè profectò grave, quàm si quis Deum vilissimæ v. g. & insensatæ materiæ, ex quibus imagines conficiuntur, nominibus appellaret, profiteretúrque palam, Deum illa haud meliorem potiorémque esse. Dum enim Divinum illi cultum præstant, Deo æqualem utique faciunt. Atque hæc blasphemia aliorum digniorum objectorum, quæ tamen Dii non sunt, cultui ἀναλόγως subest. Infinita enim vilitate & ἀδιαίρετα fordescunt, si cum Deo conferantur.
units.tr: IX. For the same reason Alcasar explains the names of blasphemy on the seven heads of the Beast as referring to the temples of idols, and Grotius explains full of names of blasphemy thus: "full of gods, who in this way are interpreted to the injury of the true God." It is therefore quite clear, as we have said, that blasphemy is put for idolatry in the accepted prophetic sarcasm. For nothing explains more fully the detestable character of idolatry than the fact that whoever worships creatures cannot worship the true God without blasphemy. Idolatry is a most certain and complete mykterismos and ekphaulismos [μυκτηρισμὸς & ἐκφαυλισμὸς], a mocking and belittling of the living God, surely as grave as if someone were to call God by the names of the basest and most senseless matter from which images are made, and openly declared that God is no better or greater than they. For in rendering him divine worship they make him equal to them. And this blasphemy lies in the worship of other worthier objects, which nevertheless are not gods, in proportion to their worth. For they are rendered contemptible beyond measure, and by an infinite baseness, when compared with God.

units.la: X. Si tamen uspiam in religioso creaturarum cultu, quo Hierarchia defungitur, blasphemia conspicua est, maximè illa in Mariolatria, seu Deiparæ cultu religioso conspicua est. Non tantùm enim ea, quæ Deo Christóque eximia sunt, Mariolatræ ὁλῷ ψυλάττω in B. Virginem conferunt: quomodo eam paria cum Christo facere Mendoza Virid. prob. 2. lib. 2. sic scribit: Christus & Maria paribus Cherubinorum alis adumbrati sunt. Nam sicut paribus vibrantur alis: ita Christus & Maria paria Deo perhibent spectacula, dum hæc ostentat ubera, ille vulnera. Nihil est quod Christus ostendendo vulnera non impetret: nihil quod Maria ostendendo ubera non exoret. Videtis, Christi & Mariæ intercessionem æqualis ferè momenti esse apud Deum? Sed eandem Deo Christóque in multis, fima virgo & prudentissima, Deum in pueritia non solùm docuit, sed & ipsamet sociando se ipsam cum Christo, & eum portando in Ægyptum fecit nociva fugere. Sextò Deus hominem nutrivit de fructibus Paradisi; sed B. Virgo nutrivit Christum de proprio suo sacratissimo lacte; ubere de Cœlo pleno, cujus minima stilla prævalet omnibus fructibus Paradisi terrestris & totius mundi. Septimò Deus dedit hominì carnem, quæ posset mori, & incinerari per peccatum, ut nunc cernimus. Sed B. Virgo dedit Deo carnem immaculatam, quæ non posset incinerari, juxta illud Psalmi: Non dabis Sanctum tuum videre corruptionem. Concludit blasphemum illud os: Reddendo ergo singula singulis, scilicet quod fecit Deus homini, & quod fecit B. Virgo ipsi Deo, videbis, ut pro solatio dicere liceat, quòd PLUS MARIA DEO, quàm ipse Deus homini fecit. Unde Deus propter B. Virginem obligatur nobis plurimùm. Quid videtur, Mariolatræ? An crassius unquam idololatræ gentiles blasphemárunt? Et tamen innumera ejusmodi crassiora etiam afferri possent. & plura etiam superius allata à nobis sunt; atque inprimis Cl. Theologi nostri Rivetus & Drelincurtius, ex Mariolatrarum scriptis corrasa, quæ perpetuum in cultu & prædconio Deiparæ blasphemandi cacoëthes produnt, publico dederunt.
units.tr: X. If blasphemy is conspicuous anywhere in the religious worship of creatures that the Hierarchy practises, it is most conspicuous in Mariolatry, that is, in the religious worship of the Mother of God. The Mariolaters do not merely transfer to the Blessed Virgin what is outstanding in God and Christ, holding to it [ὅλῳ φυλάττω] with their whole effort. Mendoza, Virid. prob. 2. lib. 2., writes that Christ and Mary are alike: Christ and Mary are shadowed by the paired wings of the Cherubim. For as things are moved by paired wings, so Christ and Mary present to God a pair of spectacles, she showing her breasts, he his wounds. There is nothing Christ cannot obtain by showing his wounds; nothing Mary cannot win by showing her breasts. Do you see that the intercession of Christ and of Mary carries almost equal weight with God? The same most holy and most prudent Virgin, he says, not only taught God in his boyhood but also, by joining herself to Christ and carrying him into Egypt, made him flee from harm. Sixthly, God fed man with the fruits of Paradise; but the Blessed Virgin fed Christ with her own most sacred milk, a breast full of heaven, one tiny drop of which outweighs all the fruits of earthly Paradise and of the whole world. Seventhly, God gave man flesh that could die and turn to ash through sin, as we now see. But the Blessed Virgin gave God flesh that was spotless and could not turn to ash, according to the verse of the Psalm: You will not let your Holy One see corruption. That blasphemous mouth concludes: if we match each thing with each, what God did for man and what the Blessed Virgin did for God himself, you will see that, to comfort us, one may say that MARY DID MORE FOR GOD than God himself did for man. Hence God is greatly bound to us on account of the Blessed Virgin. What do you think of this, Mariolaters? Have the heathen idolaters ever blasphemed more crassly? Yet innumerable such cruder examples could be brought forward, and many more have been cited by us above; and above all our learned theologians Rivetus and Drelincurtius have published them, gathered from the writings of the Mariolaters, which reveal a constant itch to blaspheme in the worship and proclamation of the Mother of God.

units.la: XI. Facit huc omnis Hierarchicorum ἱεραρχικῶν, seu voluntarius cultus, in verbo Dei non præscriptus. Hic enim Divinam virtutem & efficaciam humanis instirutis, ceremoniis & operibus tribuit, adeóque Divina profanat, & alienat. quod citra blasphemiam fieri nequit. Faciun etiam huc dogmata Hierarchicorum, veluti de libero arbitrio & gratia Dei; determinatione gratiæ per vires arbitrii; de peregrinationibus religiosis; symbolica locorum sanctitate; votorum Monasticorum dignitate; operibus
units.tr: XI. Every Hierarchical [ἱεραρχικῶν], that is, voluntary, worship that is not prescribed in the Word of God belongs here. For it attributes the divine power and efficacy to human institutions, ceremonies and works, and so profanes and alienates what is divine, which cannot be done without blasphemy. The doctrines of the Hierarchy also belong here, such as those on free will and the grace of God; the determination of grace by the powers of the will; religious pilgrimages; the symbolic holiness of places; the dignity of monastic vows; works

units.la: supererogatoriis; consiliis perfectionis Euangelicæ; meri& shy;tis operum; satisfactionibus propriis & alienis; indulgen­tiis, Capite Ecclesiæ; infallibilitate Papæ; potestate legis­lativa & judiciali Papæ; efficacia Sacramentorum ex ope­re operato, nec non Sacramentalium; charactere Sacra& shy;mentali; intentionis Sacrificulorum ad efficaciam Sacra& shy;menti necessitate; Sacramentorum spuriorum efficacia; Missæ sacrificio propitiatorio; attritionis cum absolutione conjunctæ, ipsiúsque absolutionis efficacia; dispositionum quarundam, & habitus justitiæ inhærentis virtute ad justi­ficandum peccatorem; aliáque similia, quibus Divinam virtutem humanis habitibus, actibus, operibus, ritibus communicari, abundè à nostris, in conflictu cum Pontifi­ciis; & à me quoque in Anatome & Funere Concilii Tri­dentini demonstratum est. Quàm ergo hic blasphemiarum continuarum concatenatus ordo est? Adeò ut universus ferè Papatus & religio Hierarchica ex dogmatibus & fidei articulis, cum perpetuis blasphemiis, ea quæ Deo ἰξαίρετα & propria sunt, in alios omnes derivantibus (qua in re blasphemiam consistere supra, consentientibus ipsis adver­sariis, ostendimus) conjunctus esse, præsificinè, si res ipsa putetur, dici possit. Omnis falsa doctrina, quæ non po­test conjungi cum fundamento, idque vel evertit, vel so­lum & integrum esse fundamentum non permittit, bla­sphema est. Ipsa anathemata inflicta veritati, & errores soli anathemate præcepti, qualibus Tridentina Synodus scatet, totidem blasphemiæ sunt. Atque eodem inprimis pertinent doctrinæ dæmoniorum 1 Tim. iv. 1. 2. 3. quæ Papatum certis characteribus & notis insigniunt. Denique huc faciunt errores Hierarchicorum Magici, quos infra seorsim producemus. Nam in Magia omni horrendum Majestatis Divinæ loesæ crimen admittitur, dum Deus ita honore sibi eximio defraudatur, ut non tantum creaturæ præter, imò supra Creatorem inserviat Magus, sed Sathanam etiam, Dei hostem infensissimum, Dei ipsius de celsa arce sua deturbato, vice honoret.
units.tr: of supererogation; the counsels of evangelical perfection; the merit of works; satisfactions, both one's own and those of others; indulgences; the Head of the Church; the infallibility of the Pope; the Pope's legislative and judicial power; the efficacy of the sacraments ex opere operato, and likewise of the sacramentals; the sacramental character; the necessity of the priests' intention for the efficacy of a sacrament; the efficacy of spurious sacraments; the propitiatory sacrifice of the Mass; attrition joined with absolution, and the efficacy of absolution itself; certain dispositions and the power of an inherent habit of righteousness to justify the sinner; and other similar doctrines, by which the divine power is said to be communicated to human habits, acts, works and rites. Our men have shown this amply, in their conflict with the Papists, and I too have demonstrated it in my Anatomy and Funeral of the Council of Trent. How then is there not an unbroken chain of continuous blasphemies here? So much so that almost the whole Papacy and the Hierarchical religion, bound together by its doctrines and articles of faith with perpetual blasphemies, transfers to all others what is [ἐξαίρετα] peculiar to God (in which blasphemy consists, as we have shown above, with our adversaries agreeing), could be said, if the matter were thought through, to be a kind of prodigy. Every false doctrine that cannot be joined with the foundation, and either overturns it or does not allow the foundation to be whole and alone, is blasphemy. The anathemas hurled against the truth, and the errors laid down only by anathema, with which the Tridentine Synod abounds, are as many blasphemies. And to this category above all belong the doctrines of demons, 1 Tim. iv. 1, 2, 3, which mark the Papacy with its certain characters and signs. Finally, the errors of the Magical Hierarchs belong here, which we shall set out separately below. For in all magic the horrible crime of violating the Divine Majesty is committed, since God is so defrauded of his proper honour that the magician serves not only the creature beside, or rather above, the Creator, but also honours Satan, God's most bitter enemy, in God's stead, after God himself has been thrown down from his lofty citadel.

units.la: XII. Blasphemia Hierarchiæ capitalis, omnium blasphemiarum dux & pararia est contra Scripturam. Quia enim Scriptura instrumentum est, quo Deus Diaboli regnum debellat, & suum erigit; mirum non est, quòd Diabolus omni violentia & astu telum hoc Dei inutile reddere, & calumniis proscindere nunquam desinit. Cujus conatibus mirè equidem Hierarchici succollant.
units.tr: XII. The blasphemy of the chief hierarchy, the leader and source of all blasphemies, is against Scripture. Since Scripture is the instrument by which God overthrows the kingdom of the Devil and sets up his own, it is no surprise that the Devil never stops trying to render this weapon of God useless and to tear it apart with calumnies. The Hierarchs lend his efforts remarkable support.

units.la: XIII. Prædictum est, 2 Tim. iii. 2. in ultimis diebus futuros esse homines βλασφήμος blasphemos. Blasphemiarum species quædam v. 5. poni videtur. quòd futuri sint homines ἔχοντες μόρφωσιν εὐσεβείας, τὴν δὲ δύναμιν αὐτῆς ἠρνη- μένοι habentes formam, seu formationem pietatis, sed potestatem ejus negantes. Cùmque in S. Scriptura sola pietatis veræ informatio & formula contineatur, Scripturam, non externam quandam speciem pietatis, voce μορφώσεως τῆς εὐσεβείας intelligi, nihil certè vetat. Non defore ergo sensus est, qui Scripturam habeant, ostentent, præ se ferant, sed vim & potentiam ejus, quam in ea Apostolus v. 15. collocat, quòd possit nos sapientes reddere ad salutem; abnegent: ita ut expositio hæc ex ipsis Apostoli verbis petita videri debeat. Neque mens Apostoli ea duntaxat est, quòd, dum non ostendunt tales, verbum Dei in ipsis fuisse potens, vivum & efficax, instar ancipitis gladii, penetrantis usque ad divisionem animæ & Spiritus; adéoque in se pietatem per Dei verbum formatam non esse, re ipsa pronuntiant, verbum Dei non formare pietatem; sed hoc inprimis, quòd inter eorum dogmata & principales sententias, haud postrema ea futura sit, quòd Scriptura non possit formare pietatem. quæ blasphemia utique adversus Scripturam aperta est. Qui ergo sine omni verecundia dicunt, Scripturam solam non sufficere ad formandam pietatem: per se ipsam vel Divinitatem suam vel sapientiam & pietatem non posse docere, sed recipiendam esse secundum propositionem, testimonium, authoritatem, interpretationem Ecclesiæ, vel judicis Ecclesiastici infallibilis & supremi; item Scripturam esse mutam, ambiguam, obscuram, librum hæreticorum; ii vim & potentiam Scripturæ abnegant, & clarè satis, Scripturam id præstare posse, ut formet homines ad pietatem; posse sapientes facere ad salutem, inficiantur. Viderint ergo Hierarchici, talia γυμνῆ κιφαλῆ asseverantes, annon suas adversus Scripturam blasphemias à Spiritu S. sonorè prædictas, jure merito inferatur? Sed presslius agamus.
units.tr: XIII. It was foretold in 2 Tim. 3.2 that in the last days men would be blasphemous [βλασφήμος]. A certain kind of blasphemy seems to be indicated in v. 5, where it is said that men will have "a form of godliness, but denying its power" [ἔχοντες μόρφωσιν εὐσεβείας, τὴν δὲ δύναμιν αὐτῆς ἠρνημένοι]. Since the true form and pattern of godliness is contained in Holy Scripture alone, there is certainly nothing to prevent us from understanding by "the form of godliness" Scripture itself, and not some outward appearance of piety. So there will be people who have Scripture, who display it and parade it, but who deny its force and power, by which, the Apostle says in v. 15, it can make us wise unto salvation. This interpretation ought to seem drawn from the Apostle's own words. And the Apostle's meaning is not merely this: that when such people fail to show that the word of God is in them powerful, living and effective, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, they thereby declare in fact that godliness is not formed in themselves by the word of God, that the word of God does not form godliness. Above all, it means that among their doctrines and principal opinions there will be no minor one: that Scripture cannot form godliness. This is plainly an open blasphemy against Scripture. Those who shamelessly say that Scripture alone is not sufficient to form godliness, that by itself it cannot teach either its own divinity or wisdom and piety, but must be received according to the proposition, testimony, authority and interpretation of the Church, or of an infallible and supreme ecclesiastical judge; who also say that Scripture is mute, ambiguous, obscure, a book for heretics: these men deny the force and power of Scripture, and they plainly deny that it can make people godly or wise unto salvation. Let the Hierarchs consider whether, since they assert such things with bare head [γυμνῆ κιφαλῆ], it may not rightly be inferred that their blasphemies against Scripture were loudly foretold by the Holy Spirit. But let us press the matter more closely.

units.la: XIV. Habet ergo Hierarchia Scripturam, eámque Dei verbum esse profitetur verbis. Ubi verò ad demonstrationem Divinitatis hujus venitur, ejusmodi principia, ad suæ Ecclesiæ, hoc est, Papæ authoritatem supremam stabilendam, figit, ex quibus Scripturam nec authore, nec mandante Deo exaratam, adeóque nec verè Divinam esse, consequitur. Pertendit enim, Divinitatem hanc nec ex infitis suis proprietatibus, vel signaculis Divinitatis propriis sese cuivis conscientiæ hominis manifestantibus; nec ex revelatione quapiam, & testimonio interiore Spiritus S. cognosci, sed quoad nos unicè & in solidum à testimonio Ecclesiæ dependere. Ita Cusanus Epist. 2. ad Boh. Scripturarum, inquit, authoritas constituta est ab Ecclesiæ approbatione. Eccius Enchirid. cap. de auth. Eccl. resp. ad 3. obj. hæret. crassè satis: Scriptura non est authentica nisi authoritate Ecclesiæ. Gallus quidam, Sleidano ad A. 1553. referente, non plus tribuit Epistolis Pauli, quàm fabulis cÆsopi absque Ecclesiæ authoritate. Rationem ejus rei Vitus Miletus in difcurf. 600. error. Hefshusii p.
units.tr: XIV. The Hierarchy therefore has Scripture and professes in words that it is the word of God. But when it comes to demonstrating this divinity, it lays down principles of this kind, in order to establish the supreme authority of its Church, that is, of the Pope; from these it follows that Scripture, not written by the author or commanded by God, is not truly divine. For it maintains that this divinity is known neither from its inherent properties, nor from its own marks of divinity that make themselves manifest to every human conscience, nor from some revelation and the inward testimony of the Holy Spirit, but that for us it depends solely and wholly on the testimony of the Church. Thus Cusanus, in Epist. 2 to Bohemia, says: The authority of the Scriptures has been established by the approval of the Church. Eck, in the Enchiridion, chapter on the authority of the Church, reply to the third heretical objection, says quite crudely: Scripture is not authentic except by the authority of the Church. A certain Frenchman, as Sleidan reports for the year 1553, granted the Epistles of Paul no more weight than the fables of Aesop without the authority of the Church. The reason for this is given by Vitus Miletus in his Discourse 600 on the errors of Heshusius, p.

units.la: hanc reddit: Has enim esse Æsopi fabulas, nec adeò incongruentes hominum moribus, certa traditione hominum constat. Scripturas verò esse Canonicas, vel à Deo immediatè inspiratas, fideliter & incorruptè scriptas, & ad nos transmissas, si Ecclesiæ tollas authoritatem & traditionem, unde obsecro olearii isti cognoscent? Bailius Jesuita Catech. Controv. q. 12. haud impiè minùs: Sine Ecclesiæ authoritate non plus fidei adhiberem Matthæo, quàm Tito Livio. Vt quæst. 17. Quis dixit vobis, Scripturam esse Divinam? Quis, ei potiùs credendum, quàm historiis profanis & fabulis? Andradius Defens. Concil. Trid. lib. II. p. 157. Nihil (NB) quicquam, inquit, Divinitatis inest Scripturæ, quæ nos ad credendum, quæ in illis continentur, religione aliqua constringat, sed Ecclesiæ tanta vis est & amplitudo. Thomas Bozius de Signis Eccl. lib. xvj. 10. Quicquid Divina Scriptura authoritatis habet, id totum fuit atque est ab Ecclesia. Nam singuli ejus libri confecti sunt à filiis Ecclesiæ. Stapletonus Relect. Princip. doctr. controv. 4. pag. 495. Ecclesia, inquit, taxavit Scripturas. Bellarminus de verbo Dei lib. IV. 4. Etsi Scriptura dicat, libros Prophetarum & Apostolorum esse Divinos, tamen non certò id credam, nisi priùs credidero, Scripturam, quæ hoc dicit, esse Divinam. Non etiam in Alcorano Mahumeti passim legimus, ipsum Alcoranum de Cælo à Deo missum, & tamen ei non credimus.
units.tr: as follows: For it is established by the certain tradition of men that these are the fables of Aesop, and not too unlike the customs of men. But that the Scriptures are canonical, or immediately inspired by God, faithfully and incorruptly written and handed down to us: if you take away the authority and tradition of the Church, I ask you, how will those oil-men know this? The Jesuit Bailey, in his Catechism of Controversies, question 12, says no less impiously: Without the authority of the Church I would give Matthew no more credit than Livy. Likewise question 17: Who told you that Scripture is divine? Who says it should be believed rather than profane histories and fables? Andradius, Defence of the Council of Trent, book II, p. 157: Nothing (NB) of divinity is in Scripture that binds us by any religious obligation to believe what is contained in it, but so great is the power and extent of the Church. Thomas Bozius, On the Signs of the Church, book 16, chapter 10: Whatever authority Divine Scripture has, it has entirely from the Church and always has had. For each of its books was composed by the sons of the Church. Stapleton, Relectiones on the principal doctrines of controversy, 4, p. 495: The Church, he says, has judged the Scriptures. Bellarmine, On the Word of God, book IV, chapter 4: Even if Scripture says that the books of the Prophets and Apostles are divine, I would not believe this for certain unless I had first believed that the Scripture which says this is divine. Nor do we read everywhere in the Alcoran of Muhammad that the Alcoran itself was sent from heaven by God, and yet we do not believe it.

units.la: XV. Has similésque gnomas blasphemas prorsus esse, fatebuntur ultro omnes, quibus non est æs triplex circa pectus. Sic enim de humano arbitratu Divinitas pensitatur. Uti Ethnicis Tertullianus Apolog. cap. 5. objecit. Nec verbum Dei erit verbum Dei, nisi placuerit Romæ. quæ ipsa pro lubitu Scripturam in Alcoranum, Fabulis Æsopi, Titum Livium transformare, aut saltem id efficere, ut plus authoritatis non habeat, poterit. Dicebat Judæis Christus.
units.tr: XV. All who have not a triple bronze breastplate about their hearts will readily admit that these and similar maxims are utterly blasphemous. For in this way divinity is weighed by human judgement, as Tertullian objected to the heathen in his Apology, chapter 5. Nor will the word of God be the word of God unless it pleases Rome. Rome, at its pleasure, will be able to turn Scripture into the fables of Aesop or into Livy, or at least to bring it about that Scripture has no greater authority than these. Christ spoke this way to the Jews.

units.la: Joh.v.47. S Scripturis Mosis non creditis, quomodo verbis meis credetis? At Ecclesia Romana Christo se præferens, Si verbis meis non credatis, inquit, quomodo credetis scriptis vel Mosis, vel etiam omnium Prophetarum? S. Johannes 1 Joh. v.9. dicit: Si testimonium hominum accipitis, testimonium Dei majus est. Hierarchicis contra testimonium hominum testimonio Dei vim & authoritatem largitur. Quantò rectiùs Salvianus de gubernat. lib. 3. scribit: Alia omnia, id est, humana dicta argumentis & testibus egent. Dei autem sermo ipse sibi testis est, quia necesse est, quicquid incorrupta veritas loquitur, incorruptum sit testimonium veritatis. Hi autem verbi Divini hanc ἐνέργειαν, hanc δύναμιν potentiam, qua suam Divinitatem immediatè demonstret, & se Divinum esse φανερῶσαν τῆς ἀληθείας πρὸς πάντων (ὑπὸ ἡμῶν) manifestatione veritatis ad omnem conscientiam patefaciat, abnegantes, Deum ipsum in Scriptura loquentem impotentem, verbum ejus per se non vivum, non efficax, non penetrantius gladio ancipiti; sed mortuum, inefficax, obtusum faciunt, adeóque Deo auferentes, quod ipsi maximè competit, atque illud etiam in hominies, Romanam Ecclesiam, quæ in Pythagoricum Papæ oraculum resolvitur, transferentes, blasphemiæ maximæ rei sunt. Habent res Creatæ omnes cam facultatem, ut vim suam ipsæ exercere, & per actus propriarum qualitatum se demonstrare possint. Ita lux, ignis, gladius, malleus (cum his enim Scriptura comparatur) immediatè se lucendo, urendo, secando, pulsando demonstrant, quòd lux, ignis, gladius, malleus sint. Et DEUS creator, infinitè vivens, potens, efficax, in quo omnes creaturæ sunt, vivunt & moventur, hac potentia, vita & efficacia per summam audaciam & blasphemiam spoliatur, hominésque, qui sua natura mendaces, in rebus fidei haud aliter fidem merentur, quàm si Scripturarum revelatione dicta comprobent, quod impietatem auget, alienis hisce spoliis exornantur!
units.tr: John 5.47: If you do not believe Moses' Scriptures, how will you believe my words? But the Roman Church, setting itself above Christ, says: If you do not believe my words, how will you believe the writings of Moses, or indeed of all the Prophets? St John says in 1 John 5.9: If we receive the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater. The Hierarchs, on the contrary, grant force and authority to the testimony of men against the testimony of God. How much more rightly Salvian writes in On the Government of God, book 3: All other things, that is, human sayings, need arguments and witnesses. But the speech of God is itself its own witness, because whatever uncorrupted truth speaks must be an uncorrupted testimony of truth. But these men, denying to the word of God this energy [ἐνέργειαν], this power [δύναμιν], by which it might demonstrate its own divinity immediately, and by which it might reveal itself as divine to every conscience through the manifestation of truth [φανερῶσαν τῆς ἀληθείας πρὸς πάντων] (by us [ὑπὸ ἡμῶν]), make God speaking in Scripture powerless, his word not living in itself, not effective, not sharper than a two-edged sword, but dead, ineffective and blunt. Thus they take from God what belongs to him most of all, and transfer it to men, to the Roman Church, which dissolves into the Pope's Pythagorean dictum. They are guilty of the greatest blasphemy. All created things have this faculty, that they can exercise their force themselves and display themselves through the actions of their own qualities. So light, fire, a sword, a hammer (for Scripture is compared with these) show by their own action, by shining, burning, cutting and striking, that they are light, fire, sword and hammer. And God, the creator, infinitely living, powerful and effective, in whom all creatures live, move and have their being, is stripped of this power, life and efficacy with the greatest audacity and blasphemy. Men, who are by nature liars, merit faith in matters of faith no differently than if they confirm what they say by the revelation of Scripture. And how this impiety grows, when they adorn themselves with these borrowed spoils!

units.la: XVI. Nam quod Bellarminus lib.iij. de verbo Dei cap. 10. regerit, verbum Ecclesiæ, hoc est, Concilii vel Pontificis docentis ex cathedra non esse omnino verbum hominis, sed aliquomodo verbum Dei, quia prolatum sit assistente & gubernante Spiritu S. adeoque sic Divinitatem verbi non humano, sed Divino testimonio comprobari, dilutum sanè est. Cur enim Spiritus S. ex Papa loquens majorem vim & ἀξιομάτω habeat, quàm lo- quens in scripto, à Prophetis & Apostolis Divina inspiratione consignato? Cur illud pro testimonio immediatè Divino, hoc per se pro testimonio mortuo, nauci, neque majori pretio habendo, quàm quo fabulæ Æsopi & Alcoranus haberi debent, proclamatur? Quibus etiam notis clarioribus Spiritus ex Papæ spelunca proveniens, quàm verbum à Prophetis & Apostolis proditum, Divinitatem suam demonstrat? Sic planè Papam supra Scripturam efferri oportuit, ne ambiguum esset, cui oraculum de Antichristi ἀνόμου elatione quadret. Apostoli quidem & Prophetæ θεόπνευστοι Divinitus inspirati Spiritum S. habuerunt immediatè sibi assistentem, à quo φερόμενοι lati loquebantur Sancti illi Dei homines, 2 Pet. 1. 21. Si eadem ratione Ecclesia seu Papa Spiritum S. sibi assistentem habet, ejus igitur dicta omnia cum Scripturæ Propheticæ & Apostolicæ dictis paria facient; imò majora longè, quia Papa Divinitatem Scripturæ munire, Scriptura per se nec suam nec Papæ authoritatem confirmare poterit. Sin Papæ Spiritus S. assistit mediante Scriptura, sic ut nonnisi duce Scriptura loquens, & dicta sua cuncta suffulciens, (uti sanè post clausum Scripturæ Canonem sic mediatè, non immediatè Spiritus S. Ecclesiæ verè assistit) frustra ergo Bellarminus Papæ testimonium Scripturæ scilicet testimonio prius adeóadeóque Scripturæ ipsi neutiquam subjectum pro Divino venditat.
units.tr: XVI. As for Bellarminus, who replies in book 3 of De verbo Dei, chapter 10 that the word of the Church, that is, of a council or of a pope teaching ex cathedra, is not entirely the word of man, but is in some sense the word of God, because it is uttered with the Holy Spirit assisting and governing, and who thereby claims that the divinity of the word is confirmed by a human testimony and not a divine one, this is plainly refuted. For why should the Holy Spirit speaking through the Pope have greater force and authority than the Spirit speaking in writing, a writing set down under divine inspiration by the Prophets and Apostles? Why is the one proclaimed an immediately divine testimony, while the other is called in itself a dead testimony, worth nothing and to be held in no higher esteem than the fables of Aesop or the Qur'an? By what clearer marks does a Spirit coming from the Pope's cave demonstrate its divinity than the word handed down by the Prophets and Apostles? Clearly the Pope had to be exalted above Scripture in this way, so that there would be no doubt to whom the oracle about the elevation of the lawless one [ἀνόμου] of Antichrist applies. The Apostles and Prophets, divinely inspired [θεόπνευστοι], had the Holy Spirit present to them immediately, and it was by him that those holy men of God, borne along [φερόμενοι], spoke (2 Pet. 1.21). If the Church or the Pope has the Holy Spirit present to him in the same way, then all his sayings will be equal to the sayings of the prophetic and apostolic Scriptures, and indeed far greater, since the Pope would confirm the divinity of Scripture, whereas Scripture in itself could not confirm either its own authority or the Pope's. But if the Holy Spirit assists the Pope through the mediation of Scripture, so that he speaks only under the guidance of Scripture and supports all his sayings by it (as indeed, after the canon of Scripture was closed, the Holy Spirit truly assists the Church in this mediated, not immediate, way), then Bellarminus vainly offers the Pope's testimony as divine, a testimony which depends first on the testimony of Scripture and is by no means superior to Scripture itself.

units.la: XVII. Ad Scripturæ dignitatem eximiam facit, quòd eam Scriptores Sacri non temerè vel forte quadam, sed expresso Dei mandato exarárunt: quódque ea Ecclesia curare non potest. Hæc ejusdem laus citra sacrilegium & blasphemiæ crimen delibari nequit. Delibárunt tamen Hierarchici. Bellarminus enim de Verbo Dei lib. iv. 4. sic arguit: Si Christo & Apostolis fuisset propositum verbum Dei coarctandi & restringendi ad Scripturam, inprimis rem tanti momenti Christus apertè præcepisset, & Apostoli alicubi testarentur, se ex mandato Domini scribere, quemadmodum ex mandato Domini in toto orbe docuerunt. At id nusquam legimus. Pistorius in Hodeget. pag. 32. Apostoli, inquit, non scripserunt ex proposito, sed propter incidentem necessitatem. Et pag. 33. non ex mandato. Commune ergo dogma est, non mandato aliquo Divino inductos, sed occasionibus fortuitis invitatos Scriptores sacros se ad scribendum accinxisse. Quod profecto Scripturæ authoritatem immane quantum labefactat. Quis enim authenticum documentum dixerit, quod forte fortuna, non mandante Rege ac Domino, sed occasione duntaxat invitante scriptor quispiam exaraverit? Inprimis si non suam is, sed alienam voluntatem, alienas præceptiones scripto complecti debuerit? Pari contumelia illi Scripturæ necessitatem oppugnant. Bellarminus sanè de Verbo Dei lib. iv. 4. demonstraturus, quòd Scripturæ sine traditionibus simpliciter necessariæ non fuerint, sic sententiam suam declarat, quòd necessariæ fuerint non simpliciter, sed ad bene esse, hoc est, utiles duntaxat. Inter alia hoc argumento utitur, quòd etiam extante Scriptura Judæi traditione potiùs quàm Scriptura usi fuerint, quia usque ad tempora Esdræ Scripturæ non fuerint redactæ ad formam librorum, ut facilè & commodè haberi possent; sed dispersæ in variis annalibus & chartis, & aliquando ex negligentia Sacerdotum longo tempore non inveniebantur. Impium & blasphemum hoc dogma est, in inferno cusum, & Hierarchicis obstetricantibus editum, quod homines non amantes veritatem à Divina revelatione ad humanam dictaturam; à vera regula ad fucum; ab obedientia Dei ad obedientiam Diaboli; à studio scrutandi Scripturam ad ejus contemptum; à fide veritatis ad ignorantiam & stultas opiniones; à Christo ad Antichristum; à glorificatione Dei ad ejusdem blasphemationem præcipite gradu deducit. Quid quæso magis δύσφημον, & ab omni fide abhorrens audiri potest, quàm Scripturam Divinitus inspiratam non esse necessariam? Ea scilicet, hominum sapientia, prudentia, φρόνησις, vigilantia, bonæ conscientiæ studium est, ut Scriptura utilis quidem aliquatenus, sed non necessaria sit! Necessaria est traditio, cujus tamen nulla Divina certitudo & αληροφορία haberi potest. Necessaria est Papæ vicaria potestas & infallibilitas, ut ab unius hominis ore pendeant omnes. At Scriptura, cujus revelatione nulla alia certior in mundo extat, necessaria non est!
units.tr: XVII. It contributes to the outstanding dignity of Scripture that the sacred writers did not write it rashly or by some chance, but by the express command of God; and this is something the Church cannot claim for itself. This praise of Scripture cannot be diminished without the crime of sacrilege and blasphemy. Yet the hierarchs have diminished it. For Bellarminus argues thus in De verbo Dei, book 4, chapter 4: If it had been the purpose of Christ and the Apostles to limit and restrict the word of God to Scripture, Christ would first have clearly commanded so important a matter, and the Apostles would somewhere have testified that they wrote by the command of the Lord, just as by the command of the Lord they taught throughout the world. But we nowhere read this. Pistorius, in Hodegetica, page 32: The Apostles, he says, did not write from purpose, but on account of an incidental necessity. And page 33: not by command.
