The Jesuit Baunius, Tract. 10, p. 474: No law or canon, he says, obliges parish priests to sacrifice daily, indeed he wrote, along with others, that such a law could not even be given, since a law of this kind would doubtless expose them to the danger of mortal sin, to which one bound to sacrifice daily would be exposed, since it is difficult and arduous, amid the tides of the world which wash about on all sides, never to cling to the foul sea of vices. He soon removes the fear of this danger, offering a reason: because priests, even if they commit mortal sins from time to time, can nevertheless sacrifice daily, and even take up the obligation of daily sacrificing for a stipend received. Because, he says, it is the priest's right to exercise contrition at all times, the power of returning to God at any moment of time through love and hatred of sin; if he does not fulfil this duty, let him impute the fault to himself. And so that he may remove those difficulties by which they might be most drawn back from celebrating the sacrifice daily, he speaks thus at p. 457: If, after a carnal union with a woman that day, or a voluntary pollution, the priest has confessed, will it be free for him to engage in divine service without venial fault? Villalobos denies it, &c. Sancius dissents, whose opinion seems to me both safe and to be followed in practice. Montaltius receives these words thus in the Epistles of Provence, 6: So, with Baunius as surety, shall a priest so stained with so great a sin present himself at the awful altar? How much more religiously would he obey the ancient canons of the Church, which kept priests polluted with such disgraces from the office of sacrificing in perpetuity, or at least for a long time, whom the recent doctrines of your writers drive away from sin? He agrees with Baunius on this.

units.la: Tom. II. xx MafcaMascarenhas Tract. 4. Disput. 5. num. 284. docet; & nequid sceleratam ipsius in flagitiosos Sacerdotes & laicos indulgentiam fugeret, asserit, id locum habere non in fornicatione tantùm; sed generatim in qualicunque pollutione mortaliter peccaminosa, seu habita secum, vel cum complice; & hoc sive habeatur per fornicationem, sive per adulterium, sive per peccatum contra naturam, seu quocunque alio modo. Et quamvis, inquit, P. Vasquez credat, antiquitus fuisse aliquam legem vel universalem, vel provincialem, qua per aliquot saltem horas post pollutionem prohibeatur communio, ut videntur ostendere loca superiùs dicta: hoc tamen hodie communi & universali totius orbis consuetudine est abrogatum.
units.tr: Mascarenhas, Tract. 4, Disput. 5, num. 284, teaches the same (Tom. II, xx); and lest anything escape his criminal indulgence towards sinful priests and laymen, he asserts that this holds not only in fornication, but generally in any pollution that is mortally sinful, whether undertaken alone or with an accomplice; and whether this happens by fornication, by adultery, by a sin against nature, or in any other way. And although, he says, Father Vasquez believes that there was once some law, either universal or provincial, by which communion was forbidden for at least some hours after pollution, as the passages cited above seem to show, yet today this has been abrogated by the common and universal custom of the whole world.

units.la: XLVI. Nulla equidem magis detestanda, atque à Christianorum, maximè Sacerdotum Sanctitate magis abhorrentia sunt crimina, quàm illa, inquit, libidinum furiae in corpora, in sexus, ultra jura naturae. Harum reis nein fine quidem dandam esse communionem, Eliberitanum Concilium decernit. Ancyranum, quod cum eis paulò remissius egit, non breviorum quàm viginti annorum poenitentiam indicit. Hujus decreta A. DCCLXXXIX. in Concilio Aquisgranensi cap. 49. & A. DCCCXXIX. in Concilio Parisiensi renovata sunt. Postremò varii Pontifices, & novissimè Pius V. contra Clericos Sodomitas Bullam edidit, in qua inter alia haec verba legere est: Horrendum illud scelus, quo polluta sedataque civitates à tremendo Dei judicio conflagrárunt, acerbissimum nobis dolorem inurit, gravitérque animum nostrum commovet, ut ad illud quantum fieri poterit, comprimendum studia nostra conseramus. Sanè Lateranensi Concilio cognoscitur constitutum, ut quicunque Clerici illa in continentia, quae contra naturam est, propter quam ira venit in filios diffidentiae, deprehensi fuerint laborare, à Clero dejiciantur, vel ad agendam in Monasteriis pœnitentiam detrudantur. Verum ne tanti flagitii contagium immunitatis spe, quæ maxima peccandi illecebra est, fidentius invalescat, clericos hujus criminis nefarii reos, gravius ulciscendos deliberavimus; ut qui animæ interitum non horrescunt, hos certè deterreat civilium legum vindex gladius Secularis. Itaque quod nos jam in ipso Pontificatus nostri principio hac de re decrevimus, plenius nunc fortiusque persequi intendentes, omnes & quoscunque Presbyteros, & alios clericos feculares, cujuscunque gradús & dignitatis, tam dirum nefas exercentes, omni privilegio clericali, omnique officio, dignitate & beneficio ecclesiastico præsentis canonis authoritate privamus. Gravis scilicet, Pii Papæ districto judicio; pœna, quam constat disciplina adhuc utcunque vigente vel iis, qui simpliciter fornicabantur, dictatam esse! Constat tamen inde, ex eo tempore, quo vetus illa disciplina collapsa est, ad Pium V. usque tam frequens sceleus isthoc fuisse, ut comprimendum ille duxerit; quin & patrantibus illud impune fuisse; & licuisse iis crimen illud exercentibus esse Sacerdotibus, Presbyteris, religiosis. Quo verò successu Pius Bullâ suâ crimen isthoc suppressit? Tali certè, ut ludificari illam Jesuitæ religioni non duxerint. Escobarius enim Tract. j. Exam. 8. num. 102. quærit: Num Bulla Pii V. contra Clericos Sodomitas obliget in foro conscientiæ? Pulchra scilicet quæstio, ad quam pulchrius sic respondet: Henriquez sentit, usu non esse receptam probabiliter, nec in conscientiæ foro obligare. Quòd si usu recepta sit, clericus fœminam in indebito subigens vase, non committit Sodomiam propriè, quia licet non servet debitum vas, servat tamen sexum. Nec incurrit ex Suario pœnas Bullæ intra vas masculi semen non immittens, quia delictum non est consummatum. Nec ex eodem, qui nonnisi bis aut ter in Sodomiam sint lapsi: quia Pontifex ricis Sodomiam exercentibus infligit. Suario) ante sententiam judicis declar Bullæ in foro conscientiæ incurrunt: qu nalis obligat homines ad se prodendum. exercentem Sodomiam, si sit contritus beneficio, officio, & dignitate, omnino e Puderet in [?]ordibus hisce, castis c ram aut camarinam movere, nisi vel inde constare mrate horrendum illud hoc scelus, cœlesti ... phure expiatum, patrantes etiam clericos ... clim, ac nuper etiam donaverint.
units.tr: XLVI. There are no crimes more detestable, or more contrary to the holiness of Christians, and especially of priests, than those furies of lust, he says, against bodies and sexes, beyond the laws of nature. The Council of Elvira decrees that communion must not be given to the guilty of these, not even at the end. The Council of Ancyra, which dealt with them somewhat more leniently, imposes a penance of no less than twenty years. Its decrees were renewed in the Council of Aachen in 789, chapter 49, and in the Council of Paris in 829. Finally, various popes, and most recently Pius V, issued a bull against Sodomite clerics, in which these words, among others, can be read: That horrible crime, by which cities polluted with it were burned up by the dreadful judgment of God, causes us the most bitter grief and deeply moves our mind, so that we shall apply our efforts to suppress it as far as possible. Indeed, it is known to have been decreed by the Lateran Council that any clerics found to be labouring in that unchastity which is against nature, on account of which the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disbelief, shall be cast out from the clergy or thrust into monasteries to perform penance. But lest the contagion of so great a disgrace should grow more boldly under the hope of immunity, which is the greatest allurement to sin, we have resolved to punish more severely the clerics guilty of this nefarious crime, so that those who do not shudder at the destruction of their souls may at least be deterred by the avenging sword of the secular civil laws. Therefore, intending now more fully and more strongly to pursue what we decreed at the very beginning of our pontificate on this matter, we deprive by the authority of this present canon all and any presbyters and other secular clerics, of whatever rank and dignity, who practise so dire a crime, of every clerical privilege, every office, dignity and ecclesiastical benefice. A grave penalty indeed, by the strict judgment of Pope Pius! It is agreed that the penalty was laid down, under that ancient discipline still in some measure in force, even for those who simply fornicated. Yet it is clear from this that, from the time when that old discipline collapsed until Pius V, this crime was so frequent that he thought it had to be suppressed; indeed, those who committed it went unpunished, and it was permitted to priests, presbyters and religious who practised that crime. But with what success did Pius suppress this crime by his bull? Certainly of such a kind that the Jesuits did not think it worth mocking that bull. For Escobar, Tract. 1, Exam. 8, num. 102, asks: Does the bull of Pius V against Sodomite clerics bind in the forum of conscience? A fine question indeed, to which he answers even more finely: Henriquez thinks that it has not been probably received by use, nor does it bind in the forum of conscience. But if it has been received by use, a cleric who forces a woman in an improper vessel does not commit sodomy properly, since, although he does not keep to the proper vessel, he keeps the sex. Nor, according to Suarez, does he incur the penalties of the bull who does not emit semen within the male vessel, since the offence is not consummated. Nor, by the same authority, those who have fallen into sodomy only twice or three times, because the Pope inflicts (penalties) on those who practise sodomy ... [the rest is corrupt in the text], according to Suarez, before the judge's sentence, they incur the declared penalties of the bull in the forum of conscience, which compels men to betray themselves; if one practising sodomy is contrite, he is entirely (restored) to benefice, office and dignity. It would be shameful to stir, in these pages of chastity, such filth and ..., unless it were thereby clear that this horrible crime was atoned for by heavenly ... and that clerics who committed it were even recently granted ... pardon.

units.la: ALVII. Accedunt his omnibus indulgenvenialcs venalesque, & vilissima pretia pro& absolutionibus à peccatis luxuriæ etiam gravissimis, quæ authoritate ipsius Summi ceu infallibilem judicem illi adorant, conta, latam sceleribus his indulgendi pro liriunt, cum se per indulgentissimum hunc menicum, Catholicum Ecclesiæ Mitio tantùm non invitari & animari libidinum intelligunt. Post collapsam equidem Eccl. injuncta à Sacrificulis pœnitentia trifariam puta castigatione corporis, solutione pecutiarum acquisitione. Castigatio corporis vel in verborum pallione constitit. Solutio chardus Decret. lib. xix. meminit. Si quis non potuerit jejunare, & habuerit, unde si dives fuerit, pro septem hebdomadibus ginti. Si non habuerit, unde totidem dare dos decem: Si autem multum pauper fuetres. Concilium quoque Lateranense SepSphemus, inquit, si nobilis fuerit, pœna multictetur, & pro secunda vice 50. fabricæ Basilicæ Principis Apostolorum de urbe applicandis. Et Baronius A. C. MLV. §. 9. Non ignores, quia cùm à pœnitentibus terras, possessiones agrorum videlicet accipimus, juxta mensuram muneris eis de quantitate pœnæ relaxamus. Quibus plane ostendit Damianus, bona ecclesiastica ejusmodi fieri solita redemptione aucta crevisse. Hæc jam Seculo XI. acta sunt.
units.tr: XLVII. To all this are added indulgences for sale, and absolutions from sins of lust, even the most grave, at cheap and vile prices, which they adore, by the authority of the Supreme Pontiff as an infallible judge, and which are issued for the licence of these sins, since they understand that by this most indulgent ... Catholic Church they are almost invited and encouraged in their lusts. Indeed, after the Church's discipline had collapsed, the penance imposed by the little priests was of three kinds: castigation of the body, payment of money, and acquisition [of merit]. Castigation of the body consisted in the beating of words. Burchard, Decretum, book 19, mentions payment: If someone cannot fast, and has the means, let him, if rich, pay for seven weeks ... If he has not the means, let him give as many ... ; if he is very poor ... The Lateran Council also ... Sepsphemus, it says, if he is noble, let him be fined, and for a second offence let fifty ... be applied to the building of the Basilica of the Prince of the Apostles in the city. And Baronius, A.D. 1055, §9: Do not be unaware that, when we receive lands and possessions of fields from penitents, we relieve them of part of the penalty according to the measure of the gift. Damian clearly shows that the church's goods, increased by such redemption as was customary, grew. These things were already done in the eleventh century.

units.la: - XLVIII. Ex collectis redimendæ pœnitentiæ taxationibus cusa diuque in Pœnitentiali foro usitata, tandem Lutetiæ apud Iossanum Denis. in 4. A. MDXX. Taxa Cameræ, seu Cancellariæ Apostolicæ dias in luminis auras, futura Babylonicæ Hierarchicorum impuritatis & impietatis perpetuus, omnique exceptione major testis, prodiit. De libro eo sic Claudius Espencæus in Epist. ad Tit. cap. 1. Oper. pag. m. 479. scribit: Profitat & in quæstu pro meretrice sedet Liber palam ac publicè hic (Lutetiæ, ubi ille docuit & scripsit) impressus, & hodiéque, ut olim, venalis, Taxa Camerae seu Cancellariæ Apostolicæ, inscriptus: in quo plus scelerum discas licet, quàm in omnibus omnium vitiorum Summistis & Summariis, & plurimis quidem licentia, omnibus autem absolutio emptu rientibus proposita. Parco nominibus. Nam quod ait nescio quis,
units.tr: XLVIII. From the collected tariffs for redeeming penance, printed and long in use in the penitential forum, the Taxa Camerae, or of the Apostolic Chancery, at last came forth into the light at Paris, at the press of Jean Denis, in quarto, in 1520, destined to be a lasting and, beyond all objection, unimpeachable witness to the Babylonian impurity and impiety of the hierarchy. Claude d'Espence, in his commentary on the Epistle to Titus, chapter 1 (Works, p. 479), writes of this book thus: This book, printed openly and publicly here (in Paris, where he taught and wrote), and still sold for gain like a harlot sitting for hire, is entitled the Taxa of the Camera or of the Apostolic Chancery. In it you may learn more crimes than in all the Summists and Summaries of all vices, and for many a licence is offered, and for all who buy it absolution. I will spare names. For what someone said is true:

units.la: Nomina sunt ipso penè timenda sono.
units.tr: Names are almost to be feared for their very sound.

units.la: Mirum hoc tempore, hoc schismate non suppressum tot tamque fœdorum, tamque horrendorum scelerum velut indicem adeo infamem, ut non putem, in Germania, Helvetia, & ubicunque à Romana sede defectum est, opus proflare majore hujus scandalo. Et adeò tamen non supprimitur ab Ecclesiæ Romanæ favitoribus, ut tantorum ac talium facinorum licentiæ ac impunitates, in facultatibus legatorum illuc huc venientium bona ex parte immoventur.
units.tr: It is strange that at this time, in this schism, a work so infamous, listing so many and such foul and horrible crimes, was not suppressed. I do not think that any work has circulated more scandalously in Germany, Switzerland, or wherever the Roman see has been abandoned. And yet it is not suppressed by the supporters of the Roman Church, so that the licences and impunities of such great and such crimes are, in part, brought and carried into effect through the faculties of the legates who come hither and thither.

units.la: Taxa pœnit. tentiaria impuritatis. quasvis species pecuniaæ pretio asfirmatis. exemplo tremā immobilitas ab ipso claudio. Episcopa depilla. ventur atque confirmentur, adversus quaecunque fatalia restituendi, ac etiam rios, Mamseres, Bastardos, ex quocun tu &c. cum his, qui se per adulterium po nubere possint, perjuros, Simoniacos, fa usurarios, schismaticos, haereticos, sed non absolvendi tantum, sed & ad ordine tates & beneficia, quaecunque, quotcunqu dispensandi, homicidas quoque, sed casu tarios; nam nec voluntarios quidem ex rior, presbytericidas, parricidas, matr das, sororicidas, uxoricidas, infanticid cantatrices, concubinarios, adulteros affinibus aut consanguineis, denique cor brutis &c. Habeat jam Roma pudorem frontis criminum omne genus catalogu sinat.
units.tr: The Penitentiary tariff of impurity [sets a price on] every kind of sin for money: [it grants] dispensation and absolution to those who are to be restored and confirmed, against any fatal impediment, and also to those born of adultery, bastards, from any source ... with those who can marry after having committed adultery, perjurers, simonists, usurers, schismatics, heretics; not only absolved but also admitted to orders, dignities and benefices, however many, and dispensed; also murderers, not only involuntary but also voluntary, and those who killed by chance; also presbyter-killers, parricides, matricides, sororicides, uxoricides, infanticides, witches, concubinaries, adulterers with relatives by marriage or blood, and finally incestuous persons, beasts and so on. Let Rome now have the shame of her brazen face: let her allow a catalogue of every kind of crime.

units.la: XLIX. Feralis hujus libri, Babylon gnissimi, exemplaria, ab ipsis Hierarch diximus, necnon Venetiis in Oceano Ja nibus nostris versantur. Extat etiam T tentiaria, jussu Procerum Imperii Pre in cujus titulo de causis matrimonialib gere est: In secundo consanguinitatis ve dispensatur tantum per Signoriam Pacante, per Summum Pœnitentiarium nensium 50. duc. 12. Karl. 6. In prim dispensatur in foro conscientiæ tantùm 30. duc. 7. Karl. 6. Quando adulter, v contrahendo dedit, vel de facto contr fuerit mortem alterius conjugi cum esse illo dispensatur, ut cum altero contraha tractu tantum dispensatur (dummodo tus occultum) in foro conscientiæ tantùm, & taxa est tur. 36.duc. 9. Cum eo, qui vovit perpetuam castitatem, dispensatur in foro conscientiæ tantùm, & taxa est 16.duc. Karl. 6. Si quis in sacris ordinibus fit constitutus (modò id fit occultum) uxorem duxerit, dispensatur cum illo, ut possit in conjugio manere, donec uxor vixerit, postea abstineat à matrimonio, & in illo constitutus officium B. Virginis Mariæ saltem diebus festis dicat per modum satisfactionis, & taxatur tur. 15.duc. 4. Titulo de Lapsu carnis ejusmodi dispensatio sancitur: Absolutio à lapsu carnis super quocunque actu libidinoso commisso per Clericum, etiam cum Monialibus intra & extra septa Monasterii, aut cum consanguineis, vel affinibus, aut filia spirituali, aut quibusvis aliis, sive ab unoquoque de per se, sive simul ab omnibus absolutio petatur, cum dispensatione ad ordines & beneficia, cum inhibitione, turon. 36. duc. 3. Titulo proximè sequenti de Bestialitate dispensationes bestiales ejusmodi legere est: Si verò cum illis petatur absolutio, etiam à crimine commisso contra naturam, vel cum brutis, cum dispensatione, ut supra, & cum inhibitione, turon. 90.duc. 12. Karl. 6. Si verò petatur tantùm absolutio à crimine contra naturam, vel cum brutis, cum dispensatione & cum inhibitione turon. 36.duc. 9. Absolutio pro Moniali, quæ se permisit à pluribus cognosci intra & extra septa Monasterii, cum rehabilitate ad dignitates illius ordinis, etiam Abbatialem, tur. 36.duc. 9. Absolutio pro concubinario, cum dispensatione ad ordines & beneficia, tur. 21.duc. 5. Karl. 6. & cum inhibitione tur. 36.duc. 9. Pro laico à lapsu carnis super quocunque actu libidinoso, in foro conscientiæ, tur. 6.duc. 2. Ab incestu pro laico, in foro conscientiæ tantùm, tur. 4. Si petatur pro utroque, videlicet pro viro & muliere, in utroque foro, tur. 18.duc. 4. Karl. 9. Si cum inhibitione pro pro uno tantùm, tur. 24. duc. 6. Si pro utroque cum in-hibitione, tur. 36. duc. 9. Absolutio pro laico, in foro conscientiæ, tur. 4. Ab adulterio cum incestu, pro una persona tantùm, tur. 6. Pro adultero & adultera simul, tur. 6. duc. 2. Quid quæso, reputa mecum, quisquis non plane pietatis & frontis expers es, Latialis ille flamen magis pietati, puritati, castitati adversum: quid libidinosis belluis omnibus ad explendas nefarias libidines opportunius: quid ad seducendos eos, quorum nondum animi libidinibus corrupti sunt, efficacius excogitare potuit? Quando videlicet is, nummo solo sponsore, impunitatem nefandorum sclerum, & solutionem sacrarum legum, in ipso foro Divino, sordida adeò benignitate, largiri non erubuit.
units.tr: XLIX. Copies of this deadly book, Babylon's most impure, as we have said, from the hierarchs themselves, are also in circulation at Venice and in our own hands. There is also a Penitentiary, issued by order of the magnates of the Empire; in its title concerning matrimonial causes, the following is found: In the second degree of consanguinity, dispensation is granted only by the Signory of Pavia, through the Supreme Penitentiary, 50 ducats, 12 Karl. 6. In the first, dispensation is granted in the forum of conscience only, 30 ducats, 7 Karl. 6. When an adulterer gave his promise in contracting, or in fact contracted the marriage after having caused the death of the other spouse, dispensation is granted that he may marry the other, in the forum of conscience only (provided the thing is kept hidden), and the tax is 36 ducats, 9 (Karl.). With one who has vowed perpetual chastity, dispensation is granted in the forum of conscience only, and the tax is 16 ducats, Karl. 6. If someone has been constituted in holy orders (provided this is done secretly) and has taken a wife, dispensation is granted with him that he may remain in marriage as long as the wife lives; afterwards he should abstain from marriage, and, being constituted in that office, say the office of the Blessed Virgin Mary at least on feast days by way of satisfaction; and the tax is 15 ducats, 4 Karl. Under the title On the Lapse of the Flesh, such a dispensation is sanctioned: Absolution from the lapse of the flesh for any lustful act committed by a cleric, even with nuns inside or outside the cloister, or with blood relations or in-laws, or with a spiritual daughter, or with any others, whether each one seeks absolution separately or all together, with dispensation for orders and benefices, with prohibition, [tax] 36 ducats, 3. Under the immediately following title, On Bestiality, such bestial dispensations may be read: If absolution is sought also from the crime committed against nature, or with beasts, with dispensation as above and with prohibition, [tax] 90 ducats, 12 Karl. 6. If only absolution from the crime against nature, or with beasts, is sought, with dispensation and with prohibition, [tax] 36 ducats, 9. Absolution for a nun who has allowed herself to be known by several men inside or outside the cloister, with rehabilitation to the dignities of that order, even the abbatial, [tax] 36 ducats, 9. Absolution for a concubinary, with dispensation for orders and benefices, [tax] 21 ducats, 5 Karl. 6, and with prohibition, [tax] 36 ducats, 9. For a layman from the lapse of the flesh for any lustful act, in the forum of conscience, [tax] 6 ducats, 2. From incest for a layman, in the forum of conscience only, [tax] 4. If it is sought for both, that is for husband and wife, in both forums, [tax] 18 ducats, 4 Karl. 9. If with prohibition for one only, [tax] 24 ducats, 6. If for both with prohibition, [tax] 36 ducats, 9. Absolution for a layman, in the forum of conscience, [tax] 4. From adultery with incest, for one person only, [tax] 6. For adulterer and adulteress together, [tax] 6 ducats, 2. Consider with me, I ask you, whoever you are, not wholly devoid of piety and shame: what could that Latin priest devise more favourable to beasts of every lust, for satisfying their nefarious desires, or more effective for seducing those whose minds are not yet corrupted by lusts? Since he, with a single coin as surety, did not blush to grant, in the very forum of God, with such sordid generosity, impunity for nefarious crimes and the dissolving of sacred laws.

units.la: L. Illud insuper non eorum duntaxat, qui laxis coeteroquin habenis in omne impuritatis genus præcipites ruerunt; sed eorum etiam, qui nondum pudorem omnem exuerunt, animis facem ad impietatem & luxuriam subdere potest, quòd non præteritis duntaxat, sed futuris etiam peccatis indulgentiarum φάρμακοι & olim applicari suevit, & hodieque solet. Pridem enim est, quòd tum in confessionalibus sic nuncupatis, & per omnem vitam duraturis: tum in indulgentiarum diplomatis peccata deinceps, longo etiam temporis tractu patranda liberaliter, remitti consueverunt. Unde pœnarum relaxationes non unius duntaxat vel diei, vel anni; ac ne decem quidem: vel etiam trecentorum, (quibus pœnam Purgatorii nonnulli determinabant) sed plurium chiliadum. Sola Roma, ejúsque stationes plura annorum millia numerat, quàm Romanensibus Theologis castioribus probetur. De stationibus Romæ A. MCCCCLXXV. Romæ Latinâ linguâ: post ejusdem Seculi A. XCI. Norimbergæ editus liber, Ecclesiarum Romanarum principalium inprimis septem, indulgentias prodit. Unius Ecclesiæ Lateranensis, speciminis gratia, indulgentias pandamus. In ea, sic liber ille recenset, quotidie distribuuntur 48. anni indulgentiarum, & totidem quadragenæ, ac remissio tertiæ partis omnium peccatorum. Unde Bonifacius: Si quis ad sedem nostram Lateranensem, devotionis, orationis, aut peregrinationis causa venit, ille absolvetur ab omnibus peccatis. In capella, quæ vocatur Sanctum Sanctorum, quámque mulieribus non licet ingredi, est vera & plenaria remissio omnium peccatorum. In eadem capella sunt gradus 28. qui steterunt ante domum Pilati in Hierusalem; & quicunque hos gradus ascenderit cum devotione, habet pro quolibet gradu novem annos indulgentiarum, & totidem quadragenas, ac remissionem tertiæ partis omnium peccatorum. Qui verò genuflexando gradus illos ascendit, unam animam, pro qua orat, liberat ex purgatorio. In die dedicationis, qui vocatur dies Salvatoris, est ibi plena remissio omnium peccatorum, à culpa & à pœna. Cùmque Papa primùm indulgentiam ibi largiretur, Angeli, præsente populo, dixerunt Amen. Item quando capita Petri & Pauli ibi ostenduntur, tunc Romani habent indulgentias 3000. annorum: vicini 6000. qui e longinquo venerunt, 12000. In illa Ecclesia est aurea porta, quæ tantùm in anno Jubilæo aperitur. Sunt autem tres portæ, per quarum unam Christus Hierosolymis ad mortem suam ivit. Cùmque non certò constet, quæ ex tribus istis illa sit, itur per omnes tres. Et qui devotione per illas transit, liber sit à peccatis non aliter atque homo, cùm primùm baptizatur. Etiam pro animabus itur per illas portas. Cùm Gregorius Ecclesiam illam Lateranensem denuò dedicaret, dedit tot dierum indulgentias quot guttæ cadunt si per tres dies & noctes continuè pluat. Cùmque Gregorius metueret, ne Thesaurus gratiæ profusione illa evacuaretur, Christus apparuit ei & dixit, se concedere ut plures indulgentias det; populum enim hic opus habere. Atque hæ solius Ecclesiæ Lateranensis indulgentiæ sunt, quæ certâ spe remissionis foro factâ, omnem timorem Numinis animis eripiunt, ut in peccatorum quorumvis licentiam præcipitentur. Quæ non sine periculo natæ sunt, agnoscentibus id ipsum Statibus Germaniæ Catholicis & Protestantibus, qui inter Gravamina MDXXIII. Papæ oblata, ut de Indulgentiarum nundinationibus Christianos liberam esse. Quando quilibet pro pretio peccatorum expenderat, modo peccandi impunitas tribuitur. Hinc stupra, incestus, adulteria & perlerna semel originem traxerunt.
units.tr: L. Moreover, this can set a torch to the minds not only of those who have rushed headlong into every kind of impurity with their reins otherwise loose, but also of those who have not yet cast off all shame. The remedies of indulgences (φάρμακοι) were long ago customarily applied not only to past sins but also to future ones, and they still are. For it has long been the practice that sins are remitted, in so-called confessionals that are to last a whole lifetime, and in indulgence diplomas, for sins to be committed afterwards over a long stretch of time. Hence remissions of penalties are granted not for a single day or year, nor even for ten, or three hundred (which some set as the penalty of Purgatory), but for many thousands. Rome and its stationes alone reckon more thousands of years than the more sober Roman theologians approve. A book printed in Latin at Rome in 1475, De stationibus Romæ, and a book published at Nuremberg later in the same century, in 1491, set out the indulgences of the principal churches of Rome, above all the seven. To give one example, let us set out the indulgences of the Lateran church alone. In it, as that book lists, there are distributed daily 48 years of indulgence, as many quadragenes, and the remission of a third part of all sins. Hence Boniface: "If anyone comes to our Lateran See out of devotion, for prayer, or as a pilgrim, he shall be absolved from all his sins." In the chapel called the Holy of Holies, which women may not enter, there is a true and full remission of all sins. In the same chapel are the 28 steps that stood before Pilate's house in Jerusalem; whoever climbs these steps with devotion receives, for each step, nine years of indulgence and as many quadragenes, and the remission of a third part of all sins. Whoever climbs them on his knees frees one soul, for which he prays, from Purgatory. On the day of dedication, which is called the day of the Saviour, there is full remission of all sins, of guilt and of penalty. When the Pope first granted an indulgence there, the angels, in the presence of the people, said Amen. Likewise, when the heads of Peter and Paul are shown there, the Romans have indulgences of 3000 years, those nearby 6000, and those who come from afar 12000. In that church there is a golden door, which is opened only in the Jubilee year. There are three doors, through one of which Christ went to his death at Jerusalem; since it is not certain which of the three that is, all three are passed through. Whoever passes through them with devotion is freed from sins in the same way as a man when he is first baptized. Also, they pass through these doors for the souls of the dead. When Gregory re-dedicated that Lateran church, he gave as many days of indulgence as drops fall if it rains continuously for three days and nights. And since Gregory feared that the Treasury of grace would be emptied by such a lavish outpouring, Christ appeared to him and said that he should grant more indulgences, for the people there had need of them. These, then, are the indulgences of the Lateran church alone, which, with the sure hope of remission secured in the court of law, snatch from men's minds all fear of the Deity, so that they hurl themselves into a licence for any sins whatever. These were not born without danger, as the Catholic and Protestant estates of Germany acknowledged, when among their grievances presented to the Pope in 1523 they asked that Christians be freed from the trafficking in indulgences. When anyone has paid a price for his sins, a licence to sin is granted. Hence fornications, incests, adulteries and lasting unions have had their origin.

units.la: LI. Neque minore Ecclesiam Romanam potestas illa Papæ, quâ in ipsa lege Divinâ consanguinitatis & affinitatis in matrimonio prohibente, dispensare audet, messtat, non duntaxat, sed culpam etiam incestuosis e bus adimere, adeoque ex gravissimo, peccatum, & matrimonium Deo sc facere connixus, verissimis incestibus p plet. Quam in rem plura diximus tum Sect j. th. §8 tum Anat. Concil. Trid. at nec non Differt. Sel. Tom j. Differt. xvi hibitiones Mosaicas circa gradus consanguinitatis Levit. xviii. 6. &c. expressos juris perpetui esse, adeóque à nulla potestate ri in iis posse, duodecim argumentis necessariis. Non desinunt ergo conjugia fratrum & affinium & consanguineorum in primo gradu, vel in secundo lineæ inæqualis verilitus esse; licet Papa quandoque quæstum stabiliendæ gratia, quoties sic ei videtur, ge, vel ejus saltem in persona placita ob monium etiam in foro Divino ratum firmúmque esse jubeat. Constat autem satis, Gregorium III. permisisse cuidam, ut avunculi defuncti uxorem duceret: Johannis VIII. concessione Ethelbaldum Regem Angliæ novercam suam duxisse; Martinum V. narrante Angelo de Clavasio, re cum doctoribus suis consultata, cuidam germanæ ducendæ potestatem fecisse: Julium II. Henrico VIII. Angliæ Regi gratiam ducendæ Catharinæ, fratris defuncti Arturi viduæ, fecisse; atque non ita pridem Regi Poloniæ Casimiro; quin &, superstite marito Rege Portugalliæ Alphonso, Fratri Petro, glotis ducendæ facultatem à Papa permissam esse. Plura profanæ & impiæ hujus Papalis dispensationis exempla in medium afferre supersedeo.
units.tr: LI. Nor does the power that the Roman Church ascribes to the Pope, by which he dares to dispense in marriage where the Divine law itself forbids consanguinity and affinity, show any less impiety. It not only removes the guilt of incestuous persons, but, striving to make a most grave sin into a marriage pleasing to God, it commits the truest incests. We have said much on this matter, both in Sect. j, th. §8, and in the Anatomia Concilii Tridentini, and also in Differt. Sel. Tom. j, Differt. xvi, where we have shown by twelve necessary arguments that the Mosaic prohibitions concerning degrees of consanguinity, expressed in Levit. 18.6 and following, are of perpetual right, and that no power can dispense from them. Therefore marriages of brothers, of affines and of consanguines in the first degree, or in the second degree of an unequal line, do not cease to be incestuous, even though the Pope sometimes, for the sake of gain, whenever it seems fit to him, orders such a marriage to be ratified and to stand firm even in the forum of God, or at least in the case of some favoured person. It is quite well established that Gregory III allowed someone to marry the wife of his deceased uncle; that by the grant of John VIII, Ethelbald, King of England, took his stepmother; that Martin V, as Angelo de Clavasio relates, after consulting his doctors, gave a certain man power to marry a full sister; that Julius II granted Henry VIII, King of England, the favour of marrying Catherine, the widow of his deceased brother Arthur; and not long ago the same to King Casimir of Poland; and indeed, while her husband, King Alphonso of Portugal, was still alive, the Pope granted to Brother Peter the power to marry his brother's wife. I refrain from bringing forward more examples of this profane and impious papal dispensation.

units.la: LII. Quantam porrò gratiam & existimationem huic Veneris ludo conciliari existimamus, quòd in ipsa Sede & Metropoli Hierarchici Imperii, quod à lupa originem habet, à Pontifice Optimo scilicet Maximo lupanaria permittuntur, imò etiam extruuntur? Nam Sixtum IV. Pontificem Maximum nobile lupanar Romæ extruxisse, constat. Annon publica hæc significatio est, quòd minimè opus sit hominibus, ut tanta cura & solicitudine sibi ipsis contra importunam libidinum suarum obsidionem defendendis insudent, cùm ipsa Sanctitas Pontificia ad faciles hac in re conditiones descenderit, patienterque permiserit, harum Veneris Monacharum, per urbis plateas magnifico apparatu summarum heroinarum æmulo; stipantibus Ecclesiasticis, summi gradûs ordinisque, incedentium, corporibus aburi, ea tantùm lege, ut lupæ hæ ex quæstu corporis sui annuos sibi reditus pensitent, eademque ratione Sacrosanctum hunc Sacerdotem summum, supremum civitatis Ganeonem agnoscant. Hoc verò quid aliud est, quàm matrimonium persequi, Ganearum verò patronum se gerere? Ecquod enim patrocinium majus scortatores; prostibula, ganeones exoptare pofi suffragium & approbationem, qui haberi judex infallibilis, saltem in causis Religio jusquè ipse Titulus seu inscriptio est, Sanc
units.tr: LII. Again, how much favour and esteem do we think this game of Venus gains for itself, since in the very seat and metropolis of the hierarchical empire, which takes its origin from the she-wolf, brothels are permitted, indeed even built, by the Best and Greatest Pontiff himself? For it is established that Pope Sixtus IV built a noble brothel at Rome. Is this not a public sign that men need not toil with such care and anxiety to defend themselves against the importunate siege of their own lusts, since the Pontifical Holiness himself has descended to easy terms in this matter, and has patiently allowed these Venus nuns to parade through the city's squares with a magnificent display, rivals of the greatest heroines, with ecclesiastics of the highest rank and order thronging round them, and their bodies to be ...? Only on this condition: that these she-wolves pay yearly revenues to themselves out of the earnings of their bodies, and that on the same principle they acknowledge this most sacred high priest as the supreme pimp of the city. But what else is this than to persecute marriage and to play the patron of pimps? For what greater patronage could fornicators, prostitutes and pimps desire than a vote and approval from one who is held to be an infallible judge, at least in matters of religion, and whose very title or inscription is Sanc-

units.la: LIII. Neque vel Papam ab objecto cr tarchiam & populum Romanum à fcortati adeoque Babylonicæ, foedissima labe pu quòd Papa lupanaria non probet, sed pe fione facti, uti Petrafancta, Balzacus,alii palis hujus luparum patrocinii hyperafpi addunt aliqui, atque ipse etiam Balzaetiam juris, quæ quamvis non auferat culp men immunitatem meretricibus; & dessimi tatem; quæ etiam obligèt alios ne impedia rare, quæ permittitur, & efficit, ne punia lores dum ii male agunt. Addit, esse a princeps permittat mœchari, licet mœ Hæc Theologia Jesuitica est, impuritatis giftra. Quid enim sibi vult permissio fa factum illud non aliud sit, quàm fcortatio nicationem permitti permissione facti, n quàm fornicationem permitti permissior Tum qui factum permittit, à lege is ex quid leges humanæ ferant, novimus. Sec tia quærimus: Nos verò cum Hieronym non cum Jesuitis, sentimus, Cæsarem, Papinianum, non Paulum, viris impudi re, & lupanaria permittere; indignúmqu Vicarium Christi dicit, & occupare locu fert, Cæsarem & Papinianum in eo velle quàm Christum.
units.tr: LIII. Neither can the Pope, nor the Roman people, be cleared of the charge of harlotry, and so of Babylonian, most foul stain, merely because the Pope does not approve brothels, but tolerates them by permission of the deed, as Petra Sancta, Balzacus and others maintain. Some add hyperaspists to this patronage of she-wolves, and Balzacus himself also speaks of a permission of law, which, although it does not remove the guilt of the act, grants immunity to prostitutes; and of a tolerance which also binds others not to hinder what is permitted, and which ensures that they are not punished while they behave badly. He adds that when a prince permits adultery, it is not thereby ... adultery. This is Jesuit theology, a defender of impurity. For what does "permission of the deed" mean, if the deed is nothing other than fornication? Fornication is permitted by a permission of the deed, but not by a permission of fornication... Then, whoever permits the deed is exempt from law, as we know from what human laws decree. But this is what we ask. We, however, with Jerome and not with the Jesuits, hold that Caesar and Papinian, not Paul, permit brothels to impure men; and Jerome calls such a one an unworthy Vicar of Christ, and says that it is a shameful thing to occupy the place of Christ and to wish Caesar and Papinian to be followed in this rather than Christ.

units.la: LIV. Sed quid multis? Non nudè pern approbari lupanaria, vel inde manifestum lupabus seu scortis ex usura corporis quæstum facientibus, in partem quæstûs illius venire religioni neutiquam ducit, neque acceptat duntaxat ab iis, sed extorquet etiam lucri partem. Nam Summo huic Pontifici adeo
units.tr: LIV. But why say more? That brothels are not merely tolerated is plain from the fact that the religion does not regard the profit of prostitutes or harlots who make their gain from the use of their bodies as something foreign to it. It does not only accept such money from them but also extorts a share of the profit. For this Supreme Pontiff is so far
the smell of gain is good, whatever its source
From any source.

units.la: ut sordidum illud Vespasiani vectigal urinarium longè supergressus, lupanarium etiam, nonnunquam excedente 20. millia ducatorum, reditu annuo sacrum locupletet ærarium, & unà cum Ecclesiarum proventibus, lenociniorum numeret mercedem, nihil turpe reputans, quod ad æs exit. Cornelius Agrippa de Vanit. Scient. cap. 64. ubi de lenonia agit, Lenon, inquit, fuit Pan Deus, atque Mercurius, ipseque puer Cupido; leno fuit heros ille Ulysses, leno fuit legislator Lycurgus, & Sapiens ille Solon, qui primus lupanaria ædificavit, & meretriculas juventuti prostituit. Sed & recentioribus temporibus Sixtus Pontifex Max. Romæ nobile admodum lupanar extruxit. Paulò post: Lenones olim fuerunt Corinthii, &c. nonnihil etiam ex meretricio quæstu ærario suo accumulantes emolumenti, quod quidem in Italia non rarum est, ubi etiam Romana scorta in singulas hebdomadas Julium pendunt Pontifici, qui census annuus nonnunquam viginti millia ducatos excedit: adeoque Ecclesiæ Procerum id munus est, ut unà cum Ecclesiarum proventibus etiam lenociniorum numerent mercedem. Sic enim ego illos supputantes aliquando audivi: habet (inquientes) ille duo beneficia, unum curatum aureorum viginti, alterum prioratum ducatorum quadraginta, & tres putanas in Burdello, quæ reddunt singulu hebdomadis Julios viginti. Plura eandem in rem Espencæus, cujus mox verba referam, profert. Verus autem ille Sanctus Israëlis, dissimilis lenoni huic, qui Sanctissimus audire vult, mercedem meretricis acceptare noluit, quantumvis oblatio esset voluntaria, Deut. iii. nominationi omnem impuritatem esse, ofte verò fieri omnino potest, ut quis sciens & pacto, lucri particeps fiat, sub conditione ventiæ; aut quovis modo favendi impr crum invehit, quin eo ipso improbitatis reddatur. Quod cùm in Summo illo Sace bet, causa dici non potest, quò minùs V tionem illam probare, atque eadem r mundo habenas libidini ac impuritati laxa ritò.
units.tr: beyond that filthy tax of Vespasian's on urine that he enriches the sacred treasury with a yearly revenue from brothels, sometimes exceeding 20,000 ducats, and counts among the revenues of the churches the wages of pandering, thinking nothing shameful that brings in money. Cornelius Agrippa, On the Vanity of the Sciences, ch. 64, where he treats of pandering, says: The pander was Pan the god, and Mercury, and the boy Cupid himself; the pander was that hero Ulysses, the pander was the lawgiver Lycurgus, and the wise Solon, who first built brothels and offered little harlots to the young men. In more recent times too, Sixtus, Supreme Pontiff, built a very famous brothel at Rome. A little later: The panders of old were the Corinthians, etc. They even add some gain from the harlot's trade to their treasury, which indeed is not rare in Italy, where Roman prostitutes pay Julius weekly to the Pontiff, a yearly census that sometimes exceeds twenty thousand ducats. So it is the duty of the princes of the Church to count the wages of pandering together with the revenues of the churches. For I once heard them reckoning thus: "He has two benefices, one a parish worth twenty gold pieces, the other a priory worth forty ducats, and three whores in the brothel, which bring in twenty julii each week." Espencaeus, whose words I shall quote presently, offers more on the same matter. But the true Holy One of Israel, unlike this pander who wishes to be called Most Holy, refused to accept the wage of a harlot, however freely it was offered (Deut. iii.): every impurity is an abomination. Yet it can certainly happen that someone knowingly and by agreement becomes a sharer in gain, under the condition of a payment, or in any way brings in a profit from the shamelessness of others, and is not thereby made wicked. Since this cannot be said of that Supreme Pontiff, there is no reason why we should not condemn that practice and at the same time give the reins to lust and impurity throughout the world.

units.la: LV. Lupanaria Hierarchici hàc infupe lenonio potiùs fuco incrustant, quòd pe diat, ut libidinosi pejora conari desistant, ra mala vitentur. Tolle, sic arguentes eos inducit, è Republica meretrices, cuncta adulteriis permiscentur. Nulla matrona bit, nullius viduæ pudicitia incolumis per nes ac vestales inviolatæ servabuntur. publicæ tranquillitas sine meretricibus co sancta; Cur permittantur, inquit, Rom quo modo hæ potissimùm causæ urgent, n nes lubrici abeant in carnem alterum; eas (meretrices) Romæ à Pio V. restit principatûs facessere eas jussisset, memor incontinentes viri fructum carpere tori arum florem audeant. Hoc verò quid aliu bylonicæ impuritatis, cujus Mater illa peragitur, publica confessio? Nisi enim liceat, graviora timenda esse sic ipsi fate erant facienda mala, ut bona evenirent! legi Divinæ simpliciter, & eventus relinq qui incommoda ex lege sua eventura p æquè ac Hierarchici, non iccirco temperavit, quò minùs severè ediceret: Non sit meretrix in Israelis filiabus Deut. xxiij. 17. Quæ Lei verba graviter Claudius Espencæus, Doctor Sorbonicus, de contin. lib. iij. 4. urget, ubi inter alia: Sub atis apud Judæos lupanaribus an omnia promiscua libidinibus confusa fuerunt aut etiamnum sunt? Quò minùs hanc sedis atem lex vetus impunitam tulerit, obesse etiam in hodiernum usque d em Judeorum etiam ubivis & inter quosvis degant, praxis, suos meretricium facere non permittentium, dici nequit quàm incredibili Christianorum pudore, tum etiam eorum, qui vere tales sunt, cordolio, ut Judæi filiæ scortari non liceat, Dei filiæ liceati imò Israelitæ filia meretricari non aliter possit, quàm facta per Sanctum Baptismum Christi sororem & filiam.
units.tr: LV. The Hierarchy covers its brothels with this pandering veneer, on the ground that by permitting them it prevents the lustful from attempting worse things, and that greater evils are thereby avoided. Remove, so they argue, harlots from the commonwealth, and all things will be mixed up with adulteries. No matron's chastity, no widow's modesty, will be safe from lust; the wives and virgins of the Vestals will not be preserved inviolate. Without harlots there is no tranquillity in public life. Why, they ask, are they permitted in Rome? For these reasons press most strongly, lest the lustful pass on to another's flesh. When Pius V. ordered these harlots to leave Rome, he was mindful of this, that incontinent men would dare to pluck the flower of the matrons. But what else is this than a public confession of Babylonian impurity, by which that impure mother is served? For unless it were permitted, so they say, greater evils would be feared; so the evils had to be done so that good might come of them! The Lord did not simply leave the law of God and the outcome to the rulers of the Church, nor did he, on account of the inconveniences that would arise from his law, temper it so as to lessen his severe command: Let there be no harlot among the daughters of Israel (Deut. xxiii. 17). Claudius Espencaeus, Doctor of the Sorbonne, On Continence, book 3, ch. 4, presses these words hard, and among other things says: Under the ancient law, were all things among the Jews mixed up in lust, were brothels there so that no shame was attached? That the old law did not bear this seat of impurity unpunished cannot be denied. And it is nowhere the less to be feared that the modern practice of the Jews, who wherever they live and among whomsoever, do not permit their daughters to make a trade of harlotry, can hardly be spoken of without the incredible shame of Christians, and also the grief of those who are truly such: a Jewish daughter may not play the whore, but a daughter of God may, and indeed an Israelite daughter may be made a harlot only once she has been made, through holy Baptism, a sister and daughter of Christ.
LVI.

units.la: Quænam verò illa mala sunt, quibus illa scortandi Papalis licentia medetur? Nam in regionibus & urbibus, ubi lupanaria nulla sunt, & meretrices severè coërcentur, tutior est uxorum pudicitia, rariores sunt meretrices; cynœdum verò aut catamitum esse; res est prodigio simillis. At in Italia, ubi lupanaria patent, ardet tamen flamma Scedomitica. Uxorum verò pudicitia, quæcunque est, ibi non debetur prostibulis, sed arctæ custodiæ, quà detinentur quasi captivæ. Solæ ibi meretrices aut decrepitæ anus liberæ sunt. Hoc enim libidinis ingenium est, capere ex licentia incrementum, instar ignis, qui arctatus suffocatur, at ventilatione in aëre libero suscitatur; magisque inardescit. Quomodo Hugo Cardinalis cum Curia Innocentii IV. Lugduno discessurus apud Matthæum Paris in Henrico III. Romanæ curiæ insatiabilem libidinem confessus, dicebat, multum curiæ R. debet illam urbem Nam quando illuc venerat, se reperisse tria aut quatuor lupanaria. Tunc autem ad unum omnia redacta fuisse, sed illud à porta occidentali usque ad orientalem extendi. Sed & Maria-
units.tr: But what are those evils which that papal licence to whore is supposed to cure? For in regions and cities where there are no brothels, and harlots are severely restrained, the chastity of wives is safer, and harlots are rarer. To be a sodomite or a catamite is a thing like a monstrous portent. But in Italy, where the brothels stand open, the flame of Sodom still burns. The chastity of wives, such as it is, is not owed to prostitutes there, but to close custody, in which they are held like captives. Only the harlots and the decrepit old women are free there. For this is the nature of lust: it takes increase from licence, like a fire which, when hemmed in, is smothered, but when ventilated in open air is roused and burns more fiercely. So Hugh the Cardinal, when about to leave Lyons with the Curia of Innocent IV, confessed the insatiable lust of the Roman Curia, as Matthew Paris reports under Henry III. He said: The Roman Curia owes much to that city. When he had come there he had found three or four brothels; but then everything had been reduced to one, which however stretched from the western gate to the eastern. But also Maria-

units.la: Note: marginal notes beside LVI read "Majorâ mala", "in iis locis, quibus lupanaria sunt", "nature in ipsa", "non sunt, nec timentur", "nec parrum", "tbr." Mariana ipse, quamvis Jesuita, in eo tam nestior, lib. de spectac. cap. 16. ubi eandem movet; Neque, inquit, satis occurritur scortis permissis, cùm sciamus, in quibus vitatibus ea labes maximè viget, ibi ma numerum esse; & in utramque partem ab flammatur, neque ullis resistit finibus. ubi lupanaria nulla sunt, multò continen nes, pauciora existunt adulteria. Sic non tur, neque mascula libido, sed potius sc fœdissima queque concitatur. Quod si illa permissio adulteriis, aliisque scelerib aliud tamen longè gravius malum inde e corruptio & depravatio pastoralis mun pasto in lenoniam vertitur. Apex est nec ma Ecclesiæ corruptio, quando inde nal morum, & peccandi licentia, unde exem tæ, & incitamenta ad pietatem & cas bantur. Romæ enim & in aliis urbibu quentius est, quàm videre Clericos lu tantes.
units.tr: Marginal notes beside LVI read: "Greater evils"; "in those places where there are brothels"; "nature in itself"; "they are not, nor are they feared"; "nor a little"; "tbr." Mariana himself, though a Jesuit, is in this matter not ignorant. In his book On Spectacles, ch. 16, where he raises the same point, he says: "Nor is enough provision made against harlots being allowed, since we know that in those places where this stain flourishes most, adulteries are also the most numerous and burn in both directions, and it resists no limits. Where there are no brothels, there is far more continence and fewer adulteries. Thus neither the mascular lust nor the feminine is stirred up, but rather the foulest things of every kind." And if that permission does not lead to adulteries and other crimes, it certainly leads to another, far graver evil: the corruption and depravity of the pastoral office. The shepherd turns into a pander. This is the summit of the Church's corruption, when from there comes the ruin of morals and the licence to sin, whence examples and incitements to piety ought to have come. For at Rome and in other cities it is more common to see clerics frequenting brothels than to see them...

units.la: LVII. Neque nobis duntaxat, sed n emunctiorum narium in ipso Papatu le Marianam jam laudavimus. Afferam in Sorbonici Doctoris, cujus supra etiam m plura & aculeata, quibus sic ille de Cons fœditatem detestatur; Illud sua etiamnu nonie quantum unaqueque prostituta, c in Italia, ibi observatum notat Beroald siensis, ut prostitutæ meretrices tributum gistratibus, qui vulgò præfecti bulletar vant. Romæ verò, hoc est, in totius Chr poli, quid aliud hac in resastum aut non fa-
units.tr: LVII. Not only we, but the keenest noses within Papacy itself have already been cited, Mariana among them. I shall add a Doctor of the Sorbonne, whose words above I have already cited, and many more pointed ones, in which he thus detests the foulness of the Curia. He says: "It is still observed, even now, in Italy, as Beroaldus of Siena notes, that prostitutes pay a tax to the magistrates, who are commonly called prefects of the bulletae. But at Rome, that is, in the whole head of Christendom, what else is this, in this matter, than a..."
-silii.

units.la: Paulo III. delecti pro emendanda Ecclesia Reverendissimi Cardinales, aliique viri graves inter alia consuluerunt, corrigendum & hunc turpem abusum, quo illic meretrices ut matronae incedunt, aut mulá vehuntur, assectantibus eas de media die nobilibus familiaribusque Cardinalium atque clericis, habitant etiam insignes aedes. Nulla in urbe hac, ajunt, corruptionem vidimus, praeterquam in hac omnium exemplari. Et hanc tamen turpitudinem corruptelámque unus ex consiliariis, Paulus postea IV. non sustulit, quod, ut mihi bene sum conscius, eo quo me colloquio dignatus est, quá potui ac debui modestiá, privatim suaseram. Mirum certè, tales tantósque viros consuluisse, minuendum modò scortorum sastum & luxum, non etiam semel ejicienda. An verò propter tam multos ibi cœlibes retinenda? O rem horrendam! Mihi sanè sic eos sensisse, dicere religio est. Nos Gallos, stolidos scilicet ac simplices, non posse non graviter offendi tot mille luparum in iisdem muris, sub eodem prope, quod ajunt, tecto, quotidiano conspectu, ac, velimus nolimus, occursu. Non enim jam, ut olim, sub mœnibus habitant, aut sub Mœnianis Circensibus, Martiali ob id Summœnianæ dictæ. Quærit Q. Fabius lib. vj. 4. An in lupanari cum aliena deprehensus, adulter sit? non quæsiturus, nisi certo tum loco fuissent deprehensæ. Nunc verò sub Christi vicariis, & Petri successoribus, ut alius quidam cecinit Urbs est jam tota lupanar Mater & Æneæ regnat in urbe sui.
units.tr: The most reverend Cardinals chosen by Paul III. to reform the Church, and other grave men, among other things consulted that this shameful abuse should be corrected, by which there harlots walk about like matrons, or are carried on mules, attended in broad daylight by the noblemen and household servants of the Cardinals and by clerics, and even occupy distinguished houses. In this city, they say, we have seen no corruption except in this place, the model of all. Yet this turpitude and corruption was not removed by one of the advisers, Paul IV afterwards, who, as I am well aware, I had privately urged in conversation, with whatever modesty I could and ought. It is certainly remarkable that such men and so great should have consulted only that the splendour and luxury of the whores be diminished, and not that they be cast out at once. Or should they be kept there on account of so many celibate men? O dreadful thing! For me it is indeed a matter of religion to say that they thought so. We Gauls, foolish and simple forsooth, cannot but be gravely offended that so many thousand she-wolves are within the same walls, under almost the same roof, as they say, in daily view and, whether we will or not, in our path. For they no longer live under the walls, as of old, or under the Circus of the Moenia, whence they were called Summoenianae. Quintus Fabius asks, in book 6, ch. 4: "If a man is caught with another's wife in a brothel, is he an adulterer?" He would not ask this, unless they had been caught in a certain place. But now, under the vicars of Christ and the successors of Peter, as another poet has sung: the whole city is now a brothel, and the Mother of Aeneas reigns in the city of her own.

units.la: Quódque in Solone Plutarchus scribit, Athenienses mitibus nominibus urbanè imminuendo rerum atrocitatem mitigásse, meretrices hetæras, socias, amicas nuncupantes. Ita Romanenses sua NVNDINALIA pudoris PROPVDIA, Curtisanas vocant. O Italicum acumen! men! Johannes quoque Franciscus Picus in Oratione ad Leonem X. pro morum reformatione, comparationem instituens inter filios Eli, qui in taber-naculo, ribus dormiebant ad ostium tabernaculi; Ita ut et in sacras aedes fit irruptio, & ab illis ... dor! fœminæ abiguntur ad eorum libidinem ... meritorii pueri à parentibus commodati. Petrasanêta, qui abeunt in carnem alteram ... tur his, qui ab omni corporis concessa etiam immaculatos custodire debent. Hi potiorum gradus promoventur ætatis flos ... exoleti.
units.tr: Plutarch also writes in his life of Solon that the Athenians, by softening the harshness of the thing with gentle names and with urbane understatement, called prostitutes hetaerae, companions and friends. So the Romans call their nundinalia, those cast-offs of chastity, courtesans. O Italian wit! men! John Francis Pico also, in his Oration to Leo X for the reform of morals, drawing a comparison between the sons of Eli, who slept in the tabernacle at the door of the tabernacle: So even into the sacred temples there is a break-in, and from those ... women are driven to their lust ... boys lent by their parents for vice. Petrasanta, who go into another flesh ... who ought to keep themselves unspotted by every bodily ... These are promoted to higher grades; the flower of their age ... worn out.

units.la: LVIII. Sed Papa, uti Romanus Episcopus denique ejus lenonia excusatur) non proftibulis, ut impunè corpus suum prostituant, usu Sacramentorum ea arcet, & extra sepeliri curat, & jure rhedarum prohibet ... postea? Ipse Papa dignior poena hac est, simus haberi velit, & extrui curat lupanarium ... ftum accipit. Hoc an in populo Christiano ... tum, haud facilè dixerim, puta alicubi ... fieri, ait Mariana, non ausus aperte dicere ... noniæ, quod Agrippam, & Espencæum ... Non impedivit communionis, sepulturæ ... rhedarum ademptus honos, quin talium ... tronarum facta recensione A. MDLXV. ... octo & viginti millia reperirentur. Et nunc ejusmodi reformidabunt, quæ corpus ... dæmoni manciparunt? Neque proftibulæ ... sepulturæ honore carent, sed diobolaria ... honorem eum pecunia redimere non ... non ex vivis duntaxat, sed mortuis et ... quæstum facit. Neque jus rhedarum ... cum lupabus illis scortantibus; quibus fas est ad lupanar rhedâ vehi. Denique quàm illud absurdum est, imò quàm iniquum, afficere opprobrio corpora, quorum ipse priùs, fœdâ indulgentiâ, & sceleris veɛtigalis approbatione, animas corruperis.
units.tr: LVIII. But the Pope, as Roman bishop, is finally excused of his pimping. He does not forbid prostitutes the use of the sacraments, so that they may prostitute their bodies with impunity; he has them buried outside, and he forbids them the right of carriages ... afterwards? The Pope himself deserves this punishment more, if he wishes to be thought a pimp, and he has a brothel built ... Whether this happens among the Christian people, I could hardly say; suppose it happens somewhere, says Mariana, not daring to say it openly ... Agrippa and Espencé ... The loss of communion, of burial and of the honour of carriages did not prevent, when a census of such courtesans was taken in 1565, twenty-eight thousand being found. And will women of this kind now fear, who have handed over their bodies to the devil? Nor do prostitutes lack the honour of burial; rather they buy that honour with money ... not only from the living but from the dead too ... he makes gain. Nor is the right of carriages ... with those whoring she-wolves, to whom it is lawful to be carried to the brothel in a carriage. Finally, how absurd, nay how unjust, it is to heap disgrace on bodies whose souls you yourself first corrupted by foul indulgence and by approving the tax on crime.

units.la: LIX. Superest postremum lemma, cœterorum omnium coronis, & tot occasionum, causarum, illecebrarum effectus, res ipsa, Cleri omne genus libidinibus indulgentis historia. Hic verò ne per calumniam à me quidquam dici, quiritari Hierarchici possint, domesticis testimoniis negotium conficiam. Licet enim scelera illa tenebrarum in occulto patrentur, & novissimus ac censorius ille dies ea clarissimè omnium in apricum prolaturus sit; non potuerunt tamen sic Hierarchici dedecora sua tegere, & tenebris in hoc etiam mundo involvere, quin à pluribus, iisque gravissimis etiam testibus prodita, in publicum erumperent.
units.tr: LIX. There remains the last topic, the crown of all the others, and the outcome of so many occasions, causes and allurements: the very history of the clergy, who indulge every kind of lust. Lest the Hierarchists cry out that anything is said by me out of calumny, I will settle the matter with testimonies from their own household. For although those crimes of darkness are committed in secret, and that last, censorious day will bring them most clearly into the light of all, the Hierarchists could not so cover their disgraces, nor wrap them in darkness even in this world, but that they have been betrayed by many, and by very weighty witnesses, and have burst into public view.

units.la: LX. Ab Hierarchiæ capite, Papa, ordiamur. Si enim Pontifices, Sanctissimi nomine insignes, primi & severissimi continentiæ exactores, & Ἰδιοι τῆ πιμπλῖ typi scilicet gregis, non defuerunt, qui labem impuritatis sibi contraherent, de inferioris cleri, cui Sanctitatis titulo superbire fas non est, puritate quid sentiendum sit, constabit ultrò. Nihil dicam de fatali eo tempore, quo Meretrix Fœmina Johanna Papatûs thronum occupavit, quæ fama si mendax est, non à nobis illa, sed à mendace Papatu manavit. Sed veram esse, fidem facere possemus. Nihil de deploratissimis illis temporibus, quibus, Genebrardo ad A. 908. & Baronio ad A. 897. n. 4. ingenuè confitentibus & deplorantibus non tam homines, quàm hominum monstra Petri augustam illam cathedram insederunt, à fœdissimis prostibulis, Marozia & Theodora, à matre Theodora, Romæ imperante, Pontificibus prostitutis, intrusa, uti de Johan-
units.tr: LX. Let us begin with the head of the Hierarchy, the Pope. For if pontiffs, distinguished by the name of "Most Holy", the first and strictest exactors of continence, and [Ἰδιοι τῆ πιμπλῖ], that is, the very models of the flock, were not lacking who contracted for themselves a stain of impurity, then what is to be thought of the purity of the lower clergy, who are not permitted to swell with pride at the title of "Holiness", will be evident of itself. I will say nothing of that fatal time when the harlot woman Joan occupied the throne of the Papacy; if that report is false, it came not from us but from the lying Papacy, though we could make it credible that it is true. Nor will I say anything of those most deplorable times, when, as Genebrardus at 908 and Baronius at 897, n. 4, confess and lament, not so much men as monsters of men sat on St Peter's august chair, thrust in by the most foul prostitutes, Marozia and Theodora, and by their mother Theodora, who reigned at Rome and gave popes to prostitution; as concerning John-

units.la: Jahanne XI. Ravennæ priùs Archiepiscopus, Papa Sergius III. ex Marozia Papam Joannem XI. constituit; quem ipsum quoque in adulterio deprehensum, et adulteræ marito confossum, Platina, Liutprandus, Ravennensis lib. ÿ. cap. 15. &c. ubi Theodoræ nora commemorat; Cranzius Metrop. 3. Schis. p. 631. Carriere Digesto Chronolog. morant. Lubet exemplis decem Pontificum, ordine, inde ab A. MCCCCLVIII. ad A. MDCCC. Seculi unius decursu, inde à Pio II. usque sibi succedentium, productis fidem facere ipsi Supremi Hierarchiæ Principes lueverint.
units.tr: John XI, formerly Archbishop of Ravenna, whom Pope Sergius III made pope out of Marozia. This same man, caught in adultery and stabbed by the adulteress's husband, is recorded by Platina, Liutprand, Ravennas book 5 chapter 15, etc., where he mentions Theodora's ...; Cranzius, Metropolis, book 3 of the Schism, p. 631; Carriere, Digest of Chronology and Morals. It pleases me to bring forward ten popes in order, from 1458 to 1800, over the course of one century, from Pius II onward, who succeeded one another, to show that the supreme princes of the Hierarchy themselves have borne out the case.

units.la: LXI. Pius II. sic Prol. in hist. duor. bit: Ego de me facio conjecturam, quem ricula misit. Ago superis gratias, quòd millies fugi, felicior astro Martis, quem Venere jacentem ferreo illaqueavit reticulo, quòd Deus cæteris ostentavit. Et Epist. 15 lium se fusce-pisse, non tantùm parenti fa etiam gloriatúrque. Pium excepit Paulus mâsse dicitur, quòd ipse qui non solùm Ec continentiæ antistes esse deberet, filiam culis civitatis cum summo probro versari gem Dei sciret esse, qua huic in matrimo uti pro conjugio Sacerdotum ad Julium Ruthenus, Staniflaus Orichovius scripsit tus IV. lupanaris Romæ nobilis architeæ pter hanc aliásque causas ejusmodi epita Sapidus exsculpsit: Sixte jaces tandem, deflent tua busta Scortáque, lenones, alea, vina, Venus. De quo etiam Nicolaus Machiavellus in b na lib. vij. sic scribit: Alebat inter familiares suos duos, qui omnium opinione ipsius filii erant, quos tamen magis honesto nomine palliaverat; Petrum unum, quem utpote Regularem ad Cardinalitiam dignitatem titulo S. Sixti evexit; Hieronymum alterum quem Foro Julio donavit, expulso inde Antonio Ordelaffio, qui eam urbem una cum suis majoribus aliquot jeculis in potestate habuerat. Eorundem, ne Machiavelli fidem suspectent Hierarchici, Onuphrius Panvinius in vita Sixti meminit, ubi nominatim de Petro Cardinale memorat, quòd amplissimis Sacerdotiorum reditibus auctus ita splendidus fuerit, ut pecuniæ perdendæ (uni prandio ultra xx. millia florenorum impendisse, sunt qui scribunt) natus esse videretur. Nam eo, inquit Onuphrius, biennio, quo tantùm postea supervixit, ducenta aureorum millia in victu absumpsisse; lx. verò millia æris alieni, argenti autem cælati ccc. pondo reliquisse traditur. Obiit voluptatibus confectus paulò ante obitum creatus à Sixto totius Italiæ legatus. Succedit Sixti Datarius, Innocentius VIII. qui, ut Marulli epigramma habet, Octo nocens pueros genuit, totidémque puellas, Hunc merito potuit, dicere Roma patrem.
units.tr: LXI. Pius II says thus in the Prologue to his two histories: "I make a conjecture about myself, what a net sent. I give thanks to the heavenly powers that I have escaped a thousand times, more fortunate than the star of Mars, whom Venus, lying with him, caught in an iron net, which God showed to the others." And in Epistle 15 ... not only ... acknowledged a son, but also boasts of it. Paul II succeeded Pius. It is said that he himself, who ought to have been the leader not only of continence but ..., allowed his daughter to live in the city with the greatest disgrace, though he knew she was the daughter of God; for this girl, in marriage ... to use as a wife, for the priests ... to Julius ... Ruthenus, Stanislaus Orichovius wrote. [Sixtus] IV: a noble brothel of Rome built by an architect ... Besides this and other such causes, Sapidus carved this epitaph: "Sixtus, you lie at last; your tomb is wept by whores, pimps, dice, wine and Venus." Of him Niccolò Machiavelli also writes, in his History book 7, thus: "He kept among his household two whom by everyone's opinion were his sons, though he had more respectably veiled them under an honourable name: one, Pietro, whom, being a Regular, he raised to the cardinalate with the title of St Sixtus; the other, Girolamo, whom he gave Forlì, Antonio Ordelaffi having been expelled, who had held that city in his power, with some of his ancestors, for several centuries." So that the Hierarchists may not doubt Machiavelli's trustworthiness, Onuphrius Panvinius also mentions these men in the life of Sixtus, where he names Cardinal Pietro by name, saying that he, enriched with the most ample revenues of his priesthoods, was so lavish that he seemed born to squander money (some write that he spent more than 20,000 florins on a single lunch). For in the two years he survived afterwards, he is said to have consumed 200,000 gold pieces on food, and to have left behind 60,000 in debt and 300 pounds of chased silver. He died worn out by pleasures, having shortly before his death been made by Sixtus legate of all Italy. Next comes Sixtus's successor, Innocent VIII, who, as Marullus' epigram has it: "The harmful man begot eight boys and as many girls; Rome could rightly call him father."

units.la: Nam profecto, uti lusit Sannazarius, quem inter Scriptores Ecclesiasticos Bellarminus retulit, Progenie exhaustam restituit patriam.
units.tr: For indeed, as Sannazaro jested, whom Bellarmine counted among the ecclesiastical writers: "He restored the fatherland, exhausted by its offspring."

units.la: Fuit is, observante lib. xxy. Raphaële Volaterrano, primus Pontificum, qui novus & ipse exemplum introduceret, palam liberos nothos jactandi, ac solutâ omni antiquâ disciplinâ divitiis omnibus eos cumulandi. Francifcum filium, & Theodorinam filiam Onuphrius nominat: illi patrem oppida nonnulla vicina dedisse, Laurentiique Medicis filiam Magdalenam, formosissimam puellam matrimonio junxisse; iltam Gerardo Vsumari Genuensi nuptam magnis divitiis cumulâsse, affirmat: Sed VI. monstrum ex libidine, avaritia & potentia, verius, quàm homo. Is enim, ut Onuphrius explicem, si quando negotiis non premeretur, ... ditatis genere sine discrimine dedit, mulieribus addiëtus, ex quibus quatuor filios & duas filias ... hil autem, sic iterum Volaterranus, primum Innocentii exemplo suos nothos honoribus ac majoribus extollere, quando antea res hæc non ... esse cæpit. Quomodo verò id perfecerit, ita exponit: Lucretiam filiam, inquiens, ... ficatum Hispano cuidam in matrimonium ... ablatam, Johanni Sforciæ Pisaurensi ... deinde abdicatam Aloisio Arragonio, Al... notho; quo demum interfecto Alphonso ... duci collocavit. Ex filiis verò natu min... Principem Squilatinum fecit; medium C... nalem; maximum natu Johannem ducem ... nia creari procuravit, cui etiam uxorem ... tham Regis Alphonsi. Qui cùm nocte qu... insidiis Cæsaris Cardinalis fratris inter... berim conjectus est, connivente prorsus a... cidii scelus Patre Pontifice. In quem pr... pra, Sannazarius hoc epigramma fudit:
units.tr: He was, according to Raphael Volaterranus, book 25, the first of the popes who, himself new to the practice, introduced the example of openly boasting of his illegitimate children, and, with all ancient discipline dissolved, heaped every kind of wealth upon them. Onuphrius names his son Francis and his daughter Theodorina: to the son his father gave several neighbouring towns, and he joined Magdalena, daughter of Lorenzo de' Medici, a most beautiful girl, to him in marriage; to the daughter, he asserts, he married Gerardo Usodimare of Genoa and heaped her with great riches. But he was a monster of lust, avarice and power, more truly a beast than a man. For he, as Onuphrius explains, whenever he was not pressed by business, gave away offices and benefices of every kind without distinction, being given over to women, from whom he had four sons and two daughters ... Volaterranus, again: "Nothing was more notable than that he first, following Innocent's example, raised his bastards to honours and greater dignities, when formerly this practice had not ... begun." How he accomplished this he sets out: "His daughter Lucretia," he says, "... was betrothed to a certain Spaniard, then taken from him and given to John Sforza of Pesaro ... then divorced and handed to Alfonso of Aragon, ... a bastard; when Alfonso was finally killed, he placed her with the duke ..." Of the younger sons he made one Prince of Squillace; the middle one a cardinal; the eldest, John, he saw to it was created duke, and to him also a wife ... daughter of King Alfonso. When this man was thrown into the Tiber by night, through the snares of Cesare, the cardinal, brother ..., the Pope his father winked entirely at the crime. Against which crime Sannazaro poured out this epigram:

units.la: Piscatorem hominum ne te non, Sexte, ...
units.tr: Sixtus, I cannot pass over you, the fisher of men ...
Look, you fish with nets for your own son ...

units.la: De eodem & filia Lucretia tetriora ... rius: Ergo te semper cupiet Lucretia Sex... O fatum diri nominis! hic pater ...
units.tr: On the same man and his daughter Lucretia, even fouler things: ... "Therefore Lucretia will always desire you, Sextus ..." O fate of a dreadful name! This father ...

units.la: Idem ad Martinum Caracciolum Bot... filium ejus, Cynœdi Patris impudicam ...
units.tr: The same, to Martinus Caracciolus ... his son, the shameless daughter of the catamite Father ...

units.la: Et de eodem Johannes Jovius Pontanus ...
units.tr: And about the same man, Giovanni Gioviano Pontano ...

units.la: Hoc jacet in tumulo Lucretia nomine, sedre Thais, Alexandri filia, sponsa, nurus.
units.tr: Here in this tomb lies Lucretia by name, but in fact Thais, daughter of Alexander, bride and daughter-in-law.

units.la: Epitaphium ejus apud eundem Sannazarium hoc legere est:
units.tr: Her epitaph in the same Sannazaro can be read thus:

units.la: Fortasse nescis, cujus hic tumulus sit, Adsta viator, ni piget.
units.tr: Perhaps you do not know whose tomb this is. Stop, traveller, if it does not irk you.

units.la: Titulum quem Alexandri vides, haud illius Magni est, sed hujus, qui modo Libidinosa sanguinis captus siti Tot civitates inclytas, Tot regna vertit, tot duces letho dedit, Natos ut impleat suos.
units.tr: The title you see is not that of Alexander the Great, but of this man, who, lately seized with a lustful thirst for blood, overturned so many famous cities and so many kingdoms, gave so many leaders to death, that he might fill up his own sons.

units.la: Humana jura, nec minus cælestia, Ipsôsque sustulit Deos.
units.tr: He has abolished human laws, and no less the heavenly ones, and even the gods themselves.

units.la: Ut scilicet liceret, heu scelus! patri Natæ sinum permingere, Nec execrandis abstinere nuptiis, Timore sublato semel.
units.tr: So that, alas the crime, it might be permitted to a father to defile the bosom of his daughter, and not to abstain from accursed marriages, once fear has been removed.

units.la: I nunc, Nerones & Caligulas nomina, Turpeis vel Heliogabalos.
units.tr: Go now, and name Neros and Caligulas, or even the shameful Heliogabaluses.

units.la: Hoc sat viator: reliqua NON SINIT PUDOR. Tu suspicare, & ambula.
units.tr: This is enough, traveller: shame does not allow the rest. Do you guess, and walk on.

units.la: Sed missa hac belua, sive, ut cum Guicciardino Histor. lib. vj. loquar, Dracone hoc, qui immoderata ambitione, & pestifera perfidia, omnibusque horrendæ crudelitatis, monstrosæ libidinis, & inauditæ avaritiæ exemplis universum orbem infecit; misso etiam successore ejus Pio III. Scenico viginti sex dierum Pontifice; ad Julium II. Sixti IV. ex fratre nepotem; flectamus, quem Guicciardinus idem lib. ix. ait ebriosum, deliciis voluptatibusque innutritum fuisse. Filia ei fuit, Felix nomine, quam Papa factus Johanni Jordani Ursino in matrimonium dedit, Onuphrio teste. Omitto, quæ de vi nobilibus adolescentibus illata ei à Gallis objecta fuerunt, ne hostiu nio inniti videar. Julius successòrem hab de quo hæc Jovius lib. iv. vit. Leon. Non caruit infamia, quòd parùm honestè c cularijs (erant enim è tota Italia nobilij & cum his tenerius atque liberè jocari v excusando homini: Sed quis vel optimus mus princeps in hac maledicentissima aulà los vitavit? Et quis ex adverso tam mali invidiæ tabe consumptus, ut vera demum noctium secreta scrutatus est? Ac si ar nomine sugillari inclyta virtus potuit, I periorem Principum Sixti IV. Innocenti dri VI. fama comparatus, æstimatione nentiæ laudem feret. Sic qui profligatiffi mines nondum pudorem omnem decoxi celat, probus videri potest. Hominis co & atheismum Pici Mirandulani, & Sforc ftimoniis Hift. Pap. ff. 155. convicimu drianus VI. Germanus, germana virtute p ftrofarum libidinum infamia immunis ipf men familiam, Onuphrio teste, non habu go eo, Clementem VII. ex illegitimo con P. Jovius Hiftor. lib. iij. deferibit: Nem rat, cùm neminem adamaret, præterqu cultiore causa conciliatos, his certè unis e ter favit, ut ad summos honores, aut ad j tatis locum stabilèsque divitias nullo pu Proximus ei Paulus III. aliquot spuriis r Petrum Alioisium ad Parmæ & Placent ctum, horrendæ libidini deditum licet, pensè amavit, atque exprobrantibus hoc v di vitiorum commonstratorem filio non f Quasi verò qui cœlibatum professus & simulans, damnato congressu filium gignit, genito incontinentiæ œstrum non affricet, & libidinis exemplum, quoties ille ortûs sui recordatur, non suggerat? De stupris ejus & incestibus nefandis multa horrida liber Italicè scriptus, & à Sleidano Hist. lib. xxj. contractus, & ipso quoque Thuano Citatus, commemorat. Atqui hic ille est, qui Johanne Casa, Archiepiscopo Beneventano, quem de laudibus Sodomiæ poëma confecisse, supra ostendimus, legato uti non dubitavit. Prodigiosæ inprimis libidinis, qui eum excepit, homo, Julius III. Cardinalis adhuc, Onuphrio teste, veluti furtim voluptates sequebatur. Pontifex factus votorum jam omnium compos, abdicatâ rerum curâ, hilaritati & genio suo nimium indulsit. De eodem sic Thuanus lib. vj. & xxviij. Innocentius Montanus (qui quòd in familia simiæ curam gereret, Simiæ etiam post adeptam dignitatem, nomen retinuit) summâ amplissimi ordinis infamiâ à Julio III. in Collegium Cardinalium cooptatus, majore infamia postea vitam exegit; accusatus patrem & filium caupones, ut illius uxore potiretur, interfecisse. Innocentium hunc adolescentem, quo tempore Bononiæ legatus fuerat Julius, in deliciis habuisse ferebatur. Papa ergo factus, Innocentio huic galerum suum largitus, eundem in domesticam consuetudinem rursus admisit, eíque cognomen & insignia sua attribuit. Romæ tum fama fuit, & libellis quoque perscribebatur, (sic Sleidanus commemorat) à Jove Ganymedem foveri, licet deformem. Sed nec ipse Pontifex hoc ad reliquos Cardinales dissimulare, & fertur per jocum aliquando commemorare, quàm sit lascivus adolescens & importunus. Plura de eo Papirii Massoni, quin & ipsius Pallavicini fide Hist. Pap. ff. 176. tradidimus. Denique Pium IV. Julio huic subrogatum fuisse verbis & scommatibus acutum, cibi vinique avidum, dum, in voluptates pronum &c. Onuphrius ... ftis est.
