After making this contract, he examines his Python, questions him, and even draws out curious things, as Thuanus records in his Hist. lib. cxxxii. that Cotonus did with the demon of Hadrian's Fraxinea.

units.la: XXIII. In hoc enim Exorcistico dramate & directæ & indirectæ Magiæ impietatem nullo negotio cernere est.
units.tr: XXIII. In this exorcistic drama, one can see without any difficulty the impiety of both direct and indirect magic.

units.la: Directa enim est, quia Exorcista per certa verba, characteres, ceremonias, nusquam institutas, nihil ex revelatione Divina vel naturali significantes operantésve, mira facit, aut facere præsumit, idque ope Diaboli, ex pacto non implicito duntaxat, sed explicito etiam. Nam expellit dæmonem per superiorem dæmonem; & ex ejus revelatione rei occultæ notitiam venatur. Pactum cum eodem init, cùm illum hac vel illa conditione emittit, dimittit, promissum ἀμοιβαῖον seu mutuum, & quidem in forma ab illo recipit, societatem cum eo, saltem imperfectam, init colitque. Indirecta eadem est, quia ex pacto implicito Exorcista utitur illis mediis, quibus Magi uti solent ad effectus similes. Sic enim Toletus lib. iv. cap. 14. n. 10. indirectam, seu interpretativam Magiam ipse describit.
units.tr: It is direct, because the exorcist, through certain words, characters and ceremonies nowhere instituted, which signify or work nothing from divine or natural revelation, performs, or presumes to perform, marvels, and does so by the help of the devil, under a pact not merely implicit but also explicit. For he expels a demon by a higher demon, and he hunts out knowledge of hidden things from its revelation. He enters into a pact with it when he sends it out or dismisses it on this or that condition, a promise ἀμοιβαῖον [mutual] or reciprocal, and indeed in a form that it accepts from him. He enters into and maintains fellowship with it, at least an imperfect one. It is indirect in the same way, because by an implicit pact the exorcist uses those means which magicians customarily use to achieve similar effects. Thus Toletus, lib. iv. cap. 14. n. 10., himself describes indirect or interpretive magic.

units.la: XXIV. Et sanè Magos inter & Exorcistas tanta γνῶσιςaffinitas tanta intercedit, ut ovum ovo similius non sit. Etenim primò, apud Magos omnia suis præcisè constant formulis & verbis, quibus ex præscripto artis utuntur, & vim atque efficaciam ad opera, quæ intendunt, peragenda, inesse persuasissimum habent.
units.tr: XXIV. And indeed between magicians and exorcists there is such a great γνῶσις [knowledge] of affinity that one egg is not more like another. For first, among magicians everything consists precisely in their formulas and words, which they use according to the prescription of their art, and they are firmly persuaded that power and efficacy to accomplish the things they intend are present in them.

units.la: Carmina vel Cæto possunt deducere lunam.
units.tr: Songs can even draw the moon down from heaven.

units.la: Sic planè Exorcistæ verbis & ritibus præscriptis contra dæmonem & maleficia ejus singularem efficaciam tribuunt. Efficacia illa vel naturalis, vel supernaturalis, vel magica est. Non est naturalis, quia verba habere vim naturalem vel morbos sanandi, vel noxas depellendi, merito ipse Delrio Disquisit. Mag. lib. j. cap. 4. q. 3. negat. Supernaturalis dici nequit, quia, quæ sic operantur, vim suam immediatè consequuntur à Deo, & speciali ipsius institutione ac promissione niituntur. Atqui Deus nusquam ritus & formulas exorcisticas præscripsit, neque iisdem eventum talem promisit; neque Ecclesiæ, à qua institutæ dicuntur, recepit, se ejusmodi formulis ab illa institutis pondus & virtutem supernaturalem additurum. Tum quæcunque supernaturali vi prædita sunt, eventum suum infallibiliter sortiuntur, quomodo Hierarchici eandem ob causam Sacramentis virtutem conferendi gratiam ex opere operato decernunt. Denique formulæ ejusmodi virtutem supernaturalem habent vel ex opere operantis, vel operato, uti Hierarchici loqui amant. Non prius, quia fidem, devotionem &c. ad validitatem exorcismi neque in Exorcista, neque in energumeno requirunt. Non posterius, quia sic nullum discrimen inter Sacramenta, quæ Divinæ, & Sacramentalia, ad quæ exorcismum illi referunt, quæ humanæ institutionis sunt, intercederet. Æqualem quippe ex opere operato efficaciam haberent, quod ipsimet adversarii negant. Secundò, Exorcistæ maledictis & convitiis dæmonem insectantur, quorum magnos subinde catalogos conficiunt, uti in Manuali Exorcismorum videre est. Id verò ortum est ex disciplina Apollonii Thyanæi, statuentis, convitia & maledicta esse præsentissimum contra dæmonum insultus remedium. Non sic profectò Michaël Archangelus Jud. v. 9. Neque extricant se dicentes, maledicere se Diabolo propter culpam, quia id ipsum Michaël prætexere potuissFet. Tertiò, Exorcistæ suffumigationibus, Delrione, Valesio, Mengo testibus, utuntur. Iisdem usi Magi sunt, Ethnici & Judæi Exorcistæ, Delrione Disquisit. Mag. lib. vj. cap. 2. ff. 2. q. 2. teste; nec non Hermes, Porphyrius, Proclus, Cornelius Agrippa de Philos. Occ. lib. j. cap. 43. ubi multa ille de suffitibus ad convocandos fugandósque dæmones philosophatur. Neque forte aliunde, quàm ex Kabala Magica Judæorum personatus ille Tobiæ Raphaël suum ex piscis corde & extis suffitum ad Asmodæum fugandum hausit. Quartò, Magicæ disciplinæ consulti Judæi & Gentiles contra dæmonum insultus & maleficia sua amuleta & phylacteria adhibebant; ab ipso Delrione lib. 1. cap. 4. q. 4. eo nomine damnati. Idem hodierni Exorcistæ factitant. Nam ædes exorcizandorum palmis benedictis exornant, cereum benedictum accendunt, eorum collis reliquias, agnos Dei, sacra amuleta, schedulas appendunt; stolas iisdem, imagines, cruces applicant, de quibus Manuale Exorcisticum part. 1. infiit. 6. videre est. Quintò, anxiè multa ex energumenis Magi scissitari solebant, uti ex Act. xvi. 6. nec non Apulejo Apol. 1. liquet. Ita planè Exorcistæ moderni cum Sathana in colloquium descendunt, & abstrusissima quæque ex eo percontantur. Sextò, Exorcistæ Novenas suas ex antiqua superstitione in exorcismis suis adhibent. Quamvis enim Novenam servare potiùs quàm Septenam, à superstitione Bresserus de Const. lib. vj. cap. 21. num. 293. excusatum eat; tamen numerum formalem aliquid occultare, quod dæmonis ex pacto operationem spectat, Delrio lib. 1. cap. 4. q. 2. statuit. Novemdialia tanquam superstitiosa Augustus, teste Petro Bungo Bergomate Mysler. Num. de Num. ix. abrogavit; & novem vicibus orasse Ethnicos, cùm lemures placare vellent, idem ex Alexandri Tom. II. ggg GenialiGentilibus lib. ij. 12. refert. Multa quinetiam de numero Novenario, & ejus scala Cornelius Agrippa, quem Magorum Patriarcham Hierarchici faciunt, de occulta Philosophia lib. j. 12. tradidit. Septimo Magi olim à Diabolo corporis post peractos exorcismos deserti signa flagitarunt. Cujus rei nobile exemplum Eleazarum, qui extracto dæmoni imperavit, poculum aqua plenum, quod illic posuerat, everteret, in signum, quòd Energumenum reliquisset, Iosephus Antiquit. Iud. lib. viij. 2. recitat. Similia digressionis suæ signa à dæmone petere exorcistas, ex Manuali Exorcistico part. 1. Instruct. 9. constat; & Delrio lib. vj. cap. 2. ff. 3. 7. 9. agnoscit; neque aliud exemplum antiquitatis profert, quàm illud Eleazari, quem ipsemet prius lib. ij. q. 30. ff. 3. tanquam Magum traduxerat. Quàm verò enormè facinus sit, signa petere à Diabolo, quotusquisque ignorat?
units.tr: Thus the exorcists plainly ascribe singular efficacy to their prescribed words and rites against the demon and his witchcraft. That efficacy is either natural, or supernatural, or magical. It is not natural, since Delrio rightly denies, Disquisit. Mag. lib. j. cap. 4. q. 3., that words have a natural power to heal diseases or to drive away harms. Nor can it be called supernatural, since things that work in this way receive their power immediately from God and rest on a special institution and promise of his. But God nowhere prescribed exorcistic rites and formulas, nor promised such an outcome to them; nor has the Church, from which they are said to have been instituted, received that it would add weight and supernatural virtue to formulas instituted by itself. Moreover, whatever is endowed with supernatural power infallibly produces its effect, as the Hierarchics, for this very reason, decree that the sacraments confer grace ex opere operato. Finally, formulas of this kind have their supernatural virtue either ex opere operantis or ex opere operato, as the Hierarchics like to put it. Not the former, because for the validity of the exorcism they require faith, devotion and so on neither in the exorcist nor in the person possessed. Not the latter, because then there would be no difference between the sacraments, which are divine, and the sacramentals, to which they refer exorcism, which are of human institution; for they would have an equal efficacy ex opere operato, which the adversaries themselves deny. Secondly, the exorcists assail the demon with curses and insults, of which they compile long catalogues from time to time, as can be seen in the Manual of Exorcisms. This indeed arose from the discipline of Apollonius of Tyana, who laid down that insults and curses are the most effective remedy against the assaults of demons. Michael the Archangel certainly did not do this, Jude 9: "Neither did they dare to bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee," since Michael could have pleaded the very same thing, that he was cursing the devil for his fault. Thirdly, the exorcists use fumigations, as Delrio, Valesius and Menghus bear witness. Magi used the same, pagan and Jewish exorcists, as Delrio testifies, Disquisit. Mag. lib. vj. cap. 2. ff. 2. q. 2.; and also Hermes, Porphyry, Proclus, and Cornelius Agrippa, de Philos. Occ. lib. j. cap. 43., where he holds forth at length on fumes for summoning and driving away demons. Indeed, it is probably from the Jewish Magical Kabbalah, and from nowhere else, that that character Raphael in Tobit drew his fumigation of fish heart and entrails for putting Asmodeus to flight. Fourthly, Jews and Gentiles who consulted the magical art used amulets and phylacteries against the assaults and witchcraft of demons; Delrio himself condemns them on that account, lib. 1. cap. 4. q. 4. Today's exorcists do the same. For they adorn the houses of those to be exorcised with blessed palms, light a blessed candle, and hang upon them relics of their saints, Agnus Deis, sacred amulets and little papers; they apply stoles, images and crosses to them, as can be seen in the Manual of Exorcism, part. 1. infiit. 6. Fifthly, the Magi used to inquire anxiously into many things from the possessed, as is clear from Acts 16:16 and also from Apuleius, Apol. 1. Thus the modern exorcists plainly enter into conversation with Satan and question him about the most abstruse matters. Sixthly, the exorcists employ their Novenas, drawn from ancient superstition, in their exorcisms. For although Bresser, de Const. lib. vj. cap. 21. num. 293., excuses the keeping of a nine-day period rather than a seven-day one from superstition, Delrio, lib. 1. cap. 4. q. 2., holds that a formal number conceals something that concerns the operation of the demon by pact. Augustus abolished the Novemdialia as superstitious, according to Peter Bungus of Bergamo, Mysler. Num. de Num. ix.; and the same author, from Alexander's Tom. II., Genialium Dierum lib. ij. 12., reports that the pagans prayed nine times when they wished to appease the lemures. Cornelius Agrippa, whom the Hierarchics make the patriarch of the Magi, also set down much concerning the number nine and its ladder, de occulta Philosophia lib. j. 12. Seventhly, the Magi of old demanded from the Devil, after the exorcisms were completed, signs that he had left the body. A noble example of this is that of Eleazar, who, after drawing out the demon, ordered it to overturn a cup full of water that he had placed there, as a sign that it had left the possessed; Josephus relates this, Antiquit. Iud. lib. viij. 2. Similar signs of his departure the exorcists demand from the demon, as is established by the Manual of Exorcism, part. 1. Instruct. 9.; Delrio also acknowledges it, lib. vj. cap. 2. ff. 3. 7. 9.; nor does he bring forward any other example from antiquity than that of Eleazar, whom he had himself earlier, lib. ij. q. 30. ff. 3., cited as a Magus. How monstrous a crime it is to ask signs from the Devil, how few are ignorant of that?

units.la: XXV. Grave certè etiam illud est, quòd dæmonis, cui sic expellendo Exorcistæ desudant, testimonio superstitiones suas commendare non verentur, à qua insania ipsi forte gentiles abhorruerunt. Exempla quædam Delrio lib. ij. parte j. quæst. 7. §. j. profert. Neque possum hic stigmatum Francisci commendationem similem, extantem Conformit. lib. ij. parte 2. pag. 309. præterire. Sextò, inquit Conformitatum author, authentizatur stigmatizatio beati Francisci testimonio malignorum spirituum, de quibus supra dictum est. Dæmon enim per os cujusdam mulieris cuidam Baroni habitanti in montibus juxta Eugubium dixit, loquendo inter alia de stigmatibus beati Francisci, quòd Christus videns beatum Franciscum sibi datum à Deo Patre pro signifero, ipsi sua vulnera impressit, & clavos in manibus & pedibus, & in latere dextro vulnus: sicut jam patet in corpore suo, & multi jam viderunt. Alius dæmon cuidam domino Bartholomæo, de tertio ordine
units.tr: XXV. It is certainly also grave that exorcists, while toiling at expelling the demon, are not ashamed to commend their superstitions by his testimony, a madness from which the Gentiles themselves perhaps shrank. Delrio, lib. ij. parte j. quæst. 7. §. j., sets forth some examples. Nor can I pass over here a similar commendation of the stigmata of Francis, found in the Conformit. lib. ij. parte 2. pag. 309. Sixth, says the author of the Conformities, the stigmatization of blessed Francis is authenticated by the testimony of malignant spirits, concerning whom it was said above. For a demon, through the mouth of a certain woman, said to a certain baron living in the mountains near Gubbio, speaking among other things about the stigmata of blessed Francis, that Christ, seeing blessed Francis given to him by God the Father as a standard-bearer, impressed his wounds upon him, and the nails in his hands and feet, and the wound in the right side, just as is now evident on his body, and many have already seen it. Another demon, to a certain lord Bartholomew, of the third order of blessed Francis, speaking about the sanctity of blessed Francis, among other things foretold, long before the stigmatization, for about two years, that blessed Francis himself would be stigmatized by God.

units.la: Impietatem exorcistarum Magicam augeri, quòd testimonio Diaboli superstitiones suas commendant. Francisci stigmata Diabolo testibus probata sunt. dine beati Francisci, loquens de sanctitate beati Francisci inter alia ante stigmatizationem B. F. bene per biennium, prædixit, ipsum beatum Franciscum stigmatizandum à Deo. Inquit enim dæmon: Adhuc notum est toti mundo, qualiter Christi passio in hoc homine beato Francisco renovetur. Alius dæmon peros mulieris Zantesse dixit Fratri Jacobo de Bononia de tertio ordine B. F. coram 18. testibus: Duo tantummodo sunt in Cælo signati, scilicet Crucifixus, & stomachosus ille Franciscus. Sciens enim Christus, se illi daturum stomachoso bullam suorum stigmatum, non permisit ipsum aliud de indulgentia Portiunculæ privilegium accipere, vel bullam manu hominis fabricatam. Nam sicut Rex non committit annuli sui bullam alicui, nisi propter aliquod magnum factum: ita crucifixus, quando voluit salvare populum suum, noluit illi stomachoso concedere aliud signum, nisi bullam suorum stigmatum. Hactenus dæmones de stigmatibus Francisci. An sic, qui testimonium dæmonis in re dubia admittunt, producunt, laudant, pacto expresso ad veritatem dicendam eum prius non obligarunt? Et an Magi scelesti quique majora attentárunt?
units.tr: The magical impiety of the exorcists is increased, in that they commend their superstitions by the testimony of the Devil. The stigmata of Francis have been proved by the testimony of devils. of the order of blessed Francis, speaking of the holiness of blessed Francis among other things, foretold, a good two years before the stigmatization of B. F., that blessed Francis would be stigmatized by God. For the devil said: "It is now known to the whole world how Christ's passion is renewed in this man, blessed Francis." Another devil, speaking through the mouth of a woman of Zante, said to Brother James of Bologna, of the third order of B. F., in the presence of 18 witnesses: "Only two are sealed in heaven, namely the Crucified and that hot-tempered Francis. For Christ, knowing that he would give that hot-tempered one the seal of his stigmata, did not permit him to receive any other privilege, such as the indulgence of the Portiuncula, or a seal made by human hand. For just as a king does not entrust the seal of his ring to anyone except for some great deed, so the Crucified, when he wished to save his people, was unwilling to grant that hot-tempered one any other sign than the seal of his stigmata." Thus far the devils on the stigmata of Francis. Did not those who admit, produce and praise the testimony of a devil in a doubtful matter first bind him, by an express pact, to tell the truth? And did not the wicked magicians attempt even greater things?

units.la: XXVI. Non energumenos duntaxat Exorcistæ, sed Maleficiatos etiam, hoc est, per fortilegium & veneficium quoddam morbo extraordinario vexatos & effascinatos, exorcismis suis liberare se profitentur.
units.tr: XXVI. Exorcists profess that they free by their exorcisms not only the possessed (energumeni) but also the bewitched (maleficiati), that is, those vexed and fascinated by an extraordinary illness brought on through a certain sorcery and poisoning.

units.la: Exorcismi illius formulas tertia pars Manualis Exorcismorum repræsentat. Quòd si pertinacior Sathanas cedere nolit, (raró quippe, si res peragatur sçriò, ad optatum finem pervenitur) tum verò Exorcista exulceratus comicam actionem suam claudit protestatione simili, qualis etiam locum habet in Exorcismis Energumenorum finiendis; quæ Manual. Exorc. par. 2. pag. 205. ejusmodi recitatur: Quandoquidem superbi ac maledicti dæmones ad Divini nominis invocationem
units.tr: The third part of the Manual of Exorcisms sets out the formulas of this exorcism. But if the more obstinate Satan is unwilling to yield (for indeed, if the thing is carried out in earnest, the desired end is rarely reached), then the exorcist, exasperated, closes his comic performance with a protestation similar to that which also has its place in ending the exorcisms of the possessed. It is recited in this form in Manual of Exorcisms, part 2, p. 205: "Since you proud and accursed devils, at the invocation of the divine name,

units.la: Exorcismus Maleficiatorum magicâ impietate laboratûs. nem ab hujus creaturæ ejus vexatione non desistitis, ne il-lud vobis impune futurum existimetis, quoniam ignis, grando, nix, glacies & spiritus procellarum pars erit calicis vestri. Adeo scilicet impotentes etiam fuerunt Christus & Apostoli, quorum exemplo & authoritate novi Exorcistæ se tuentur: Sed de hoc quicquid sit, quomodo à Magiæ crimine Exorcismos ejusmodi absolvent? Veluti cùm per eos Maleficos etiam absentes diræ torquent quàdam, si Diis placet, dæmonum in illos reactione. Quòd si, uti Grillandus quæst. 2. de Sortil. num. 4. argutatur, maleficia non nisi arte dæmonis tolli possunt; quia juxta regulam juris nihil tam naturale est, quàm eodem genere quodque dissolvi, quo colligatum esse reperitur; sequetur, ideo in Maleficiis Exorcismos exerceri, ut Satan cogatur dissolvere, quæ ipse colligaverit; quod annon sit indirectè ejus opem invocare, ut prodasse putetur, cùm desinit nocere, uti Lactantius Institut. lib. v. 16. loquitur, ipsi certè viderint. Denique cum Adversarii ipsimet statuant, illicitum esse non tantum maleficia maleficiis curare, apud Delrionem lib. vi. cap. 2. ff. 1. q. 2. sed etiam, tentare id rebus superstitiosis & vanis; licet id Delrione agnoscente, multi Canonistæ & Theologi Pontificii haud nefas duxerint: petere à Malefico parato, ut maleficium maleficio tollat; quamvis Aureolus in 2. dist. 34. q. 2. & Angelus de Clavasio v. Maleficium n. 13. id licitum esse pertendant: vi & verberibus à maleficis, aut etiam precibus opem implorare; uti fusius contra Remigium disputat Delrio, nisi probabiliter credat, inquit hic, illud posse fieri modo aliquo licito: denique juxta Johannem Hesselium à Lovanio, reclamante licet Delrione, Maleficii signa destruere, ut Diabolus nocere desinat; quomodo Exorcistæ suis exorcismis licitè & citra Magiæ saltem participatæ crimen vel persuadere, vel cogere Diabolum ad sanandos Maleficiatos possunt, cùm nulla probabili ratione sibi persuadere ausint, Sathanam maleficium modo licito remoturum; aut id non facturum destructione signi, ex cujus pacto operatus fuerat?
units.tr: Exorcism of the bewitched, afflicted by magical impiety. …from this creature's vexation do not desist. Do not think this will go unpunished for you, since fire, hail, snow, ice and the spirit of storms shall be the portion of your cup. So then Christ and the apostles were also so powerless, by whose example and authority the new exorcists defend themselves! But whatever be the case here, how will they absolve such exorcisms from the crime of magic? Just as when, through them, certain curses are hurled even against absent sorcerers, by a kind of rebound of demons upon them, if it pleases the gods. But if, as Grillandus argues (q. 2 de Sortil., n. 4), spells can be removed only by the art of the devil, because by the rule of law nothing is so natural as that each thing be dissolved by the same kind by which it is found to be bound; it will follow that exorcisms are performed in cases of witchcraft so that Satan may be compelled to undo what he himself has bound. Is this not indirectly to invoke his aid, so that he may be thought to have benefited when he ceases to harm, as Lactantius says (Institutes, bk. v, ch. 16)? Let them see to that themselves. Finally, since the opponents themselves hold it unlawful not only to cure witchcraft by witchcraft (Delrio, bk. vi, ch. 2, ff. 1, q. 2) but also to attempt this by superstitious and vain means; although Delrio acknowledges this, many Papist canonists and theologians have not thought it a sin to ask a sorcerer who is ready to remove a spell by a spell; though Aureolus (on 2 dist. 34, q. 2) and Angelus de Clavasio (v. Maleficium, n. 13) maintain it is lawful to implore help from sorcerers by force and blows, or even by prayers; as Delrio disputes more fully against Remigius, unless he probably believes, as he says, that this can be done by some lawful means: finally, according to Johannes Hesselius of Louvain, though Delrio protests, to destroy the signs of witchcraft so that the devil ceases to harm. How then can exorcists, by their exorcisms, lawfully and without at least the guilt of participating in magic, either persuade or compel the devil to heal the bewitched, since they dare not persuade themselves by any probable reasoning that Satan will remove the witchcraft by a lawful means, or will not do so by destroying the sign by whose pact he had worked?

units.la: XXVII. Affinis huic est exorcismus, quo Diabolum Exorcistæ compellunt ad restituendum chirographum,quo ab eo seducti eidem se obligárunt; nec non Eucharistiam ipsam à suis clientibus acceptam. Extat Exorcismus pro chirographo Manual. parte 2. pag. 206. & pro Eucharistia ibid. pag. 210. Non potest autem Diabolus ad restitutionem vel chirographi, vel Eucharistiæ adigi, quin exorcismis evocetur eò, ubi priùs non erat, quod Magicum planè & necromanticum est. Et mirum planè est, Hostiam consecratam, hoc est, ex hypothesi Hierarchicorum, Christum ipsum sic tradi Diabolo posse, ut nonnisi ægrè & exorcismorum tormentis atque balistis ab eo recipi possit. Siccine ergo Christus Rex ille invictus gloriæ, in potestatem Diaboli venire, & ad inferos deportari potest? Quid ergo de eo fieret, nisi per exorcismos Sathanas ad restitutionem compelleretur? Quo jure vel Manuale Inst. 2. par. 1. inter Energumenorum notas refert, quòd rerum sacrarum præsentiam, Missæ sacrificium præsertim, ferre nequeant: vel Delrio lib. vj. cap. 2. ff. 3. q. 2. remediis spiritualibus contra dæmonem certissimis accensetEucharistiam venerabilem, si non solum illam præsentem ferre, sed etiam auferre, & ablatam mordicus retinere, sola exorcismorum vi sibi extorquendam potest? Annon sic quiritari cum Labane Hierarchici, & cum Diabolo expostulare possunt: Quare furatus es Deos meos, Genef. xxxi. 30. Stultitia est, inquit ad eum locum à Lapide, quod Deos dicit, qui se à furibus custodire nequeunt. Et Deus verus Israëlis erit, qui se à Diabolo sartum tectumque custodire nequit.
units.tr: XXVII. Akin to this is the exorcism by which exorcists compel the devil to restore the bond by which those seduced by him bound themselves to him, and likewise the Eucharist itself, received from their clients. There is an exorcism for the bond in Manual, part 2, p. 206, and for the Eucharist ibid., p. 210. The devil cannot, however, be forced to restore either the bond or the Eucharist without being summoned by the exorcisms to a place where he was not before, which is plainly magical and necromantic. And it is truly astonishing that the consecrated Host, that is, on the hypothesis of the hierarchists, Christ himself, can be so handed over to the devil that he can be recovered from him only with difficulty and by the torments and crossbows of exorcisms. Is Christ, then, that unconquered King of glory, able to come into the power of the devil and be carried off to hell? What then would become of him, unless by exorcisms Satan were compelled to restore him? By what right does the Manual (Inst. 2, par. 1) list among the signs of the possessed that "they cannot bear the presence of sacred things, the sacrifice of the Mass above all;" or Delrio (bk. vi, ch. 2, ff. 3, q. 2) count among the most certain spiritual remedies against the demon the venerable Eucharist, if it can be wrested from him by the power of exorcisms alone, so that he not only bears its presence but also carries it off and holds it fast once taken? Can they not complain with Laban and expostulate with the devil: "Why have you stolen my gods?" Genesis 31:30. "It is foolish," says Lapide on that passage, "to call them gods which cannot guard themselves from thieves." And will he be the true God of Israel who cannot keep himself safe and sound from the devil?
ggg 3
XXVIII.

units.la: XXVIII. Sicut autem pro hominibus ex maleficio ægris Exorcista est Medicus: ita veterinariam idem exercet pro jumentis & bestiis per maleficia afflictis; purgat ædes malis spiritibus vexatas; parat remedia contra invisibilem lactis, butyri, aliarúmque rerum per incantationes abalienationem: exorcizat lac, butyrum, caseum, ova; denique Exorcista est DEUS Averruncus, qui omnia mala suis conjurationibus propulsare potest. Aqua, terra, aër, ignis, omniáque ex quatuor elementis mixta; tempestates etiam, nubes, tonitrua, fulmina, grandines, quæque peculiares suas conjurationes habent, quas in flagello Dæmonum, Hieronymo Mengo authore scripto, legere est, nempe videlicet Hierarchicis Nephelæ diotæ, Guteutæ, & Phylactériis in Synodo Trullana can. 61. damnati desinunt. Sic planè nomen Dei sumitur in vanum, verbum ejus profanatur, commercium & familiaritas cum Diabolo initur, superstitio alitur; Sathanæ occasio illudendi hominibus submi-nistratur, fiduciæ Christianæ vis & efficacia extinguitur, multa dæmoni tribuuntur, quæ vel immediatè à Deo hominess exercente fiunt, vel causas naturales habent, denique ea homines tum aggrediuntur, tum per media planè illicita exequuntur, quæ nec mandato & promissione Dei ulla, nec exemplo Sanctorum nituntur. Ipse Delrio lib. vj. Anaceph. monit. ÿ. contra nubium, aliarúmque ejusmodi rerum infectatores fusè disputat, eo argumento, quòd nubes & tempestetes sint vel à Deo, vel à Diabolo. Si à Deo, exorcismus instituetur sacrilegè contra authorem naturæ. Si à Diabolo, ejúsque maleficio, tum Exorcistis pactum cum Diabolo intercedat oportet.
units.tr: XXVIII. As the exorcist is the physician for people sickened by witchcraft, so the same man practises veterinary medicine for beasts of burden and other animals afflicted by sorcery. He cleanses houses troubled by evil spirits and prepares remedies against the invisible bewitching of milk, butter and other goods by incantations. He exorcises milk, butter, cheese and eggs. In short, the exorcist is God Averruncus, who can avert every evil by his conjurations. Water, earth, air, fire, and everything mixed from the four elements; storms too, clouds, thunder, lightning and hail, each of which has its own special conjurations, which may be read in the Flagellum daemonum written by Hieronymus Mengus, are all condemned by the Trullan Synod, canon 61, under the names Nephelae diotae, Guteutae and Phylacteria, as the hierarchical ... [sic] cease. Thus the name of God is plainly taken in vain, his word is profaned, a commerce and familiarity with the Devil is entered into, superstition is fed, Satan is given the opportunity to mock men, the power and efficacy of Christian trust is extinguished, many things are attributed to the demon which are done either directly by God acting upon men or have natural causes, and finally men both undertake these things and carry them out by means plainly unlawful, which rest on no command or promise of God and no example of the saints. Delrio himself, in Anacephalaeosis book 6, admonition 7, argues at length against those who pursue clouds and similar things, on the ground that clouds and storms come either from God or from the Devil. If from God, exorcism would be undertaken sacrilegiously against the author of nature. If from the Devil and his sorcery, then the exorcists must have a pact with the Devil.

units.la: XXIX. In Manuali eodem Exorcismorum pag. 295. præscribitur etiam Exorcismi formula contra quæcunque animalia noxia, vermes, mures, serpentes, & alia quæcunque agros vel aquas insigniter efficientia & corrumpentia.
units.tr: XXIX. In the same Manual of Exorcisms, page 295, a form of exorcism is also prescribed against all harmful animals, worms, mice, snakes, and whatever else notably spoils and corrupts fields or waters.

units.la: Ubi non solùm Exorcista dæmones, ut mala ista amoveant, adjurat, sed ipsos quoque vermes exorcizat & adjurat, ut confestim abeant; imò imperat severè, ut decrescant deficiántque. Exempla memorata digna adducit Felix Malleolus Canonista, Præpositus Solodurensis, & Cantor Tigurinus, in tractatibus de Exorcismis; quæ Majorum nostrorum miserè seductorum praxin ob oculos ponunt. Ita, narrante eo, S. Wilhelmus, Episcopus Lausannensis, ab anguillis lœsus, omnes anguillas è ditione sua exorcismis expulit & relegavit: B. Pruminius insulam S. Marci prope Constantiam, venenatis inquinatam vermibus, adjurationibus mundavit: Georgius de Salutiis, Episcopus Lausannensis, tum vivens, contra sanguisugas, Salmonibus & aliis piscibus infestas, processum judiciarium instituit, sicut contra facinorosos fit. Publico igitur judicio damnatas, adjurationibus ex sacra Scriptura depromptis; ex lacu ejecit: Ejusdem Episcopi officialis Plebano Bernensi adversus easdem pestes similem procedendi formulam, d. 24. Martii A. C. MCCCCLI. tradidit: Benedictus à Monteferrat, Lausannensis etiam Episcopus actione adversus bruchos ex agro Bernensi ad Ecclesiasticum tribunal Lausannense citatos, instituit. Hæc de Lausannensibus duntaxat & Constantiensibus Episcopis Malleolus. Addit similia de Curiensibus, processum geminum instituere adversus animalia suetis. Solemnia tot in mundo Episcopos, prævia inprimis & recepta publica Exorcismi talis formula, in illa errorum & superstitionis nocte delirasse, cui dubium esse potest?
units.tr: Here the exorcist not only adjures the demons to drive away these evils, but also exorcises and adjures the worms themselves, that they depart at once; indeed he commands them sternly to shrink and perish. Felix Malleolus, canon lawyer, provost of Solothurn, and cantor of Zurich, in his treatises On Exorcisms, adduces memorable examples which set before our eyes the practice of our wretchedly deluded forefathers. So, by his account, Saint Wilhelm, bishop of Lausanne, injured by eels, expelled and banished all the eels from his territory by exorcisms. Blessed Pruminius cleansed the island of Saint Mark near Constance, polluted with poisonous worms, by adjurations. Georgius de Salutiis, bishop of Lausanne, while still living, instituted a judicial process against leeches infesting the salmon and other fish, as is done against criminals. Having condemned them by public judgment, he cast them out of the lake with adjurations drawn from holy Scripture. The same bishop's official gave a similar form of proceeding against the same pests to the parish priest of Bern, on 24 March 1451. Benedict of Montferrat, also bishop of Lausanne, instituted an action against locusts cited from the fields of Bern before the ecclesiastical court of Lausanne. Malleolus reports these things about the bishops of Lausanne and Constance alone. He adds similar things about the bishops of Chur, who instituted a double process against animals of that kind. Who can doubt that so many bishops throughout the world, using especially the established public form of such exorcism, were raving in that night of errors and superstition?

units.la: XXX. Ad hæc Delrio lib. iij. p. 2. q. 4. s. 8. cum Malleolo hoc confligens primò in genere respondet, Exorcismos & Ecclesiasticas depulsiones animalium probari, quas publicus Ecclesiæ usus recepit &c. In Ritualibus Romanis expressas habere formulas legitimas, &c. Deinde
units.tr: XXX. In reply to these things, Delrio, book 3, part 2, question 4, section 8, contending with Malleolus on this point, first answers in general that exorcisms and ecclesiastical expulsions of animals are approved by the public use the Church has received, etc. That the Roman Rituals contain legitimate formulas expressed, etc. Then

units.la: Delrio adversus Malleolum, exorcismos commendantem; nec non Suarez
units.tr: Delrio against Malleolus, who commends exorcisms; and likewise Suárez

units.la: de in specie de formula Exorcismi ab Episcopo Lausannensi dictati, regerit, nihil in ea contineri, quod improbari possit, nisi forte actus judiciarios vanos & superfluos, quod ipsum quoque de publica praxi Constantiensi & Crienfi sentiendum sit. Nos universum hoc drama exorcisticum Magicæ vanitatis accusamus merito, quia præceptum & promissionem Dei nullam habet; nomen Dei in vanum sumit, Scripturæ verbis temerè abutitur, torquens ea in finem alienum, cujus gratia edita non sunt; & imperio coërcere creaturas inanimatas & irrationales, nullius hominis dicto audientes, præsumit. Nam quod Suarez Tom. y. de Relig. lib. iv. 2. & ex eodem Gretserus de Benedict. lib. y. 7. contendunt, adjurationes per imperium directè etiam versari circa creaturas irrationales, non quoad intelligentiam, sed quoad efficaciam & effectum, cujus finis sit obedientia non moralis, sed quasi physica, quomodo Christus mari & ventis imperâsse legitur; frivolum plane est, tum quia absoluta ejusmodi Dei potentia & virtus thaumaturgica æquè in creaturas non cadit, ac non potentia creandi. Si, quod Navarrus Manual. cap. 27. num. 13. verè asserit, superstitionis est credere, quòd possit excommunicari locusta, bruchus, aut aliud genus vermium & animalium irrationalium; quidni adjuratio etiam creaturarum irrationalium, nedum cum excommunicatione conjuncta, superstitionem sapiet? Denique nulla ratione adjurationes ejusmodi excusari possunt, sive dicantur tendere in Deum, sive in creaturas, interveniente deprecatione ad Deum. Si ad creaturas, stolidæ sunt, quia creaturæ ejusmodi non intelligunt. Si interveniente deprecatione ad Deum, adeóque ad Deum referuntur, temeritate haud vacant, quia juxta ipsum Thomam 22. q. 95. art. 2. adjuratio per modum deprecationis pertinet ad eos, qui Divina invocatione miracula faciunt. Neque etiam modus deprecationis & imperii in eodem numero exorcismo jungi possunt, ut qui dicit: Exorcizo te creatura per Deum vivum; simul & Deum deprecatur, ut creaturis iis, expulsis inde dæmoniis benedicat; & Diabolo imperet, ut per illas damnum facere desinat.
units.tr: in particular, concerning the form of exorcism dictated by the bishop of Lausanne, replies that nothing is contained in it which could be disapproved, except perhaps vain and superfluous judicial acts, which must be judged the same of the public practice at Constance and Chur. We, however, rightly accuse this whole exorcistic drama of magical vanity, because it has no command or promise of God; it takes the name of God in vain, abuses the words of Scripture rashly, twisting them to an end foreign to that for which they were given, and presumes to restrain by command inanimate and irrational creatures, which obey no man's word. For what Suárez, Tome 5 on Religion, book 4, chapter 2, and Gretser after him, On the Blessings, book 5, chapter 7, maintain, namely that adjurations by command also bear directly on irrational creatures, not as to understanding, but as to efficacy and effect, whose end is not moral obedience but as it were physical obedience, as Christ is read to have commanded the sea and the winds; this is plainly frivolous, both because such absolute power and thaumaturgical virtue of God falls on creatures no more than the power of creating does. If, as Navarrus truly asserts in Manual, chapter 27, number 13, it is superstition to believe that a locust, a grasshopper, or any other kind of worm or irrational animal can be excommunicated, why would not the adjuration of irrational creatures, let alone when joined with excommunication, smack of superstition? Finally, such adjurations cannot be excused on any ground, whether they are said to be aimed at God or at creatures, with prayer to God intervening. If at creatures, they are foolish, since creatures of that kind do not understand. If with prayer to God intervening, and so referred to God, they are not free of rashness, because according to Thomas himself, 2-2, question 95, article 2, adjuration by way of prayer belongs to those who work miracles by invoking the divine name. Nor can the mode of prayer and the mode of command be joined in the same exorcism, as in one who says: I exorcise you, creature, through the living God, and at the same time prays to God that he bless those creatures, once the demons have been expelled from them, and commands the Devil to cease doing harm through them.

units.la: XXXI. Deinde cùm Delrio approbet Exorcismos, quos vocat Ecclesiasticos, qua fronte damnat ibidem, agricolarum & mulierculârum adjurationes, quibus hominum vel bestiarum morbos sanent, pro quibus Malleolus propugnat? Utrinque enim verba adhibentur optima, ex Scripturis petita, ad usus verò tales neque à Deo, neque à natura instituta. Pari etiam successu exercentur. Alexander Macedo, cùm pirata captus ad ipsum deductus esset, interrogavit, qua ille re fretus auderet maria infestare? Respondit pirata intrepidè: Ego, inquiens, quoniam id unico navigio facio, vocor pirata. Tu, cùm idem facias magna classe, Rex appellaris. Idem certè agricolæ & mulierculæ Delrioni respondere possent: Nos, cùm vel febrim, vel vaccæ aut equi læsionem, optimis etiam verbis & preculiis exorcizamus, vocamur incantatores & incantatrices. Tibi autem Episcopi, cùm idem in exorcizandis anguillis, sanguisugis & bruchis fecerint, Sancti & venerandi Patres cluent. XXXII. Idem Delrio lib. vj. cap. 3. adversus Godelmannum Exorcismos Hierarchicorum à Magica impietate purgare conatur. Qua ratione purget, operæ pretium erit paucis discutere. In exorcismo, inquit, persona, res, verba & intentio reperiuntur. Singula ille expiare conatur. Præste sequamur. Persona, inquit, culpa nulla. Non obsessi, cui licet ab Ecclesia remedium petere, quam novit pharmacopœam à Christo morbis spiritualibus institutam. Non exorcistæ. Nam institutus hic ordo jam ab Apostolorum fermè temporibus. Non eorum ornatus. Tum. II.
units.tr: XXXI. Further, since Delrio approves the exorcisms he calls ecclesiastical, with what face does he there condemn the adjurations of farmers and old women by which they heal diseases of men or beasts, which Malleolus defends? For in both cases the very best words, taken from the Scriptures, are used, yet for such uses they have been instituted neither by God nor by nature. They are also practised with equal success. When Alexander the Great had a captured pirate brought before him, he asked by what right he dared to infest the seas. The pirate answered fearlessly: "Because I do it with a single ship, I am called a pirate; you, because you do the same with a great fleet, are called king." The farmers and old women could certainly answer Delrio in the same way: when we exorcise a fever or an injury to a cow or horse, even with the best words and prayers, we are called enchanters and enchantresses. But you, since the bishops have done the same in exorcising eels, leeches and locusts, are celebrated as holy and venerable Fathers.

units.la: Nam stelâ cinguntur, eámque energumenis injiciunt; quæ meminêre feliciter sic usum Pontium Bonævallensem Abbatem. Sciunt hac dæmonem quasi ligari, & memorem fieri, eum esse Christi captivum, & à Christo subjugatum. Superpelliceum induunt, quia hoc officii & ordinis eorum signum est: sicque significant, se in pugnam non privata temeritate, sed ab Ecclesia auctoratos procedere. Non sic personas Delrio expiat. Obsessus enim à Deo & piis omnibus remedia petere potest legitima, in verbo Dei definita. Ubi verò ab Exorcistis adhibita remedia verbum Dei definivit? Neque media illicita vera Ecclesia adhibet: & quæ talia adhibet, vera Ecclesia, pharmacopœa Christi non est. Qui proin talia à quocunque requirit, haud lev.ius peccat, quàm Saul pythonissam in consilium adhibens. Exorcista vel ordinatus est, vel non est ordinatus. Ille verus exorcista non est, quia, uti Clementem supra dicentem audivimus, ἐξ ουρανοῦ ὁ χαρισματικός, Exorcista non fit ordinatione, sed libera voluntate Dei. Christus sanè initio Evangelicæ prædicationis, & aliquot post seculis, haud equidem ordinaria & perpetua vocatione Exorcistas instituit, sed quibusdam servis suis in nomine suo dæmones eiiciendi potestatem concessit. Apostoli, Episcopi, Presbyteri, purique sæpiùs laici, hoc dono, secundùm Spiritus S. instinctum utebantur, ita ut Tertullianus de corona Mil. cap. 11. suo tempore quosdam Christianos milites, non certum utique ordinem, Diabolos per exorcismos fugandi dono prædites fuisse, testetur. Neque sanè donum extraordinarium perpetuum in Ecclesia ordinem constituere potest. Exorcista porrò non ordinatus, ipso Delrione lib. vj. Anaceph. mon. 10. judice, extraordinarii juris, seu privilegii documenta ostendere debet talia, ut judicio Ecclesiæ idonea censeantur. Nulla verò non ordinati Hierarchicorum Exorcistæ ejusmodi documenta verbo Dei conformia producunt, quæ veræ Ecclesiæ judicio approbari queant. Neutri proin veri Exorcistæ sunt, utpote vocatione Divina legitima destituti æquè ac quivis Exorcistæ alii Judæi & gentiles, cum Diabolo congredientes, & quæstûs sui gratia cum eodem colludentes. Ipsæ subtiles eorum impostura, quibus infirmas mulierculas, quæ se obsessas fingunt, ad fabulam subornant, ut Exorcistis fidem conciliant, nimis evidentia malæ fidei argumenta præbent. Nota est historia Martæ Brosseriæ, à Thuano lib. cxxxiii. fusè narrata, quam, detecta Lutetiæ fraude, ausi sunt Romam deducere, ut de Senatu conquererentur.
units.tr: XXXII. The same Delrio, book 6, chapter 3, against Godelmann, tries to purge the exorcisms of the hierarchs from magical impiety. It will be worth our while to examine briefly how he purges them. "In an exorcism," he says, "a person, a thing, words and intention are found." He tries to purge each of these. Let us follow him step by step. "The person," he says, "is free of fault: not the one possessed, who may lawfully seek a remedy from the Church, which knows the pharmacy instituted by Christ for spiritual diseases. Nor the exorcist; for this order was instituted almost from the times of the Apostles. Nor are their vestments..." Then ... "For they gird themselves with a stole and place it upon the one possessed, which blessed Abbot Pontius of Bonneval is recorded to have used successfully. They know that by this the demon is as it were bound and made mindful that he is Christ's captive and subdued by Christ. They put on the surplice, because this is the sign of their office and order, and so they signify that they go into battle not by private rashness but authorized by the Church." Delrio does not purge the persons in this way. For the one possessed may seek from God and all the pious lawful remedies, defined in the Word of God. But where has the Word of God defined the remedies used by exorcists? The true Church does not use unlawful means, and whatever church uses such means is not the true Church, and does not have the pharmacy of Christ. Therefore whoever demands such things from anyone sins no less than Saul, who took a witch into counsel. An exorcist is either ordained or not ordained. That one is not a true exorcist, because, as we heard Clement saying above, [ek ouranou ho charismatikos], an exorcist is not made by ordination but by the free will of God. Christ indeed, at the beginning of the Gospel preaching and some centuries afterwards, instituted exorcists not by an ordinary and perpetual calling, but granted to certain of his servants the power of casting out demons in his name. Apostles, bishops, elders, and often even plain laymen used this gift according to the instinct of the Holy Spirit, so that Tertullian, in On the Crown of the Soldier, chapter 11, attests that in his time certain Christian soldiers, not indeed a fixed order, were endowed with the gift of putting Devils to flight by exorcisms. Nor can an extraordinary gift, being perpetual, establish an order in the Church. Moreover, an exorcist who is not ordained, by Delrio's own judgment in Anacephalaeosis, book 6, admonition 10, must show documents of such an extraordinary right or privilege, so that they may be judged fit by the judgment of the Church. But no unordained exorcists of the hierarchs produce documents of that kind, conformable to the Word of God, which could be approved by the judgment of the true Church. Therefore neither are true exorcists, being destitute of lawful divine calling, just as any other exorcists, Jews and Gentiles, who consort with the Devil and collude with him for the sake of their gain. Their own subtle impostures, by which they suborn weak old women, who pretend to be possessed, to act out a fable so as to win credit for the exorcists, provide all too evident arguments of bad faith. The story of Marta Brossier, told at length by de Thou, book 133, is well known; when the fraud was detected at Paris, they dared to take her to Rome, to complain before the Senate.

units.la: Inter alia, remedia miseræ applicata, Clerus Aurelianensis suffitum quendam, ex libro, Flagellum dæmonum dicto, adhibebat, quem inseram, ut quales Exorcistæ sint, appareat. Recipe, inquiunt, Galbani, sulphuris, Assæ fœtidæ, Aristolochiæ, Hypericonis, rutæ, uncias tres. Et omnia simul conjurata ac benedicta sequenti benedictione projice in ignem, & vexatum, velit nolit, diu fac super ignem suffumigari. Huic addunt benedictionem horribilem contra Spiritus malignos. Hoscine Exorcistas cum exorcismis suis, quales in Thesauro Exorcismorum A.M.DCVIII. Coloniæ impresso, cujus titulus ad fugandum vel audacissimum dæmonem idoneus est: Thesaurus Exorcismorum & conjurationum terribilium, cum practica probatissima diversorum authorum; Christus instituit? Tales Apostoli fuêre? Hanc artem pii veteres exercuêre? Hic ordo ab Apostolorum fermè (cautè sic Delrio loquitur, quia à Christo vel Apostolis institutum asseverare non potuit) temporibus institutus est? Si ergo, juxta ipsum Delrionem loc. cit. pacti dæmoniaci suspecti sunt laici & Clerici non præditi ordine exorcistarum: qui hoc munus quasi ex officio, aut peculiari gratia, donec Dei usurpant: illi quoque Clerici & religiosi, qui quasi proprium sibi vindicant; suspecti, imò comperti eruntc. runt Exorcistæ Hierarchicorum omnes, qui idem facitant. Neque interest, quas formulas usurpent, ab Ecclesia (quam pro vera nequicquam venditant) probatas an improbatas; cum ex verbo Dei probare eas nequeant; & ipsi Exorcistæ in Papatu haud raro formulas ritúsque ab Ecclesia non probatos usurpent; adeò ut sæpè Maleficiatus idem ab uno Exorcista ad potentiorem transfeat. Denique habitus à Delrione descriptus, Exorcistas eosdem prodit. Stola enim Exorcistæ dæmoni injecta, eundem ligari Delrio ait, planè sicut Magi Ethnici vestitu, lineis, coronis, &c. quasi vinculis quibusdam Diabolum ligare solebant, Eusebio Præpar. Ev. lib. v. 6. narrante. Unde verò hæc stolæ vis? A natura? Negabit. A Deo supra naturam operante? Ubi revelatio, quæ rei fidem faciat? Ubi institutio Divina, quæ stolæ hanc efficaciam largiatur? A dæmone ergo omnis est, qui se ligatum simulat, ut te liget.
units.tr: Among the other remedies applied to the wretched woman, the clergy of Orléans used a certain fumigation taken from a book called the Flagellum daemonum, which I will insert so that it may appear what sort of exorcists they are. "Take," they say, "galbanum, sulphur, asafoetida, birthwort, St John's wort, and rue, three ounces each. Consecrate and bless all these together, then cast them with the following blessing into the fire, and have the afflicted person fumigated over the fire for a long time, whether he likes it or not." To this they add a "terrible blessing against evil spirits." Do these exorcists, with their exorcisms (such as those in the Thesaurus Exorcismorum, printed at Cologne in 1608, whose title alone would frighten off even the boldest demon: Thesaurus Exorcismorum et conjurationum terribilium, cum practica probatissima diversorum authorum), have Christ as their founder? Were the Apostles like this? Did the pious men of old practise this art? Was this order instituted "almost" from the time of the Apostles (Delrio speaks cautiously in this way, since he could not assert that it was instituted by Christ or the Apostles)? If, then, as Delrio himself says in the passage cited, demoniacal pacts are to be suspected in "laymen and clerics who do not have the order of exorcists, who claim this office as if it were their duty or by special grace, until God takes it away; and also clerics and religious who claim it as their own," then all the exorcists of the hierarchy who do the same will be suspected, indeed found out. Nor does it matter whether the formulas they use have been approved or disapproved by the Church (which they vainly peddle as the true Church), since they cannot prove them from the Word of God; and the exorcists themselves in Papacy quite often use formulas and rites not approved by the Church, so that the afflicted person often passes from one exorcist to a more powerful one. Finally, the habit described by Delrio betrays the same exorcists. For Delrio says that when a stole is put on the demon, it is thereby bound, just as the heathen magi used to bind the devil with garments, threads, garlands and the like, as Eusebius reports in Praeparatio evangelica book 5, chapter 6. But whence comes this power of the stole? From nature? He will deny it. From God working above nature? Where is the revelation that would make this credible? Where is the divine institution that would grant the stole this efficacy? So the whole thing comes from the demon, who pretends to be bound so that he may bind you.

units.la: XXXIII. Pergit Delrio à personis ad res. Rerum, inquit, quæ adhibentur, vitium nullum invenias. Si adsunt accensi cerei, testantur, lucis adventum expectari à vera luce Christo, & fugam potestis tenebrarum. Si flagella & alapæ accedunt, moderatè fit, non ut corpus obsessi lædatur, sed ut contumeliæ impatiens obsessor, dissugiat.
units.tr: XXXIII. Delrio goes on from persons to things. "You will find no fault," he says, "in the things that are used. If lighted candles are present, they testify that the coming of light is awaited from the true Light, Christ, and the flight of the powers of darkness. If whips and blows are applied, this is done in moderation, not so that the body of the afflicted person may be harmed, but so that the besieger, who cannot bear insult, may flee."

units.la: Manum exorcizandis imponere docuére Apostoli & B. Martinus. Eucharistiam in hunc finem energumenis & ostendere, & fumendum præbere, efficax & frequens semper fuit. An sic, Delrio, res omnes, quibus, ceu remediis, Exorcistæ vestri utuntur, bona fide recitasti? Atqui inter res illas etiam est ipse Diabolus, ex quibus conftituitur princeps, qui alios ejiciat; quod licitum esse, Hieronymus Mengus in Flagello dæmonum tuetur: sunt amuleta, thus, panis, sal benedictum, rami palmarum, campanæ, agni cerei, oleum, aqua incensa, galbanum, sulphur, hypericum, ruta &c. à quibus Diabolum affici, vexari,
units.tr: The Apostles and St Martin taught that hands should be laid on those to be exorcised. To show and to offer the Eucharist to the energumens for this purpose has always been effective and common. Did you, Delrio, report all the things that your exorcists use as remedies in good faith? And yet among those things is the devil himself, from whom the prince is constituted who casts out the others; Hieronymus Mengus defends this as lawful in his Flagellum daemonum. There are amulets, incense, bread, blessed salt, palm branches, bells, wax lambs, oil, water that has been exorcised, galbanum, sulphur, St John's wort, rue, and so on, by which the devil is usually affected, troubled,

units.la: five res iis iis adhiberi foliat; vexari, cruciari, pelli Mengus, aliique defendunt. Etiam sanguine humano postibus illito fugari dæmonia Ludovicus Banairolus à Serario Comment. in Tob. cap. 8. citatus statuit. Taceo ceremonias plures,nec non figuras,quas inter cruces multiplicatæ eminent. Hæc aliáque vim afficiendi & pellendi dæmonem habent vel à natura; vel ab institutione Divina. Non ab illa, quia res ejusmodi corporeæ nil valent in dæmonem, quod ipse etiam Raphaël de la Torre, Doctor Pontificius Disput. 17. adversus Delrionem, Serarium, Mengum demonstrat. Non ab hac, quia Divinâ ad efficaciam ejusmodi in dæmonem exerendam institutione destituuntur. Eucharistia maximè obsignat gratiam spiritualem, non demum dæmonem fugat, ad quam etiam sumendam Energumenus, quandiu talis est, dispositus neutiquam est. Horribilis proin hæc Sacramenti profanatio est, quando ceu pharmacum quoddam in φαρμακείαν convertitur. Neque etiam quid significent ejusmodi media; sed quid operentur, & unde operentur, edisserere nobis Delrio, simulque, cur similibus mediis utentes incantatores aperti Magiæ crimine arcessendi, at Exorcistæ ab eodem absolvendi sint, exponere debuit.
units.tr: or by which these things are customarily used on him. Mengus and others maintain that the devil is troubled, tormented and driven out by them. Ludovicus Banairolus, cited from Serarius, Commentary on Tobit chapter 8, even holds that demons are put to flight by human blood smeared on the doorposts. I say nothing of the several ceremonies, and of the figures, among which the multiplied crosses stand out. These and other things have the power to affect and drive out the demon either from nature or from divine institution. Not from nature, because such bodily things have no power against the demon, which the Papist doctor Raphael de la Torre himself demonstrates against Delrio, Serarius and Mengus in his Disputation 17. Nor from institution, because such things lack the divine institution that would give them efficacy against the demon. The Eucharist chiefly seals spiritual grace; it does not drive out the demon, and an energumen, as long as he is such, is by no means fit to receive it. This profanation of the Sacrament is therefore horrible, when it is turned into a sort of drug, into pharmakeia [φαρμακεία]. Nor was Delrio bound to explain to us what such means signify, but what they accomplish and whence they accomplish it; and at the same time he ought to have set out why incantators using similar means must be summoned for the open crime of magic, while exorcists are absolved of it by the same man.
XXXIV.

units.la: Neque hîc tutum est confugere ad asylum approbationis & improbationis Ecclesiæ, ut licita videlicet judicentur media, quæ probavit Ecclesia Papalis, illicita, quæ improbavit; tum quia Pontificiæ Ecclesiæ authoritas apud alias Ecclesias, quæ impietatis Magicæ mediorum ejusmodi usum insimulant, nullo in numero est: tum quia approbationis suæ veritatem nullo certo principio demonstrat: tum quia nullius Ecclesiæ Hierarchicorum conclavis, nullius Papæ judicio determinatum est, quæ media, qui ritus, quæ formulæ, quibus casibus, quæ ars & methodus exorcizandi tantum adhibenda sit: tum quia media plurima ante ullam Ecclesiæ discussionem vel approbationem, nullo discrimine, usurpata sunt: tum denique quia fatentur celebres Doctores, sibi hactenus certa signa, quibus ante daemoniaca legitima à superstitionis discernant, comperta non fuisse, uti ex Raphaële de la Torre Disp. 3. ff. 30. & Gregorio de Valentia ad 2. 2. disp. 6. quaest. 13. puncto 3. aliisque abundè colligitur. Valentia enim ipse fluctuans miriones suos Exorcistas in bivio miseros relinquit, generalibus legis cuncta involvit, & pauca licet, ac vix centesimam Exorcisticae praxeos partem attingens, nihil tamen determinat, neque ullam Ecclesiae determinationem indicat. Et quicquid salvi conductus signis diacriticis & ceremoniis aut ex permissione aut consensu Ecclesiae, Episcopi, aut Theologicae facultatis huc accersunt, nihil aliud hinc confici potest, quàm quòd Magia hic & nunc licita sit, quia non peragatur sine permissione seu conniventia Ecclesiae, Episcopi cujuspiam vel Papae. Nos verò ipsam Ecclesiam, Papam ipsum sic permittentem, connivントem impietatis ejusdem accusamus merito.
units.tr: Nor is it safe here to take refuge in the sanctuary of the Church's approval and disapproval, namely, that the means which the Papal Church has approved are judged lawful, and those it has disapproved unlawful. This is so, first, because the authority of the Papal Church counts for nothing among the other churches, which accuse the use of such means of the impiety of magic; second, because it demonstrates the truth of its approval from no certain principle; third, because it has not been determined by the decision of any conclave of the hierarchy or of any pope which means, which rites, which formulas, in what cases, and what art and method of exorcising alone are to be used; fourth, because very many means were used without any distinction, before any discussion or approval by the Church; and lastly, because learned doctors confess that they have not yet found certain signs by which genuinely demoniacal cases may be distinguished from superstition, as is abundantly gathered from Raphael de la Torre, Disputation 3, folio 30, and from Gregorio de Valencia on 2.2, disputation 6, question 13, point 3, and others. For Valencia himself, wavering, leaves his thousands of exorcists wretched at the crossroads, wraps everything in general rules, and, although he touches on a few things and scarcely the hundredth part of exorcistic practice, he determines nothing and indicates no determination of the Church. And whatever they summon here, by way of the distinguishing signs of a safe-conduct and ceremonies, from the permission or consent of the Church, a bishop or a theological faculty, nothing else can be concluded from this than that magic is lawful here and now, because it is not carried on without the permission or connivance of the Church, of some bishop or of the Pope. But we rightly accuse the Church itself, and the Pope who thus permits it, of conniving at that same impiety.

units.la: XXXV. De verbis rem expeditam esse, ait Delrio. Ex Thyraeo enim monet, illa vel ad Deum, vel ad Sanctos, vel ad daemonem dirigi. Ad Deum dirigi, ut peccata remittat, misereatur obsessi, potentiâ suâ daemonem comprimat, ut exire compellat. Hoccine, inquit, Magi cum dicent? Tollant igitur orationem omnem, ut jejunia suffulére. Negent fidem historiarum omnium, quibus efficacitas orationis in expulsione daemonum contestata, repuant Christi Domini authoritatem, id Lucae cap. ix. asserentis. Ad Sanctos dirigi, ut Dei amicos, gratiâ valentes, ut nobis impetrent, quae petimus; eorumque adjungi interdum merita, ut primò & praecipuè Deus filii merita aspicians, & oculos ultra porrigens ad iis tincta & imbuta merita Sanctorum, citiùs moveatur. Ad daemonem nem denique dirigi, increpando eum severè, comminatorie & per modum imperii, sicut habet authoritatem à Deo: quo modo loquendi & ejiciendi dæmonem Apostoli utebantur, secuti exemplum Christi, & Sanctorum Ecclesiæ primitivæ. Nec Christi Jesu, inquit, nomen solum inculcatur, sed & alia Dei nomina, & cuncta Christi miracula, juxta illud Prudentii: torquetur Apollo Nomine percussus Christi, nec fulmina verbi Ferre potest: arcitant miserum tot verbera linguæ, Quod laudata Dei resonant miracula Christi.
units.tr: XXXV. Delrio says the matter of words is settled. For he advises, following Thyraeus, that they are directed either to God, or to the saints, or to the demon. Directed to God, "that he may forgive sins, have mercy on the besieged, restrain the demon by his power, and compel him to depart. Will the magicians say this? Then let them take away all prayer, as they have abolished fasting. Let them deny the trustworthiness of all histories, in which the efficacy of prayer in the expulsion of demons is attested, and let them reject the authority of Christ the Lord, who asserts this in Luke chapter 9. Directed to the saints, as friends of God who have influence to obtain for us what we ask, and to whose merits, sometimes, are added, so that God, looking first and chiefly at the merits of his Son, and extending his eyes further to the merits of the saints steeped and imbued in them, may be moved more quickly." Directed finally to the demon, "by rebuking him sternly, threateningly and in the manner of a command, as one who has authority from God; which is the manner of speaking and of casting out demons that the Apostles used, following the example of Christ and of the saints of the primitive Church. Nor is the name of Jesus Christ alone repeated," he says, "but also the other names of God and all the miracles of Christ, according to the saying of Prudentius: Apollo is tortured, struck by the name of Christ, nor can he bear the thunderbolts of the Word; so many blows of the tongue harass the wretched one, that the praised miracles of God resound."

units.la: Addunt alia nonnulla: petunt nomen dæmonis, exemplo Christi Marc. III. ut sciamus, cum quibus confligendum: petunt causam ingressûs, ut à similibus peccatis alii caveant, & eo vitato facilius sanetur energumenus: signum egressûs petunt, ut constet jam verè liberatum ægrum. Mendax quidem Diabolus est; sed exorcismi verum invito extorquent. Denique jubent illum proficisci in infernum, vel desertum aliquod, sub spe Divinæ ratificationis. Hactenus Delrio.
units.tr: They add some other points as well: they ask the demon's name, following the example of Christ in Mark 3, so that we may know whom we are to contend with; they ask the cause of his entry, so that others may beware of similar sins, and by avoiding them the energumen may be healed more easily; they ask for a sign of his departure, so that it is established that the sick man is truly freed. The Devil is indeed a liar, yet the exorcists wring the truth from him against his will. Finally they order him to depart into hell, or into some desert, in hope of divine confirmation. So far Delrio.

units.la: XXXVI. Sicut licita sunt bella, quæ leges & necessitas tuendæ publicæ honestatis & tranquillitatis exigit: ita preces Ecclesiæ sunt haud dubiè utiles & necessariæ. Magnam enim vim habet deprecatio justi efficax, Jac. v. 16. Sed quemadmodum bella, quæ præter legitimam necessitatem geruntur, nihil à latrocinio differunt, & sunt coram Deo tantò detestabiliora, quantò speciosiori Regiæ Majestatis prætextu geruntur: ita Exorcismi, qui præter verbum & vocationem Dei, verbis quantumvis sacris, & Divinitùs inspiratis, exercentur, tantò sunt abominabiliores coram Deo incantationes, quantò majori sanctitatis specie geruntur. Tales sunt Exorcismi Hierarchicorum, prætextu verborum ad Deum, Sanctos (qui per merita sua invocari sine idololatriæ crimine nequeunt) & dæmonem, velati. Quomodo Judæi etiam exorcistæ tam impiè non fuerunt, ut dæmonem pulsuri ad Deum verba nulla dirigerent; sed Magi tamen iidem verissimi, quia destituti dono & vocatione, verbis suis ad Deum directis singularem efficaciam tribuerunt. Sic plane Exorcistæ Hierarchicorum in formulis suis adhibent verba concepta, quibus singularem efficaciam adscribunt, putà Nomina Dei, Angelorum & Sanctorum, etiam vulgò ignota, cujusmodi sunt Hel, Heloym, Heloah, Sabaoth, Efercherech, Adonai, Jehova, Jah, Tetragrammaton, Saday, Messias, Hagios, Ischyros, HoTheus, Athanatos, Soter, Emanuel, Agla, Alpha & Omega &c. quæ nomina ordine isthoc interjectis crucibus ita collocata invenire est in conjuratione apud Mengum, in Flagello pag. 225. & alibi passim. Quarum etiam vocum singularem vim & efficaciam idem Mengus Prolegom. cap. 8. asserit, quamvis, fatente eodem, Paulus Grillandus sustineat, nomina ejusmodi vana esse & Magis usitata. Ejusdem farinæ sunt brevia & schedulæ, continentes sancta verba Dei, aut nomina Dei, quæ clam obscso alligari, eíque ad tollendam dæmonis vexationem applicari posse, idem Mengus Proleg. cap. 2. & 11. docet. Sed & verbis contumeliosis adversùs dæmonem, perpetuisque mysterismis & scommatibus haud vulgarem efficaciam Mengus tribuit, & ceteris omnibus conclamatis, ad hanc veluti sacram anchoram confugit, pag. 37. ut Sacerdos imponat Spiritibus (qui præ metu superioris dæmonis veritatem revelare non audent) nomina irrisiva, putà dicendo: Primus post principalem vocetur Fachinus, secundus pistor, tertius coquus Acheruntis, & hujusmodi. An sic Christus, sic Apostoli dæmones pepulere? An verba ejusmodi ad Deum directa, cum opinione singularis efficaciæ eorundem, fidelis precationis nomine venire nire possunt? Planè uti jejunia piscaria veri jejunii nomine hypocritæ venditant.
units.tr: XXXVI. Just as wars are lawful when the laws and the necessity of defending public honour and tranquillity demand them, so the prayers of the Church are beyond doubt useful and necessary, for "the effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much" (Jas. 5:16). But just as wars waged beyond lawful necessity differ in nothing from robbery, and are the more detestable before God the more they are carried on under the more specious pretext of royal majesty, so exorcisms performed without the word and calling of God, however sacred and divinely inspired the words, are the more abominable incantations before God the more they are carried on under the greater show of holiness. Such are the exorcisms of the Hierarchs, veiled under the pretext of words addressed to God, to the saints (who cannot be invoked through their merits without the crime of idolatry), and to the demon. The Jewish exorcists were not so impious as to direct no words to God when about to drive out a demon; yet the same were most true magicians, because, lacking the gift and the calling, they ascribed singular efficacy to their words directed to God. Thus the exorcists of the Hierarchs plainly use in their formulas set words, to which they ascribe singular efficacy, for example the names of God, of the angels and of the saints, even those commonly unknown, such as Hel, Heloym, Heloah, Sabaoth, Efercherech, Adonai, Jehova, Jah, Tetragrammaton, Saday, Messias, Hagios, Ischyros, HoTheus, Athanatos, Soter, Emanuel, Agla, Alpha & Omega, and so on. These names, set out in this order with crosses interposed, can be found in the conjuration in Mengus, in the Flagellum, p. 225, and elsewhere throughout. Mengus in the Prolegomena, chap. 8, also asserts the singular power and efficacy of these words, although Paulus Grillandus, as Mengus admits, maintains that names of this kind are empty and more commonly used by magicians. Of the same stripe are the little slips and scraps containing holy words of God or names of God, which, as Mengus teaches in the Prolegomena, chapters 2 and 11, may be secretly tied to the body and applied for removing the demon's vexation. Mengus also attributes no small efficacy to words of abuse against the demon, and to endless mysteries and mockeries; and, all other remedies having been exhausted, he takes refuge in this as if it were a sacred anchor, p. 37: that the priest impose on the spirits (who, for fear of the superior demon, do not dare to reveal the truth) mocking names, saying for instance: "Let the first after the principal be called Fachinus, the second the baker, the third the cook of Acheron," and suchlike. Did Christ and the Apostles drive out demons in this way? Can words of this kind, directed to God, with the belief in their singular efficacy, come under the name of faithful prayer? They peddle these things as the fasts of fish-eating under the name of true fasting, like hypocrites.

units.la: XXXVII. Non diffitentur Hierarchici ipsi, extare in Papatu varias exorcizandi formulas periculosas & superstitiosas, quibus prævertendis editum est Manuale Exorcismorum, cujus parte I. Insl. j. Exorcistis edicitur, serió caveant omnes alias preces & ceremonias, quantumcunque bonæ & piæ apparent, quàm quæ in approbato Manuali præscribuntur, adhibere, nisi obtentâ venia, & consulto Ordinario. Ante expurgationem igitur illam, formulas superstitiosas & Magicas obtinuisse, inficias ire nequeunt. Sed & Delrio ipse lib. vj. Anaceph. num. 10. fatetur, plures Clericos & Religiosos peculiares exorcizandi formulas, & ritus habere diversos à communis Ecclesiæ ritibus & formulis. Quin Index Expurgatorius A. M. DCXII. Madriti excusus authoritate solenni, præscribit, ut ex libro, qui inscribitur Ordo baptizandi cum modo visitandi, Venetiis A. M. DLXXV. impressō, sol. 314. deleatur tota Exorcismus Luciferina (licuit scilicet Hispanis Inquisitoribus Exorcismum facere generis fœminini) cujus initium est: Adesto Domine tui famuli, &c. Deleatur item, inquiunt, alia Exorcismus Cypriani, cujus initium est: Ego Cyprianus, &c. usque ad Euangelium Johannis, quod est ad calcem &c. Unde colligere est, vel ipso Tribunali sacro teste, etiám in Rituales libros Hierarchicorum, qualis est illè Ordo baptizandi, Exorcismos planè Diabolicos & detestandos irrepsisse.
units.tr: XXXVII. The Hierarchs themselves do not deny that in Papacy there are various dangerous and superstitious formulas for exorcising, against which a Manual of Exorcisms was published; its part I, Instr. 1, Exorcists are directed to take care seriously not to use any other prayers and ceremonies, however good and pious they may appear, than those prescribed in the approved Manual, unless with permission obtained and the Ordinary consulted. Before that purging, therefore, they cannot deny that they had superstitious and magical formulas. But Delrio himself, in Book 6, Anacephalaeosis, no. 10, admits that many clerics and religious have their own particular formulas and rites of exorcising, differing from the common rites and formulas of the Church. Indeed the Expurgatory Index printed at Madrid under solemn authority in 1612 prescribes that from the book entitled Order of Baptizing with the Manner of Visiting, printed at Venice in 1575, page 314, there be deleted the whole Luciferian Exorcism (it was evidently permitted to the Spanish Inquisitors to make an exorcism of the feminine gender), whose beginning is: "Be present, Lord, to your servant," etc. Also to be deleted, they say, is another Exorcism of Cyprian, whose beginning is: "I, Cyprian," etc., up to the Gospel of John, which is at the end, and so on. From this one may infer, with the sacred Tribunal itself as witness, that even into the ritual books of the Hierarchs, such as that Order of Baptizing, there crept exorcisms that are plainly diabolical and to be detested.

units.la: XXXVIII. In verbis ad dæmonem imperantibus, exorcismi proram & puppim constituere solent. Imperant porrò Exorcistæ dæmoni, & imperando eundem cogunt, ut doceat & revelet ea, quæ faciunt ad ædificationem proximi & salutem obsessi (ita Diabolus per imperium Exorcistæ fit doctor & salvator hominum) ut indicet na- men collocatur,
units.tr: XXXVIII. The prow and stern of exorcisms are usually set up in the words commanding the demon. Exorcists go on to command the demon, and by commanding compel him to teach and reveal those things which serve the edification of the neighbour and the salvation of the one possessed (so the Devil by the exorcist's command becomes the teacher and saviour of men), to disclose his na-

units.la: Tom. II. iii men suum, socios, causam ingressus, quo modo crucietur maximè, quis eum expellere debeat: (ita fit doctor ipsius Exorcistæ, sui proditor & confitens religiosus:) ut confesse ratificet: ut promittat, se expulsum non relicturum socium, nec redituru m , & daturum signum egressus: & restituturum ablata, Eucharistiam imprimis (sic Exorcista cum Diabolo contrahit, adeoque cum eo pactum expressum init; fingente obsequium, quod ultrò præstat) ut confiteatur aliquam fidei veritatem, & virtute ejus Deo exhibeat reverentiam, flectendo genua, inclinando caput, terram ter percutiendo, adorando trinitatem (en Diabolum per imperium Exorcistæ poenitentem, reverentem Dei:) ut Lucifer, omnesque potestates infernales, daemones contumaces & inobedientes in inferno crucient: ut daemon principalis obsidens secum inferiores daemones educat: ut conceptis verbis juret (formulâ juramenti præscriptâ ei tali: Ego &c. ex nunc invoco Deum iratum &c. voco similiter Luciferum cum omnibus aliis principibus furiis & poenis infernalibus &c. Sic daemonis jam juramentum etiam fit controversiæ omnis finis. Vah foetidam & Diabolicam Theologiam:) Hæc aliáque plus quam Manliana imperia nomen Dei atrociter profanantia, & religionem universam ludibrio exponentia, in Manuali Navarri, Maximiliani ab Eynattem, Mengi flagello daemonum, cum horrore legere est. Dæmones scilicet ipsos dicto suo audientes obsequentésque habent. Quomodo etiam, Malleolo de Exorcism. tract. j. narrante, S. Theodulus, Sedunensis Episcopus, ingentem campanam, à Leone Papa sibi donatam, per daemonum obsequia Româ Sedunum portandam curavit. Quare enim non, inquit Malleolus, sic Viri Catholici proficerent, ut ipsis obedirent daemonia? Nummi & fenestrae extant, quibus non tantùm Theoduli, Patroni Sedunensis, sed etiam campanæ, imò &c. imò & Diabolorum campanam tergo gestantium vorago insculpta conspicitur, frustrà Delrione, rerum Helveticarum ignaro, historiam suspectante.
units.tr: me, his companions, the cause of his entry, how he is to be most tortured, who ought to expel him: (so the exorcist becomes the teacher of the Devil himself, his betrayer and a religious confessor), to ratify his confession; to promise that, once expelled, he will not leave behind a companion, nor return, and will give a sign of his departure, and will restore what he has taken, above all the Eucharist (so the exorcist contracts with the Devil and thus enters into an express pact with him, the Devil feigning the obedience he freely offers), to confess some truth of the faith, and by its virtue to show reverence to God, bending the knees, bowing the head, striking the ground three times, adoring the Trinity (behold the Devil, by the exorcist's command, made penitent and reverent towards God), that Lucifer and all the infernal powers, and the stubborn and disobedient demons, be tormented in hell; that the principal demon possessing him lead out the lesser demons with him; that he swear in set words (a formula of oath is prescribed for him, such as: "I, etc., now invoke the angry God," etc., "I likewise call upon Lucifer with all the other princes, furies and infernal punishments," etc. Thus the demon's oath too becomes the end of every controversy. Oh, foul and diabolical theology!). These and other commands, more than Manlian in their atrocious profaning of God's name and their exposure of the whole of religion to ridicule, may be read with horror in the Manual of Navarrus, of Maximilian ab Eynatten, and in Mengus's Scourge of Demons. Evidently they have demons obedient and submissive to their word. Likewise, as Malleolus relates in On Exorcisms, tract. 1, Saint Theodulus, bishop of Sion, had a huge bell, given to him by Pope Leo, carried from Rome to Sion by the services of demons. For why, says Malleolus, should Catholic men not so prosper that demons obey them? There are coins and windows extant in which is engraved not only Theodulus, patron of Sion, but also the bell, and even the abyss of the Devils carrying the bell on their backs, in vain suspected of being a fabrication by Delrio, who was ignorant of Swiss history.

units.la: XXXIX. An ergò fidem facere potes, Delrio, an potes, quisquis te exorcistam jactas, eo modo loquendi & ejiciendi dæmonem, Apostolos usos esse, exemplum Christi secutos? Etenim Christus, Divina virtute & potestate præditus, Marci ix. 25. sic dæmonem pepulit: Ἐγὼ σοι ἐπιτάσσω, ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ. Ego tibi præcipio, exi ex eo. An imperio suo ligavit dæmonem, subegit pronuntiare, jurare, fidem confirmare, vera narrare, signum dare egressus, stipulari, quòd comites secum abducere, & redire nolit? An tale quid fecerunt uspiam Apostoli, fideles alii veteris Ecclesiæ? Illi verò dono illo ejiciendi dæmones præditi, illud non usurpabant sine speciali instinctu Spiritus Dei, nec de effectu dubitabant, miraculorum fide præditi; qui confestim sequebatur post orationem ad Deum, & imperium ad dæmonem nomine Dei. Neque eum in finem artem componebant, præscribentes varias formulas & rerum etiam corporalium, post specialem adjurationem, applicationes. Novi autem hi exorcistæ, non Christi, non Apostolorum, sed filiorum septem Scevæ Judæi Pontificis (Act. xix. 12. 13.) æmuli, nec dono miraculorum, nec vocatione Divina instructi, ex præscripto novæ artis & methodi, cujus constitutiones & præcepta vix numerari possunt; dæmonibus imperare tentant. Quibus haud raro non tam verbis, quàm re ipsa impurus ille Spiritus respondet: Jesum novi, Paulum scio. Sed vos qui estis? Hoc verò facit, quoties adversùs imperia eorum se contumacem gerit. Gerit autem sæpissimè, nunquam gesturus, si imperia illorum talia essent, qualia fuerunt Christi & Apostolorum, qui irrito conatu nunquam aliquid dæmoni imperarunt. Si Christus iis æquè ac Apostolis dedit jus imperii in malos Spi-
units.tr: XXXIX. Can you then, Delrio, or whoever you are that boast yourself an exorcist, make it credible that the Apostles used this manner of speaking and of driving out demons, and followed the example of Christ? For Christ, endowed with divine power and authority, drove out the demon thus (Mark 9:25): Ἐγὼ σοι ἐπιτάσσω, ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ. I command you, come out of him [Ἐγὼ σοι ἐπιτάσσω, ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ]. Did he bind the demon by his command, force him to pronounce, to swear, to confirm the faith, to tell the truth, to give a sign of his departure, to stipulate that he would not take companions with him and would not return?
