Did the Apostles, or other faithful men of the early Church, ever do anything of the kind? They, endowed with that gift of driving out demons, did not use it without the special impulse of the Spirit of God, nor doubted the outcome, being endowed with faith in miracles, which followed immediately upon prayer to God and command to the demon in the name of God. Nor did they compose an art for this purpose, prescribing various formulas and the application of bodily things after a special adjuration. But these new exorcists, the rivals not of Christ or the Apostles but of the seven sons of Sceva the Jewish chief priest (Acts 19:12–13), without the gift of miracles and without divine calling, try to command demons according to the rule of a new art and method, whose regulations and precepts can scarcely be counted. To these, not seldom, that unclean spirit replies not so much in words as in deed: "Jesus I know, and Paul I know. But who are you?" He does this whenever he shows himself stubborn against their commands. He shows himself so very often, though he would never do so if their commands were of the kind that Christ's and the Apostles' were, for these never attempted anything against a demon in vain. If Christ gave to these men, as to the Apostles, the right of command over the evil spirits—

units.la: qua Magick impietatis convincentur. los Spiritus, censebitur Deus in ipsis & per ipsos imperare dæmonibus. Deo verò imperanti dæmonem non obsequi, quid absurdius est? Atque hæc ipsa imperiorum impotentia apud obsessos plures certissimam fidem facit tum illa Divina non esse, successum aliàs infallibilem habitura: tum imperia, quæ successum habere videntur, non vi ulla Divina, sed consensione & simulatione mera Sathanæ, vel Exorcistarum etiam impostura, successum habere. Nam, ut aurea illa Johannis de Hassia repetam, ipse simulat se captum, ut te capiat: se vinctum, ut te vinciat: se tuo imperio subditum, ut te sibi subdat. Quin etiam potest (sic Raphaël de la Torre de Potest. Eccl. coërcendi dæmones disput. 3. pag. 14. scribit) unus dæmon alterum ejicere è loco aut ab hominibus per collusionem; sive dæmon ejiciendus sit ordinis inferioris, sive non: videlicet quia invicem sibi obsequuntur propter aliquos malos fines, & quodammodo paciscuntur, ut unus exeat ad alterius voluntatem. Denique velim Exorcista aliquis mihi Jesuitam Cotonum v. g. adjurantem, & conjurando Sathanæ imperantem, ut doceat de vita Regis, Geneva plagiaria, locis Scripturæ Purgatorium probantibus &c. à Mago simili conjuratione & imperio dæmonem ligante, vinciente, ad facienda imperata cogente distinguat.
units.tr: by which the impiety of magic is convicted. The spirits, it will be thought, that God himself commands through them and in them. But that a demon should not obey God when he commands, what could be more absurd? And this very powerlessness of commands, observed among many of the possessed, gives certain proof that these commands are not Divine, since they would otherwise have infallible success; and that commands which seem to succeed do so not by any divine power but by the mere consent and pretence of Satan, or even by the trickery of the exorcists. For, to repeat that golden saying of John of Hesse: he pretends to be seized so that he may seize you; to be bound so that he may bind you; to be subject to your command so that he may subject you to himself. Indeed, one demon can (so Raphaël de la Torre writes in de Potest. Eccl. coërcendi dæmones disput. 3. pag. 14.) expel another from a place, or from men, by collusion, whether the demon to be expelled be of the lower order or not: namely, because they obey one another for certain evil ends, and in a way make a bargain, so that one goes out at the other's will. Finally, I should like some exorcist to tell me how he distinguishes his own adjuration of Satan, when he commands him by conjuration to tell about the life of the King, or to prove Geneva a plagiarist, or to prove Purgatory from passages of Scripture, as a Jesuit such as Coton does, from a magician's similar conjuration and command that binds and fetters the demon and forces him to do what he is ordered.

units.la: XL. Præterire hic non possum magni illius Ignatianos inter nominis, Petri Canifii, adjurare dæmonem soliti per nomen Mariæ, non Christi. Is adhibitâ statuâ Mariæ Qetins gensis, imperiis suis subigebat dæmonem Mariæ laudes decantare, septies terram sculari, Mariam ut Deum adorare, quinquies Orationem Dominicam & toties Angelicam salutationem recitare: quinimò non tantùm intercessoris & benedicentis munere defungi, orando hunc in modum: Maria gratiâ plena. Gratia & misericordia sit cum omnibus in hoc templo versantibus. Oro Deum pro ipsis; sed etiam Ecclesiastæ, concionando hæc in verba: Et Christiani, nàs Diaboli cogimur obedire Mariæ, & vos ipsi obedientiam negabitis? Quî tandem egredi cœactus sæpius ingeminavit: Væ, væ, væ mihi misero. Intra viginti annorum spatium nullus dæmonum tantis tormentis subjectus fuit, quantis ego. Historiam Hasenmullerus Hist. Jesuit. cap. 8. pag. 308. commemorat. Gemelkum est, quòd Delrio lib. iv. part. 3. q. 7. inducit dæmonem Laodunensis energumenæ ex ore Calvinianos irridentem & exclamantem, nihil sibi ab iis timendum, quoniam amici essent & fœderati. Idem lib. vj. cap. 2. §. 3. q. 3. utitur testimonio sagæ cujusdam ad probandos exorcismos, quòd illa puellam lemuribus ad Jesuitas amandaret. Misso Cotoni quæstiones, Monachi Michaelis historiam Ludovici Gaufridi, aliorum, judicium controversiarum fidei à dæmoniis exposcentium infandam. Macte Viri Exorcistæ! Flectere cùm nequeatis superos, ut impietati vestræ suffragentur, Acheronta imperiis vestris movete alacriter, ut fides vestra, exorcismi vestri, testimonio tali haud forte indigni, propitium habeant.
units.tr: XL. I cannot pass over here the famous Petrus Canisius, one of the Ignatians, who was accustomed to adjure demons by the name of Mary, not of Christ. Using a statue of Mary, he compelled the demon by his commands to sing Mary's praises, to bow seven times to the ground, to adore Mary as God, and to recite the Lord's Prayer five times and the Angelic Salutation as many times. Nay more, he did not merely perform the office of intercessor and benefactor, praying in this manner: Mary, full of grace. Grace and mercy be with all who dwell in this temple. I pray God for them; but also, as preacher, he spoke these words: And Christians, we are forced by the Devil to obey Mary, and will you yourselves refuse obedience? Why then, as he was compelled to depart, he cried out repeatedly: Woe, woe, woe is me, wretched one. Within the space of twenty years no demon was subjected to such torments as I have been. Hasenmüller recounts this history in Hist. Jesuit. cap. 8. pag. 308. It is also worth noting that Delrio, in lib. iv. part. 3. q. 7., introduces the demon of the possessed woman of Laudun mocking and shouting from her mouth against the Calvinists, that they had nothing to fear from them, since they were friends and allies. The same author, in lib. vj. cap. 2. §. 3. q. 3., uses the testimony of a certain witch to prove the exorcisms, namely that she was sending the girl with lemures to the Jesuits for love. I pass over Coton's questions, the history of the monk Michael, the story of Louis Gaufridi, and others, the monstrous judgment on controversies of faith that demons are asked to give. Well done, men of exorcism! Since you cannot move the gods above to support your impiety, stir up Acheron by your commands, so that your faith and your exorcisms may have as their propitious witness one not unworthy of such testimony.

units.la: XLI. Denique de intentione Exorcistæ sic Delrio: Illa Magica non est, quia speraт & cupit duntaxat pro officii sui ratione ac munere, Divina potestate sibi concessa & promissa, dæmonem in Dei nomine ejicere, & sue consortem natura ea miseria eripere. Officii rationem frustrà ille urget. Quæ enim per miraculum duntaxat fiunt, officio & muneri ordinario neutiquam subjacent. Neque Divinam potestatem probat, quam præte xentes etiam filii Sceuæ adeò non Diabolum expulerunt, ut eum potius infestorem dominumque passi sint. Non noscet multos Christus, jactantes etiam: Nonne in nomine tuo dæmonia ejecimus Matth. vii. 22? Concessam sibi & promissam non magis probabunt, quàm concessam sibi similiter & promissam Sive denique quod intentionem exorcistæ quam cum Magorum intentione convenire probatur. missam potestatem morbos omnes sanandi, linguis diversis loquendi, mortuos suscitandi. Destituti ergò dono, vocatione, mandato, promissione, nihil in nomine Christi, nihil potestate Divina agunt; sed implicitò saltem cum Sathana pacto constrictos se produnt, quamcunque præ se mentem & intentionem ferant. Sed verendum profectò est, ne eorum intentio conveniat cum intentione Magorum, hoc unum satagentium, ut scientes abscondita, & facientes humanis viribus altiora, suis concupiscentiis inserviant, & Thaumaturgi, miraculorum patratores adeòque Deo similes videantur. Quod vel solæ eorum fraudes creberrimæ, & μύθοι πσοφισμένοι fabulæ, arte compositæ, ab Erasmo etiam in lepido Dialogo, cui nomen Exorcismus dedit, irrisæ & exagitatæ testantur. Licet enim quondam Ambrosius Serm. 91. de Invent. Corp. S. Prot. & Gervasii negare visus fuerit, fieri posse, ut quisquam se Energumenum simulet; experientia tamen contrarium clarissimè testatur, nec ipsi adversarii inficiantur.
units.tr: XLI. Finally, Delrio says this about the exorcist's intention: It is not magical, because he hopes and desires only, in keeping with the reason and function of his office, to cast out a demon in the name of God, by the divine power granted and promised to him, and to rescue his fellow-sufferer from that miserable condition. But he presses the reason of his office in vain. For things that happen only by miracle are in no way subject to an ordinary office and function. Nor does he prove the divine power, which the sons of Sceva also claimed, yet they did not cast out the Devil at all, but rather suffered him to become their attacker and master. Will Christ not recognise many who boast, "Have we not cast out demons in your name?" (Matt. 7:22)? They will no more prove the power granted and promised to them than the power granted and promised similarly to them, namely to heal all diseases, speak in various tongues, and raise the dead. Deprived therefore of the gift, the calling, the commission and the promise, they do nothing in the name of Christ, nothing by divine power; but they betray themselves as bound at least implicitly by a pact with Satan, whatever mind and intention they profess. Yet it is truly to be feared that their intention agrees with the intention of the magicians, who busy themselves with this one aim: that, knowing hidden things and doing what is higher than human powers, they may serve their own desires, and may appear as wonder-workers and doers of miracles, and so like God. This is shown by their very frequent frauds and cunningly devised fables [μῦθοι σεσοφισμένοι], which Erasmus also mocked and ridiculed in his witty Dialogue entitled Exorcismus. For although Ambrose once seemed to deny, in Serm. 91. de Invent. Corp. S. Prot. & Gervasii, that it can happen that anyone should pretend to be possessed; experience clearly proves the opposite, and even the adversaries do not deny it.

units.la: XLII. Ab Exorcismis in genere, atque in specie iis, qui extra Sacramenta obtinent, ad Benedictiones, quæ ipsæ tamen Exorcismorum quandam rationem habent, pergimus.
units.tr: XLII. We now proceed from exorcisms in general, and in particular from those which are used outside the sacraments, to blessings, which nevertheless have something of the character of exorcisms.

units.la: Utiles & necessarias esse benedictiones quasdam creaturarum, ad usum nostrum Divinitùs destinatarum, ultrò fatemur. Ita cibi, quibus vescimur confervandi corporis ergò, cum benedictione, hoc est, verbo, precibus, piis votis & gratiarum actione sanctificantur. 1. Tim. iv. 3. 4. Par ratio symbolorum Sacramentalium, Divinitus ad usum suum legitimum institutorum, quibus Dei verbo præeunte & gubernante, Christi videlicet mandato & exemplo, solenniter benedicimus. Hæc benedictio pia, utilis & necessaria est. Dispar plane ratio est benedictionis illius, qua creaturis quibusvis benedicendo eam virtutem & efficaciam homines imprimere conantur, quam ex neque ex
units.tr: We readily admit that certain blessings of creatures, divinely appointed for our use, are useful and necessary. Thus foods, which we eat for the preservation of the body, are sanctified by blessing, that is, by the word, prayers, pious wishes and thanksgiving (1 Tim. 4:3-4). The sacramental elements, divinely instituted for their proper use, are in the same way solemnly blessed, with God's word going before and guiding, namely by Christ's command and example. This blessing is pious, useful and necessary. The case is entirely different with that blessing by which men, blessing creatures of any kind, try to impress on them a power and efficacy which they have neither from their own nature and the intention of God the Creator, nor from a supernatural institution and certain divine revelation.

units.la: Benedictionum licitarum & Magicarum differimen explicatur. que ex natura sua & intentione Dei Creatoris: neque ex institutione supernaturali certaque revelatione Divina habent. Quæ haud dubie species quædam Magiæ implicitæ est; consitente haud obscure Augustino Hummæo, qui axiomata ex Thomæ doctrina collegit, cujus hæc verba ex 2.2.Th. q. 96. art. 2. legere est: Uti rebus ad eos effectus assequendos, procreandos vel prænuntiandos, quorum ille res, neque causæ sunt, neque legitima secundùm Divinam vel naturalem institutionem signa, superstitiosum est, & à religione Christiana alienum. Ita si quis, extra usum Sacramentorum, de quibus hic non agitur, petat, uti Hierarchici in Missali suo solent, ut hic panis sit omnibus sumentibus salus mentis & corporis &c. ut Deus vino benedicat, ut sit contra omnes morbos & venenata, & immunda, atque universas inimicorum insidias tutamentum, remedium contra periculum corporis & animæ, & prægustatio ad vitam æternam &c. non vacabit Magiæ saltem implicitæ crimine, quia certis verbis & ritibus, à quibus discedere nefas ducit; creaturas certas, contra naturæ ac institutionis Divinæ ordinem, ad usum supernaturalem & Spiritualem referit. Neque enim aliam ob causam agricolarum & mulierculARUM benedictiones Magicæ impietatis convincuntur, quàm quia benedicendo, creaturis efficaciam & virtutem quandam impertiri conantur, quam nec ex natura sua, nec ex Divina institutione obtinent.
units.tr: Between lawful and magical blessings. This is undoubtedly a kind of implicit magic, as Augustinus Hummaeus clearly agrees, who gathered his axioms from the teaching of Thomas. His words may be read in 2.2, q. 96, art. 2: To use things to obtain, produce or foretell those effects of which those things are neither causes nor legitimate signs by divine or natural institution, is superstitious and foreign to the Christian religion. So if anyone, outside the use of the sacraments (which is not the subject here), asks, as the hierarchs customarily do in their Missal, that this bread may be health of mind and body to all who eat it, and that God bless the wine, that it may be a protection against all diseases and poisons and unclean things, and against all the snares of enemies, a remedy against danger to body and soul, and a foretaste of eternal life, he will not be free of at least the guilt of implicit magic, because by fixed words and rites, from which it is wicked to depart, he directs certain creatures to a supernatural and spiritual use, contrary to the order of nature and of divine institution. Indeed, the blessings of farmers and old women are convicted of magical impiety for no other reason than that, by blessing, they try to impart to creatures a certain efficacy and power which they have neither from their nature nor from divine institution.

units.la: XLIII. Benedictionibus ejusmodi Papatus fatet to- tus.
units.tr: XLIII. The whole Papacy abounds in blessings of this kind.

units.la: Vulgares & speciales tot sunt, ut numerus earum iniri nequeat. Ecclesiasticas vero & communes ex Missali, Pontificali, Cæremoniali, Rituali seu Pastorali, Durantis Rationali & libris Exorcisticis discere est. Libet velut in quodam formulas nonnullas, quibus creaturarum quarundam metamorphoses & incantationes Mystæ hi peragunt
units.tr: Common and particular ones are so many that their number cannot be counted. The ecclesiastical and general ones can be learned from the Missal, the Pontifical, the Caeremoniale, the Ritual or Pastoral, Durandus's Rationale, and the exorcism books. Let us set out, as in a kind of display, some of the formulas by which these mystics perform the transformations and incantations of certain creatures.

units.la: repræsentare. Aquæ benedictionem ejusmodi Pontificale pag. 101. & 166. exhibet: Exorcizo te creatura aquæ in nomine Pa†tris omnipotentis, & in nomine Jesu †Christi, filii ejus Domini nostri, & in virtute Spiritus †Sancti. Ut fias aqua exorcizata ad effugandam omnem potestatem inimici; & ipsum inimicum eradicare, & explantare valeas cum Angelis suis apostaticis. Ubi Canon ait: Benedictam aquam super eos spargat, ibi addit glossa, ut per eam tollantur venialia peccata. Salis, quo aqua benedicta seu lustralis miscetur, ejusmodi benedictio Ritual. de benedict. pag. 226. extat: Exorcizote, Creatura Salis &c. ut efficiaris Sal exorcizatum in salutem credentium &c. ut effugiat atque discedat à loco, in quo aspersum fuerit, omnis phantasia & nequitia, vel versutia Diabolica fraudis, omnisque spiritus immundus adjuratus per eum, qui venturus est judicare &c. Agnorum Dei cereorum benedictionem Ceremoniale Romanum lib. 1. sol. 81. exhibet. Inter alia sic benedicens loquitur: Et quemadmodum ille Agnus innoceus tua voluntate immolatus in ara crucis Jesus Christus filius, protoplastum nostrum de Diabolica potestate eripuit: sic isti Agni immaculati virtutem illam accipiant, quos consecrandos offerimus in conspectu Divinæ Majestatis tuæ. Tu eos bene †dicere, Sanctifi†care, & consecra†care digneris, ut tua larga benedictione sanctificati, eandem virtutem accipiant contra omnes Diabolicas versutias & fraudes maligni spiritus, ut illos devotè super se ferentibus nulla tempestas eisdem prævaleat, nulla adversitas dominetur. Similes benedictionum Agnorum cereorum formulas alias supra Dissert. xj. §. 2. Thesi 77. &c. exhibuimus. Exorcismum incensi, sulphuris, myrrhæ, ligni, aloës &c. ejusmodi Mengus in flagello dæmonum Append. pag. 63. recitat: Exorcizo te creatura incensi, vel sulphuris, vel myrrhæ, vel ligni aloë, vel camphoræ, vel assæ fœtidæ per Deum †vivum, per Deum †Sanctum, per Sanctissimam Trinitatem &c. ut sis in defensionem nostram, & efficiaris perpetua suffumigatio exorcizata, benedicta & consecrata in salutem nostram & omnium fidelium Christianorum, & perpetua pœna sis omnibus malignis spiritibus, & fortissimus ac infinitus ignis eorum, & magis quàm sit infernalibus spiritibus sulphur & ignis infernalis, & omnis pœna &c. Ibidem pag. 25. 26. benedictionem R. Hellebori albi, Florum genestæ; & pag. 55. rutæ recitat. Herbarum benedictio vulgaris, in Ritualibus obvia, hæc est: Domine Sancte Pater &c. Tu bene †dicere, & sanct†ificare digneris has creaturas herbarum, sicut benedixisti quinque panes in deserto, & duos pisces, & satiasti quinque millia hominum virorum, omnésque qui utuntur ex eis, bene †dicere, sanct†ificare digneris, ut eis sit sanitas animæ & corporis, in nomine Pa†tris, Fi†lii & Spiritus †Sancti. Et omnibus hominibus pecoribúsque, quì ex hoc gustaverint, omnem putredinem, & omnia phantasmata Diaboli, & omnem morbum, & omnem pestilentiam, & dolorem expellere digneris. Herbas quasdam sic benedictas moris nonnullis est die S. Johannis incendere, iisdemque ad tempestates sedandas, tonitrua, fulgetra, grandines, ipsúmque Diabolum depellendum utuntur. Pari ratione benedicunt campanis, imò easdem baptizant, ut, sic Durandus Rational. lib. j. 4. scribit, per illarum tactum & sonitum fideles invicem invitentur ad præmium, & crescat in eis devotio fidei; fruges, mentes & corpora credentium serventur, procul pellantur hostiles exercitus, & omnes insidiæ inimici, fragor grandinum, procella turbinum, impetus tempestatum & fulgurum temperentur; infestáque tonitrua, & ventorum flamina suspendantur.
units.tr: The Pontifical, on pages 101 and 166, gives such a blessing of water: I exorcise you, creature of water, in the name of God the Father almighty, and in the name of Jesus Christ, his Son our Lord, and in the power of the Holy Spirit, that you may become water exorcised to drive out all the power of the enemy, and that you may be able to root out and uproot the enemy himself with his apostate angels. Where the Canon says, let him sprinkle the blessed water upon them, the gloss adds that venial sins may thereby be removed. For the blessing of the salt that is mixed with blessed or lustral water, the Ritual, on the blessings, page 226, has this: I exorcise you, creature of salt, etc., that you may become salt exorcised for the salvation of believers, etc., that every phantasm and wickedness, or devilish cunning of diabolical fraud, and every unclean spirit adjured by him who is to come to judge, may flee and depart from the place where you have been sprinkled. The Caeremoniale Romanum, book 1, page 81, gives the blessing of the Agnus Dei wax cakes. Among other things, the one blessing says: And just as that innocent Lamb, Jesus Christ the Son, sacrificed at thy will on the altar of the cross, snatched our first parent from the power of the devil, so may these immaculate Lambs receive that power, which we offer to be consecrated in the sight of thy divine Majesty. Deign to bless, sanctify and consecrate them, that being sanctified by thy generous blessing they may receive the same power against all the devilish wiles and frauds of the evil spirit, so that no storm may prevail over those who devoutly carry them upon themselves, and no adversity may rule over them. We have already set out similar formulas for blessing the Agnus wax cakes elsewhere, in Dissertation 11, section 2, thesis 77, etc. Mengus, in his Scourge of Demons, appendix, page 63, recites an exorcism of incense, sulphur, myrrh, wood, aloes and so on: I exorcise you, creature of incense, or sulphur, or myrrh, or aloes wood, or camphor, or asafoetida, by the living God, by the holy God, by the most holy Trinity, etc., that you may be for our defence and become a perpetual exorcised, blessed and consecrated fumigation for our salvation and that of all faithful Christians, and that you may be a perpetual punishment to all evil spirits, and a most strong and endless fire to them, and that sulphur and infernal fire may be more to the infernal spirits than they are, and every punishment, etc. On the same page, 25 and 26, he recites the blessing of white hellebore and broom flowers, and on page 55, of rue. The common blessing of herbs, found in the Rituals, is this: Lord, holy Father, etc., deign to bless and sanctify these creatures of herbs, just as you blessed the five loaves in the desert and the two fishes, and satisfied five thousand men, and deign to bless and sanctify all who use them, that there may be health of soul and body for them, in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. And deign to drive out from all men and beasts who taste of this every rot, and all the phantasms of the devil, and every disease, and every pestilence, and pain. Some have the custom of burning herbs so blessed on the feast of St. John, and use them to calm storms, thunder, lightning and hail, and to drive away the devil himself. In the same way they bless bells, and indeed baptize them, so that, as Durandus writes in his Rationale, book 1, chapter 4, by the touch and sound of these the faithful may be invited to one another to reward, and devotion of faith may grow in them; the crops, minds and bodies of believers may be preserved, hostile armies and all the snares of the enemy may be driven far away, the crash of hail, the storm of whirlwinds, the force of tempests and lightnings may be tempered, and hurtful thunder and blasts of wind may be held back.

units.la: Spiritus procellarum & aerea potestates prosternan- tur.
units.tr: The spirits of the storms and the aerial powers are overthrown.

units.la: XLIV. Hæc similésque benedictiones quid aliud sunt, quàm Zoroastræi susurri, quibus illi Væjovis Romani Dardanarii iucantationes suas peragunt? Atque benedictiones ejusmodi interposito identidem signo crucis perficere, adeóque efficaciam omnem benedictionis in eo collocare illi solent. Esse equidem signi illius usum antiquissimum, nulli inficias imus. Sæpè enim veteres ejus meminerunt. Neque hoc in dubium nos revocamus; sed illud potius, quomodo & quo fine ab illis adhibitum fuerit. Nam sœpius signi nomen orationi fidelium ad Christum effusæ dederunt; cui hoc signum, tanquam religionis suæ professionem addiderunt. Id sequens superstitio non observans, signo & memoriali absolutè sumpto virtutem mortis ac passionis Christi adeóque, quam miserabilem animæ servitutem esse, S. Augustinus de Doctr. Christ. lib. iij. 5. pronuntiavit, signo, quod rei est, adscripsit, sicque id, quod improprie dicebatur, proprie intellexit; atque ita primum illum & superstitione carentem usum in abusum profanum & magicum convertit. Nam à signo externo crucis, eóque certo numero, pari vel impari, scrupulosè repetito, uti ex formulis allatis liquet, benedictionis & sanctificationis efficaciam suspendit. Ita in officio etiam Missæ prima vice ter signum illud fit, cùm dicitur. Hæc dona &c. Secunda quinquies dicendo, quam oblationem; tertia bis; quarta quinquies; quinta iterum bis, & secundùm Thomam ter; sexta ter; septima quinquies, quæ omnes vices sua habent mysteria, à præside Durantio de Rit. Eccl. lib. v. 45. explicata. Et Bellarminus quidem Controv. vj. lib. iv. 7. locum S. Pauli 1 Tim. iv. 5. ubi S. Paulus creaturas quasdam sanctificari docet dià λόγου καὶ ἐντεύξεως per verbum & preces fœdè detorquens, per verbum intelligit signaculum crucis; atque eandem παρεμβυτὴν Theophylacto & Chrysostomo falsò acceptum refert, cùm vim sanctificationis totam illi posuerint in gratiarum actione & verbo Dei,mentionem tantùm facientes signi crucis, tanquam ceremoniæ eo tempore usitatæ, non certo utique numero, vel scrupulosâ observantiâ, nedum ut efficaciam benedictionis abeo, ceu verbo Dei suspenderent, sed ut notarent significarentque, unde illa benedictionis per verbum & preces vis proficiscatur, à Christo nimirum crucifixo. Unde etiam Claudius Guiliaudus, homo Pontificius, Sorbonæ totius judicio probatus, sic locum S.Pauli explicat: Per verbum Dei & orationem sanctificantur: Quoniam per verbum Dei scimus credimúsque, nihil jam commune aut pollutum esse; per orationem, cùm Deum oramus, ut ea nobis donet, & pro datis gratias agimus. Sed secum ipse Bellarminus discors, Apostolum verbo Dei signum crucis intelligere pertendit; & tamen alibi Tomo j. Controv. j. lib. iv. 7. negat, in sacra Scriptura præcipi, quòd creaturæ signo crucis sanctificandæ sint.
units.tr: XLIV. Are these and similar blessings anything other than the Zoroastrian whisperings with which those Roman Vejovis-Dardanarii perform their incantations? Blessings of this kind are commonly completed by repeatedly interposing the sign of the cross, and they place all the efficacy of the blessing in it. We do not deny that the use of that sign is very ancient; the ancients often mention it. Nor do we call this into doubt, but rather how and to what end it was employed. For they often gave the name of the sign to the prayer of the faithful poured out to Christ, and added this sign to it as a profession of their religion. Superstition, not observing this, took the sign and the memorial taken absolutely, and ascribed to the sign, which is the thing itself, the power of the death and passion of Christ, and of that wretched servitude of the soul which Augustine, in On Christian Doctrine 3.5, declared it to be. Thus what was said improperly it understood properly, and so it turned that first use, which was free of superstition, into a profane and magical abuse. For it makes the efficacy of blessing and sanctification depend on the external sign of the cross, repeated scrupulously at a fixed number, even or odd, as is clear from the formulas cited. Thus in the office of the Mass the sign is made three times the first time, when one says Hæc dona etc.; the second time five times, saying quam oblationem; the third time twice; the fourth five times; the fifth again twice, and by Thomas three times; the sixth three times; the seventh five times. Each of these occasions has its own mysteries, explained by the president Durandus in On the Rites of the Church 5.45. Bellarmine indeed, in Controversies 6.4.7, badly distorts the passage of St Paul at 1 Tim. 4:5, where Paul teaches that certain creatures are sanctified through word and prayer [διὰ λόγου καὶ ἐντεύξεως]; he understands the word as the sign of the cross, and he reports that the same interpretation [παρεμβυτήν] was wrongly attributed by Theophylact and Chrysostom. Yet they placed the whole power of sanctification in thanksgiving and the word of God, mentioning the sign of the cross only as a ceremony then in use, not at a fixed number or with scrupulous observance, and certainly not so as to make the efficacy of the blessing depend on it as on the word of God. They mentioned it to note and signify whence that power of blessing through word and prayer proceeds, namely from Christ crucified. Hence also Claudius Guilliaudus, a Papist man approved by the judgment of the whole Sorbonne, explains the passage of St Paul thus: They are sanctified through the word of God and prayer: because through the word of God we know and believe that nothing is now common or polluted; through prayer, when we pray God to grant them to us, and give thanks for what has been given. But Bellarmine, at odds with himself, contends that the Apostle means by the word of God the sign of the cross; and yet elsewhere, in Tome 1, Controversies 1.4.7, he denies that it is commanded in Holy Scripture that creatures be sanctified with the sign of the cross.

units.la: XLV. Benedictionum signaculo crucis certo numero formato sanctificatarum formulis, quales suprà recitavimus, eosdem Hierarchici effectus, qui in formulis illis continentur, tribuunt. Bellarminus Controv. vj. lib. iij. 7. rerum sic benedictarum effectus supernaturales tres enumerat, valere eos ad delenda peccata venialia, fugandos dæmones, & curandos morbos afferens. Quo vero pacto reliquos naturalibus sic benedictis supernaturales effectus deputantes, causam suam à vetularum, aliorúmque Magorum benedictionibus illi disparabunt? Non poterunt utique ullo, nisi Divinæ institutionis tabulas, verbum mandati & promissionis producant. Cedò autem institutionem Diviuam, verbum mandati & promissionis: In traditione, non scriptura, si institutionem & verbum illud ostendere libue. rit, ubi ergò illa traditio? In facto, inquient, corde & ore Ecclesiæ, Romanæ scilicet & Papæ. Jam ergò eadem actio magica erit, quando à Papa Romano non præscribitur, probatur, laudatur: magica esse desinet, quando à Papa præscribitur, laudatur. Solum ergò jam præscriptum, placitum, arbitrium Papæ, actionem Magicam, non magicam efficiet; sicut iisdem judicibus; Papa ex non peccato, peccatum facere potest. Poterit proin Papa eadem ratione, qua cæteris creaturis signo crucis benedictis supernaturales effectus tribuit, similes etiam effectus benedicendo tribuere v. g. chartæ, cui inscriptum est verbum Abracadabra, quomodo inter cæteros Q. Serenus Præcept. de medic. cap. de curanda femitert. rationem febris curandæ explicat hoc modo:
units.tr: XLV. The Hierarchs attribute the same effects contained in those formulas to blessings sanctified by the sign of the cross formed at a fixed number, such as we have recited above. Bellarmine, in Controversies 6.3.7, lists three supernatural effects of things so blessed, asserting that they avail to blot out venial sins, to put to flight demons, and to cure diseases. But by what means will those who ascribe supernatural effects to things blessed in the natural way distinguish their cause from the blessings of old women and other magicians? They will in no way be able to do so unless they produce the tablets of divine institution, the word of command and promise. But show me the divine institution, the word of command and promise. If they wish to show that institution and that word by tradition, not by Scripture, then where is that tradition? In the deed, they will say, by the heart and mouth of the Church, namely the Roman Church and the Pope. Then the same action will be magical when it is not prescribed, approved and praised by the Roman Pope; it will cease to be magical when it is prescribed and praised by the Pope. So the mere prescription, pleasure, or will of the Pope will make the action magical or non-magical; just as, by the same judges, the Pope can make a sin out of what is not a sin. Therefore the Pope can, by the same reasoning by which he attributes supernatural effects to other creatures blessed with the sign of the cross, attribute similar effects by blessing, for example, to a paper on which the word Abracadabra is written. Among others, Q. Serenus, in Precepts of Medicine, the chapter on curing tertian fever, explains the method of curing fever in this way:
Write on the paper what is called Abracadabra [illegible, about 3 letters] often ———
Remember to tie it with thread and wear it round the neck.

units.la: XLVI. Si enim, liceat Syllogismo hoc rem constringere, aquâ, oleo, aliisque rebus benedictione Pontificia consecratis ad morbos, uti benedictionum formulæ inter alia promittunt, & Bellarminus aliique tuentur, curandos & depellendos uti licet; licebit etiam chartâ, cui inscribitur Abracadabra, appensâ collo uti ad hemitritæum depellendum, modò hæc charta benedictione Pontificia consecretur. Atqui hæc charta, etiamsi more Pontificio consecretur & benedicatur, non potest, citra Magiæ crimen, licitè adhiberi ad hemitritæum depellendum, idque hanc ob causam, quia Deus chartam ad hunc usum non creavit, neque instituit extra ordinem, ut morbum eum curaret.
units.tr: XLVI. For if, to press the matter with a syllogism, it is permissible to use water, oil, and other things consecrated by Papist blessing against diseases, as the formulas of blessing promise among other things, and as Bellarmine and others defend, to be cured and driven away, then it will also be permissible to use a paper inscribed with Abracadabra, hung around the neck, to drive away the semitertian fever, provided this paper is consecrated by Papist blessing. But this paper, even if it is consecrated and blessed in the Papist manner, cannot be lawfully used to drive away the semitertian fever without the crime of magic. The reason is that God did not create the paper for this use, nor institute it outside the ordinary order to cure that disease.

units.la: Ergò eandem ob causam non licet, citra Magiæ crimen, aquâ, oleo, herbis, aliisque rebus benedictione Pontificia consecratis uti ad curandos morbos, vel alios etiam efsectus supernaturales, ad quos producendos neque suâpte natura, neque Divina institutione infallibiliter revelata valent. Propositio manifesta est ex verbis Bellarmini. Is enim loc. cit. postquam secundam suam propositionem, quæ sic habet: Recte ad effectus supernaturales efficiendos & significandos utimur aquâ, oleo aliisque rebus benedictione consecratis, describisset; Nota, inquit, illa omnia, quæ diximus in Ecclesia benedici propter tres fines, atque in illis numerat curationem morborum. Illa omnia significat; quæ prima propositione comprehenderat; aquam, oleum, panem, cereos, cineres, & similia. Similium autem nomine significat omnes Dei creaturas, quod confirmat probatio, quam adjungit ex verbis Apostoli: Omnis creatura Dei bona est, &c. De illis ergo omnibus, id est, de omnibus Dei creaturis affirmat Bellarminus, eas, si Pontificio more benedicantur, recte adhiberi ad curandos morbos, similesque supernaturales effectus. Et in Missali quidem, Cap. de variis benedictionibus, commemorantur varia; atque in genere est benedictio una ad quaecunque comestibilia. In Magistro Sententiarum adjunguntur alia, quibus Ecclesiam Dei jam diu Papa fascinavit, veluti rosa benedicta. Et Anglo-Rhemenses in 1. Tim. iv. non solum varia numerant particularia præter ea, quæ Bellarminus loc. cit. recensuit, verum etiam ex Gregorio adjungunt, omnia munuscula, cujusmodi crebra ad nos mittuntur Româ per Jesuitas, rosas benedictas, agnos Dei &c. posse similiter adhiberi ad usus supernaturales, postquam fuerint benedictione Pontificia consecrata. Verum verba Bellarmini satis complectuntur id, de quo agimus. Addit enim arbores posse benedici ad morbos depellendos, quarum partes rami sunt, & res similes. Fuit autem antiquitus charta confecta ex ramorum cortice. Hodie vero conficitur ex lino; quod in illis est, quæ expresse fatentur posse ad ejusmodi usus benedici. Atramentum vero, qua literæ
units.tr: For the same reason, then, it is not permissible, without the crime of magic, to use water, oil, herbs, and other things consecrated by Papist blessing to cure diseases, or other supernatural effects either, for the production of which they are not effective either by their own nature or by divine institution infallibly revealed. The proposition is plain from Bellarmine's own words. For he, loc. cit., after describing his second proposition, which reads: We rightly use water, oil, and other things consecrated by blessing to effect and signify supernatural effects, says: Note, he says, that all those things which we said are blessed in the Church for three ends, and among these he counts the cure of diseases. All refers to those things which his first proposition had comprehended: water, oil, bread, candles, ashes, and similar things. By the name of similar things he means all the creatures of God, which the proof he adds from the words of the Apostle confirms: Every creature of God is good, etc. Bellarmine therefore affirms of all these, that is, of all God's creatures, that if they are blessed in the Papist manner they may rightly be used to cure diseases and similar supernatural effects. In the Missal, in the chapter On various blessings, various things are mentioned, and in general there is one blessing for all edible things. In the Master of the Sentences other things are added, by which the Pope has long since bewitched the Church of God, such as blessed rose. The Anglo-Rhemists, on 1 Tim. 4, not only list many particular things besides those Bellarmine recounted loc. cit., but also add from Gregory all the little gifts, such as those frequently sent to us from Rome through the Jesuits, blessed roses, Agnus Deis, etc., can similarly be used for supernatural purposes once they have been consecrated by Papist blessing. But the words of Bellarmine sufficiently embrace what we are discussing. For he adds that trees can be blessed to drive away diseases, whose parts are branches, and similar things. Formerly paper was made from the bark of branches; today it is made from linen, which is among those things which they expressly admit can be blessed for such uses. Ink, moreover, with which the letters are written on the paper,

units.la: { } iteræ in charta scribuntur, fit ex aqua, quam similiter benedictione sua sanctificant. Charta ergò, atramentum, linum, in hoc amuleto Abracadabra æquè sunt creaturæ Dei, atque aqua, linum, oleum, rosa &c. adeóque æquè ac illæ benedici possunt. Constat ergò propositio Major. Minor haud minùs evidens est, non licere videlicet citra Magiæ crimen, charta, seu amuleto, quod Abracadabra sibi inscriptum habet, uti ad depellendum hemitritæum, quia Deus chartam eam ad usum hunc nec naturaliter nec supernaturaliter instituit; uti adversarii nulli diffitentur, & res ipsa docet. Nam ad curandum hemitritæum naturaliter chartam illam non conducere, manifestum ex eo est, quòd quæcunque naturaliter ad curandos morbos adhibentur, curationem faciunt ex tribus illis partibus medicinæ, puta victu, manu & medicamentis; charta verò illa ex nulla harum partium morbos curat. Neque etiam supernaturaliter ad curationem morbi illius adhiberi potest, quia spiritus Dei revelavit quæ suprà vim naturæ instituta sunt, & adhibenda docent ad curandos morbos; de chartæ autem illius virtute supernaturali ad curandum hemitritæum nihil revelavit. Unde prono alveo fluit conclusio, non licere videlicet, citra crimen Magiæ, eandem ob causam aquâ, oleo, herbis, aliisque creaturis benedictione Pontificia consecratis ad curandos morbos, aliósque effectus supernaturales, uti. Qui ergò & benedicunt eum in finem, & benedictis rebus utuntur, quod Hierarchici faciunt, Magicæ impietatis manifesti sunt.
units.tr: is made from water, which they likewise sanctify by their blessing. Therefore paper, ink, linen, in this amulet Abracadabra, are equally God's creatures with water, linen, oil, rose, etc., and so can be blessed just as those can. The major premise therefore stands. The minor is no less evident: namely, that it is not permissible, without the crime of magic, to use a paper or amulet which has Abracadabra written on it, to drive away the semitertian fever, because God instituted that paper for this use neither naturally nor supernaturally; as the adversaries deny nowhere, and the thing itself teaches. For that paper does not naturally conduce to curing semitertian fever, as is manifest from the fact that whatever is naturally used to cure diseases effects the cure through those three parts of medicine, namely diet, the hand, and medicines; but that paper cures disease by none of these parts. Nor can it be used supernaturally for the cure of that disease, because the Spirit of God has revealed what has been instituted above the power of nature and taught to be used for curing diseases, and has revealed nothing about the supernatural virtue of that paper for curing semitertian fever. Hence the conclusion flows down a sloping channel: namely, that it is not permissible, without the crime of magic, for the same reason, to use water, oil, herbs, and other creatures consecrated by Papist blessing to cure diseases and other supernatural effects. Therefore those who bless them to that end, and use the blessed things, as the Hierarchs do, are manifestly guilty of magical impiety.

units.la: XLVII. Sed & iis omnibus, qui rudimentis Christianæ religionis vel ex solo catechismo imbuti sunt, dubium esse nequit, nefas esse ejusmodi creaturas quomodocunque benedictas ad supernaturales effectus, ad quos à Deo institutæ non sunt, adhibere, etiamsi res ejusmodi consecrentur benedictione non dico Pontificia; sed etiamsi adhibeatur loco signi crucis, ceremoniæ ab hominibus inventæ; ceremonia Divinitùs instituta, velut elevatio manuum. Duo enim sunt mandata, ex quibus hoc efficitur; alterum: Ne sint tibi Dii alii; cui succenturiatur illud; Non sit maleficus & incantator inter vos Deuter. xviii. 11. alterum: Non sumes nomen Dei in vanum. Exod. xx. 3. 7. Priori docemur omnem cultum, honorem, fiduciam, obedientiam summo Deo debitam, sic eidem deferre, ne quidquam ex ipsis creaturis ad alios usus adhibeamus, quàm ipse instituit, & verbo suo comprobavit. Posteriori sic docemur sanctificare nomen Dei, ut ne precationibus aut quibuscunque verbis sacris abutamur ad quascunque creaturas nobis ad alios fines distinatas, in alium, quàm Deus voluit, usum consecrandas. Nec invocatio igitur nominis Divini supra creaturas, nec ceremonia Divinitùs instituta, nedum Pontificia benedictio, superstitioni incoëta penitùs, efficere potest, ut creaturæ effectus, ad quos à Deo institutæ non sunt, edant; & qui effectus ejusmodi prævia invocatione, & ceremoniâ etiam Divinâ, nedum Pontificiâ benedictione tentant, utriusque præcepti violati, ipsiusque etiam impietatis Magicæ rei sunt.
units.tr: XLVII. Moreover, no one who has been instructed in the rudiments of the Christian religion, or even only in the catechism, can doubt that it is wrong to use such creatures, however they have been blessed, for supernatural effects for which God has not instituted them. This holds even if such things are consecrated not, I say, by Papist blessing, but by a ceremony devised by men in place of the sign of the cross, or even by a ceremony divinely instituted, such as the lifting up of hands. Two commandments establish this. The first is: "Thou shalt have no other gods before me," to which is added: "Let there not be among you one who is a sorcerer or an enchanter" (Deut. 18:11). The second is: "Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain" (Exod. 20:3, 7). By the first we are taught to render to the supreme God all the worship, honour, trust and obedience due to him, and so not to put any creature to any use other than the one he himself has appointed and confirmed by his word. By the second we are taught to hallow the name of God, so that we do not abuse prayers or any sacred words to consecrate any creatures, which are destined for other ends, to a use other than God willed. Therefore neither the invocation of the divine name over creatures, nor a divinely instituted ceremony, much less a Papist blessing, which is wholly foreign to superstition, can bring it about that creatures produce effects for which God has not instituted them. Those who attempt such effects by a prior invocation and a ceremony, even a divine one, and much more by a Papist blessing, are guilty of violating both precepts, and are also guilty of the impiety of magic itself.

units.la: XLVIII. Bellarminus Controv. vij. lib. iij. 7. negat, se benedicendo violare vel præceptum Dei primum, quo vetamur alios habere Deos, adeóque magiæ litare: vel tertium, quo nomen Dei in vanum sumere prohibemur. Non illud, quia, inquit, malefici & incantatores sunt, qui Diaboli potestate aliquid mirum operantur: non hoc, quia assumere nomen Dei in vanum proprie nihil est aliud quàm pejerare, ut rectè explicat Concilium Toletanum vij. c. 2. At qui aquam benedicunt, nec pejerant, nec Diabolum invocant, sed solùm religiosè Deum precantur. Tota enim virtus æquæ lustralis nititur verbo Dei & oratione. Hæc Bellarmini exceptio si pondus habet, absolvetur pariter à Magiæ crimine, qui chartâ, cui inscribitur Abracadabra, cruce modò & benedictione sanctificatâ, ad morbum hemitritæum curandum utitur, quia talis nec pejerat, nec Diabolum invocat. Neque enim pejerat, qui sanctificat creaturas ad ejusmodi usus: neque necesse est, ut omnes, qui istiusmodi amuletis utuntur, Diabolum invocent. Imò Bernhardo Gordonio, aliisque Medicis Christianis testantibus, manifestum est, ejusmodi amuleta sæpè adhiberi cum invocatione nominis Dei, non autem cum invocatione dæmonum. Testantur id ipsum formulæ Magicæ, quæ in Magorum libris occurrunt, velut apud Cornelium Agrippam, Petrum de Alano, ubi Divinæ illæ appellationes Jah, El, Adonai, Elohim, Elohe Zebaoth, Elion, Sadai &c. nec non phrases & loca Scripturæ frequenter occurrunt. Quid ergò aliud restat, quàm ut Magia universa, solo crucis signo & invocatione nominis Dei super creaturas interveniente, & instrumenta mutante, in Ecclesiæ gremium recipiatur. Non ergò Magus & incantator is tantùm est, qui Diabolum expresse invocat, ejusque ope arduum quid tentat: sed is quoque, qui creaturis sive more Pontificio, sive invocatione vera solius Dei benedictis utitur ad effectus, ad quos Divinitùs producendos instituta non sunt. Quod ad Magiam implicitam utriusque generis, superiùs à nobis descriptam sufficit. Si enim hujusmodi quid efficient sacræ istæ res, efficient non virtute Dei, qui effectus ejusmodi creaturis illis nec indidit, nec promisit: sed Dæmonis ope; adeóque veré Magicæ erunt. Ita verissimè Martinus Navarrus Enchirid. Confess. cap. 31. & cum eo Scholastici & Theologi uno consensu omnes docent, eos, qui putant ea, quæ efficiuntur opera Magorum, divinantium & incantatorum, etiamsi ad sanitatem perveniatur, effici virtute verborum & rerum quas applicant, cùm hujusmodi res juxta naturam suam ad ad similem effectum producendum tali virtute careant, peccare mortaliter, quoniam talem effectum dæmon efficit per alias causas naturales, quas ad id, ob factum expresse vel tacitè cum incantatore conventum applicat, secundum Thomam quæst. 96. art. 2. & S. Antoninum par. 2. tit. 12. can. 1. & reliquos omnes in secundum librum Sententiarum dist. 3. S. Paulus Ephes. v. 5. dicit, avarum esse idololatram. Quam ob causam? Potest enim avarus invocare nomen veri Dei. Nempe fiduciam ponit in pecunia, quam in solo Deo collocare debuit; adeóque pecuniam suam Deum suum facit. Sic illicitis mediis utens, & creaturis tribuens eos effectus, quos Deus iis nec in verbo, nec in natura tribuit, sive nomen Dei super eas invocet, sive non magus & incantator est, & alios Deos habet, quia non acquiescit ordine Dei, atque id à Deo expectat, quod non Dei, qui nusquam promisit, sed solius dæmonis ope contingit. Neque etiam is duntaxat nomen Dei in vanum sumit, qui pejerat; sed etiam qui nomen Dei non sanctificat, uti sanctificare debuit, eo abutitur, atque illud quocunque modo profanat. Mandata enim quævis Dei non exteriora duntaxat facta prohibent, sed generalem habent sententiam, atque brevissimo compendio omnia ea, quæ ad pietatem & sanctitatem pertinent, constringunt.
units.tr: XLVIII. Bellarmine, Controv. vij. lib. iij. 7., denies that by blessing he violates either the first precept of God, by which we are forbidden to have other gods and so to sacrifice to magic, or the third, by which we are forbidden to take the name of God in vain. Not the first, he says, because it is only those who work some wonder by the power of the Devil who are sorcerers and enchanters; not the third, because to take the name of God in vain properly means nothing other than to perjure oneself, as the Council of Toledo rightly explains, vii. c. 2. But those who bless water neither perjure themselves nor invoke the Devil, but only piously call upon God. For the whole virtue of holy water rests on the word of God and on prayer. If this objection of Bellarmine has any weight, then he who uses paper inscribed Abracadabra, sanctified only by the cross and a blessing, to cure the hemitritaeus fever will likewise be absolved of the crime of magic, since such a man neither perjures himself nor invokes the Devil. For he who consecrates creatures to such uses does not perjure himself, nor is it necessary that all who use amulets of this kind invoke the Devil. Indeed, since Bernhard Gordonius and other Christian physicians bear witness, it is plain that such amulets are often used with the invocation of the name of God, and not with the invocation of demons. The magical formulae that occur in the books of the magicians bear witness to the same thing, as in Cornelius Agrippa and Peter of Alano, where the divine names Jah, El, Adonai, Elohim, Elohe Zebaoth, Elion, Sadai, and so on, as well as phrases and passages of Scripture, frequently occur. What then remains, but that all magic be received into the bosom of the Church, when the sign of the cross alone and the invocation of the name of God are interposed over creatures and merely change the instruments? Therefore he is not only a magician and enchanter who expressly invokes the Devil and by his help attempts some difficult thing, but also he who uses creatures blessed either in the Papist manner or by the true invocation of God alone, for effects which they were not instituted by God to produce. As for implicit magic of either kind, what we have described above is sufficient. For if these holy things effect anything of this kind, they effect it not by the power of God, who neither gave nor promised such effects to those creatures, but by the help of the Devil; and so they are truly magical. Thus most truly Martín de Azpilcueta, Enchirid. Confess. cap. 31., and with him the Schoolmen and theologians all teach with one voice, that those who think that the effects produced by the works of magicians, diviners and enchanters, even when health is restored, are brought about by the power of the words and things they apply, when such things by their nature lack that power to produce a similar effect, sin mortally, since the Devil produces such an effect through other natural causes, which he applies to this end because of a compact made expressly or tacitly with the enchanter, according to Thomas, qu. 96, art. 2, and St Antoninus, part 2, tit. 12, can. 1, and all the rest on the second book of the Sentences, dist. 3. St Paul says in Ephesians 5:5 that the covetous man is an idolater. Why so? For the covetous man can invoke the name of the true God. But he places his trust in money, which he ought to have placed in God alone, and so makes his money his god. Thus, using unlawful means and attributing to creatures those effects which God has given them neither in his word nor in nature, whether or not he invokes the name of God over them, he is a magician and enchanter, and has other gods, because he does not acquiesce in the order of God, and expects from God what does not come from God, who has promised nothing of the kind, but comes only by the help of the demon. Nor does he alone take the name of God in vain who perjures himself; but also he who does not hallow the name of God as he ought to, and misuses it, and profanes it in any way whatever. For the commandments of God forbid not only outward deeds, but have a general sense, and by a very brief summary bind all those things that pertain to piety and holiness.

units.la: XLIX. Sequuntur errores Magici, quibus Sacramen- ta, Baptismus & Cœna Domini polluuntur.
units.tr: XLIX. Follow the magical errors, by which the sacraments, Baptism and the Lord's Supper, are polluted.

units.la: Et Baptismus quidem variis exorcismis contaminatur. Salem enim, aquam & oleum, ut in Magicis fit adjurationibus, iis Hierarchici destinant usibus, quos nec à natura habent, nec à Deo acceperunt. Et benedictio quidem salis in Ritualibus eorum sic habet: Exorcizo te, creatura salis, in nomine Dei Patris omnipotentis † & in charitate Domini nostri Jesu Christi † & in virtute Spiritus Sancti † exorcizo te per Deum vivum † per Deum verum † per Deum San
units.tr: Baptism is indeed contaminated by various exorcisms. For they devote salt, water and oil, as is done in magical incantations, to uses which they neither have from nature nor have received from God. The blessing of the salt in their Rituals runs thus: I exorcise you, creature of salt, in the name of God the Father almighty † and in the charity of our Lord Jesus Christ † and in the power of the Holy Spirit † I exorcise you by the living God † by the true God † by the holy God

units.la: Tom. II. 111 Eium † per Deum † quite ad tutelam humani generis precreavit, & populo venienti ad credulitatem per servos suos consecrari precepit, ut in nomine Sancti & Trinitatis efficiaris salutare Sacramentum, ad effugandum inimicum. Proinde rogamus te, Domine Deus noster, ut hanc creaturam salis sanctificando sanctifices † & benedicendo benedicas † ut fiat omnibus accipientibus perfecta medicina, permanens in visceribus eorum, in nomine ejusdem Domini nostri Jesu Christi, qui venturus est judicare vivos & mortuos, & Seculum per ignem, Amen. Salis sic benedicti in Baptismo usus hic mox indicatur: Deinde immittat modicum salis benedicti in os infantis, dicens: N. Accipe salem sapientiæ. Propitiatio tibi sit in vitam æternam, Amen. In hac Salis benedictione & usu non unum, sed plura & concatenata peccata concurrunt. Pauca notabimus. Primò, horrendus in ea est nominis Divini abusus, utpote quod usurpatur ad mirificam quandam potentiam derivandam in creaturam salis, quam illa à Deo nec in creatione, nec in supernaturali quapiam institutione accepit, adeóque aliunde quàm à dæmone habere nequit. Secundò, benedictio habet, Deum hanc consecrationem salis præcepisse. Ubi verò, quando, quo verborum tenore præcepit? Tertiò, addit, sal effici salutare Sacramentum. Aquam Baptismi, Panem & vinum Eucharistiæ Deus hoc honore dignatus est: sal nequaquam. Bis tamen in Baptismo Papistico administratur. Primò, siccum, purum, deinde aquæ mixtum. Aqua semel tantùm, nec pura illa, sed sale & oleo mixta. A potiori igitur si denominatio valet; hoc sacramentum salis potiùs quàm aquæ nuncupabitur. Quartò, additur, sal institutum esse ad effugandum dæmonem. Unde verò id benedicentes illi exorcistæ probant? Deus certè nusquam ad hunc effectum instituit. Si Papa instituit, viderit, unde efficacia illa sali immittatur. Quintò, subjungitur, Sal fieri perfectam medicinam, & propitiationem in vitam æternam. Quem honorem Sacræ literæ Christo deferunt, cujus meritum est panacea nostra Esaj. LIII. 5. quem proposuit Deus propitiationem per fidem in sanguine, Rom. III. 25. I. Joh. II. 2. quæ propitiatio juxta Divinam institutionem, purâ baptismi aquâ fidelibus obsignatur.
units.tr: Vol. II, p. 111. God † who from the beginning created you for the protection of the human race, and commanded that you be consecrated by his servants for the people coming to faith, so that in the name of the Holy Trinity you may become a saving sacrament, for driving away the enemy. Therefore we beseech you, Lord our God, that by sanctifying this creature of salt you may sanctify it † and by blessing you may bless it † so that it may become a perfect medicine for all who receive it, abiding in their bowels, in the name of the same Lord our Jesus Christ, who is to come to judge the living and the dead, and the world by fire. Amen. The use of salt so blessed in Baptism is then indicated here: Then let him put a little of the blessed salt into the infant's mouth, saying: N., receive the salt of wisdom. May it be a propitiation for you unto eternal life. Amen. In this blessing and use of the salt, not one sin but many linked sins come together. We shall note a few. First, there is a dreadful abuse of the divine name, since it is invoked to derive a certain wondrous power into the creature of salt, which it received from God neither in creation nor in any supernatural institution, and so can have only from the devil. Second, the blessing says that God commanded this consecration of salt. But where, when, and in what wording did he command it? Third, it adds that the salt is made a saving sacrament. God has deigned to give this honour to the water of Baptism, and to the bread and wine of the Eucharist, but by no means to salt. Yet in Papist Baptism it is administered twice: first dry and pure, then mixed with water. Water is used only once, and not pure but mixed with salt and oil. Therefore, if naming is decisive, this sacrament should be called a sacrament of salt rather than of water. Fourth, it is added that salt was instituted for driving away the devil. But from where do those exorcists who bless it prove this? God certainly never instituted it for this effect. If the Pope instituted it, let him see from where that efficacy is infused into the salt. Fifth, it is added that the salt becomes a perfect medicine and a propitiation unto eternal life. This is the honour which the Sacred Letters give to Christ, whose merit is our panacea (Isa. 53:5), whom God set forth as a propitiation through faith in his blood (Rom. 3:25; 1 John 2:2), and which propitiation, according to the divine institution, is sealed to the faithful by pure water of baptism.

units.la: L. Salis sacramento, quod vocant, exorcismos subjiciunt binos, quibus primò immundum spiritum indefinite, deinde spiritum immundum omnem ex baptizando ejiciunt; quos in Pastorali Ruræmundano, & Rituali Romano prolixè recitatos legere est. Neque hic finis est. Sathan enim ad instar erucarum in oleribus tenellæ infantis animæ mordicùs adhæret, nec facilè se divelli patitur. Igitur post omnes Exorcismos Parochus apponit infantis naribus sputum suum, cum his verbis: In odorem suavitatis. Addit mox: Tu autem effugare dæmon, quasi odori sputi Sacerdotis cedere debeat dæmon, qui ad Exorcismos fulmina intonantes, pedem non movit. Quis ritus hos superstitiosos planè esse dubitat? Nam nec à Christo instituti, nec ab Apostolis usurpati sunt: & nullo insuper modo necessarii, quin potiùs Christianorum fidelium infantibus contumeliosi, parentibus ipsis terrifici sunt. Neque enim liberi fidelium obsessi sunt à Diabolo, utpote sancti & mundi, I. Cor. VII. 14. ac proinde etiam baptismo, ad quem Spiritus malignus accessum non habet, offerendi. Sic author Comment. qui Ambrosio adscribuntur, ad h. l. eos Sanctos dicit, tum quia ex licitis conjugiis, tum quia sub creatoris veneratione nati sunt. Novis verò Exorcistis his si credimus, non solùm illi immundi, sed cacodæmonum pleni sunt, qui difficulter, nec nisi potentissimis Exorcismorum machinis fugari possunt. Tristis sanè cogitatio mulierum parturientium animos subeat oportet, dum secum
units.tr: L. To the sacrament of salt, as they call it, they add two exorcisms, by which first the unclean spirit in general and then every unclean spirit is cast out of the one to be baptized. These may be read at length in the Pastorale Ruremundanum and the Roman Ritual. Nor is this the end. For Satan, like caterpillars among the vegetables, clings fast to the tender soul of the infant and does not easily allow himself to be torn away. Therefore, after all the exorcisms, the parish priest puts his spittle on the infant's nostrils, with these words: For a odour of sweetness. Immediately he adds: And you, demon, flee away, as if the devil, who did not move a foot at the thundering exorcisms, ought to yield to the smell of the priest's spittle. Who doubts that these superstitious rites are plainly such? For they were neither instituted by Christ nor used by the Apostles, and they are by no means necessary; rather, they are insulting to the infants of faithful Christians and frightening to the parents themselves. For the children of believers are not possessed by the Devil, being holy and clean (1 Cor. 7:14), and therefore they are to be offered to baptism too, to which the evil spirit has no access. So the author of the Commentaries ascribed to Ambrose, on this passage, calls them holy, both because they are born of lawful marriages and because they are born under the veneration of the Creator. But if we believe these new exorcists, the infants are not only unclean but full of cacodaemons, which can be driven out only with difficulty, and not without the most powerful machinery of exorcisms. Surely the sad thought must come into the minds of women in labour, as they reflect to themselves:

units.la: {a} Exorcismum, quibus in eodem Baptismo daemones ex baptizando ejiciuntur, vanitas. cum reputant, nunquam se parere infantem, quin simul cum eo pariant dæmonem; & si contigerit infantem non baptizatum mori, eum corporaliter à dæmone obsessum, eò abreptum iri, quò indulgentissima mater ne voto quidem vel cogitatione, ad invisendum eum, aspirare velit.
units.tr: {a} The exorcisms by which demons are cast out of the one baptized in the same Baptism are vanity. that they never bear an infant without bearing a demon along with it; and if it happens that an unbaptized infant dies, that it is carried off, bodily possessed by the devil, to a place where the most indulgent mother would not even wish, by vow or thought, to visit it.

units.la: LI. Quid quòd ritus illos Exorcismorum similésque suppleri volunt post baptismum non solennem, vel ab hæreticis, uti yccant, collatum, uti ex Rituali Romano de Sacram. Bapt. pag. 41. colligitur? Plerique etiam omnes Scholastici, qui in 4. Sent. dist. 6. scripserunt, Sacramentalia illa (sic enim vocant) in necessitate omissa, esse supplenda, si infans convaluerit. Cui verò bono infanti jam baptizato Exorcismi illi inservient? An baptizatus jam adhuc à dæmone obsessus tenetur? Et tamen baptismo labem peccati Originalis abstergi, Tridentinis Patribus visum. Quid magis superstitiosum, magicum, quàm compellare dæmonem, ubi non est; adeóque advocare absentem? Nam quòd Pastorale Rursmundanum pag. 44. in rubrica, supplementum illud exorcismorum referri ad perfectiorem dæmonis ejectionem & pleniorem purgationem statuit, dilutum est; quia baptismo infantem plenè à dæmone & peccato solvi, tralatitia Hierarchicorum doctrina est; adeò ut & nobis & S. Paulo irascantur, docentibus, remanere in baptizatis aliquid, quod peccati veri nominis rationem habeat.
units.tr: LI. What of the fact that they want these rites of exorcism and similar ones to be supplied after a baptism that was not solemn, or was conferred by heretics, as they say, as is gathered from the Roman Ritual, On the Sacrament of Baptism, p. 41? Indeed nearly all the Scholastics who wrote on the Fourth Book of the Sentences, distinction 6, hold that those sacramentals (for so they call them), omitted in necessity, are to be supplied if the infant recovers. But what good will those exorcisms do to an infant already baptized? Is the baptized child still held by the devil? And yet it seemed good to the Fathers of Trent that the stain of original sin is wiped away by baptism. What is more superstitious and magical than to summon a demon where there is none, and so to call up one who is absent? For that the Pastorale Ruremundanum, p. 44, in its rubric, declares that this supplement of exorcisms refers to a more complete expulsion of the demon and a fuller purification, has been refuted, since it is a traditional doctrine of the hierarchs that the infant is fully freed from the devil and sin by baptism; so much so that they are angry with us and with St. Paul, who teach that something remains in the baptized which has the character of sin in the true sense.

units.la: LII. In his porrò Baptismalibus exorcismis nihil non superstitionem & magiam redolet. Præterquam enim quòd non ulla vocatione & virtute Divina dæmonis expulsio tentatur, cuncta etiam præscriptis constant formulis, à quibus si vel tantillum declinaveris, perit mysterium. Tot numero debent esse cruces, tot exsufflationes; quas ternas adhibent plerique, quia numero Deus impare gaudet. Celeb. leb. Witakerus Præleƒt. de Sacram, contr. de Bapt. q. 6. monet, pueros à nonnullis vicies exsufflari, tricies puellas, forte quòd in fœmineo sexu tenacior sit dæmon.
units.tr: LII. Moreover, in these baptismal exorcisms there is nothing that does not smell of superstition and magic. For apart from the fact that the expulsion of the demon is attempted by no divine calling or power, everything also consists of prescribed formulas, and if you deviate from them even slightly, the mystery perishes. There must be so many crosses, so many exsufflations; most of them use three, because God delights in an odd number. The celebrated Whitaker, in his Lectures on the Sacraments, against the controversy on Baptism, question 6, warns that boys are exsufflated by some twenty times, girls thirty times, perhaps because the devil is more tenacious in the female sex.

units.la: LIII. Haud equidem diffitemur, Exorcismi usum quendam in veterum baptismo obtinuisse. Cœterùm, præterquam quòd consuetudo illa Apostolis & Apostolicis viris incognita planè fuit, & aliquot post eorum decessum seculis usurpari cœpta; alterius etiam & diversissimi generis exorcismi illorum fuerunt ab iis, qui in Ecclesia Romana hodiè recepti sunt. Aliquando enim Exorcismi nomine iis venit Catechismus, sive institutio prævia baptizandi: aliquando abrenuntiatio solennis Sathanæ & pompis ejus facta, quæ hodie demum post Exorcismum fit. Sed insuper, quod reicaput est, Exsufflatio & Exorcismus, similésque ceremoniæ à veteribus adhibitæ sunt, non tanquam ulla ratione in baptizando effectivæ; (Sacrorum quippe signorum efficacia omnis ab institutione Divina pendet, hos verò ritus humanæ inventionis esse, ipsi Pontificii fatentur) sed tanquam umbræ & figuræ hieroglyphicæ, quibus vis & efficacia Baptismi Divinitùs instityти Catechumenis & populo duntaxat significaretur. Id quod ex pluribus S. Augustini aliorúmque locis, nostri demonstrârunt.
units.tr: LIII. We do not, indeed, deny that some use of exorcism prevailed in the baptism of the ancients. But besides the fact that this custom was entirely unknown to the Apostles and apostolic men, and began to be employed some centuries after their death, those exorcisms of theirs were also of a different and very distinct kind from those now received in the Roman Church. For sometimes by the name of exorcism was meant the catechism, or preliminary instruction of the one to be baptized; sometimes a solemn renunciation of Satan and his pomps, which today is made only after the exorcism. But further, what is most important, the exsufflation and exorcism, and similar ceremonies, were used by the ancients not as if they were in any way effective in baptizing (for the efficacy of the sacred signs depends wholly on divine institution, and the Papists themselves confess that these rites are of human invention), but as shadows and hieroglyphic figures, by which the power and efficacy of Baptism, divinely instituted, was signified to the catechumens and to the people only. This our men have demonstrated from many passages of St. Augustine and others.

units.la: LIV. Exorcismis præmissis diffidentes, oleum salutis addunt, oleum Catechumenorum, quod ex superstitiosa consecratione, ad omnem Diaboli exercitum eradicandum vim habere maximam putant. Postremò, aquam exorcizatam, & sale ac chrismate itidem exorcizatis conditam, gratiam conferre statuunt ex opere operato, quod nimis profectò magicum est. Hanc enim vim aqua nec ex se, nec ex condimentis, nec ex Divina institutione habet. Lavacrum est regenerationis & renovationis Spiritus S. quam videlicet Spiritus S. efficit, lavacrum aquæ obsignat Tit. iii. 5. Salvat nos baptisma: non ipsum proprie signum, sed signatum; non res terrena, sed coelestis, non depositio sordium carnis, lavacrum externum, sed interrogatio bonae conscientiae apud Deum, quae paraphrasis est ἐπερώτημα & fiduciae nostrae, quam ex resurrectione Christi ad Deum habemus, 1. Petr. iii. 21. Unde Baptismum Sacramentum fidei Augustinus Epist. 23. appellat. Illi contra ex aqua idolum faciunt, uti quidem magiam secundam idololatriam esse, ex Tertulliano supra docuimus.
units.tr: LIV. Having put exorcisms first, the distrustful add oil of salvation, the oil of the catechumens, which they think, because of its superstitious consecration, has very great power to root out the whole army of the Devil. Finally, they hold that water exorcised, and seasoned with salt and chrism exorcised in the same way, confers grace ex opere operato, which is surely far too magical. For water has this power neither from itself, nor from its seasonings, nor from divine institution. Baptism is "the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit" (Tit. 3:5), which the Holy Spirit effects and the washing of water seals. Baptism saves us: not the outward sign itself but the thing signified; not an earthly thing but a heavenly one; not "the putting away of the filth of the flesh," an outward washing, but "the answer of a good conscience toward God," which is a paraphrase of ἐπερώτημα and of the confidence we have toward God from the resurrection of Christ (1 Pet. 3:21). Hence Augustine, in Epistle 23, calls baptism Sacramentum fidei, the sacrament of faith. The Papists, on the other hand, make an idol out of the water, though we have shown above from Tertullian that magic is a second idolatry.

units.la: LV. In Eucharistia longe gravius Hierarchici peccant, Aquae enim Baptismi substantiam relinquunt: Panem vero & vinum Eucharistiae, quinque verborum praevio murmure, deificant, efficiuntque adeo, ut Iesus Nazarenus, qui ante plus quam mille sexcentos annos Hierosolymis crucifixus est, atque inde in Coelum ascendit, & ad dextram Dei, mansurus ibi usque ad consummationem rerum omnium, consedit, prolatis verbis, Hoc enim est corpus meum, nec pluribus, nec paucioribus, cum carne, sanguine & ossibus, Panacearum speciemque tantummodo, laxeque pendentium accidentium tenui palliolo contectus & amictus, personaliter appareat. Quod certe Magiae speciem illam Pythonissae Endorensis, Samuelem personatum & palliatum repraesentantis impietatem, omniaque necromantiae monumenta multis parasangis superat.
units.tr: LV. In the Eucharist the hierarchs sin far more gravely, for they leave the substance of the baptismal water as it is. But the bread and wine of the Eucharist, with a murmur of five words before them, they deify, and so bring it about that Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified at Jerusalem more than sixteen hundred years ago, from there ascended into heaven, and sat at the right hand of God, there to remain until the consummation of all things, appears in person, with flesh, blood and bones, not more and not fewer, at the words Hoc enim est corpus meum, covered and clothed only in the appearance of the species and the thin cloak of the loosely hanging accidents. Surely this kind of magic far surpasses the magic of the witch of Endor, who presented Samuel masked and cloaked, and all the monuments of necromancy, by many leagues.

units.la: LVI. Hinc adeo deificationem illam panis & vini, quam monstrosum vocabulo Transsubstantiationem appellant, magicis exemplis illustrant, quae supra Diss. xi. §. 1. Thesi XLIII, XLIV. allegata, denuo allegare instituti ratio jubet. Gabriel Biel in Canone Missae lect. 4. sic scribit: Breviter annotandum, quid in Missae celebratione Sacerdos sua virtute efficiat. Circa quod advertendum, quod aliquid ab alio effici vel fieri, tripliciter potest accipi. Nam aliquid dicitur ab alio fieri vel naturali potestate, vel meritoria operatione, vel assistente virtute. Naturali turali potestate, &c. Tertio modo (quo postea probat transsubstantiationem fieri) aliquid dicitur ab aliquo fieri aliqua virtute occulta, non insistente ei, à quo tale fieri dicitur, sed assistente; secundum quem modum (NB) malefici & incantatrices quosdam effectus producere dicuntur, & extrahere lac vaccarum de sedibus, seu manubriis securium, quod fit non virtute naturali maleficorum, neque ex eorum merito, sed virtute occulta sive bona, sive mala assistente. Ita Cœlius Rhodiginus Antiq. lect. lib xvi. 14. Quæstio, inquit, diu agitata veteribus est, insitne vis aliqua verbis certâ quâdam formulâ enuntiatis? Equidem Christianæ veritatis cultor qui possit inficiari? Quando Princeps illererum ac Summi Patris Filius, ex vero verus Deus, præfatione Sacerdotis brevissima svocetur (NB) eliciatúrve à cœlesti sede. Cuí simile quiddam & prisco-rum vana superstitio aut habuit, aut credidit: quando & Tullum Hostilium Pisonis tradidêre monumenta, ex Numæ libris eodem operatum sacro, Jovem elicere Cælo, quem & inde Elicium vocabant, quod in Fastis cecinit Poëta nobilis, conatum, &c. Huc pertinent Francisci, quæ Conformit. lib. 1. parte 2. pag. 177. extant, verba: Ut quid non cognoscitis veritatem, & creditis in Filium Dei, qui quotidie se humiliat. Sicut quando è Regalibus sedibus venit in uterum virginis; quotidie venit ad nos ipse humilis apparens, quotidie descendit de sinu Patris super altare in manu Sacerdotis? Ita Biel idem, qui suprà, Lect. 4. in Can. Missæ: Cœli, inquit, Regina & mundi domina prolatis octo verbulis: Ecce ancilla Domini; fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum; semel concepit Dei Filium & mundi Redemptorem. Isti autem à Domino consecrati, quinque verbis, contextam consecrationis formam cum debita intentione proserentes, eundem Dei virginisque Filium advocant quotidie corporaliter , in sacrificium & criminum purgationem. Blasphemiam auget Alexander de Ales parte iv. q. 53. membro 2. ubi veram esse opinionem , dicentem, quòd corpus Christi defertur , quocunque species deferuntur , ut in ventrem canis , vel suis , vel in alia loca immunda ; nec non Thomas Aquinas p. iij. q. 80. art. 3. ubi asserit, simus aut canis busltiam consecratam manducet , substantiam corporis Christi non desinere esse sub speciebus , quandiu species illæ manent, sicut etiam , si projiceretur in lutum. Verba Authorum supra producticra recitavi. Quibus addo Claudium Espencæum Continuat. 3. Conf. referentem , quod illam Christi de Cœlo deductionem in altare ex Sacerdotibus & Ecclesiasticis sæpè audiverit; quos tamen excusare nolit , uti nec Sententiarios , Quæstionarios , Rationarios , Manipularios , Scholasticos , si qui ita locuti sint, de quibus consilium illud Quintiliani suggerit: Diu non nisi Optimus quisque , & qui credentem sibi minimè fallat , legendus est. Sic ergò quinque, non plures, nec pauciores, voculæ illæ, Hoc enim est corpus meum , Christum ad dextram throni Majestatis confidentem, denuò à cœlesti sede evocatum & elicitum humiliant, ut in magno periculo versetur, ne à canibus, suibus, muribus aut vermibus comedatur, vel in lutum projiciatur. O tenebras ! O cœcitatem! O impietatem Magicam extremam !
units.tr: LVI. Hence they illustrate that deification of bread and wine, which they monstrously call transubstantiation, with magical examples, which the plan of this work now bids us cite again, after they were cited above in Diss. xi. §. 1. Theses XLIII, XLIV. Gabriel Biel, in Canone Missae, lect. 4, writes thus: It should be briefly noted what the priest effects by his own power in the celebration of the Mass. Here it must be observed that something can be effected or done by another in three ways. For something is said to be done by another either by natural power, or by meritorious operation, or by assisting power. By natural power, etc. In the third way (by which he afterwards proves that transubstantiation takes place) something is said to be done by someone by some hidden power, not inhering in him by whom such a thing is said to be done, but assisting; and in this way (NB) sorcerers and enchantresses are said to produce certain effects, and to draw milk from cows out of the seats or handles of axes, which is done not by the natural power of the sorcerers nor by their merit, but by a hidden power, whether good or bad, assisting. So Caelius Rhodiginus, Antiq. lect. lib. 16, c. 14: The question, he says, has long been debated by the ancients: whether there is any power in words pronounced in a certain fixed formula? Indeed, who, being a worshipper of Christian truth, could deny it? When the Prince of the angels and Son of the Most High Father, true God from true God, is summoned by the brief preface of the priest (NB), and is drawn down from his heavenly seat. Something similar was held, or believed, by the vain superstition of the ancients, when the records of Piso relate that Tullus Hostilius, having performed the same sacred rite from the books of Numa, summoned Jupiter down from heaven, whom they then called Elicius, as the famous poet sang in the Fasti, and so on. To this belong the words of Francis found in the Conformities, lib. 1, part 2, p. 177: Why do you not recognise the truth, and believe in the Son of God, who humbles himself every day? As when he came from the royal seats into the womb of the virgin; every day he comes to us, appearing in humility, every day he descends from the bosom of the Father upon the altar in the hand of the priest? Biel again, as above, Lect. 4, in Can. Missae: The Queen of heaven and mistress of the world, with eight words uttered: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word; once conceived the Son of God and Redeemer of the world. But those consecrated by the Lord, uttering with due intention the form of consecration woven together in five words, summon the same Son of God and the Virgin bodily every day, for sacrifice and the purging of sins.
