Legitimate ministers, feeding the flock for Christ alone and not for themselves and their lusts, and, as the good shepherd was wisely said to do [ὁ δεῖνα], shearing and not flaying, have been appointed as stewards and ministers, empowered to preach the Gospel, dispense the sacraments and faithfully observe the order and decorum freely established in the Church, and nothing else.

units.la: gimine Ecclesia, religionis cognoscenda medium, Verbo Dei inprimis, asseriatur. piscentiis suis pascentes, & quod boni pastoris esse sapienter ὁ δεῖνα dixit, tondentes, non deglubentes; Oeconomi adeoque & Ministri, non alia quàm ex praescripto praedicandi Euangelium, Sacramenta dispensandi, & ordinem atque decorum omne liberè in Ecclesia constitutum, ritè custodiendi, potestate pollentes subrogati sunt. Denique quoad religionis cognoscendæ media, verbum Dei Solius in arce dominandi, summoque authoritatis culmine repositum, omnibúsque legendum, meditandum, sequendum propositum, commendatum unicè, & supra traditionem, authoritatem hominum & signaturam Bestiæ adeò exaltatum est, ut jam ne pueri quidem, juxta vaticinium Esaiæ xxxv. 8. aberrare possent, commenta humana, μύθοι σοφισμένοι, seu fabulæ artificiosè compositæ, ad orcum relegatæ: Linguarum, Originalium inprimis, & sanioris περὶ ζωῆς οἰκοδομῆς facientis Philosophiæ studia ex suo exilio, quo diu damnata jacebant, revocata sunt. Hoc scilicet brevi coelestis ille splendor subitò ex æthere erumpens, universamque terram collustrans; hoc nova quædam Pentecoste, tantam in Ecclesiam Metamorphosin inducens, effecit.
units.tr: Church, the means of knowing religion, above all the Word of God, is asserted. Finally, as to the means of knowing religion, the Word of God alone has been placed on the citadel of dominion and at the highest summit of authority, proposed and commended to all to be read, meditated upon and followed, and exalted above tradition, the authority of men and the mark of the Beast, so that now not even children, according to the prophecy of Isaiah 35:8, could go astray. Human inventions, μύθοι σοφισμένοι [cunningly devised fables], or fables artfully composed, have been relegated to the pit. The studies of languages, the original tongues above all, and of that sounder philosophy which builds up life [περὶ ζωῆς οἰκοδομῆς], have been recalled from the exile in which they had long lain condemned. This, in short, is what that heavenly splendor bursting suddenly out of the ether and lighting up the whole earth accomplished; this new Pentecost brought about so great a metamorphosis in the Church.

units.la: XXVI. Ubi jam apud eos, quos sic Spiritus S. suo φωλισμῷ renovavit, Papistica illa κειμήλια, idola & altaria? Ubi cuculli, rosaria, globuli preculares, grana consecrata, horæ canonicæ? Ubi anniversaria manium καθάρματα, missarum solennia, indulgentiarum diplomata, suffragia pro defunctis, suffumigia pro vivis, aqua februa, ciborum, vestium, dierum discrimina? Ubi chrismata & exorcismi? Ubi stigmata Francifci, peregrinationes ad statuas, tabellæ votivæ, mortuorum adoratio? Ubi denique
units.tr: XXVI. Where now, among those whom the Holy Spirit has so renewed with his [φωλισμῷ] light, are those Papistical treasures [κειμήλια], the idols and altars? Where are the cowls, rosaries, prayer beads, consecrated grains, and canonical hours? Where are the anniversaries for the spirits of the dead [καθάρματα], the solemnities of the Masses, the diplomas of indulgences, the suffrages for the dead, the incense for the living, the februal water, and the distinctions of foods, garments and days? Where are the chrism and exorcisms? Where are the stigmata of Francis, the pilgrimages to statues, the votive tablets, the adoration of the dead? Where, finally,

units.la: Somnia, terrores magici, miracula, sagæ, Nocturni Lemures, portentaque Thessala?
units.tr: Dreams, magical terrors, miracles, witches, nocturnal ghosts and Thessalian portents?

units.la: Ut retineant religionem tot Seculis usurpatam, ut nos in Ecclesiæ suæ gremium reducant, cur non portentosa aliqua de Spectris, de Lemuribus, de Inferis comminiscuntur? Cur non mortuorum apparitiones fingunt? Omnia tentata hactenus, sed nihil usquam succedit. Nimirum cœlesti hac luce perfusus, sapere cœpit Orbis Christianus, patefactæ sunt nebulonum fraudes, aperti doli, detracta persona. Bernense scelus, quod Chronica nostra recensent, aliáque fictis istis visionibus atque miraculis fidem derogárunt. Monachorum somnia atque aniles fabulæ pro nihilo ducuntur: contemnuntur & Papæ tonitrua è pelvi. Bullæ ipsæ Papales, pro bullis habentur. Nihil præter Euangelium jam admittimus. Et quoniam vox cœlestis de Christo, Ipsum audite, præcipit, nihil jam moramur authoritatem Papæ & Sanctulorum ejus, Dominici, Francisci, &c. nihil deliramenta Monachorum, nihil apparitiones mortuorum. Ipsum jam, ipsummet, inquam, Christum audire solum volupe est. Itaque eò jam promotum fere est, ut mendax & fucosa superstitio sublata propemodùm è medio, atque extincta radicitùs è mortalium plurimorum animis videatur.
units.tr: To keep the religion that has been practised for so many centuries, and to lead us back into the bosom of their Church, why do they not invent some portentous tales about spectres, ghosts and the underworld? Why do they not fabricate apparitions of the dead? They have tried everything so far, but nothing succeeds anywhere. Clearly the Christian world, bathed in this heavenly light, has begun to be wise. The frauds of the scoundrels have been exposed, their deceits brought to light, and their mask torn off. The Bernese crime, which our chronicles record, and other such fabricated visions and miracles, have destroyed trust. The dreams of monks and old wives' tales are counted as nothing; the thunders of the Pope are scorned as coming out of a basin. Papal bulls themselves are regarded as mere paper. We now admit nothing but the Gospel. And since the heavenly voice concerning Christ commands, Hear him, we no longer dwell on the authority of the Pope and his saints, Dominic, Francis and the rest, nor on the ravings of monks, nor on the apparitions of the dead. To hear Him alone, Christ Himself, I say, is now a pleasure. Thus things have advanced so far that the lying and painted superstition seems to have been almost removed from the midst and uprooted from the minds of very many mortals.

units.la: XXVII. Sic planè Papa cum omni suo syrmate hactenùs visus sedere, & solis instar lucere in Cœlo, cecidit in terram. Cecidit Babylon, cùm sic verus justitiæ Sol splendore suo collustrav it terram: & spiritualia Papatûs fundamenta, prætextus Catholicæ Ecclesiæ, Christi œcumenicus Vicariatus, Petri personalis & ordinaria successio, aliáque ejusmodi, quorum ascititio fuco Meretrix illa toti mundo nequiter imposuit; subruta sunt: Quomodo Apoc. ix. 1. buccinante quinto Angelo, stella ex Coelo cecidisse dicitur. Cui casui Regis Babylonis mysticè casus in terram Esai. xiv. 12. respondet. Sicut in Coelo sedebat, & stella fuerat, opinione hominum: ita lapsus est in terram, cùm homines eam opinionem de ipso persuasionémque abjecerunt, atque Papa stupor ille mundi, jam vulgi fabula factus est. Convenit, quòd Apoc. xiv. 8. post praedicationem aeterni Euangelii coeptam, similiter casus Babylonis sic annuntiatur: Cecidit, cecidit Babylon urbs illa Magna. Desumtum id est ex Esai. xxi. 9. ubi de Babylone Chaldaica sermo est; quae cecidisse dicitur, quando motus bellici initia apparuerunt. Sic plane Papatus cecidit, seu cadere coepit, quando Splendore Euangelii illustrati homines pii, Deinque reverentes, aperuerunt oculos, & Hierarchiam Babylonem esse, doctrinâ, ceremoniis, cultu ejus omni & gubernatione, cum verbo Dei & doctrinâ Euangelii publicè jam & clarè sonante, comparata, agnoverunt, abominationes ejus & turpitudines abhorruerunt, communionem ejus neglexerunt, foedae nundinationi ejus nuntium remiserunt, nihil amplius Regnis, Provinciis, Civitatibus in istam voraginem conferentibus, quin potius nidorem illum culinae ex offertoriis Missarum, ignemque purgatorii luculentissimum extinguentibus; Annatas, Indulgentias, Pallia, Regalia, seu pretia ex iis hactenus redacta, & id genus alia ... ad cuticulam profusius curandam pertinentia, subtrahentibus; denique universam factionem Papalem, Babylonicae impietatis tonvictam, res suas sibi habere & ... multum plorare jusserunt.
units.tr: XXVII. Thus the Pope, who until now seemed to sit with all his finery and shine like the sun in heaven, has fallen to the earth. Babylon has fallen, since the true Sun of righteousness has thus illumined the earth with his brightness; and the spiritual foundations of the papacy, the pretext of the Catholic Church, the ecumenical vicariate of Christ, the personal and ordinary succession of Peter, and other such things, by whose counterfeit paint that harlot wickedly imposed on the whole world, have been overthrown. Just as, when the fifth angel sounded the trumpet, a star is said to have fallen from heaven (Rev. 9:1), so to this fall the figurative fall of the king of Babylon in the earthly sense corresponds (Isa. 14:12). As he sat in heaven and was a star in the opinion of men, so he has fallen to earth, when men have cast off that opinion and persuasion about him, and the Pope, the amazement of the world, has now become a fable of the common people. It is fitting that after the preaching of the eternal Gospel had begun, Rev. 14:8 announces the fall of Babylon in the same way: Fallen, fallen is Babylon, that great city. This is taken from Isa. 21:9, where the speech concerns Chaldean Babylon, which is said to have fallen when the first signs of war appeared. So the papacy has plainly fallen, or began to fall, when pious men, enlightened by the splendour of the Gospel and reverent of God, opened their eyes and recognised that the hierarchy was Babylon, comparing it with the word of God and the doctrine of the Gospel now sounding publicly and clearly, in its teaching, its ceremonies, all its worship and government; they abhorred its abominations and filthiness, neglected its communion, sent back its shameful traffic with a refusal, and, since no more kingdoms, provinces or cities were contributing to that abyss, they extinguished that kitchen smell from the offerings of the Masses and the very bright fire of purgatory; they withdrew annates, indulgences, palliums, regalia, or the prices obtained from them until now, and other things of that kind pertaining to curing the skin more lavishly; finally they ordered the whole Papal faction, convicted of Babylonish impiety, to keep their own goods and to mourn greatly.

units.la: XXVIII. Non tamen hac quidem vice sic cecidit Papa, ut Regnum plane nullum; suumque veluti ...
units.tr: XXVIII. Yet the Pope has not fallen on this occasion in such a way that he has entirely no kingdom, and for a certain time he did not keep his, as it were, ...

units.la: Ἀπὸ quoddam ad tempus non retineret. Nam & Babylon primùm lapsa, non illicò regnum suum dominationémque universam perdidit, sed & domicilium custodiámque quandam, & domicilii sui, custodiæque incolas quosdam retinuit. Postquam enim cecidit, statim de ea Apoc. xviii. 2. enuntiatur: Et facta est domicilium dæmoniorum, & custodia omnis spiritús immundi, & custodia omnis avis immundæ & invisæ. Alludit Prophetia ad Esai. xxxiv. 11. 15. Sicut in Civitatibus desolatis serpentes & infaustæ aves dominari solent, ita factum innuit, ut in Babylone lapsa, loco serpentum dæmonia, loco avium impurarum & invisatum, homines mali, rapaces, truculenti, obscœni habitent.
units.tr: For Babylon, too, when first fallen, did not at once lose her kingdom and her whole dominion, but she retained a certain dwelling and guard, and some inhabitants of that dwelling and guard. For after she fell, it is at once said of her (Rev. 18:2): And she has become a dwelling of demons, and a prison of every unclean spirit, and a prison of every unclean and hateful bird. The prophecy alludes to Isa. 34:11, 15. Just as serpents and ill-omened birds are wont to rule in deserted cities, so it signals that, in fallen Babylon, instead of serpents there are demons, and instead of unclean and hated birds there live wicked, rapacious, savage and obscene men.

units.la: XXIX. Post casum Papatûs, & separationem ab eodem, Ecclesiæ, quæ hactenùs in eo captiva suspirave-rat, duo hominum genera in ejusdem communione re- manserunt.
units.tr: XXIX. After the fall of the papacy and the separation from it, two kinds of men have remained in communion with the Church, which until then had sighed in captivity within it.

units.la: Prius eorum, qui fundamenta Christianæ Religionis abnegare perrexerunt, & in omni impietate sua Babylonica obdurati, signaturam Bestiæ prona voluntate receperunt, retinueruntque. Posterius eorum, qui tametsi corpore adhuc cum eodem conjuncti, quia non statim omnes profunditates Sathanæ iis innotuerunt, suspirantes tamen, & emendationem sperantes; quin & propter scandala aliundè, cujuscunque culpâ id fieret, iis obiecta, quò se conferrent, ancipites hærent; adeóque corpore magis, quàm affectu animóque intra Babylonis illius spiritualis mœnia se continent.
units.tr: The first kind are those who have persisted in denying the foundations of the Christian religion, and, hardened in all their Babylonish impiety, have willingly received and kept the mark of the Beast. The second kind are those who, although still joined to that body, because not all the depths of Satan have yet been made known to them, nevertheless sigh and hope for amendment; and yet, on account of scandals objected to them from elsewhere, by whose fault soever this happens, they hesitate uncertainly about where to betake themselves, and so they keep themselves within the walls of that spiritual Babylon more in body than in affection and mind.

units.la: Sicut Babylon Chaldaica, egresso inde Zorobabele, unà cum populo Israëlitico, illicò cœpit fieri habitaculum hominum impurorum: licèt non omnes simul Israëlitæ egrederentur, sed paulatim multi exirent, qui lo-
units.tr: Just as Chaldean Babylon, once Zerubbabel had gone out from it together with the Israelite people, at once began to become a habitation of impure men, although not all the Israelites went out at the same time, but many went out gradually,

units.la: cccccꝛ co licet cum impuris hominibus juncti, animo tamen disjunctissimi erant: ita, quando Ecclesia coepit ex Babylone spirituali egredi, illico coepit illa fieri habitaculum daemoniorum & impurarum avium, licet multi corpore conjuncti, animo disjuncti, in eo censu non sint. Sed, ut continuatur egressio populi, ita Babylonis desolatio proficit. Eatenus igitur de nonnullis, qui nondum Babylone exiverunt, spem habere possumus, quod ad Babylonem non pertineant, quatenus spem habere possumus, eos nescire, quid Babylone geratur, & quae sit causa eorum, qui ex ea egrediuntur; adeoque non habere doctrinam Babylonis, sed per verba fundamenti veritatem didicisse, & amorem Dei ad parendum certo ipsius verbo concepisse, denique suspirare propter peccata, quae in Babylone fiunt. Prius vero illud genus hominum Spiritus S. daemonia, aves impuras & odiosas, Babyloneműque eorum domicilium & custodiam insignit:
units.tr: although joined in place with impure men, were nonetheless most completely separated in mind; so, when the Church began to go out from spiritual Babylon, at once that place began to become a habitation of demons and of impure birds, although many who are joined in body and separated in mind are not in that number. But, just as the going out of the people continues, so the desolation of Babylon advances. Thus, as far as some who have not yet come out of Babylon are concerned, we may have hope, in so far as we may hope that they do not belong to Babylon, because they do not know what goes on in Babylon and what is the cause of those who go out from it; and so they do not hold the doctrine of Babylon, but have learned the truth through the words of the foundation, have conceived love of God to obey His sure word, and finally sigh on account of the sins that are committed in Babylon. But the first kind of men the Holy Spirit marks out as demons, unclean and hateful birds, and their Babylon as a dwelling and a prison:

units.la: XXX. Cujus enim, quaeso, post separationem fidelium, veritatis professorum, domicilium Papatus, spiritualis illa Babylon, factus est, in quo doctrinae daemoniorum obtinent, & castra sua metantur homines, qui iis delectantur unice: in quo non tolerantur pii, qui se discipulos verbi Divini profitentur, & volunt pie vivere: saltem, qui timent in nomine Dei facere, cujus Deus author non est, & quod nunquam ille praecepit: in quo denique nonnisi homines flatibus aereis tenebrosi hujus seculi acti, & doctores cum inauspicata voce corvorum & bubonum instar, pervolitantes regnant? Jam olim quidem Bernhardus lib. iv. Confid. sic Papam Eugenium compellavit: Inter haec tu Pastor procedis, multo & pretioso circumdatus ornatu. Si audedrem dicere, DÆMONUM magis, quàm ovium PASCUA hæc sunt. Quantò magis dæmonum pascua evaserunt tum, cùm veræ oves Christi, vocem ejus, Pastoris unici, audientes, arida illa & deserta Babylonis loca deseruerunt, secúmque irrigua & salubria, si qua supererant, pascua abduxerunt?
units.tr: XXX. For, I ask, after the separation of the faithful, the professors of the truth, what has become of the dwelling of the papacy, that spiritual Babylon, in which the doctrines of demons prevail, and men who take delight in them alone pitch their camp; in which the pious who profess themselves disciples of the divine Word and wish to live piously are not tolerated, at least those who fear to act in the name of a God whose author He is not, and which He never commanded; in which, finally, only men driven by the windy blasts of this dark age, and teachers flying about with an ill-omened voice like crows and owls, hold sway? Long ago Bernard (On Consideration, book 4) addressed Pope Eugene thus: Among these things you walk forth as a shepherd, surrounded with much costly ornament. If I dared to say it, these are rather the pastures of demons than of the sheep. How much more have they become pastures of demons, when the true sheep of Christ, hearing the voice of their one Shepherd, have deserted those dry and desert places of Babylon, and have led away with them whatever wholesome and well-watered pastures were left?

units.la: XXXI. S. Johannes Apoc. xvi. 13. 14. sexto Angelo phialam suam in fluvium illum magnum Euphratem effundente, vidisse dicitur, ex ore Draconis, & ex ore Bestiæ, & ex ore Pseudoprophetæ prodeuntes Spiritus tres immundos, similes ranis.
units.tr: XXXI. St John, Rev. 16:13, 14, says that when the sixth angel poured out his bowl upon the great river Euphrates, he saw coming out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits like frogs.

units.la: Erat enim, inquit, πνεύματα δαιμόνων, spiritus dæmonum, facientes signa, qui exeunt ad Reges terræ, & totius habitabilis, ut congregent illos in bellum diei illius magnæ Dei omnipotentis. Tripartitum illud spirituum, Papæ emissariorum, & Tot-Orbi-perambuli-technorum, Draconico homicidii, Bestiali cupiditatis rerum temporalium, & Pseudoprophetico mendacii, falsæque doctrinæ afflatu turgentium agmen suprà, ubi crudelitatem Babylonis repræsentavimus, explicatiùs paulò dedimus. Cùmque eorum operatio, & totius phialæ sextæ prophetia cum Babylonis hoc casu planè conveniat, ubi attentiùs consideranti liquebit, hæc ipsa utique dæmonia, post factam piorum secessionem, in Babylone remansisse, & in eadem ceu custodia sua detineri, liquet, tametsi non tam Deus, quàm eorum cupiditates, avaritia, hypocrisis, mollities & adamata vitæ luxuries, splendor fortunæ, & similia, in carcere illo eosdem detinet. Hæc enim, non quicquam aliud, eò illos propellit, ut Regnum illud Avaritiæ & Impietatis, tanquam portum negotiationis suæ, tanto conatu contra conscientiam suam defendant.
units.tr: For they are, he says, πνεύματα δαιμόνων [spirits of demons], working signs, who go out to the kings of the earth and of the whole inhabited world, to gather them to battle on the great day of God Almighty. We have set out somewhat more fully above, where we described the cruelty of Babylon, that threefold company of spirits, the emissaries of the Pope and the globe-trotting cheats of every sort, swelling with the dragon's breath of murder, the beastly breath of lust for temporal goods, and the false prophet's breath of lies and false doctrine. And since their operation, and the whole prophecy of the sixth bowl, agree plainly with this fall of Babylon, it becomes clear to anyone who considers more attentively that these very demons, after the separation of the pious, have remained in Babylon, and are held there as in their prison; although it is not so much God who holds them in that prison as their own desires, avarice, hypocrisy, softness and love of a luxurious life, the splendour of fortune, and such things. For these drive them, and nothing else, to defend with such great effort, against their own conscience, that kingdom of Avarice and Impiety, as the harbour of their trade.

units.la: XXXII. Ubi doctrinæ dæmoniacæ regnant, ibi domicilium dæmoniorum fixum haud dubiè est. In Papatu autem doctrinas dæmoniacas regnare, manifestum est, quia in eodem impletum est S. Pauli vaticinium 1. Tim. iv. 1. 2. 3. his verbis conceptum: Spiritus tamen expresse dicit, posteremis temporibus quosdam à fide defecturos, attendentes spiritibus erroneis & doctrinis dæmonum, per hypocrisin falsiloquorum, cauteriatam habentium conscientiam, prohibentium inire matrimonium, & jubentium abstinere à cibis, quos Deus condidit ad participationem cum gratiarum actione fidelibus, & qui veritatem agnoverunt. Hæc vaticinium Papatui, ex eo inprimis tempore, quo ab eodem Ecclesia Christi secessit, ex amussim congruere, singuli fere apices demonstrant. Primò enim, prædicit S. Paulus apostasiam à fide, eámque futuram posteremis seu novissimis temporibus. Papatum autem à fide defecisse, ex ejusdem erroribus tyrannicis, in Christum ejusque officia arietantibus, Idololatricis & Magicis suprà probavimus, & à fide decidere cœpisse eundem ὑστέροις καιροῖς, novissimis temporibus, hoc est, uti pluribus Josephus Medus de Apostasia novissimorum temporum pag. 103. &c. post Imperii Romani ruinam, quod tempus juxta Calendarii Prophetici stylum, novissimorum temporum nomine venire solet, ex historia & prophetiæ ipsius filo liquet. Secundò, apostasiæ tribuitur iis, qui attendunt spiritibus seductoribus. In quibus proin est σχῆμα, attentio, ad spiritus hominum, qualis videlicet includit opinionem, quòd hi homines mendacium loquentes, habeant spiritum, cui attendendum sit; quique adeò errare, fallere vel falli ipse nequeat: & cui jubenti simpliciter, præcipientique, non demonstranti ex Scripturis, jussa, ἀΘαυαπίσως credendum parendúmque fit. Sic planè Papicolæ ποσοχῶ ἀδοκίμασον, attentionem rebus non exploratis, commodandam, hoc est, fidem implicitam, quæ in Papæ, assistentiam perpetuam Spiritus S. adeóque infallibilitatem in rebus fidei, quoad jus, & (sic enim hodiè Jesuitastri saltem sciscunt) quoad factum, jactantis, tanquam Pontificii imperii nervum, postulant præstántque. Sed spiritui tali cœcam fidem substringere Spiritus S. quod res est, ποσοχῷ πνεύματι πλάνῳ, attendere spiritui deceptori, appellat. Tertiò, eadem apostasia tribuitur iis, qui attendunt διδασκαλίαις δαιμονίων, doctrinis dæmoniorum. Sive autem δαιμόνια hic Deastros, Angelos, Sanctósque in Divorum religiosè colendorum censum vocatos, significant, uti quidem idem, qui supra, Vir doctissimus Jesephus Medus, Theologus Anglus, eodem doctissimo libro probare sustinuit, quid Dæmoniorum, hoc est, Deastrorum religioso cultu, & idololatria in Papatu frequentiùs? Sive Cacodæmones notantur, do-strinæ dæmoniacæ, à Sathana introductæ, quas procedente etiam hoc tractatu demonstramus, tam manifestè in Papatu obtinent, ut res jam tum gesta, non gerenda demùm describi videri possit. Quartò, Prophetia apostasiæ hujus & dæmoniacarum doctrinarum certos quosdam characteres figit, eosque maximè obvios & notorios. Nam sic deficientes & dæmoniacis doctrinis, seu spiritibus deceptoribus attendentes, dicuntur mendacium locuturi in hypocrisi, cauteriatam habere conscientiam, vetare uxores ducere, jubere abstinere à cibis. Sunt enim Spiritus ii, quibus deficientes à fide attendunt, deceptores. In deceptione autem duo sunt; ut, qui decipere velit, tum gratum aliquid jucundum exhibeat atque ostentet, quale quid menda-cium est, quo maximè homo naturalis delectatur: tum tegat ea, quæ proponit, ut videantur utilia, aut sal-tem non appareat, ea esse noxia; hoc est, ne videantur pugnare cum eo, quod de Deo & via justitiæ cognitum est, & ignorari non potest, quod fit per ψευδεπίγραφον, seu simulationem eam, qua assumitur nomen Christi, voluntas sequendi Scripturam Euangelicam, accipiendi signa foederis, quædam cum fidelibus communia dicendi, faciendive, abstinendi à gentilium Idololatria, eamque insectandi, Judæos & Hæreticos singulari cum zelo oppugnandi, præfertur. Altera sic docentium nota est, quòd habent conscientiam cauterio adustam. Cauterium, quo sic conscientia aduritur, sunt concupiscentia ingens, hypocrisis, fraus, sophismata, quibus se indurant & obstupefaciunt, qui ita à fide deficiunt, & dæmoniacas doctrinas inducunt. Sed clarissimi omnium characteres deficientium à fide, & dæmoniacas doctrinas introducentium sunt, quòd vetent illi uxores ducere, & jubeant abstinere à cibis, quos Deus condidit. Hæc de Hierarchicis prædicta esse, meridiani solis radiis scriptum est. Papæ enim ve-tant eos, qui Episcopi, Presbyteri, Clerici esse volunt, uxores ducere; & cibis certis in jejunio abstinere præcipiunt.
units.tr: XXXII. Where teachings of demons reign, there is without doubt a fixed dwelling of demons. That demonic teachings reign in Papacy is plain, because in it the prophecy of St Paul in 1 Tim. 4:1-3 has been fulfilled, expressed in these words: "But the Spirit expressly says that in the latter times some will fall away from the faith, giving heed to deceiving spirits and doctrines of demons, through the hypocrisy of liars, having their conscience seared, forbidding marriage and commanding abstinence from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by the faithful and by those who have known the truth." That nearly every detail of this prophecy fits Papacy exactly, especially from the time when the Church of Christ withdrew from it, is shown as follows. (1) First, St Paul foretells an apostasy from the faith, and that it will occur in the latter or last times [ὑστέροις καιροῖς]. That Papacy has fallen from the faith, through its tyrannical errors which strike against Christ and his offices, and through its idolatrous and magical practices, we have proved above; and that it began to fall away in the latter times, that is, as Joseph Mede shows at length in his book on the apostasy of the last times, p. 103 and following, after the ruin of the Roman Empire (a period which, in the style of the prophetic calendar, is usually called "the last times"), is clear from history and from the thread of the prophecy itself. (2) Second, the apostasy is attributed to those who give heed to seducing spirits. In this there is a figure of speech, an attention to the spirits of men, which evidently implies the opinion that these men, who speak lies, have a spirit to whom attention must be paid, a spirit which cannot err, deceive or be deceived; and whose commands, given simply and imperatively without proof from Scripture, must be believed and obeyed without examination [ἀβασάνιστως]. Thus the Papists plainly demand and enforce an attention to matters unexamined [προσέχειν ἀδοκίμαστα], that is, an implicit faith, which they assert to be the sinew of the Papal empire: a faith in the perpetual assistance of the Holy Spirit in the Pope, and so in his infallibility in matters of faith, both as to right and (for so the Jesuitasters at least now claim) as to fact. But that the Holy Spirit binds such blind faith to a spirit, which is what it truly is, he calls "giving heed to a deceiving spirit" [προσέχοντες πνεύματι πλάνῳ]. (3) Third, the same apostasy is attributed to those who give heed to "doctrines of demons" [διδασκαλίαις δαιμονίων]. Now whether "demons" here means the deities, angels and saints received into the number of the divinities to be worshipped religiously, as the learned Joseph Mede, an English theologian, maintained in the same learned book, what is more frequent in Papacy than the religious worship of demons, that is, of deities, and idolatry? Or whether evil demons are meant, the demonic doctrines introduced by Satan, which we show in the course of this treatise prevail so openly in Papacy that the thing, already done, may seem to be described rather than still to be done. (4) Fourth, the prophecy of this apostasy and of demonic doctrines fixes certain characters, and these are very obvious and notorious. For those who fall away and give heed to demonic doctrines or deceiving spirits are said to speak lies in hypocrisy, to have a seared conscience, to forbid marriage and to command abstinence from foods. Indeed the spirits to which those who fall from the faith give heed are deceivers. In deception there are two elements: the one who wishes to deceive first displays and sets forth something pleasing and agreeable, such as a lie, in which natural man especially delights; then he conceals what he proposes, so that it appears useful, or at least that it is not seen to be harmful; that is, so that it does not seem to conflict with what is known about God and the way of righteousness, and so that it cannot be recognised. This is done by a pseudepigraphic disguise [ψευδεπίγραφον], or simulation, by which the name of Christ is assumed, the will to follow the Gospel Scripture is put forward, the signs of the covenant are received, certain things common to the faithful are said or done, idolatry of the Gentiles is abstained from and attacked, and Jews and heretics are opposed with singular zeal. The other mark of such teachers is that "they have their conscience seared with a branding iron." The branding iron by which the conscience is so burned consists of immense concupiscence, hypocrisy, fraud and sophistries, by which those who thus fall from the faith and introduce demonic doctrines harden and stupefy themselves. But the clearest of all the marks of those who fall from the faith and introduce demonic doctrines is that they "forbid marriage and command abstinence from foods which God created." It is written as plainly as the rays of the midday sun that these things were foretold of the hierarchical men. For the Popes forbid those who wish to be bishops, presbyters or clergy to marry, and they command abstinence from certain foods in fasting.

units.la: XXXIII. Qua verò etiam hîc, ut in reliquis omnibus Hierarchici φιλολόγων ἰσαγωγεῖς, mendaciloquorum hypocrisi, utuntur: quo cauterio conscientiam suam obstupefaciunt? Negant in universum, Apostolum loqui de omnibus, qui vetant nuptias, sed de quibusdam duntaxat, qui matrimonium, ceu rem malam, universis interdicunt; cujusmodi olim Encratitæ, Carpocratiani, MaManichæi, Marcionitæ, alii fuerint. Hæc mala renitentium conscientia est. Fingunt enim ex suo ingenio non in universum de omnibus, sed de quibusdam, Apostolum loqui, atque ita fas esse prohibere alicui, quod nefas sit prohibere omnibus. Cum tamen interdictum hoc in uno esse justum, in alio injustum & daemoniacum esse non possit. Christus enim & Apostoli omnes eundem Spiritum, eandem puritatem & sanctitatem habere volunt. Et Presbyteri typi esse gregis debent. Quod igitur prohibetur paucis, toleratur quidem, sed reprehenditur in omnibus, & ostenditur esse res inhonesta, indecora, turpis, mala. Quod dogma cum veteribus Hæreticis Encratitis, Manichæis, &c. Papistæ commune habent. Verbis ergo, se nuptias, ut rem malam, prohibere negant: re affirmant, & cauteriatam conscientiam produnt. Legitimum enim amorem, & legitimas nuptias dicunt esse contrarias puritati Sacerdotis: & magis contrarias, quàm scortationem. Quare enim prohibent, si non esse contrarias Sacerdotis Sanctitati reputant? Sacerdotem propter tractatum corpus Christi, cœlibem esse oportere sanciunt: atque idem corpus Christi uxoratis, quorum puriores manus sunt, quàm Sacerdotum labia, in os inferunt. Quid verò multis? Conjugii illud Papale interdictum, manifestè injustum, impium, daemoniacum est, tum, quia contrarium est honori matrimonii, quod Deus instituit, quódque S. Paulus & ... in omnibus, in omni genere hominum, τιμιον honorabile, seu honoratum esse Hebr. xiii. 4. declaravit: tum, quia Spiritui S. & ... donis ejus, quæ liberè, uxoratis & non uxoratis distribuit, contrariatur, dum uxoratos per dona sua Ecclesiæ utiles esse vetat, adeóque Spiritum S. extinguit: tum quia pro[illegible, ~6 letters] hibendo matrimonium incenditur, πόρνείας, & occasio fornicationi vagisque & infamibus libidinibus datur: tum, quia ratio hujus præcepti, fictum scilicet Sacerdotium, quo corpus & sanguis Christi in manibus & ventriculo hominis offeratur, cum Christi gloria pugnat: tum, quia vera hujus præcepti ratio est constabilitio hujus Hierarchiæ, & conservatio dependentiæ Cleri universi à Papa: tum, quia laqueum conscientiæ injicit, 1. Cor. vii. 35. tum, quia præcepto Christi Matth. xix. 12. & Pauli 1. Cor. vii. 2. Col. ii. 18, 19, 20, 21. repugnat: tum denique, quia interdictum illud temerarium & plenum τλήμης & ἀνωδίας est, non tantùm, quia ex propriæ prudentiæ præsumtione oritur; sed etiam, quia conjugium sic interdicentes, id faciunt abjecto timore, quem illis Prophetiæ Dan. xi. 37. & hujus loci injungunt.
units.tr: XXXIII. But what do the hierarchical men here use, as in all the rest, the hypocrisy of liars, these "introducers of philologists" [φιλολόγων εἰσαγωγεῖς], by which they stupefy their conscience? They deny altogether that the Apostle is speaking of all who forbid marriage, but only of certain persons who absolutely forbid marriage to everyone, as if it were an evil thing; such as the Encratites, Carpocratians, Manichaeans, Marcionites and others were long ago. This is the bad excuse of a resisting conscience. For they invent, out of their own cleverness, that the Apostle speaks not of all but of certain persons, and that it is therefore lawful to forbid something to some which it would be wrong to forbid to all. Yet this prohibition cannot be just in one case and unjust and demonic in another. For Christ and all the Apostles desire the same Spirit, the same purity and holiness. And presbyters ought to be examples [typi] of the flock. What is therefore forbidden to a few is indeed tolerated, but is condemned in all, and is shown to be a dishonourable, unseemly, base and evil thing. The Papists share this doctrine with the ancient heretics, the Encratites, Manichaeans and others. Therefore in words they deny that they forbid marriage as an evil thing; in fact they affirm it, and betray a seared conscience. For they say that lawful love and lawful marriage are contrary to the purity of a priest, and more contrary than fornication. Why then do they forbid it, if they do not think it contrary to the holiness of a priest? They decree that a priest must be celibate because he handles the body of Christ; and yet they put that same body of Christ into the mouths of married men, whose hands are purer than the lips of priests. But why say more? That Papal prohibition of marriage is manifestly unjust, impious and demonic: first, because it is contrary to the honour of marriage, which God instituted, and which St Paul also declared to be "honourable [τίμιος] in all, in every kind of man" (Heb. 13:4); second, because it opposes the Holy Spirit and his gifts, which he distributes freely to the married and the unmarried, since by forbidding the married to be useful to the Church through their gifts it extinguishes the Holy Spirit; third, because by forbidding marriage it kindles fornication [πορνεία], and gives occasion to fornication, wandering and infamous lusts; fourth, because the reason for this precept, namely a fictitious priesthood by which the body and blood of Christ are offered in the hands and belly of man, fights against the glory of Christ; fifth, because the true reason for this precept is the establishment of this hierarchy and the preservation of the dependence of the whole clergy on the Pope; sixth, because it casts a snare upon the conscience (1 Cor. 7:35); seventh, because it contradicts the precept of Christ (Matt. 19:12) and of Paul (1 Cor. 7:2; Col. 2:18-21); and finally, because that prohibition is rash and full of arrogance [τλήμη] and folly [ἀνοήτος], not only because it arises from the presumption of one's own prudence, but also because those who forbid marriage in this way do so with the fear cast aside, which the prophecy of Daniel 11:37 and this passage enjoin upon them.

units.la: XXXIV. Par deficientium illorum à fide, & daemoniacis doctrinis attendentium ψευδολογία ἐν ὑποκρίσει, & cauteriata conscientia se prodit, dum præceptum abstinendi à cibis, quos Deus condidit, quódque charaterem eorum, qui apostasiam & daemoniacas doctrinas invexerunt, Apostolus fecit, interpretantur de iis, qui jubent abstinere ab omnibus cibis, & quidem, ut à re mala. Quis enim omnes cibos, & ut rem malam prohibere potest? Annon enim iidem haeretici, qui carnem à malo Deo esse dixerunt, ederunt tamen biberúntque? Sicut nemo omnibus conjugium prohibere potuit, quin genus humanum extingui cuperet: sic nemo omnibus cibos omnes prohibere potuit. Restringere ergo apostasiam ad ejusmodi conditiones stolidas, non aliud est, quàm apostasiam quandoque futuram fuisse, negare, adeóque Prophetiam ipsam infringere. Cœterum, rùm, Apostoli verba validarum instar compedum, Pontificios constringunt. De iis enim vaticinatur, qui in hypocrisi mendacia locuturi; adeóque etiam hanc ipsam epistolam, & totam Scripturam probaturi, & tamen hanc Prophetiam impleturi erant: quod palam est à Pontificiis fieri, qui & Prophetiam eam pro Divina habent, & exactè implent, facientes id, quod factu-ros Apostatas à fide, prædictum est. Iidem cibos quosdam prohibentes, eosdem noxios esse, vel impuros, reclamantes licet, arguunt. Neque illud obstat, quòd certis tantùm diebus vetant; quia etiam Lex Divina V. T. certos cibos ad tempus duntaxat vetans, eosdem Legaliter impuros declaravit. Ita fermentatus etiam pa-nis Israëlitis in Paschate, quo solo vetitus erat, impurus fuit, & edentes imò domos ipsas, in quibus erat, polluit. Neque etiam juvant exempla magna, quibus hic utuntur iidem, quæ per sophisticen usurpata, sunt cauterium illud, quo conscientiam suam, quoad hoc præceptum, exurunt. Dicunt enim, jejunatores fuisse Eliam, Danielem, Johannem, Christum, Christianos Veteres. Quasi scilicet vel Apostolus, vel nos apostasiam collocaremus in eo, ut quis carnem suam subigat, & temperanter vivat, aut etiam orandi causa, sua sponte vel communi consensu jejunet. In eo potiùs cum Apostolo collocamus, quòd homines hypocritæ & mendaces, præceptum dent de distinctione ciborum, vel etiam partem religionis in eo ponant, si voveant abstinentiam à certis cibis; & quòd homines talibus, tanquam Spiritum Dei singulari ratione habentibus, & pro lubitu docentibus, præcipientibúsve attendant.
units.tr: XXXIV. Likewise, those who fall away from the faith and attend to demonic doctrines, lying in hypocrisy [ψευδολογία ἐν ὑποκρίσει], and whose conscience is seared, betray themselves when they interpret the precept of abstaining from foods that God created, and the marks the Apostle gave of those who introduce apostasy and demonic doctrines, as applying to those who command abstinence from all foods, and indeed as from something evil. For who can forbid all foods, and forbid them as an evil thing? Did not those same heretics, who said that flesh comes from an evil god, nonetheless eat and drink? Just as no one could forbid marriage to all people without wishing the human race to be extinguished, so no one could forbid all foods to all people. To restrict apostasy to such foolish conditions is nothing other than to deny that apostasy would ever come, and so to overturn the prophecy itself. Moreover, the words of the Apostle bind the Papists like strong fetters. For he prophesies of those who would speak lies in hypocrisy, who would also approve this very epistle and all Scripture, and yet were going to fulfil this prophecy. This is plainly done by the Papists, who both hold that prophecy to be divine and fulfil it exactly, doing what was foretold that apostates from the faith would do. The same men, forbidding certain foods, argue that those foods are harmful or unclean, though they protest. Nor is it an objection that they forbid them only on certain days, for the divine Law of the Old Testament, forbidding certain foods only for a time, likewise declared them legally unclean. Thus leavened bread was unclean for the Israelites at Passover, the only time it was forbidden, and those who ate it, indeed the very houses in which it was, were defiled. Nor do the great examples which these same men use help them. Seized upon by sophistry, these examples are that cautery by which they sear their own conscience with regard to this precept. For they say that Elijah, Daniel, John, Christ and the ancient Christians were fasters. As if either the Apostle or we placed apostasy in this, that someone subdues his flesh and lives temperately, or fasts of his own accord or by common consent for the sake of prayer. Rather, we place it with the Apostle in this: that hypocritical and lying men give precepts about the distinction of foods, or even place part of religion in it when they vow abstinence from certain foods; and that men attend to such men, as if they had the Spirit of God in a singular way and taught or commanded at their pleasure.

units.la: XXXV. His ergò charaćteribus Papatui exaćtissimè
units.tr: XXXV. By these marks fitting the Papacy most exactly,

units.la: congruentibus, ad liquidum perducitur, in eodem, non alibi, apostasiam à fide, & doctrinas illas dæmoniacas, quas novissimis temporibus invalituras, Spiritus S. prædixit, regnare, adeóque in eodem dæmoniorum domicilium fixum esse. Nam duo illa Papatûs dogmata, puta de Conjugio Sacerdotum, & Jejunio piscario, dæmoniacas doctrinas neutiquam absolvunt, sed characteres duntaxat notissimi eorum sunt, ex quibus clarissimè cognosci possit & debeat, quinam illi sint, qui novissimis temporibus à fide deficient, & doctrinas dæmoniacas cujusmodi ipsæ etiam characteristicæ illæ sunt, invehent. Neque illud obstat, quòd apostasia à fide, & doctrinæ illæ dæmoniacæ etiam ante Reformationis tempora in Papatu obtinuerunt. Nec enim domicilium dæmonum Roma, dæmoniacas doctrinas sectata licet, dici potuit, quamdiu cum eadem vera Ecclesia commixta fuit: sed tum demùm, cùm secedente ab eadem verâ Ecclesiâ, non alii fere remanserunt, quàm ii, qui dæmoniacas doctrinas pridem equidem introductas, nunc demùm confirmatas, & anathematis etiam roboratas, mordicùs retinerent, & in erroribus illis se obdurarent.
units.tr: are brought clearly to light: that in this very place, and nowhere else, apostasy from the faith and those demonic doctrines, which the Holy Spirit predicted would prevail in the latest times, reign, and so the dwelling of demons is fixed in this very place. For those two dogmas of the Papacy, namely concerning the marriage of priests and the fast from fish, do not in themselves constitute demonic doctrines, but are only the most well-known marks of them. From these marks it can and must be most clearly recognised who they are that will fall away from the faith in the latest times, and what kind of demonic doctrines they will introduce, of which these very characteristic marks are examples. Nor is it an objection that apostasy from the faith and those demonic doctrines held sway in the Papacy even before the time of the Reformation. For Rome, although it followed demonic doctrines, could not be called the dwelling of demons as long as it was mixed with the true Church. Only when the true Church had withdrawn from it did there remain hardly anyone other than those who clung stubbornly to demonic doctrines, introduced long before but now at last confirmed and strengthened even by anathema, and who hardened themselves in those errors.

units.la: XXXVI. Cujusmodi Ecclesia Romana, post secessionem ab eadem Ecclesiæ Euangelicæ, evaserit, vel sofla Ecclesiæ definitio à Bellarmino perhibita, demonstrat. Is nempè de Eccl. Milit. cap. 2. Ecclesiam
units.tr: XXXVI. What sort of Church the Roman Church became after the Evangelical Church seceded from it, even the definition of the Church given by Bellarmine demonstrates.

units.la: definit cœtum hominum ejusdem Christianæ fidei professione, & eorundem sacramentorum communione colligatum, sub regimine legitimorum Pastorum, ac præcipuè uuius Christi in terris Vicarii, Romani Pontificis. Porrò definitionem suam sic explicat, ut tradat, illam solùm comprehendere eos, qui spe aut timore aliquo temporali profitentur fidem, etiamsi nullam habeant virtutem internam, & sint sicut capilli, aut ungues, aut mali humores in corpore humano. Dignum profecto tali capite corpus, & dignum tali corpore caput: Deinceps cap. 7. disputat, etiam reprobos esse membra Ecclesiæ Catholicæ, & cap. 10. non adversùs Calvinistas duntaxat, quos vocat, sed etiam adversùs Johannem de Turrecremata, etiam infideles occultos esse vera Ecclesiæ membra, pertendit. Cùm ergò Bellarminus ad hoc, ut membrum aliquis sit corporis veræ Ecclesiæ, ullam virtutem internam requiri neget, ac eos solùm comprehendat, qui spe aut timore aliquo temporali profitentur fidem, & pro Capite agnoscunt Papam; qui homo peccati & filius perditionis est, & ejusdem Ecclesiæ suæ membra vera, etiam reprobos & infideles occultos constituat; quàm parùm ejusmodi Ecclesia malignantium à dæmoniorum domicilio distet, res ipsa clamat. Neque enim membra ejusmodi Ecclesiæ, virtute interna nulla prædita, reprobi, occulti, infideles, dæmoniis præstare dici possunt, quia vel fidem Christianam profitentur ore, & corde abnegant, adeóque speciem pietatis habentes, potentiam ejusdem tollunt: vel Sacramenta ad tales non pertinentia, injustè usurpant: vel Papam pro capite suo agnoscentes, ab unico veróque Ecclesiæ Capite, Christo, deficiunt. Hypocritica ejusmodi confessio, sacramentorum, ceu gratiæ pignorum, rapina & sacrilegium, denique defectio à Christo Capite parùm profecto, vel nihil à Dæmoniis eos disparare possunt.
units.tr: He defines the Church, in his book On the Militant Church, chapter 2, as a gathering of men bound together by the profession of the same Christian faith and the communion of the same sacraments, under the rule of lawful pastors, and especially of the one Vicar of Christ on earth, the Roman Pontiff. Moreover, he explains his definition so as to teach that it comprises only those who profess the faith out of some hope or temporal fear, even if they have no inner virtue, and are like the hairs, or the nails, or the bad humours in the human body. Surely a body worthy of such a head, and a head worthy of such a body! Afterwards, in chapter 7, he disputes that even the reprobate are members of the Catholic Church, and in chapter 10 he maintains, not only against the Calvinists, as he calls them, but also against John of Torquemada, that even hidden unbelievers are true members of the Church. Since, therefore, Bellarmine denies that any inner virtue is required for someone to be a member of the body of the true Church, and comprises only those who profess the faith out of some hope or temporal fear and acknowledge the Pope as head, and makes the true members of his Church include even the reprobate and hidden unbelievers, the thing itself cries out how little such a Church of evildoers is distant from the dwelling of demons. For the members of such a Church, endowed with no inner virtue, reprobate, hidden, and unbelieving, cannot be said to differ from demons. Either they profess the Christian faith with the mouth and deny it in the heart, and so, having the appearance of godliness, deny its power; or they unjustly usurp the sacraments, which do not belong to such people; or, acknowledging the Pope as their head, they fall away from Christ, the one true Head of the Church. Such hypocritical confession, plunder and sacrilege of the sacraments, which are pledges of grace, and finally defection from Christ the Head, can separate them very little, or not at all, from demons.

units.la: XXXVII. Pertinent huc etiam novæ illæ creaturæ, quas Concilium Tridentinum, à Calice Babylonicæ Meretricis ebrium, in medium Ecclesiæ theatrum evomuit,
units.tr: XXXVII. To this belong also those new creatures whom the Council of Trent, drunk from the cup of the Babylonian Harlot, has vomited into the middle of the Church's theatre,

units.la: nec non no- vus Triden- tini concilii creaturis colligitur. muit, puta Fideles fornicarii, fideles adulteri, fideles molles, fideles masculorum concubitores, fideles fures, fideles avari, fideles ebriosi, maledici, rapaces, &c. Talia enim sanctis Patribus illis, non sine Numine, ne quorum domicilium sit Romana Ecclesia, dubitari amplius posset, exciderunt Seff. vj. cap. 15. ubi sic illi probaturi scilicet, quolibet mortali peccato amitti gratiam, sed non fidem, loquuntur: Adversus etiam hominum quorundam callida ingenia, qui per dulces sermones & benedictiones seducunt corda innocentium, asserendum est, non modo infidelitate, per quam & ipsa fides amittitur, sed etiam quocunque alio mortali peccato, quamvis non amittatur fides, acceptam justificationis gratiam amitti, Divinae Legis doctrinam defendendo: qua a Regno Dei non solum infideles excludit, sed & (NB) FIDELES quosque fornicarios, adulteros, molles, masculorum concubitores, fures, avaros, ebriosos, maledicos, rapaces, caeterosque omnes, qui lethalia committunt peccata. Bellos prosecto fideles, genuinae Babylonis incolas, a Patre Diabolo genitos, Patrisque sui genio ingenioque praeditos. Non his fidelium augustum illud nomen, sed Daemoniorum, qui ipsi quoque credentes, non tamen fideles, contremiscunt; justius appellatio quadrat.
units.tr: and the new creatures of the Council of Trent are also gathered together: namely, faithful fornicators, faithful adulterers, faithful effeminates, faithful men who lie with men, faithful thieves, faithful covetous, faithful drunkards, slanderers, robbers, etc. For such things fell from those holy Fathers, not without the divine will, so that there could be no further doubt whose dwelling the Roman Church is. In Session 6, chapter 15, where they set out to prove that by every mortal sin grace is lost, but not faith, they speak thus: "Against also the crafty minds of certain men, who by smooth words and blessings seduce the hearts of the innocent, it must be asserted that not only by unbelief, through which faith itself is lost, but also by any other mortal sin, although faith is not lost, the grace of justification received is lost, in defending the doctrine of the Divine Law, which excludes from the Kingdom of God not only unbelievers but also (NB) FAITHFUL of every kind: fornicators, adulterers, effeminates, men who lie with men, thieves, covetous, drunkards, slanderers, robbers, and all others who commit deadly sins." Certainly fine faithful, genuine inhabitants of Babylon, begotten by their father the Devil, and endowed with their father's disposition and character! The august name of faithful does not suit them; the name of demons, who also believe yet are not faithful and tremble, fits far more justly.

units.la: XXXVIII. Non Daemoniorum duntaxat domicilium, sed etiam φυλακή, custodia omnis spiritus im- mundi, & avis immundae atque exosae, Babylon esse debuit.
units.tr: XXXVIII. Babylon ought to have been the dwelling not only of demons but also a custody [φυλακή], a prison of every unclean spirit and of every unclean and hateful bird.

units.la: Cui non statim hic φυλακῇ, custodiae, seu claustra, monasteria, religiosorum καt' ἀντίφεσιν talium, qui plerique sane (bonos simplicesque paucos forte excipio) flatibus aereis, tenebrosi hujus Seculi acti, cor-
units.tr: Does this not at once bring to mind the custody [φυλακῇ], or the cloisters and monasteries of religious men, so called by antiphrasis [κατ' ἀντίφρασιν], most of whom (I perhaps except a few good and simple souls), driven by the aerial winds of this dark age, cor-

units.la: {y} Ioan. 3. corvorum & bubonum instar Pontificium Regnum pervolitant, in mentem veniunt ? Volucres immundæ, sic Rupertus explicat, & odibiles omnes superbi tam demones, quàm homines recte intelliguntur. Volatus námque volucrum levitatem & vanitatem significat superbientium. Nec verò qualibuscúnque volucribus, sed immundis assimilantur, verbi gratia, noctuis, sive upupis, quæ stercoribus humanis insidere delectantur. Immundæ aves eædem etiam voraces, rapaces sunt. Ea porrò de impuritate, crudelitate & avaritia Hierarchiæ universæ, atque in eadem etiam Religiosorum superiùs diximus, quæ huc reservata dubium neutiquam relinquunt, quorum in Hierarchica Babylone symbolum immundos Spiritus, immundas illas, & exosas aves Spiritus S. esse voluerit.
units.tr: {y} Ioan. 3. of ravens and owls, flit over the Papal kingdom? Unclean birds, Rupert explains, and all proud demons as much as men are rightly understood as hateful. For the flight of birds signifies the lightness and vanity of the proud. Nor are they likened to any birds at all, but to unclean ones, for example owls or hoopoes, which delight to settle on human dung. Unclean birds are also greedy and rapacious. What we said above about the impurity, cruelty and avarice of the whole Hierarchy, and of the religious orders within it, which is reserved for this place, leaves no doubt at all as to whom the Holy Spirit meant to be symbolised in the hierarchical Babylon by unclean spirits and by those unclean and hateful birds.

units.la: XXXIX. In eo censu haud postremi Jesuitæ Λεχάμψοι, Lojolæ socii, ferales, si qui alii, bubones sunt, quorum singulares hæreses Historia Papatûs edidseruit. Esse illos ὄρνεα μιμιομένα, volucres exosas omnibus, ipsis etiam reliquis in Papatu ordinibus, eas ad orcum ipsum, si facultatem haberent, properè relegaturis, in propatulo omnium est. Eorundem crudelitas, impuritas, avaritia, lippis & tonsoribus nota est. Vel sola Theologia illorum Moralis & Casuistica, de qua peculiari dissertatione & in eadem Papatûs historia nonnulla diximus, impuritatis doctrinæ illorum testis omni exceptione major est. Atque ne injuriam iis, quæsitissimum honoris sui sensum habentibus, facere videar, operæ pretium, testimonio domestico, Censuræ videlicet Facultatis Theologicæ Parisiensis, in librum Amadæi Guimenii, plerαque Theologiæ Moralis Jesuiticæ capita complexum, publica authoritate ante annos viginti, & quod excurrit,
units.tr: XXXIX. Among this company are not the least of the Jesuits, the Lechampsoi [Λεχάμψοι], the companions of Loyola, deadly owls if any others are; their singular heresies the History of the Papacy has set forth. That they are birds imitating [ὄρνεα μιμούμενα], hateful to all, even to the other orders within the Papacy, which would hurl them down quickly to the pit itself if they had the power, is plain to everyone. Their cruelty, impurity and avarice are known even to bleary-eyed men and barbers. Their Moral and Casuistical Theology alone, of which we have said something in a separate dissertation and in the same History of the Papacy, is a witness to their doctrine of impurity beyond all exception. And lest I seem to do an injustice to men who have a most refined sense of their own honour, it is worth citing domestic testimony, namely the Censure of the Faculty of Theology of Paris, published by public authority some twenty years ago against the book of Amadeus Guimenius, which embraces most of the chapters of Jesuit Moral Theology, and what follows.

units.la: Iesuitæ pro cæteris avis impuræ esse, cum ex aliis, tum ex Theologia eorum, Casuistica nec non Censura ejusdem Facultate Parisiensi adornata, in qua permulta ejus Propositionibus damnavit ... demonstrat. rit, vulgatæ, & Parisiis apud Guilhelmum Desprez impressæ, impuritatem impietatemque Sacerrimæ illius Societatis, propalare duxi. Ex ea enim jubare meridiano clarius elucescet, ubi, judicibus sanioribus iis, qui in Pontificia communione viventes, nondum planè cauterio exustam conscientiam habent, stabulentur doctrinæ illæ dæmoniacæ, & domicilium suum dæmonia fixerint. Nam Guimenium, adeóque Jesuitas plerósque omnes, quorum Interpretem Guimenius egerat, ipsa illa Censura ex eorum numero esse, quos in novissimis temporibus surrecturos prædixit Apostolus, attendentes spiritibus erroris, & doctrinis dæmoniorum, &c. candidè fatetur. Sed Censuram ipsam de verbo ad verbum repræsentemus.
units.tr: Iesuitae are unclean birds beyond the rest, both from other evidence and from their Theology, Casuistry and also the Censure of the same Faculty of Paris, in which it condemned very many of their propositions ... demonstrates. Since it has been made public and printed at Paris by Guillaume Desprez, I have thought it worth exposing the impurity and impiety of that most accursed Society. For from it will shine forth more clearly than the noonday sun where those demonic doctrines have their stalls, and where demons have fixed their dwelling, with the saner judges, those who live in the Papal communion and whose conscience is not yet wholly seared by cautery. For the Censure itself frankly admits that Guimenius, and therefore most of the Jesuits whose interpreter Guimenius had been, are among those whom the Apostle foretold would arise in the last times, giving heed to spirits of error and doctrines of demons, etc. But let us set out the Censure itself word for word.
THE CENSURE OF THE SACRED FACULTY OF THEOLOGY OF PARIS.

units.la: In Librum, cui titulus est, AMADÆI GUIMENII LOMARENSIS,
units.tr: On the book entitled, "A Little Work of Amadeus Guimenius of Lomar,

units.la: Olim primarii Sacræ Theologiæ Professoris, opusculum, singularia universæ ferè Theologiæ Moralis complectens: Adversus quorundam expositulationes contra nonnullas Iesuitarum opiniones Morales ad Tractatus de peccatis; de opinione probabili, &c. Editio novissima, &c. Lugduni, sumtibus Phil. Bordeę & Guillelmi Barbier, 1664. cum Appr. & Superiorum permissu.
units.tr: Formerly Principal Professor of Sacred Theology, comprising almost all the particular points of the whole of Moral Theology: Against certain persons' complaints about some Moral opinions of the Jesuits, concerning the Treatise on sins, on probable opinion, etc." Newest edition, etc. Lyon, at the expense of Philippe Borde and Guillaume Barbier, 1664, with approval and by permission of the superiors.

units.la: Immanem Pseudo-Theologorum de rebus moralibus scribendi libidinem, Summi Pontificis Alexandri VII. omniúmque ferè Gallicanæ Ecclesiæ Præsulum auctoritate, ac suâ Censurâ, in damnatâ Casuistarum Apologiâ compressam penitùs æstimaverat Sacra Facultas Parisiensis, ut in ... risienrisiensis. Neque sibi ampliùs quicquam in tam Sancto negotio agendum superesse autumabat, nisi ut Sancti Augustini freta consiliis, aeternum diligeret homines, quorum interfecerat errores, & sine superbia de veritate praesumeret, quae sine saevitia pro veritate certaverat, ac pro illis oraret, quos redarguerat atque convicerat. Cum ecce tranquillitatis Ecclesiasticae hostis acerrimus, nec tam Casuistarum, quàm spurcitiarum omnium quc scelerum Patronus, suis e latebris larvatâ fronte prodiit, Amadaeus Guimenius; qui se ex eorum esse numero satis superque comprobavit, quos in novissimis temporibus surrecturos praedixit Apostolus: Attendentes spiritibus erroris & doctrinis daemoniorum in hypocrisi loquentium mendacium, & cauteriatam habentium suam conscientiam, errantes & in errorem mittentes. Edidit quippe ille auctor opusculum, seu potius Anti-Euangelium in rebus spurcissimis obscoena curiositate ac sagacitate indagandis horrendum: ut mirum sit alicujus pudoris hominem, quippe primarii Theologiae Professoris sibi nomen affingit, tot monstra efformare ac scribere potuisse; quae modestioris ingenii Vir sine rubore ac verecundia legere non posset. Neque suos modo errores propalare de industria tentavit; verum etiam aliorum ejusdem furfuris scriptorum foeces, apertis nescio cujusdam, quam ab extrinseco vocant, probabilitatis canalibus, in corda fidelium effundere conatus est. Quamobrem cùm anno Domini 1664. die prima, mensis Septembris, Honorandus M. N. ANTONIUS DE BREDA, ejusdem Facultatis Doctor & Syndicus, in solenni congregatione habitâ in aula majore Collegii Sorbonae, post Missam de Spiritu Sancto, ut moris est, factam, Librum ad Facultatem detulisset, cui hic titulus erat inscriptus: Amadæi Guimenii Lomarensis olim primarii Sacræ Theologiæ Professoris opusculum, singularia universæ fere Theologiæ Moralis complectens: adversus quorundam expostulationes contra nonnullas Jesuitarum opiniones Morales ad Tractatus de peccatis; De opinione probabili, &c. Editio novissima, Lugd. sumtibus Phil. Borde, Laur. Arnaud. Petri Borde, & Guillelmi Barbier, 1664. cum Appr. & superiorum permissu. Cumque idem Honorandus M. N. Syndicus, scandala expositet; quibus quotquot sunt Viri frugi, atque Euangelicæ disciplinæ amatores sinceri, occasione horribilis libelli, afficerentur. Sacra Facultas, pro eâ quà pollet authoritate, non uno, sed pluribus Seculis totius orbis Christiani consensu probatâ, Apostolici dicti potissimum memor, quo sibi præscriptum novit, ut eos arguat & increpet in omni patientiâ & doctrinâ, qui sanam doctrinam non sustinent, sed ad sua desideria coacervant sibi Magistros prurientes auribus, & à veritate auditum avertunt, intelligitque necesse esse; ut Doctores verè Christiani tanquam boni Ministri Christi Jesu, enutriti verbis fidei & bonæ doctrinæ, eos redarguant, qui docent quæ non oportet, turpis lucri gratiâ: atque adeò à S. Cypriano edocta imperiti esse medici tumentes vulnerum sinus manu parcente, contrectare: Hujus libri examinandi provinciam tredecim selectis Doctoribus cum D. Decano ac Syndico commisit. Qui quidem cum repetitas inter se collationes per mensem integrum habuissent, in solenni congregatione apud Sorbonam, post Missam de Spiritu S. ut moris est, celebratam, plurimas propositiones ex prædicto Libro in indiculum collectas, primum Faculñtati
units.tr: The Sacred Faculty of Paris had judged that the monstrous itch of pseudo-theologians to write about moral matters had been thoroughly suppressed by the authority of Pope Alexander VII and of nearly all the prelates of the Gallican Church, and by its own censure, in the condemned Apology of the Casuists. It believed that nothing more remained to be done in so holy a business, except to follow the counsel of St. Augustine: to love men eternally, whose errors it had overthrown, and not presume on the truth with pride, which it had fought for without cruelty, and to pray for those whom it had refuted and convicted. Then, behold, an open enemy of ecclesiastical tranquillity, not so much a patron of the Casuists as of every kind of filth and crime, Amadeus Guimenius, came out of his hiding place with a masked face. He has more than sufficiently proved that he belongs to the number of those whom the Apostle foretold would arise in the last times: attending to spirits of error and doctrines of demons, speaking lies in hypocrisy, having their own conscience seared, erring and leading into error. That author has indeed published a little work, or rather an anti-Gospel, dreadful in its filthiest matters, probing them with obscene curiosity and cunning. It is remarkable that a man of any modesty, who gives himself the name of principal Professor of Theology, could have framed and written so many monsters, which a man of a more moderate nature could not read without blushing and shame. Nor has he merely tried deliberately to publish his own errors; he has also tried to pour the dregs of other writers of the same filth into the hearts of the faithful, through the open channels of what they call, from outside, probability, I know not what. Therefore, when in the year of the Lord 1664, on the first day of September, the Honourable Master N. Antonius de Breda, Doctor and Syndic of the same Faculty, in a solemn assembly held in the great hall of the Sorbonne College, after the Mass of the Holy Spirit had been celebrated, as is customary, had brought before the Faculty a book bearing this title: A little work of Amadeus Guimenius of Lomar, formerly principal Professor of Sacred Theology, comprising almost all the points of the whole of Moral Theology: against certain persons' complaints about some Moral opinions of the Jesuits, concerning the Treatise on sins; On probable opinion, etc. Newest edition, Lyon, at the expense of Philippe Borde, Laurent Arnaud, Pierre Borde, and Guillaume Barbier, 1664, with approval and by permission of the superiors. And when the same Honourable Syndic set out the scandals with which all who are upright men and sincere lovers of evangelical discipline were affected on the occasion of this dreadful pamphlet, the Sacred Faculty, by the authority it holds, which has been approved not by one but by several centuries and by the consent of the whole Christian world, and mindful especially of the apostolic saying by which it knows it is charged to rebuke and reprove, with all patience and teaching, those who do not endure sound doctrine, but heap up for themselves teachers after their own desires, tickling their ears, and turn away their hearing from the truth, and understood that it was necessary that true Christian teachers, as good ministers of Christ Jesus, nourished in the words of faith and of good doctrine, should refute those who teach what they ought not, for the sake of base gain: and so, taught by St. Cyprian that it is the mark of an unskilled physician to handle the swollen recesses of wounds with a sparing hand, it committed the task of examining this book to thirteen selected Doctors together with the Dean and the Syndic. These, after holding repeated conferences among themselves for a whole month, in a solemn assembly at the Sorbonne, after the Mass of the Holy Spirit had been celebrated as is customary, first reported to the Faculty, on the first day of October, the many propositions collected into a list from the aforesaid Book.

units.la: {*} Syndicus. tati retulerunt die 1. mensis Octobris. Quas propositiones Sacra Facultas, nunquam errari aestimans in defensione nimia veritatis, & in rejectione nimia falsitatis, ex famoso illo Amadæi Opusculo excerptas, typis mandari jussit, eâsque sive ab authore propugnatas, sive non defensas, infelici tamen illius solertia, contra mentem, & ad mentem ejus ex variis scriptoribus ab ipso depromtas, adeóque externæ, quam tuetur, probabilitatis fundamentis fulcitas ac stabilitas examinandas censuit: ut uno censuræ ictu non unicum modò scriptorem, sed & alios quoscunque fumosæ laxiorisque Theologiæ Agyrtas percuteret, qui, ut recte ait S. Cyprianus: Cùm felices homines dicunt, illos in errorem mittunt; cùm peccantes blandimentis adulantibus palpant, peccandi fomitem subministrant, nec delicta comprimunt sed nutriunt. Ac ne quis forsan illud minùs æquum existimet, quòd Sacra Facultas propositiones nonnullas ex eodem libello excerptas, damnaverit, quas author nec probare, nec improbare, imò & aliquando repudiare videtur; omnes monitos vult hunc Amadæi in miserabili illa lucubratiuncula fuisse scopum, ut Casuistarum quorumlibet patrocinium susciperet, atque omnibus, quemadmodum ipse in operis sui præfatione testatur, Theologiæ Professoribus veritatis speculum Jesuiticæ, absque nævo referens, doctrinæ vultum suo objiceret opusculo. Quamobrem postquam in operis sui præliminæ Propositiones, quæ, ut improbabiles, scandalosæ, temerariæ, & erroneæ, & Jesuitarum commenta in libro Anonymi notantur, vindicandas aggressus est, hanc toti suo operi coronidem imponit. Ex dictis jam apparet, quâ veritate, quo jure, quo zelo Anonymus in suo garriat libello propositiones præobjectas &c. {*} ... falsas, improbabiles, scandalosas, temerarias & erroneas, &c. Quomodo enim scandalosae & erroneae, quas Ecclesia in tot tantisque Doctoribus, opinionibus, opiniones non corrigit &c. nullibi ergo scandalum, nullibi error. Ex quo aperte intelligitur, id praesertim hoc suo libello molitum fuisse Amadaeum, ut omnes illas propositiones ab omni censura immunes, atque externae probabilitatis munimine tutas praestaret. Cum igitur iidem deputati a Sacra Facultate Doctores, saepius inter se super illis propositionibus convenissent, notisque assectas ad Facultatem detulissent, eadem Facultas toto negotio pro more, in deliberationem per D. Decanum, in quatuordecim Comitiis generalibus misso, de praedictis propositionibus selectis & examini subjectis sic censuit.
units.tr: Syndic. ...to the Faculty, on the first day of October, reported them. The Sacred Faculty, judging that one never errs in too great a defence of truth and in too great a rejection of falsehood, ordered that these propositions, excerpted from that notorious little work of Amadeus, be printed. It judged that they should be examined, and that they should be supported by the foundations of external probability which it defends, whether they were defended by the author or not, and whether they had been drawn from various writers by him, contrary to his intention or according to it, through his unhappy cleverness. Its aim was that, with one stroke of its censure, it would strike not only this one writer but all other quacks of smoky and overly lax theology who, as St. Cyprian rightly says: when they call sinning men happy, they lead them into error; when they flatter sinners with fawning caresses, they supply fuel for sin, and do not check offences but feed them. And lest anyone think it less fair that the Sacred Faculty has condemned some propositions excerpted from the same little book, which the author seems neither to prove nor to disprove, and even at times to reject, I want everyone to know that this was the aim of Amadeus in that wretched little nightwork: to take up the patronage of any Casuists whatever, and, as he himself testifies in the preface of his work, to present to all Professors of Theology a mirror of truth, reflecting the face of Jesuit doctrine without a blemish, in his little work. Therefore, after he had undertaken, in the preliminaries of his work, to vindicate the propositions which are noted as improbable, scandalous, rash, and erroneous, and as Jesuit inventions in the book of the Anonymous, he places this crown upon his whole work: From what has been said it is now evident with what truth, with what right, with what zeal the Anonymous chatters in his little book that the propositions objected above etc. are...false, improbable, scandalous, rash and erroneous, etc. For how can those be scandalous and erroneous which the Church, in so many and such great Doctors, does not correct in opinions etc.? Therefore there is nowhere scandal, nowhere error. From this it is clearly understood that Amadeus laboured especially in this little book so that he might render all those propositions free from every censure and safe under the defence of external probability. Therefore, when the same Doctors deputed by the Sacred Faculty had met together several times over those propositions, and had brought them to the Faculty marked with their notes, the same Faculty, in accordance with custom, referred the whole matter for deliberation through the Dean, in fourteen general assemblies, and on the aforesaid propositions, selected and subjected to examination, judged as follows.

units.la: PROPOSITIONES EXCERPTAE EX LIBRO AMADAEI GUIMENII &c. DE EBRIETATE
units.tr: PROPOSITIONS EXCERPTED FROM THE BOOK OF AMADAEUS GUIMENIUS, &c., ON DRUNKENNESS
Page 3, number 1.

units.la: Mirum non est, quod hi Doctores doceant, ebrietatem esse licitam ad vitandam mortem, quando alii ad conservandam etiam salutem licere putant.
units.tr: It is no wonder that these teachers teach that drunkenness is lawful to avoid death, when others think it lawful even to preserve health.

units.la: · Pag. 70. Ad evitandum grave malum, quod aliter vitari non potest, licitum est inebriare authorem.
units.tr: · Page 70. To avoid a grave evil which cannot otherwise be avoided, it is lawful to make the author drunk.

units.la: P. 108. n. 2. Ex quo principio fe inebriantem ad vitandam mortem, ab extrinseco aliter imminentem, excusant à culpâ.
units.tr: Page 108, number 2. On the strength of this principle they excuse from fault a man who makes himself drunk to avoid death threatening him from outside.

units.la: CENSURA. Doctrina his propositionibus contenta, est falsa, scandalosa & contraria verbis Apostoli.
units.tr: CENSURE. The doctrine contained in these propositions is false, scandalous, and contrary to the words of the Apostle.

units.la: . DE CONTUMELIA. p. 86. n. 2. & 3. Quando contumeliosus non speratur se cohibiturus; sed perstiturus in contumelia semel dicta, aut alias aggressurus, is, qui eam patitur, potest licitè illi dicere: Mentiris, &c. Et sanè difficilè videtur, quòd hoc non liceat.
units.tr: . ON INSULT. Page 86, numbers 2 and 3. When an insulting person is not expected to restrain himself, but will persist in the insult once uttered, or will go on to attack again, the one who suffers it may lawfully say to him: "You lie," &c. And indeed it seems hard to see why this should not be lawful.

units.la: .CENSURA. Hæc propositio intellecta hoc sensu, quòd liceat dicere, Mentiris, per modum convicii, falsa est, & Scripturæ Sacræ contraria.
units.tr: CENSURE. This proposition, understood in this sense, that it is lawful to say "You lie" by way of insult, is false and contrary to Holy Scripture.

units.la: De HOMICIDIO. p 6. Licitum est desiderare alteri mortem, & de illa gaudere, non quatenus illi mala; sed quatenus tibi bona: v. g. ut ei in bonis succedas.
units.tr: On MURDER. Page 6. It is lawful to wish another dead and to rejoice in it, not insofar as it is evil for him, but insofar as it is good for you: for example, so that you may succeed him in his goods.

units.la: P. 7. n. 2. A mortali excusatur mater, quæ mortem filiabus exoptat, quia occasione ipsarum, malè secum agitur à marito, aut injuriis afficitur.
units.tr: Page 7, number 2. A mother who wishes death on her daughters is excused from mortal sin, because on account of them her husband treats her badly or inflicts injuries on her.

units.la: P. 87. n. 3. Eum qui imponit falsum testimonium alicui, ut suam justitiam & honorem defendat, non peccare mortaliter: cur ergò pecccabit ex eo quòd convicianti dicat: mentiris? & quidem si pro defensione honoris licet alterum occidere, cur non & vocare mendacem?
units.tr: Page 87, number 3. A person who bears false witness against someone in order to defend his own justice and honour does not sin mortally. Why then will he sin by saying "you lie" to one who insults him? And indeed, if it is lawful to kill another in defence of honour, why is it not also lawful to call him a liar?
Page 98.

units.la: Credo, quòd per injuriam percussus, possit statim repercutere, etiamsi invasor non deberet ultra progredi, sed ad vitandam ignominiam & dedecus: posset qui colaphum, exempli gratiâ, accepit, gladio statim repercutere, non ad sumendam vindiƈtam, sed ad vitandam infamiam.
units.tr: I believe that one struck by an injury may at once strike back, even if the attacker ought not to go further, but to avoid disgrace and dishonour: one who has, for example, received a slap may at once strike back with a sword, not to take vengeance, but to avoid infamy.

units.la: Potest etiam interfici qui Virum aliquem honoratum conviciis & maledictis afficit, nec potest aliter cogi ut taceat; talis enim est invasor honoris.
units.tr: Also, one who heaps insults and abuse on some honourable man may be killed, and he cannot otherwise be forced to be silent; for such a man is an assailant of honour.

units.la: Respondeo esse cuipiam licitum prædictum injuriantem & detrahentem, notabiliter famam alterius, clàm occidere, si nullâ aliâ viâ talis famæ læsionem evitare queat, in praxi tamen difficile est hoc modo defensionis uti.
units.tr: I answer that it is lawful for anyone to kill secretly a person who notably injures the good name of another by such insult and slander, if he cannot avoid the injury to that reputation by any other way; in practice, however, it is hard to use this kind of defence.

units.la: Nescio ab alio, quàm à Basilio Pontio improbabilem dici opinionem asserentem, patrem posse occidere filiam in adulterio deprehensam, & maritum similiter uxorem; me enim judice, stando authoritati, est probabilis, & stando rationi, quam debuisset percallere Basilius, certa & evidens.
units.tr: I know of no one but Basilius Pontius who calls the opinion improbable which asserts that a father may kill a daughter caught in adultery, and a husband likewise his wife; for in my judgement, relying on authority it is probable, and relying on reason, which Basilius ought to have understood thoroughly, it is certain and evident.

units.la: CENSURA. Hæ propositiones sunt falsæ, scandalosæ, & respectivè pietati, charitati & justitiæ con- trariæ; vindictæ, crudelitati & avaritiæ viam aperien- tes.
units.tr: CENSURE. These propositions are false, scandalous, and, in their respective ways, contrary to piety, charity and justice, opening the way to revenge, cruelty and greed.

units.la: De DUELLO p. 88. n. 3. Posséntque pro illa citari Doctores asserentes, honoris defendendi causâ, non solùm licere acceptare duellum absque animo pugnandi, sed etiam ad illud provocáre.
units.tr: On DUELLING. Page 88, number 3. And teachers may be cited for it who assert that, for the sake of defending honour, it is lawful not only to accept a duel without intending to fight, but even to provoke one.

units.la: Ad vitandam infamiam, quando prudenter judicatur non superesse aliud remedium, nisi acceptatio, & in præfixum locum egressio, quamvis sequatur congressio, & ex ista mors, vel vulneratio alicujus concertantium, licitè potest acceptari. Idem dici debet de oblatione.
units.tr: To avoid infamy, when it is prudently judged that there is no other remedy except acceptance and going out to the appointed place, even though a meeting follows and from it the death or wounding of one of the combatants, the challenge may lawfully be accepted. The same should be said of the offer.

units.la: CENSURA. Hæc doctrina falsa est, scandalo- sa, contraria juri divino & humano, tam Ecclesiastico, quàm civili, imò & naturali.
units.tr: CENSURE. This doctrine is false, scandalous, contrary to divine and human law, ecclesiastical as much as civil, and indeed even natural.

units.la: De PROBABILITATE p. 27. n. 1. Ex authoritate unius tantùm, posse quem illam (nempè opinionem) in praxi amplecti, licet à principiis intrinsecis falsam & improbabilem existimet.
units.tr: On PROBABILITY. Page 27, number 1. On the authority of one teacher alone, a person may in practice embrace that opinion, even though he judges it false and improbable on intrinsic principles.

units.la: P. 28. n. 3. Eit quot Doctores militent pro sententia Tanneri, cujus unius authoritas sufficeret ad efficiendam probabilem.
units.tr: Page 28, number 3. So many teachers fight for the opinion of Tanner that the authority of him alone would suffice to make it probable.
