Forte dolebit etiam primo coetu per Babylonis casum antiqui illius Dei sui Panacei cultus theatralem splendorem intercidere, quem Majores eorum ita amplexi olim fuerunt, ut omnes fortunas suas cum eodem quasi conjunxissent, quem propterea posteri eorum summo studio, tanquam Regnorum suorum palladium conservatum cupiverunt semper, quòd suo statui commodum usque & proficuum haetenùs experti sunt, & sibi etiam quodammodo metuere cogantur, siquidem illud Idolum ita concideret. Mercatores quinam sint, & quæ corum merces, abunde Dissertatione superiori discussimus. Flebunt illi lugebúntque, ὅτι ἡ γέμων ἐμπορία αὐτῶν ἀπώλετο οὐκ ἀγοράζει, quia mercimonium illorum nemo amplius emit, v. 11. Quæ enim Mercatoribus justior querelarum causa dari poterit, quàm si mercium suarum æstimationem deteriorem fieri sentiant? Cremata Babylone & eversa, fucus mercium Babylonicarum toti mundo innotescet; accidéntque illis, quod Demetrio illi Idolopoeo, ejúsque confortibus, quorum quæstus per S. Pauli conciones, idolorúmque ruinam intercepum est, Act. xix. 24, 25. Tertii Ordinis, Nauticæ turbæ, planctus, etsi quoad plangentium gestus lugubrior, quàm priorum, videri poterit, minori tamen strepitu perficietur. Clamabunt illi, videntes fumum incendii Babylonis, dicéntque v. 18. Quæ similis Civitati illi Magnæ? Fortè illi in mundo circumspicient Civitatem Magnam, cui, deletâ hâc, nomen suum dare possint. Vel certè verba hæc erunt contendentium pro authoritate Civitatis illius,& restitutionem ejus flagitantium. Conjecto in capita sua pulvere, vicem gesturo mitrarum & coronarum, quibus redimiti fuerant, clamabunt, & flentes lugentesque dicent v. 19. Væ, væ, Civitas illa Magna, in qua ditati sunt omnes habentes naves in mari ex pretiositate ejus: quia unâ horâ desolata est. Lugebunt merito interitum Meretricis, apud quam inveniebant mercedem nequitiæ, quam nunc gratis exercere cogentur.
units.tr: Vol. II. mmmmm and their lament will be scarcely pathetic. Indeed they will stand afar off [ἀπὸ μακρόθεν], for fear of her torment, not daring to bring her aid or apply an effective remedy to her suffering. Rather, they will marvel at God's judgment on the overthrow of Babylon, saying in v. 10: Woe, woe, that great city Babylon, that mighty city, for in one hour has your judgment come. They will marvel that that false Church could be destroyed so suddenly, a Church which had such powerful defenders in the world and such strong, deep roots that it was commonly regarded as impregnable. Perhaps at first they will also grieve that through Babylon's fall the theatrical splendour of that ancient cult of their god Panaceas will perish, which their forefathers once embraced so fully that they had, as it were, joined all their fortunes to it. Their descendants have always desired to preserve it with the greatest zeal, as the palladium of their kingdoms, because they have experienced its advantage and profit for their state until now, and they are even forced to fear for themselves, since that idol would collapse in this way. Who the merchants are, and what their wares are, we have discussed fully in the preceding dissertation. They will weep and mourn, because no one buys their merchandise any more [ὅτι ἡ γέμων ἐμπορία αὐτῶν ἀπώλετο οὐκ ἀγοράζει], v. 11. For what more just cause of complaint can be given to merchants than that they perceive the value of their wares to be diminished? With Babylon burnt and overthrown, the sham of Babylonian merchandise will become known to the whole world; and what happened to that silversmith Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen, whose gain was cut off by St. Paul's sermons and the ruin of idols, will happen to them, Acts 19:24, 25. The lament of the third order, the seafaring crowd, though in its gestures it may appear more mournful than that of the former, will be carried out with less noise. Seeing the smoke of Babylon's burning, they will cry out and say in v. 18: What city is like this great city? Perhaps they will look about in the world for a great city to which they can give their name once this one is destroyed. Or certainly these words will be those of men contending for the authority of that city and demanding its restoration. Throwing dust on their heads, taking the place of the mitres and crowns with which they had been adorned, they will cry out, and weeping and mourning will say in v. 19: Woe, woe, that great city, in which all who had ships on the sea were made rich by her costliness, for in one hour she is made desolate. They will rightly mourn the destruction of the harlot, through whom they found the wages of wickedness, which they will now be forced to practise for nothing.

units.la: LXVIII. Hinc adeò liquet, Babylonis excidium cum mundi totius excidio conjunctum non fore; quia consummato eo supererunt Reges, Mercatores, Nautæ, ipsáque etiam, uti ex cap. xix. colligitur, fidelium Ecclesia, propter quam solam mundus durat. Parùm enim probabilis iri, nonnullorum opinio est, Romam quidem, Babylonis Metropolin, ante finem mundi incendio consumtum iri; sed Babylonem reliquam ad finem usque Mundi perseveraturam. Illa enim Babylon comburetur & destructur penitùs, cujus scortationem, abominationes, dominium in Regna terræ, casum priorem, & ab eadem separationem Ecclesiæ hactenùs continua Prophetiæ serie Spiritus S. pertexuit. Hanc porrò Babylonem non Urbem solam mœnibus septam, sed Politiam Religiosam, & statum Hierarchicum universum figurare, Dissert. iij. ß. 13, 14, &c. pluribus comprobavimus. Non ergò Babylonis finalis excidium solam Romanam Urbem, sed universam Politiam Religiosam Babylonicam involvet, & potestatem Cathedræ abolebit. Manebunt tamen ad finem Mundi & illustrem usque adventum Domini apostatæ, seu defectores improbi, Christo occasionem præbituri finiendi tempus patientiæ, celeremque in eos interitum adducen-
units.tr: LXVIII. From this it is therefore clear that the destruction of Babylon will not be joined with the destruction of the whole world; for when that has been accomplished, the kings, merchants and sailors will survive, and also, as is gathered from ch. 19, the Church of the faithful itself, for whose sake alone the world endures. For the opinion of some is hardly probable, that Rome, indeed the metropolis of Babylon, will be consumed by fire before the end of the world, but that the rest of Babylon will persist until the end of the world. For that Babylon will be burned and utterly destroyed whose fornication, abominations, dominion over the kingdoms of the earth, former fall, and the separation of the Church from her, the Holy Spirit has woven into the continuous series of prophecy until now. Moreover, we have shown at length that this Babylon signifies not the city alone enclosed by walls, but the whole religious polity and the hierarchical state, Dissert. iii. §§ 13, 14, etc. Therefore the final destruction of Babylon will involve not only the Roman city but the whole Babylonian religious polity, and will abolish the power of the Chair. Yet there will remain until the end of the world, and until the glorious coming of the Lord, apostates or wicked defectors, who will give Christ the occasion to end the time of patience and to bring swift destruction upon them

units.la: di. Tales erunt Mercatores lugentes, aliique, veritati vi- Etas dare manus nescii. Deleta tamen Babylone, hi ipsi quoque deleti censebuntur merito: quia potestate, quae Babylonis anima est, & authoritate Religionis omni pri- vati, in mundo agent. Etenim si apostatae hi non pote- runt efficere, ut non Ecclesia omnis in loco colligatur, ipsi contra cogentur occultari, vagari, vixque adeo locum in- venient, in quo tutò religionem profiteri audent, faris uti- que consumti & deleti videbuntur. Planè sicut populus Judaicus confunctus delectúsque censebatur tum, cùm co- rum Politia in toto mundo deleta est, nèque restitui in æternum poterit; quanquam Judæi hinc inde palantes & Christum æternum Regem blasphemantes, non desint; Atque juxta illud exemplum actum iri cum Regno Baby- lonis & Anti-Christi, manifestè Prophetia nostra Apo- cal. XVIII. 8, 9, &c. arguit, ubi licet dicatur, Babylonem veluti lapidem molarem magnum in mare cum impetu conjectum iri; mox tamen multos procul staturos, & ca- sum Babylonis deploraturos, subjicitur: quemadmodum scilicet Judæi nunc procul stantes, casum Hierosolymæ deplorant.
units.tr: Such will be the mourning merchants, and others who know not how to give their hands to the truth. Yet, Babylon having been destroyed, these men too will rightly be considered destroyed, because they will act in the world with the power which is the soul of Babylon and with the authority of religion deprived of everything. For if these apostates cannot bring it about that the whole Church is not gathered in one place, they will themselves be forced to hide and wander, and will hardly find a place where they dare to profess religion openly; and so they will seem to be utterly consumed and destroyed. Just as the Jewish people were considered cut off and rejected when their polity was destroyed throughout the whole world, and it cannot be restored for ever; although Jews wandering here and there and blaspheming Christ the eternal King are not lacking. And that the affair of the kingdom of Babylon and Antichrist will go in accordance with that example, our prophecy Rev. 18:8, 9, etc. clearly argues, where, although it is said that Babylon will be cast into the sea with violence like a great millstone, it is immediately added that many will stand afar off and lament the fall of Babylon: just as, to be sure, the Jews now standing afar off lament the fall of Jerusalem.

units.la: LXIX. Hac ergo ratione & Babylon ante adventum
units.tr: LXIX. In this way, therefore, Babylon also, before the coming

units.la: Domini plagis suis confecta, penitùs succidetur: & ó Christi, in reliquis tamen illis apostasiae suis non ante Παρουσίαν illam, abolebitur penitùs, hoc est, ad nihilum redigetur, adventùs Domini, hoc est, jubar quoddam Regni ipsius præcessurum adventum ad judicandum vivos & mortuos, significat. Solemus enim dicere, Regem venire, qui in via est, cujus anteambulones videmus. Ita aurora Solis an- tecambula, Παρουσίας affulgentia praesentiæ vel ad- venventus Solis dici potest, licet nondum Sol horizontem illum ingressus sit.
units.tr: Having been worn down by the Lord's blows, it will be utterly cut off; and the Christ's... in those other remaining apostasies of its own, it will be entirely abolished, before that parousia [Παρουσία], that is, reduced to nothing, before the coming of the Lord. That is, a certain radiance of his kingdom signifies the coming that will precede his judging of the living and the dead. For we are accustomed to say that a king is coming when we see those who walk before him on the road. So dawn may be called the forerunner of the sun, and the shining forth of the parousia [Παρουσίας] may be called the presence or the coming of the Sun, although the sun has not yet entered that horizon.

units.la: LXX. Neque etiam Babylonis finale excidium cum mundi excidio conjunctum iri illud evincit, quòd Apocal. xix. 19. 20. post bellum illud Bestiæ, Regum terræ & exercitus eorum cum sedente in equo & exercitu ejus, subjicitur. Et prehensa est Bestia, & cum ea Pseudo-propheta, qui fecerat signa coram ea, quibus seduxerat eos, qui acceperunt signaturam Bestiæ, & adorantes imaginem ejus. Vivi conjecti sunt ambo in stagnum ignis, quod ardet sulphure. Ubi Bestia (posterior nempe eadem cum Babylone Apoc. xiii. 14. &c) & Pseudo-propheta, distinguuntur ut status, & statûs Caput; ad ostendendam scilicet Capitis, & simul statûs unà cum Capite ruinam. Sicut autem supplicium Corachi, Dathanis & Abiromi non ideò cum consummatione seculi conjunctum erat, quia vivi in infernum, hoc est, exitium & tormenta sempiterna descenderunt: sic neque Bestiæ & Pseudo-prophetæ supplicium cum fine mundi connexum erit, quia vivi in stagnum ignis conjicientur. Quanquam etiam tum ζῶντς vivi, adeóque corporaliter non occisi, in stagnum ignis conjecti dici poterunt, quando à judicio & supplicio suo superstites, scd Statu & Politia sua penitùs privati, incipient illa videre & audire, quæ dolorem & invidiam infernalem creabunt, & cum ulcere malæ conscientiæ conflictabuntur, perpetuisque adeò ardoribus æstuabunt. Sic Zach. xiv. 12. &c. plaga populorum, qui contra Hierosolymam belligerati sunt, definitur, quòd stantibus super pedibus suis caro & oculi & lingua tabescent. Sed de eo quicquid sit, fata viam invenient, & destinationem eorum Deus, justus Judex, ad consolationem Ecclesiæ, & Regni sui incrementum implebit.
units.tr: LXX. Nor does it prove that the final destruction of Babylon will be joined with the destruction of the world, because at Rev. 19:19-20 it is placed after the battle of the Beast, the kings of the earth and their armies, against him who sat on the horse and his army: And the Beast was taken, and with him the false prophet, who had done signs before him, by which he had deceived those who received the mark of the Beast and worshipped his image. These two were cast alive into the lake of fire, which burns with brimstone. Here the Beast (the latter being, of course, the same as Babylon, Rev. 13:14, etc.) and the false prophet are distinguished as the state and the head of the state, evidently to show the ruin of the head and, along with the head, of the state. But just as the punishment of Korah, Dathan and Abiram was not joined with the consummation of the age, though they went down alive into hell, that is, into destruction and everlasting torments, so neither will the punishment of the Beast and the false prophet be connected with the end of the world, though they will be cast alive into the lake of fire. Yet even then they may be called living [ζῶντες], and so not killed bodily, when, surviving their judgment and punishment but utterly stripped of their state and polity, they begin to see and hear those things which will create grief and infernal envy, and they will be struck by the ulcer of an evil conscience and will thus seethe with perpetual burnings. So Zech. 14:12, etc., describes the plague of the peoples who waged war against Jerusalem: their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their sockets, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth. But whatever be the case with this, the fates will find their way, and God, the just Judge, will carry out their destiny, for the comfort of the Church and the increase of his kingdom.

units.la: LXXI. Sic fuit planctus Regum, Mercatorum, & Nautarum. Coeterùm, Angelus planctum hunc interpellans Coelum, Apostolos & Prophetas ad jubila invitat. Laetare, sic Apoc. xviii. 20. hortatur, super ea Coelum, & Sancti Apostoli & Prophetae, quia judicavit Deus judicium vestrum de ipsa. Quae aperta erit plangentium derisio. Est autem in verbis iis apostrophe in Scripturis usitata, veluti Esai. i. 2: Audite Coeli, &c. qua ad communem fidelium omnium laetitiam, non ex carnali affectu, sed puro corde, ob vindicatum laesi honoris Divini, laesae Ecclesiae, pupillae suae nefas, testificandam Deus concludet. Laetabitur justus, cum viderit ultionem: pedes lavabit in sanguine improbi. Dicetque homo utique est fructus justo, utique est Deus, est judex in terra Psal. lviij. 11, 12. Itaque luctus Sanctorum convertetur in gaudium interminabile, & laetitia impiorum peribit.
units.tr: LXXI. So was the lament of the kings, the merchants, and the sailors. Meanwhile the Angel, interrupting this lament, calls heaven, the Apostles and the Prophets to rejoicing. "Rejoice," he urges, as in Revelation 18:20, "over her, heaven, and holy apostles and prophets, because God has judged your judgment upon her." This will be an open mockery of the mourners. Now, in these words there is an apostrophe, a figure in common use in Scripture, as in Isaiah 1:2: "Hear, heavens," etc. By it God will conclude that a joy common to all the faithful is to be testified, not from carnal affection but from a pure heart, on account of the vindication of the wronged honour of God, of the wrong done to his wronged Church, his ward. "The righteous will rejoice when he sees the vengeance; he will wash his feet in the blood of the wicked. And man will say, Surely there is a reward for the righteous; surely there is a God who judges on earth" (Psalm 58:11, 12). Thus the mourning of the saints will be turned into unending joy, and the gladness of the impious will perish.

units.la: LXXII. Compellat Angelus Coelum, vel proprie dictum, vel metaphorice Ecclesiam; vel Synecdochice Coelites, puta Apostolos & Prophetas, hoc est, sive Spiritus eorum consummatos: sive eos omnes, qui propter doctrinam Apostolorum & Prophetarum non dilexerunt animas suas usque ad mortem, sive Prophetarum & Apostolorum in communi munere successores, omnesque adeo pios, doctrinâ Apostolicam & Propheticam in terris docendi munere defungentes, qui Meretricis hujus malitiâ premebantur maximè; quibus proin majorem consolationis mensuram Deus impertietur.
units.tr: The Angel addresses heaven, either properly so called, or metaphorically the Church; or, by synecdoche, the inhabitants of heaven, namely the Apostles and Prophets, that is, either their spirits made perfect; or all those who, for the sake of the doctrine of the Apostles and Prophets, did not love their lives unto death; or the successors of the Prophets and Apostles in their common office, and indeed all the godly who discharge the office of teaching the apostolic and prophetic doctrine on earth, and who were especially oppressed by the malice of this harlot. To these God will therefore grant a greater measure of consolation.

units.la: Hoc enim erit illud tempus denuntiatum. Apoc. xi. 18. quo Deus dabit mercedem servis suis Prophetis, & Sanctis timentibus nomen ejus, parvis & magnis, corrumpétque eos, qui corruperunt terram. Sic plane v. 24. in Babylone inventus dicitur sanguis Prophetarum & Sanctorum, & OMNIUM mactatorum in terra. Ex quo colligitur, Apostolorum & Prophetarum appellationem non tam angustè heic esse accipiendam, uti vulvulgò accipitur, sed per eos omnes illos indicari, qui munerum istorum aliquid vel ad Christi gloriam, vel ad Babylonis redargutionem quocunque in loco terræ, & quocunque tempore obierunt, & Babylonis sævitiam eo nomine experti sunt. Deducunt autem nos hæc Angeli verba ad illud Christi Matth. xxiii.35. quo Sacerdotibus & Scribis Propheticidis improperat: Ut veniat super vos omnis sanguis justus, qui effusus est super terra, à sanguine Abelis justi, usque ad sanguinem Zachariæ, Filii Barachiæ. Sicut igitur Hierosolymæ sanguis Abelis: sic Babyloni sanguis mactatorum omnium imputatur. Homicida enim unus cum omnibus homicidis communionem habet, & unà cum omnibus homicidis punitur. Revelabit terra sanguines suos, & non amplius occisos suos teget. Esai. xxvi: 2. quia in generatione illa omne homicidium punietur, & Deus testabitur se inquisitorem sanguinis longè fagacius, quàm Hispanici & Romani Inquisitores, tot innocentum sanguinem effundentes, veros fideles omni studio & indagine sua in hac terra inquirere & cingere potuerunt.
units.tr: For this is the time foretold, Rev. 11:18, when God will give the reward to his servants the prophets, and to the saints who fear his name, small and great, and will destroy them, who have corrupted the earth. So too at v. 24 it is said that there was found in Babylon the blood of prophets and saints, and of ALL who have been slain on the earth. From this it is gathered that the names of apostles and prophets are not to be taken so narrowly here as they commonly are, but that by them ALL are meant who have undertaken some part of these offices, whether for the glory of Christ or for the refutation of Babylon, in whatever place on earth and at whatever time, and who have on that account experienced Babylon's savagery. But these words of the angel lead us to that saying of Christ, Matt. 23:35, in which he reproaches the priests and scribes as murderers of the prophets: That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel even unto the blood of Zacharias, son of Barachias. Just as the blood of Abel is imputed to Jerusalem, so the blood of all the slain is imputed to Babylon. For one murderer shares fellowship with all murderers and is punished together with all of them. The earth shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain, Esai. xxvi: 2. For in that generation every murder will be punished, and God will show himself a seeker into blood far more keenly than the Spanish and Roman Inquisitors, who shed the blood of so many innocents, could ever search out and surround true believers with all their zeal and investigation on this earth.

units.la: LXXIII. Invitati ad lætitiam Cœli, Apostoli, Prophetæ, omnésque adeò fideles in lætitiam incredibilem erumpent toti, & gratulantium gestientiúmque voces invicem ineffabili gaudio perfusi, reddent. Solebat hactenùs Babylon, quoties Sanctos vicit, hymnum illum suum Panegyricum, Te Deum laudamus, concinere, atque sic Deo in Cœlis illudere. Sic Roma post ferales Eoas illas Parisienses, Bartholomæi nomine infames; post subjugatam Bohemiam, Palatinatum: victam Rupellam, atque novissimè non semel hymnum illum suum ingenti cum solennitate & lætitia cantavit, vel potiùs reboavit. Babylone ergò ipsa deletâ, cantores Sanctissimi, turba multa in Cœlo, hoc est, Sancti plurimi, Cœlestis Hierosolymæ συμφωνίαν; Seniores viginti quatuor, & quatuor animalia; omnésque Servi Dei, qui timent eum, parvi & magni; suum illud Halleluja, seu verum Te Deum laudamus, sonora voce decantabunt, gloriam, honorem, & potentiam dantes DEO Vindici & Agno Sponso suo, quòd judicavit Meretricem Magnam, quæ corrupit terram scortatione sua, & vindicavit sanguinem servorum suorum ex manu ejus: quòd Regnum capessivit Dominus Deus omnipotens: quòdque venerunt nuptiæ Agni, (per Babylonicum huncce Rivalem interpellatæ & sufflaminatæ hactenus) & uxor ejus se præparavit. Apoc. xix. 1 —— 11. De sacerrimo isthoc & triumphali cantico, admirabilique epinicio, mysteriis haud dubiè refertissimo, nihil, quàm pauca dicere præstat. Erit, erit tempus, cùm gaudium isthoc consummabitur, & omnes recto corde præditi, victæ & in æternum exitium præcipitatæ, Babyloni insultabunt, & HALLELUJAH illud lætissimo pectore succinent.
units.tr: LXXIII. The apostles and prophets, and indeed all the faithful, invited to the joy of heaven, will break out wholly into incredible gladness, and, overcome with unspeakable joy, will return to one another their voices of congratulation and exultation. Hitherto Babylon, whenever she had conquered the saints, used to sing her own panegyric, Te Deum laudamus, and so mock God in heaven. So Rome, after that deadly Parisian slaughter of the eve, infamous for the name of Bartholomew, after the subjugation of Bohemia and the Palatinate, after the conquest of La Rochelle, and most recently more than once, has sung that hymn of hers with great solemnity and joy, or rather bellowed it back. Therefore, with Babylon herself destroyed, the most holy singers, a great multitude in heaven, that is, very many saints of the heavenly Jerusalem, symphony [συμφωνίαν]; the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures; and all the servants of God who fear him, small and great; will sing out with a loud voice their own Halleluja, or true Te Deum laudamus, giving glory, honour and power to God the avenger and to the Lamb their bridegroom, because he has judged the great harlot, who corrupted the earth with her fornication, and has avenged the blood of his servants at her hand; because the Lord God omnipotent has taken up his kingdom; and because the marriage of the Lamb has come (hitherto hindered and obstructed by this Babylonish rival), and his wife has prepared herself. Apoc. xix. 1–11. Concerning this most sacred and triumphal song, and admirable hymn of victory, doubtless very full of mysteries, it is worth saying only a few things. The time will come, will come, when this joy will be made complete, and all who are upright in heart, when Babylon is conquered and cast down into eternal destruction, will exult over her and sing out HALLELUJAH with the most joyful heart.

units.la: LXXIV. Concludimus, Hierarchiam seu Clerum Ecclesiæ Romanæ dominantem, ob impietatem multiplicem Severum Dei Judicium provocantem, illud aliquatenus jam subivisse, & finale illud ac decretorium porrò subituram esse; adeóque, cùm cetera omnia paria esse, gravissimis rationum ponderibus demonstraverimus, BABYLONEM MAGNAM, MATREM SCORTATIONUM ET ABOMINATIONUM TERRÆ esse, cui proin sit confusio æterna! Tibi verò, O DOMINE, MAGNIFICENTIA, ET ROBUR, ET GLORIA, ET VICTORIA, ET HONOR IN ÆTERNUM. AMEN. HALLELUJA.
units.tr: LXXIV. We conclude that the ruling hierarchy, or clergy, of the Roman Church, by provoking the severe judgment of God through its manifold impiety, has already in some measure undergone that judgment and will undergo the final and decisive one still to come. Therefore, since all else is equal, we have demonstrated by the weightiest arguments that BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH, deserves eternal confusion! But to Thee, O LORD, BE MAGNIFICENCE, AND POWER, AND GLORY, AND VICTORY, AND HONOUR FOR EVER. AMEN. HALLELUJAH.
F I N I S.

units.la: Marcelli Malpighii Opera Omnia; seu Thesaurus locupletissimus Botanico-Medico-Anatomicus, viginti quatuor tractatus complectens & in duos tomos distributus. Editio Novissima, cum omnibus Codicibus hactenus publici Juris factis collata, nunc primum elegantissimâ methodo dispositia, variis Iconibus, ut & Authorum diversorum opusculis (materiam hanc spectantibus) illustrata, quibus omnes Editiones hactenus caruerunt, notis marginalibus, amplissimis passim adaucta, crasis emendata Sphalmatis, & uberrimis Illustrata Indicibus, tam Capitum quam Rerum & Verborum, In Quarto 2. voll. cum figuris æneis 1687. Cum Privilegiis.
units.tr: The Complete Works of Marcellus Malpighius; or the most abundant Thesaurus of botany, medicine and anatomy, comprising twenty-four treatises and distributed into two volumes. Newest edition, collated with all the copies published hitherto, now first arranged in a most elegant method, illustrated with various engravings and with the short works of various authors on this subject, which all earlier editions lacked, greatly enlarged in many places with marginal notes, the mixture corrected and the printer's errors amended, and provided with very full indexes of chapters, things and words.
